title: Snatch
tagline: Stealin' stones and breakin' bones.
overview: Unscrupulous boxing promoters, violent bookmakers, a Russian gangster, incompetent amateur robbers and supposedly Jewish jewelers fight to track down a priceless stolen diamond.
plot:
Snatch is a 2000 crime comedy film written and directed by Guy Ritchie and produced by Matthew Vaughn. Set in the London criminal underworld, it has an ensemble cast including Jason Statham, Stephen Graham, Dennis Farina, Brad Pitt, Alan Ford, Benicio del Toro, Lennie James, Rade Šerbedžija, Jason Flemyng and Vinnie Jones. Its two intertwined storylines follow the pursuit of a stolen diamond and a small-time boxing promoter, played by Statham, who becomes entangled with a sadistic gangster played by Ford.

In Antwerp, robbers disguised as Orthodox Jews steal an 84-carat diamond. Their leader, Franky Four-Fingers, travels to London to fence it through the dealer Doug the Head for the American crime figure Cousin Avi. One of the robbers steers Franky toward Boris the Blade, an ex-KGB arms dealer, and secretly urges Boris, his brother, to steal the stone. Meanwhile, unlicensed promoter Turkish and his partner Tommy are drawn into a fight for crime boss Brick Top, but their boxer, Gorgeous George, is knocked out by Mickey O'Neil, a bare-knuckle champion among the Irish Travellers who had just swindled Tommy over a caravan. Turkish recruits Mickey as a replacement in return for a new caravan for his mother, and Brick Top orders that Mickey throw the fight.

Exploiting Franky's gambling habit, Boris sends him to a bookmaker and hires small-time crooks Sol, Vinny and Tyrone to rob it and grab Franky. The robbery fails, but Franky is abducted and killed by Boris, who takes the diamond. Avi hires the bounty hunter Bullet Tooth Tony, setting off a chain of chases and shootouts in which Boris dies and the stone passes to Sol and Vinny, whose dog then swallows it and escapes. Avi accidentally shoots Tony while aiming at the dog and goes home. Brick Top's men burn down Mickey's mother's caravan, killing her, but in the fixed fight Mickey gets up and knocks out his opponent, having bet on himself, and the Travellers massacre Brick Top and his crew. Turkish and Tommy find the dog, have a vet remove the diamond, and sell it through Doug, bringing Avi back to London.

Shot in London and Buckinghamshire in late 1999, the film opened in the United Kingdom on 1 September 2000, setting an opening record for an 18-certificate film, and grossed $83.6 million worldwide on a $10 million budget. Critics found it perhaps style over substance but praised its snappy dialogue and dark comedy, giving it 74% approval on Rotten Tomatoes; it has gained a cult following.

title: Charlie and the Chocolate Factory
tagline: Prepare for a taste of adventure.
overview: A young boy wins a tour through the most magnificent chocolate factory in the world, led by the world's most unusual candy maker.
plot:
Charlie and the Chocolate Factory is a 2005 musical fantasy film directed by Tim Burton and written by John August, based on Roald Dahl's 1964 children's novel. Johnny Depp stars as the eccentric candy maker Willy Wonka and Freddie Highmore as Charlie Bucket, alongside David Kelly, Helena Bonham Carter, Noah Taylor, Missi Pyle, James Fox, Deep Roy and Christopher Lee. It is the second film adaptation of the book, after Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory (1971), and the Dahl estate gave Warner Bros. a high degree of creative input during its long development.

Charlie is a kind boy who lives in poverty with his parents and four bedridden grandparents in a crooked little house in the shadow of Wonka's enormous chocolate factory. Years earlier, Wonka closed the factory to the public because of industrial espionage by rival confectioners, firing all his workers, including Charlie's Grandpa Joe. Charlie's father has recently lost his job at a toothpaste factory. One day Wonka announces that he has hidden five Golden Tickets in Wonka Bars around the world; the finders will receive a tour of the factory and a lifetime supply of chocolate, and one will win a special extra prize.

The first four tickets are found by the gluttonous Augustus Gloop, the spoiled Veruca Salt, the aggressively competitive gum-chewer Violet Beauregarde and the know-it-all video game addict Mike Teavee. After two failed attempts, Charlie finds the last ticket with money he picks up from the snowy street and chooses Grandpa Joe to accompany him. Inside the factory, Wonka leads the children and their parents through a series of fantastical rooms, staffed by the tiny Oompa-Loompas, played by Deep Roy, who sing a mocking song each time one of the badly behaved children falls victim to temptation and is removed from the tour. Flashbacks reveal Wonka's lonely childhood with his strict dentist father, played by Christopher Lee, which explains his strange relationship with family and the choice he offers the last child remaining.

The film received generally positive reviews, with praise for its visuals, Danny Elfman's score and its fidelity to Dahl's story, while Depp's unusual interpretation of Wonka divided critics. It grossed about $475 million worldwide, becoming one of the highest-grossing films of 2005, and earned an Academy Award nomination for Best Costume Design.

title: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
original_title: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
tagline: One ring to rule them all
overview: Young hobbit Frodo Baggins, after inheriting a mysterious ring from his uncle Bilbo, must leave his home in order to keep it from falling into the hands of its evil creator. Along the way, a fellowship is formed to protect the ringbearer and make sure that the ring arrives at its final destination: Mt. Doom, the only place where it can be destroyed.
plot:
The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring is a 2001 epic fantasy film directed by Peter Jackson, who wrote the screenplay with Fran Walsh and Philippa Boyens. Adapted from The Fellowship of the Ring, the first volume of J. R. R. Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings, it opens Jackson's trilogy. New Line Cinema financed and distributed the film, but it was shot and edited entirely in New Zealand alongside the other two parts, with filming beginning on 11 October 1999. It premiered at the Odeon Leicester Square in London on 10 December 2001 and opened in the United States on 19 December.

In the Second Age, the Dark Lord Sauron secretly forged the One Ring to dominate the other Rings of Power given to Elves, Dwarves and Men. Isildur of Gondor cut it from Sauron's hand, but the Ring corrupted him and was lost after his death, later passing to the creature Gollum and then to the hobbit Bilbo Baggins. At his 111th birthday in the Shire, Bilbo departs and leaves the Ring to his nephew, Frodo. The wizard Gandalf the Grey discovers what it is and that Sauron has learned the words "Shire" and "Baggins" from the captured Gollum. Frodo sets off with his gardener, Samwise Gamgee, while Gandalf is imprisoned by the wizard Saruman, who has joined Sauron. Joined by Merry and Pippin and pursued by the nine Nazgûl, the hobbits are guided by the Ranger Strider, but Frodo is stabbed with a Morgul blade on Weathertop. Strider's beloved, the Elf Arwen, carries him to Rivendell, where Gandalf, freed by a Great Eagle, rejoins them.

At a council called by Arwen's father, Elrond, it is agreed that the Ring must be destroyed in the fires of Mount Doom in Mordor. At Parth Galen, Boromir tries to seize it, then dies defending Merry and Pippin, who are captured by Saruman's Uruk-hai. Frodo resolves to go on alone, but Sam refuses to leave him.

title: The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers
original_title: The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers
tagline: A New Power Is Rising.
overview: Frodo and Sam are trekking to Mordor to destroy the One Ring of Power while Gimli, Legolas and Aragorn search for the orc-captured Merry and Pippin. All along, nefarious wizard Saruman awaits the Fellowship members at the Orthanc Tower in Isengard.
plot:
The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers is an epic fantasy film of 2002 directed by Peter Jackson, the second part of his trilogy adapted from J. R. R. Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings, written by Fran Walsh, Philippa Boyens, Stephen Sinclair and Jackson. Elijah Wood returns as Frodo, with Sean Astin as Sam, Andy Serkis as Gollum, Viggo Mortensen as Aragorn, Ian McKellen as Gandalf, Orlando Bloom as Legolas, John Rhys-Davies as Gimli, Bernard Hill as King Théoden, Christopher Lee as Saruman and David Wenham as Faramir.

Frodo and Sam are lost in the rocky Emyn Muil. They capture Gollum, a former bearer of the One Ring, and Frodo, moved to pity, lets him guide them toward Mordor despite Sam's distrust. Aragorn, Legolas and Gimli chase the Uruk-hai who seized Merry and Pippin into Rohan, where riders under Éomer, exiled by a king under the sway of Saruman and Wormtongue, destroy the orcs; the hobbits escape into Fangorn Forest. There the three hunters meet Gandalf, returned from death after slaying the Balrog. At Edoras he frees Théoden from Saruman's control, and the king leads his people to Helm's Deep. On the way, Éowyn falls for Aragorn, who falls in a wolf-rider attack and is presumed dead, but survives. In Rivendell, Elrond persuades Arwen to leave Middle-earth, while Galadriel convinces him to send elves to aid Rohan.

In Fangorn, Merry and Pippin befriend Treebeard, an Ent. When the Ent council declines to join the war, Pippin leads Treebeard past the forests Saruman has felled, and the furious Ents storm Isengard, flooding it and trapping Saruman in his tower. At Helm's Deep, the outnumbered defenders are joined by elves under Haldir, but the Uruk-hai blast through the wall and Haldir falls. Aragorn persuades Théoden to ride out in a last charge at dawn, when Gandalf and Éomer arrive with the Rohirrim and rout the enemy. Meanwhile Gollum steers Frodo and Sam away from the Black Gate, and the hobbits are captured by Faramir, Boromir's younger brother, who learns of the Ring and resolves to take it to his father in Gondor. In the ruins of Osgiliath a Nazgûl nearly seizes Frodo, until Sam saves him and reminds him there is still good worth fighting for. Faramir lets them go, but Gollum, feeling betrayed, plots to lead them to "her" at Cirith Ungol and reclaim the Ring.

Released in December 2002, the film grossed $923 million worldwide, the highest of the year. It won Academy Awards for visual effects and sound editing and was nominated for Best Picture.

title: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King

tagline: The eye of the enemy is moving.
overview: Aragorn is revealed as the heir to the ancient kings as he, Gandalf and the other members of the broken fellowship struggle to save Gondor from Sauron's forces. Meanwhile, Frodo and Sam take the ring closer to the heart of Mordor, the dark lord's realm.
plot:
The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King is a 2003 epic fantasy film directed by Peter Jackson from a screenplay he wrote with Fran Walsh and Philippa Boyens. Based on The Return of the King, the third volume of J. R. R. Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings, it is the sequel to The Two Towers (2002) and the final installment of Jackson's trilogy. The ensemble cast includes Elijah Wood, Ian McKellen, Viggo Mortensen, Sean Astin, Liv Tyler, Orlando Bloom, Cate Blanchett, John Rhys-Davies, Bernard Hill, Billy Boyd, Dominic Monaghan, Hugo Weaving, Miranda Otto, David Wenham, Karl Urban, John Noble, Andy Serkis and Ian Holm.

The film opens with the story of how Sméagol, a river-dwelling hobbit, murdered his cousin Déagol for the One Ring and was transformed by it into the wretched Gollum. In the present, after the victory at Helm's Deep, Gandalf, Aragorn, Legolas, Gimli and King Théoden of Rohan reunite with Merry and Pippin at Isengard. When Pippin looks into Saruman's seeing-stone, the palantír, he glimpses Sauron's plan to attack Minas Tirith, the capital of Gondor. Gandalf rides there with Pippin to warn the city's grief-stricken steward, Denethor, and has Pippin light the beacons calling Rohan to Gondor's aid.

Meanwhile Frodo and Sam continue toward Mordor with the Ring, guided by Gollum, who secretly schemes to turn Frodo against Sam and reclaim the Ring by leading them into the lair of the giant spider Shelob. As Sauron's vast armies besiege Minas Tirith, the riders of Rohan charge to the city's defense, and Aragorn, urged by Elrond to claim his destiny as heir to the throne of Gondor, takes the Paths of the Dead to summon an army of oath-breaking spirits. After the Battle of the Pelennor Fields, the surviving leaders march on the Black Gate of Mordor to distract Sauron, giving Frodo and Sam their last chance to reach Mount Doom and destroy the Ring.

The Return of the King was a critical and commercial triumph. It grossed more than $1.1 billion worldwide, becoming only the second film at the time to pass that mark and the highest-grossing film of 2003. It won all eleven Academy Awards for which it was nominated, including Best Picture and Best Director, tying the record held by Ben-Hur and Titanic, and is widely regarded as one of the greatest films ever made.

title: Spirited Away
tagline: Prepare to be spirited away.
overview: A young girl, Chihiro, becomes trapped in a strange new world of spirits. When her parents undergo a mysterious transformation, she must call upon the courage she never knew she had to free her family.
plot:
Spirited Away is a 2001 animated fantasy film written and directed by Hayao Miyazaki, produced by Studio Ghibli. The film follows Chihiro, a 10-year-old girl who is moving to a new home with her parents.

As they drive through the countryside, Chihiro's father becomes distracted and stops at a mysterious tunnel. Unbeknownst to them, this tunnel leads to a magical world where spirits reside. Chihiro's parents are turned into pigs by the witch Yubaba, who runs a bathhouse for spirits.

Chihiro is forced to work in the bathhouse, where she encounters various strange creatures and characters, including Haku, a young man with a mysterious past. As Chihiro navigates this new world, she must use her wit and resourcefulness to survive and find a way to free herself from Yubaba's grasp.

Throughout her journey, Chihiro faces numerous challenges and obstacles, including the bathhouse's strict rules and the wrath of Yubaba. However, with the help of Haku and other allies, Chihiro discovers her own strength and determination, ultimately leading her to confront Yubaba and reclaim her parents.

One of the most striking aspects of Spirited Away is its exploration of themes such as identity, growth, and the complexities of adulthood. Chihiro's journey can be seen as a metaphor for the challenges of growing up and finding one's place in the world.

The film features stunning animation, with intricate details and vibrant colors that bring the magical world to life. The characters are equally well-developed, with complex personalities and motivations that add depth to the story.

Overall, Spirited Away is a timeless classic that has captivated audiences worldwide with its enchanting tale of self-discovery and empowerment. Its themes and characters continue to resonate with viewers of all ages, making it one of Studio Ghibli's most beloved and enduring films.

title: O Brother, Where Art Thou?
tagline: They have a plan... but not a clue.
overview: In the deep south during the 1930s, three escaped convicts search for hidden treasure while a relentless lawman pursues them. On their journey they come across many comical characters and incredible situations. Based upon Homer's 'Odyssey'.
plot:
O Brother, Where Art Thou? is a 2000 American crime comedy film written, produced, and directed by the Coen brothers. The movie is loosely based on Homer's Odyssey, set in the Deep South during the Great Depression.

The story follows three escaped convicts: Ulysses Everett McGill (played by George Clooney), Pete Hogwallop (played by John Turturro), and Delmar O'Donnell (played by Tim Blake Nelson). The trio is on the run from the law, searching for a hidden treasure that they believe will lead them to freedom.

The movie begins with the three convicts escaping from prison in Mississippi. They are pursued by the ruthless Sheriff Bill Skaggs (played by John Goodman), who is determined to capture them and bring them back to justice. Along the way, they encounter various characters, including a blind man named Big Dan Teague (played by Danny Glover) who becomes their ally.

As they journey through the rural South, the three convicts face numerous challenges, including run-ins with the law, wild animals, and treacherous terrain. They also sing and dance to bluegrass music, which becomes a recurring theme throughout the film.

Throughout their journey, Ulysses, Pete, and Delmar encounter various women, including Penny (played by Holly Hunter), who becomes Ulysses' love interest. However, their quest for treasure is constantly thwarted by Sheriff Skaggs and his deputies.

As the story unfolds, the three convicts begin to realize that they are not as different from each other as they initially thought. They develop a sense of camaraderie and loyalty, which ultimately helps them overcome their differences and work together to achieve their goal.

The movie's climax features an epic musical number, "I'll Fly Away," in which the three convicts sing and dance with Big Dan Teague and his family. The song is a celebration of freedom and redemption, and it marks a turning point in the story as Ulysses, Pete, and Delmar finally find what they have been searching for.

In the end, Ulysses and Penny escape from Sheriff Skaggs' clutches, while Pete and Delmar are captured. However, in a surprising twist, Pete is revealed to be the long-lost son of Big Dan Teague, and he is welcomed into his family as a member. The movie ends with Ulysses and Penny riding off into the sunset, free at last.

Overall, O Brother, Where Art Thou? is a quirky and entertaining film that combines elements of comedy, drama, and music to create a unique and memorable cinematic experience.

title: Bad Education
overview: Two children, Ignacio and Enrique, know love, the movies and fear in a religious school at the beginning of the 1960s. Father Manolo, director of the school and its professor of literature, is witness to and part of these discoveries. The three are followed through the next few decades, their reunion marking life and death.
plot:
In 1980 Madrid, struggling film director Enrique Goded is looking for his next project when he receives an unexpected visit from an actor looking for work. The actor claims to be Enrique's boarding school friend and first love, Ignacio Rodriguez. Ignacio, who is now using the name Ángel Andrade, has brought along a short story titled "The Visit", hoping that Enrique would be interested in filming it—and giving him the starring role. Enrique is intrigued since "The Visit" describes their time together at the Catholic boarding school, while also including a fictional account of their reunion years later as adults.
"The Visit" is set in 1977. It tells the story of a transgender drag queen with the stage name Zahara, whose birth name is Ignacio. Zahara plans to rob a drunken admirer but discovers that the man is her boyhood lover Enrique Serrano, so she defiles him in his sleep instead. The encounter stirs angry memories, and Zahara visits her old school to confront Father Manolo, who abused her there when she was a boy. She demands one million pesetas from Manolo in exchange for halting publication of her manuscript, also called "The Visit".
That story is set in a Catholic boarding school for boys in 1964. At the school, Ignacio, a 10-year-old student with a beautiful boy soprano voice, is the object of lust of Father Manolo, the school principal and literature teacher. Ignacio falls in love with his classmate Enrique, and the two go to the local cinema and grope each other. Manolo discovers them together that night and becomes enraged. Ignacio offers to submit to the priest's molestation in exchange for having his friend not punished, but Manolo still expels Enrique anyway.
The director, Enrique Goded, wants to adapt the story but balks at Ángel's condition that he be cast as Zahara, feeling that the Ignacio he loved and the Ángel of today are totally different people. Suspicious, he drives to see Ignacio's mother in Ortigueira, Galicia and learns that in fact Ignacio has been dead for four years and that the man who came to his office is actually Ignacio's younger brother, Juan. Enrique's curiosity is piqued, so to "see how far [Juan] would go"—and without letting on what he knows—he casts Ángel/Juan in the role of Zahara. Ángel becomes Enrique's sexual partner, and Enrique revises the script so that it ends with Father Manolo, whom Zahara was trying to blackmail to get money for sex reassignment surgery, having Zahara murdered. After the scene is shot, Ángel breaks out in tears unexpectedly.
The film set is visited by Manuel Berenguer, formerly Father Manolo, who has resigned from the clergy. Berenguer confesses to Enrique that the new ending of the film is not far from the truth: Ignacio, a transsexual junkie, did blackmail him, but Berenguer managed to string her along—while mostly falling hard for Ignacio's younger brother, Juan.

title: Donnie Darko
tagline: 28 days, 6 hours, 42 minutes, 12 seconds... that is when the world will end.
overview: After narrowly escaping a bizarre accident, a troubled teenager is plagued by visions of a large bunny rabbit that manipulates him to commit a series of crimes.
plot:
Donnie Darko is an American science fiction psychological thriller of 2001 written and directed by Richard Kelly in his feature debut. Jake Gyllenhaal plays Donnie, a troubled teenager, with Jena Malone as Gretchen Ross, Maggie Gyllenhaal as his sister Elizabeth, Mary McDonnell as his mother Rose, Patrick Swayze as the motivational speaker Jim Cunningham, Noah Wyle as the science teacher Dr. Monnitoff and Drew Barrymore.

On 2 October 1988, in a Virginia suburb, Donnie sleepwalks out of his house, drawn by a mysterious voice, and meets a figure in a grotesque rabbit costume called Frank, who tells him the world will end in 28 days, 6 hours, 42 minutes and 12 seconds. Waking on a golf course, he returns home to find that a jet engine of unknown origin has crashed into his bedroom. As the visions continue, a psychiatrist diagnoses daylight hallucinations. When Frank asks Donnie whether he believes in time travel, Donnie consults Monnitoff, who gives him The Philosophy of Time Travel, a book by Roberta Sparrow, a seemingly senile old woman known locally as Grandma Death.

Sleepwalking at Frank's urging, Donnie floods the school. He begins dating Gretchen, a newcomer hiding from a violent stepfather. Donnie mocks the gym teacher Kitty Farmer's lessons drawn from Cunningham's teachings and insults Cunningham at an assembly. At a movie, while Gretchen sleeps, an unmasked Frank, his right eye a bleeding hole, persuades Donnie to burn down Cunningham's house. Firefighters find a stash of child pornography in the ruins, and he is arrested. Rose replaces Kitty as chaperone of their daughters' dance troupe on a trip to Los Angeles.

With both parents away, Donnie and Elizabeth throw a Halloween party, where Gretchen, distraught over her missing mother, sleeps with Donnie. Hours before the deadline, he takes Gretchen and two friends to Sparrow's house, where two bullies are robbing it. As the boys fight in the road, an oncoming car runs over Gretchen. Its driver is Elizabeth's boyfriend, Frank Anderson, wearing the rabbit costume, and Donnie shoots him in the eye. At dawn, as a vortex forms, Donnie drives Gretchen's body to a ridge and watches the plane carrying his mother home lose an engine into the vortex. The 28 days unwind, and Donnie wakes on 2 October, laughing as the engine crashes into his room and kills him.

Released soon after the September 11 attacks, the film was barely promoted and grossed just $517,375 in its first run, but it gained a cult following.

title: Brokeback Mountain
tagline: Love is a force of nature
overview: Two modern-day cowboys meet on a shepherding job in the summer of '63, the two share a raw and powerful summer together that turns into a lifelong relationship conflict
plot:
Brokeback Mountain is a 2005 American romantic drama film directed by Ang Lee, based on the short story of the same name by Annie Proulx. The film stars Heath Ledger and Jake Gyllenhaal as two cowboys who fall in love in rural Wyoming.

The movie begins with an elderly Ennis Del Mar (Heath Ledger) recounting his life story to a nurse, telling her about his childhood growing up on a ranch in Wyoming. As a young man, Ennis meets Jack Twist (Jake Gyllenhaal), a new cowboy hired by the ranch owner, Joe Aguirre. The two men are forced to share a tent during their stay at the ranch, and they develop an instant attraction towards each other.

Despite their strong feelings, Ennis and Jack come from different worlds and have different expectations for their lives. Ennis wants to settle down with a family of his own, while Jack is more free-spirited and wants to travel the world. The two men share a brief but intense romance during their stay at the ranch, which leaves them both emotionally scarred.

Years go by, and Ennis and Jack go their separate ways. Ennis marries Alma (Michelle Williams), a woman he meets while working on a construction site in Denver, and they have two children together. However, Ennis's feelings for Jack never truly fade away, and he is haunted by memories of their time together.

Meanwhile, Jack travels the world, taking on various jobs and experiencing different cultures. He eventually settles down with a man named Lureen (Anne Hathaway), who bears him two sons. Despite his outward success, Jack is unhappy and unfulfilled, feeling like a part of him is missing.

The film's plot takes a dramatic turn when Ennis and Alma are forced to confront the reality of their marriage. Ennis's feelings for Jack resurface, and he begins to question his life choices. In a shocking twist, Ennis kills himself in a motel room, leaving behind a note that reveals his true feelings.

The film ends with an elderly Jack visiting Ennis's grave, where he is met by the ghost of Ennis. The two men share a final moment together, and it becomes clear that their love has endured even after death. The film's ending is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the audience to ponder the nature of Ennis and Jack's relationship.

Throughout the film, Ang Lee masterfully explores themes of love, identity, and the human condition. The cinematography is breathtaking, capturing the vast beauty of the Wyoming landscape. The performances by Ledger and Gyllenhaal are outstanding, bringing depth and nuance to their characters.

Brokeback Mountain was a critical and commercial success, earning several Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture, Best Director, and Best Actor for Heath Ledger's posthumous win. The film's impact on the LGBTQ+ community was significant, helping to raise awareness about gay rights and challenging societal norms around same-sex relationships.

plot:
Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon is a 2000 wuxia film directed by Ang Lee, produced by China Film Co-Production Corporation, and written by James Schamus, David Koepp, and Wang Dulu. The film is set in 18th-century China during the Qing dynasty.

The story begins with the introduction of Shu Lien (Michelle Yeoh), a skilled warrior and bodyguard who has been tasked with protecting the legendary Green Destiny sword from falling into the wrong hands. Shu Lien's life takes a dramatic turn when she meets Jen Yu (Zhang Ziyi), a young and beautiful woman who is revealed to be the daughter of a powerful warlord, Fa Zhou.

Jen Yu is being pursued by the ruthless General Ruan (Chow Yun-fat) and his men, who seek to capture her and use her as leverage to gain control over the region. Shu Lien agrees to help Jen escape from General Ruan's forces, but their journey together sets off a chain of events that exposes long-buried secrets about Jen's past.

title: Akira
tagline: Neo-Tokyo is about to E.X.P.L.O.D.E.
overview: A secret military project endangers Neo-Tokyo when it turns a biker gang member into a rampaging psychic psychopath that only two teenagers and a group of psychics can stop.
plot:
Akira is a 1988 anime science fiction film directed by Katsuhiro Otomo, based on his own manga series of the same name.

In post-apocalyptic Neo-Tokyo, a young biker gang member named Shotaro Kaneda is involved in a street racing accident that kills one of his friends. As a result, he is hospitalized and discovers that he has developed telekinetic powers after being exposed to a mysterious energy known as "Akira".

The story begins with the introduction of Colonel Shikishima, who is investigating a series of bizarre occurrences in Neo-Tokyo. He soon discovers that Akira, a powerful psychic child, has been released from his containment facility and is wreaking havoc on the city.

Kaneda's friend Tetsuo Shima, who was involved in the accident that gave Kaneda his powers, begins to exhibit similar telekinetic abilities after being exposed to Akira. As Tetsuo's powers grow stronger, he becomes increasingly unstable and violent, causing chaos throughout the city.

Meanwhile, a secret government agency known as the Public Security Section 9 is formed to deal with the crisis. The team consists of Colonel Shikishima, his deputy Lieutenant Gendo, and three other members: Bodo, Lila, and Kei. They are tasked with capturing Akira and stopping Tetsuo's rampage.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Akira is not just a simple psychic child, but a powerful being who has been manipulated by the government to further their own interests. The true purpose of the government's experiments on Akira is revealed to be the creation of a new breed of super-soldiers using his powers.

The climax of the film takes place in an abandoned amusement park, where Kaneda and Tetsuo engage in a fierce battle. In the end, Kaneda manages to defeat Tetsuo by using his own telekinetic powers against him, but not before Tetsuo's body is severely damaged.

In the aftermath, Akira is taken into custody by Colonel Shikishima, who reveals that he has been working to uncover the truth about the government's experiments on Akira. The film ends with a sense of hope and renewal, as Kaneda reflects on the events that have transpired and the lessons he has learned.

Throughout the film, Otomo explores themes of psychic powers, government conspiracies, and the consequences of playing with forces beyond human control. The animation is highly detailed and expressive, bringing the post-apocalyptic world to life in a way that is both visually stunning and thought-provoking.

Overall, Akira is a classic anime film that has become a cult favorite around the world. Its blend of science fiction, action, and psychological drama makes it a must-see for fans of the genre.

title: Lost in Translation
tagline: Everyone wants to be found.
overview: Two lost souls visiting Tokyo -- the young, neglected wife of a photographer and a washed-up movie star shooting a TV commercial -- find an odd solace and pensive freedom to be real in each other's company, away from their lives in America.
plot:
Bob Harris is a burnt out American film star who arrives in Tokyo to appear in lucrative advertisements for Suntory's Hibiki whiskey. He stays at the Park Hyatt Tokyo and is miserable due to problems within his twenty-five-year marriage and a midlife crisis.
Charlotte, another American staying at the hotel, is a young Yale graduate in philosophy who is accompanying her husband John while he works as a celebrity photographer. She is feeling similarly disenchanted as she questions her marriage and is anxious about her future. They both struggle additionally with bouts of jet lag and culture shock in Tokyo and pass the time loitering around the hotel, Charlotte also trying ikebana by chance.
Charlotte is repelled by a vacuous Hollywood actress named Kelly, who is also at the hotel promoting a film. Kelly bumps into Charlotte and John, gushing over photography sessions she has previously done with him. Bob and Charlotte frequently cross paths in the hotel and eventually start to connect in the hotel bar.
After several encounters, when John is on assignment outside Tokyo, Charlotte invites Bob into the city to meet some local friends. They bond over an evening in Tokyo, where they experience the city nightlife together and end up singing at a karaoke box. In the days that follow, Bob and Charlotte spend more time together, and their friendship strengthens. One night while watching television and drinking sake, while neither can sleep, the two share an intimate conversation about Charlotte's personal uncertainties and their married lives.
Bob has a cold conversation with his wife, then spends the night with a jazz singer from the hotel bar. Charlotte hears the woman singing in Bob's room the next morning, leading to tension between Bob and Charlotte during a shabu-shabu lunch together. The pair encounter each other in the evening and Bob reveals that he will be leaving Tokyo the following day.
Bob and Charlotte reconcile and express how they will miss each other, making a final visit to the hotel bar. The next morning, when Bob is leaving the hotel, he and Charlotte share sincere but unsatisfactory goodbyes. On Bob's taxi ride to the airport, he sees Charlotte on a crowded street, stops the car, and walks to her. He then embraces her and whispers something in her ear. The two share a kiss and say goodbye before Bob departs.

title: The Dark Knight
tagline: Welcome to a world without rules.
overview: Batman raises the stakes in his war on crime. With the help of Lt. Jim Gordon and District Attorney Harvey Dent, Batman sets out to dismantle the remaining criminal organizations that plague the streets. The partnership proves to be effective, but they soon find themselves prey to a reign of chaos unleashed by a rising criminal mastermind known to the terrified citizens of Gotham as the Joker.
plot:
A gang of masked criminals rob a mafia-owned bank in Gotham City, betraying and killing each other until the sole survivor, the Joker, reveals himself as the mastermind and escapes with the money. The vigilante Batman, district attorney Harvey Dent, and police lieutenant Jim Gordon ally to eliminate Gotham's organized crime. Batman's true identity, the billionaire Bruce Wayne, publicly supports Dent as Gotham's legitimate protector, believing Dent's success will allow him to retire as Batman and romantically pursue his childhood friend Rachel Dawes—despite her being with Dent.
Gotham's mafia bosses gather to discuss protecting their organizations from the Joker, the police, and Batman. The Joker interrupts the meeting and offers to kill Batman for half of the fortune their accountant, Lau, concealed before fleeing to Hong Kong to avoid extradition. With the help of Wayne Enterprises CEO Lucius Fox, Batman finds Lau in Hong Kong and returns him to the custody of the Gotham police. His testimony enables Dent to apprehend the crime families. The bosses accept the Joker's offer, and he kills high-profile targets involved in the trial, including the judge and police commissioner Gillian Loeb. Although Gordon saves the mayor, the Joker threatens that his attacks will continue until Batman reveals his identity. He targets Dent at a fundraising dinner and throws Rachel out of a window, but Batman rescues her.
Bruce struggles to understand the Joker's motives, to which his butler Alfred Pennyworth says that "some men just want to watch the world burn." Dent claims he is Batman to lure the Joker out, who attacks the police convoy transporting Dent. Batman and Gordon apprehend the Joker, and Gordon is promoted to commissioner. At the police station, Batman interrogates the Joker, who says he finds Batman entertaining and has no intention of killing him. Having deduced Batman's feelings for Rachel, the Joker reveals she and Dent are being held separately in buildings rigged to explode. Batman races to rescue Rachel while Gordon and the other officers go after Dent, but they discover the Joker has given their positions in reverse. The explosives detonate, killing Rachel and severely burning Dent's face on one side. The Joker escapes custody, extracts the fortune's location from Lau, and burns it, killing Lau in the process.
Coleman Reese, a consultant for Wayne Enterprises, deduces and tries to expose Batman's identity, but the Joker threatens to blow up a hospital unless Reese is killed. While the police evacuate hospitals and Gordon struggles to keep Reese alive, the Joker meets with a disillusioned Dent, persuading him to take the law into his own hands and avenge Rachel. Dent defers his decision-making to his now half-scarred, two-headed coin, killing the corrupt officers and the mafia involved in Rachel's death.

title: Ocean's Eleven
tagline: Are you in or out?
overview: Less than 24 hours into his parole, charismatic thief Danny Ocean is already rolling out his next plan: In one night, Danny's hand-picked crew of specialists will attempt to steal more than $150 million from three Las Vegas casinos. But to score the cash, Danny risks his chances of reconciling with ex-wife, Tess.
plot:
Ocean's Eleven is a heist film directed by Steven Soderbergh, released in 2001 by Warner Bros. Pictures. The movie follows the story of Danny Ocean (played by George Clooney), a charismatic thief who plans to rob three Las Vegas casinos simultaneously.

The story begins with Danny Ocean, a former casino security expert, being released from prison after serving a five-year sentence for a previous heist. He reunites with his old friend and partner-in-crime, Rusty Ryan (played by Brad Pitt). The two men devise a plan to rob three of the most secure casinos in Las Vegas: the Bellagio, the Mirage, and the MGM Grand.

The team consists of Danny's old crew, including Basher Tarr (Carl Reiner), Saul Bloom (Scott Caan), Livingston Dell (Eddie Jemison), and Yen (Shaobo Qin). They also recruit a few new members, including Terry Benedict's (Andy García) ex-wife, Tess Ocean (Julia Roberts), who becomes an integral part of the team.

The plan is to infiltrate the casinos by posing as high-rollers, gaining access to the vaults, and using advanced technology to disable the security systems. The team faces numerous challenges, including a rival thief, Reuben Tishkoff's (Elliott Gould), who tries to sabotage their plans.

As the heist unfolds, Danny's personal life becomes complicated. He is still in love with Tess, but she has moved on and is now married to Terry Benedict, a ruthless casino owner. The team must navigate the complex web of relationships and alliances to achieve their goal.

The climax of the movie takes place at the Bellagio, where the team executes their plan flawlessly. However, things take a turn when Danny's true intentions are revealed, and he decides to rob Terry Benedict instead of just the vaults. The team successfully pulls off the heist, but not without some unexpected twists and turns.

In the end, Danny and his crew escape with millions of dollars, leaving behind a trail of chaos and destruction. As for Tess, she finally finds her way back to Danny, and they share a romantic moment together.

Overall, Ocean's Eleven is a clever and entertaining heist film that features a talented ensemble cast, witty dialogue, and impressive action sequences. The movie's success can be attributed to its well-crafted plot, memorable characters, and Soderbergh's direction, which brings the story to life with style and sophistication.

title: Back to the Future Part II
original_title: Back to the Future Part II
tagline: Getting back was only the beginning.
overview: Marty and Doc are at it again as the time-traveling duo head to 2015 to nip some McFly family woes in the bud. But things go awry thanks to bully Biff Tannen and a pesky sports almanac. In a last-ditch attempt to set things straight, Marty finds himself bound for 1955 and face to face with his teenage parents -- again.
plot:
Back to the Future Part II is the 1989 sequel to Back to the Future, again directed by Robert Zemeckis, with a script by Bob Gale based on a story the two devised together. The second installment of the franchise, it brings back Michael J. Fox as Marty McFly, Christopher Lloyd as Doc Brown, Lea Thompson as Lorraine and Thomas F. Wilson as Biff Tannen, with Elisabeth Shue replacing Claudia Wells as Marty's girlfriend Jennifer and Jeffrey Weissman taking over the role of George McFly from Crispin Glover. Made for $40 million, it was shot back-to-back with Part III, and its effects work broke new ground for Industrial Light & Magic.

Picking up on 26 October 1985, Doc whisks Marty and Jennifer to 2015 to save their future children. Doc knocks Jennifer out to keep her from learning about her own future, and Marty poses as his lookalike son to turn down a robbery planned by Biff's grandson Griff. Goaded into a fight, Marty escapes on a hoverboard and Griff's gang is arrested. Before leaving, Marty buys a sports almanac listing results from 1950 to 2000, which Doc throws away after warning him against profiting from time travel. An elderly Biff picks it up, and while Marty and Doc retrieve Jennifer, who glimpses a disappointing future at the McFly home, he takes the DeLorean to give the almanac to his younger self.

Back in 1985, Marty and Doc find Hill Valley turned into a lawless dystopia ruled by Biff, now rich and corrupt from betting. In this timeline he has murdered George, married Lorraine and had Doc committed. Learning that Biff received the almanac on 12 November 1955, Marty and Doc return to that day, where Marty must recover the book while avoiding his other self, who is busy reuniting his parents at the school dance. After a chase on the hoverboard, Marty takes the almanac and burns it, restoring the timeline. But lightning strikes the DeLorean with Doc inside, and it vanishes. A Western Union courier then hands Marty a letter written by Doc in 1885, and Marty runs to find the 1955 Doc, who has just sent the other Marty home and faints at the sight of him.

Released on 22 November 1989, the film set a Thanksgiving opening record, grossed $333 million worldwide and was the third-highest-grossing film of 1989. Critics found it more uneven than its predecessor, giving it a 63% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes. It earned an Academy Award nomination for Best Visual Effects and won the BAFTA for special visual effects. Part III followed in May 1990.

title: K-PAX
tagline: Change the way you look at the world.
overview: Prot is a patient at a mental hospital who claims to be from a far away planet. His psychiatrist tries to help him, only to begin to doubt his own explanations.
plot:
A man calling himself “prot” is committed to the Psychiatric Institute of Manhattan after claiming he is an extraterrestrial from the planet 'K-PAX', 1,000 light years away in the Lyra constellation. There, psychiatrist Dr. Mark Powell attempts to cure him of his apparent delusions. However, prot is unwavering in his ability to provide cogent answers to questions about himself, K-PAX, and its civilizations. His medical examination only reinforces his story, as prot can see ultraviolet light and he is completely resistant to the effects of Thorazine. Powell introduces him to a group of astrophysicists who are befuddled when prot displays a highly detailed level of knowledge about the star system he claims to be from and which had previously been unknown to them.
Prot also wins over the other patients at the institute, each of whom believes unquestioningly that he is indeed from K-PAX. Prot, who claims to have journeyed to Earth by means of "faster-than-light travel," explains that he can take a single person with him when he returns. Thereafter, most of the patients at the Institute ask prot to take them with him.
Upon learning that many of his patients expect to leave Earth on July 27, Powell confronts prot, who explains that it is a predetermined date. However, Powell believes this to be a significant date in prot's life, a day on which he suffered severe psychological trauma. Powell decides to subject prot to regression hypnosis, which works well. Using information gained from these sessions, Powell figures out that prot may simply be an alter ego of Robert Porter, a man from New Mexico who had worked as a 'knocker' (animal slaughterer) in a local abattoir, and attempted suicide in 1996, after his wife and child had been murdered by a drifter. Powell tries to confront prot with this knowledge, showing him a photo of Robert Porter in a high school yearbook and stating that it is in fact prot himself; but prot‘s reaction is one of bemusement, and he cryptically tells Powell that he hopes he will take good care of Robert now that he has found him.
On July 27, as the hospital staff watches, the camera in prot‘s room cuts to static at the precise time prot had said he would be departing Earth. A moment later, Powell finds Porter lying on the floor in his room, catatonic, prot having apparently left Porter's body for the light travel back to K-PAX. As Robert is being wheeled out of the room, none of the other patients recognizes him as prot, and claim that prot has left. In addition, one of the patients is missing: Bess, a woman mute since her home had been destroyed in a fire, and who had been among those patients who had asked prot to take them to K-PAX. She is never found again. Remaining patients believe prot had taken her to K-PAX. Powell continues to take care of the catatonic Porter and tells him about how the patients he helped have gone on to live normal lives again, but Robert does not respond.

title: Saw
tagline: Live or die. Make your choice.
overview: Obsessed with teaching his victims the value of life, a deranged, sadistic serial killer abducts the morally wayward. Once captured, they must face impossible choices in a horrific game of survival. The victims must fight to win their lives back, or die trying...
plot:
Saw is a 2004 American psychological horror film directed by James Wan and written by Leigh Whannell. The film stars Cary Elwes, Danny Glover, Michael Emerson, Ken Leung, and Donnie Wahlberg.

The movie begins with Dr. Lawrence Gordon (Cary Elwes), a successful surgeon who finds himself chained in a run-down industrial bathroom with no recollection of how he got there. He soon discovers that he is not alone, as another prisoner, Adam Faulkner (Leigh Whannell), has also been left chained in the room. The two men are informed by a mysterious figure known as Jigsaw (Tobin Bell) through a video message that they have 60 minutes to escape the room or face a gruesome death.

As the game begins, Gordon and Faulkner realize that they must work together to find a way out of the room. However, their efforts are hindered by the fact that they do not know each other's skills or expertise. The two men start to suspect that Jigsaw is using them in some twisted experiment, but they cannot figure out what it is.

As time runs out, Gordon and Faulkner discover a series of clues left behind by Jigsaw, including a cryptic message on the wall and a hidden key. They also learn that Jigsaw has a personal connection to their lives, having been a successful surgeon himself who became disillusioned with his work.

Throughout the film, the tension builds as Gordon and Faulkner try to outsmart each other and find a way out of the room. However, it becomes clear that one of them will not survive. title: The Interpreter
tagline: The truth needs no translation.
overview: After Silvia Broome, an interpreter at United Nations headquarters, overhears plans of an assassination, an American Secret Service agent is sent to investigate.
plot:
In the fictional Southern African country of Matobo, rebel leader Ajene Xola drives two men, Simon Broome and Philippe, to an abandoned stadium. They discuss how President Edmond Zuwanie's regime has ruthlessly exterminated most of the population and intimidated the survivors into silence. Upon their arrival at the stadium, they find three schoolboys, who point Xola and Simon in the direction of corpses left by Zuwanie's security apparatus, while Philippe stays in the car. When Xola and Simon return to the playing field, they are executed by the boys whose actions connect them to Zuwanie's secret police. Philippe clambers out of the car and hides, taking pictures of a car arriving carrying Zuwanie's lackeys, and then escapes.
Simon's sister, Silvia, works at the United Nations Interpretation Service in New York. A white African born in the United States to a British mother and white Matoban father, she was raised in Matobo and studied in France. Her diverse background leads to UN Security Chief Lee Wu wryly describing her as "being the UN".
The UN is considering indicting Zuwanie, to stand trial in the International Criminal Court. Initially a liberator, over the past 20 years he has become as corrupt and tyrannical as the government he overthrew, and is now responsible for ethnic cleansing. Zuwanie is soon to visit the UN and put forward his own case to the UN General Assembly, in an attempt to avoid the indictment.
A random security scare forces the evacuation of the UN headquarters. When Silvia returns at night to retrieve some personal belongings, she overhears two men discussing an assassination plot in Ku (the Matoban lingua franca). She runs from the building when the men become aware of her presence. The next day, while interpreting in a meeting, Silvia recognizes words from the phrases she overheard the night before. She reports the incident to UN security; the plot's target appears to be Zuwanie.
The US Secret Service assigns Dignitary Protection Division (DPD) agents Tobin Keller and Dot Woods to investigate, as well as protect Zuwanie when he arrives. Zuwanie's personal head of security, former Dutch mercenary Nils Lud, arrives in New York. Keller, whose estranged wife was killed in a car accident just weeks earlier, learns Silvia's parents and sister were killed by landmines laid by Zuwanie's men in the past, and that she has dated Xola. Although Keller is suspicious of Silvia's backstory, the two grow close, in part because of their shared grief, and Keller ends up protecting her from attacks.
Philippe calls Silvia to meet and informs her of Xola's death, but lies and says he does not know what happened to Simon. She attempts to obtain information by way of Kuman-Kuman, an exiled Matoban minister living in New York, only to almost be killed in a bus bombing perpetrated by Lud's right-hand man, Jean Gamba; Kuman-Kuman, along with Keller's subordinate Doug, are amongst the dead.

title: Lucky Number Slevin
tagline: Wrong Time. Wrong Place. Wrong Number.
overview: Slevin is mistakenly put in the middle of a personal war between the city’s biggest criminal bosses. Under constant watch, Slevin must try not to get killed by an infamous assassin and come up with an idea of how to get out of his current dilemma.
plot:
Two bookies are separately ambushed and murdered. In a bus terminal, a young man is approached by Goodkat, who tells the story of Max: two decades earlier, Max borrowed money from the Mob to bet on a fixed horse race after eavesdropping on conversations between mobsters, only for the horse to collapse and die just short of the finish line. To set an example to make sure nobody else will try to bet on a fixed race, the Mob killed Max, his wife, and his son Henry. Goodkat then describes the "Kansas City Shuffle", a misleading double bluff, and kills the young man, taking the body in a truck.
In New York City, Slevin Kelevra is staying in his friend Nick Fisher's apartment and, upon being visited by neighbor Lindsey, discusses Nick's disappearance and why the apartment was unlocked. Lindsey suggests that Nick might be missing. After she leaves, Slevin is kidnapped by two henchmen who, mistaking Slevin for Nick, take him to "The Boss". The Boss orders him to repay a gambling debt or kill the son of his rival, "The Rabbi". Believing The Rabbi is responsible for assassinating his son (seen in the intro), The Boss wants The Rabbi's gay son, Yitzchok "The Fairy", to be killed in revenge. Slevin returns to the apartment but is kidnapped again, this time by two of The Rabbi's Jewish henchmen. The Rabbi also mistakes Slevin for Nick and also demands he repay a gambling debt. Slevin tells The Boss he will kill Yitzchok. Meanwhile, it becomes apparent that Goodkat is involved with both sides, that he is responsible for Nick's debts being called in, and that he plans to kill Slevin after Yitzchok dies and make it look like they both committed suicide.
Slevin is approached by Detective Brikowski, who is investigating The Boss and The Rabbi. Brikowski has also been informed that Goodkat is back in town for the first time in twenty years and thinks there is a connection between The Boss, The Rabbi, Goodkat, and Slevin. After pretending to be gay, Slevin gets invited to Yitzchok's apartment, where he kills Yitzchok, and Goodkat (revealed to be working with Slevin) kills the bodyguards. They use the man Goodkat killed in the airport (revealed to be Fisher) in Slevin's place. The two then kidnap The Boss and The Rabbi, whom they restrain in The Boss's penthouse. There, Slevin reveals he is Henry, Max's son. The mobsters who killed Max were The Boss and The Rabbi. Goodkat was the assassin hired to kill young Henry. After an attack of conscience, Goodkat raised Henry as his own. They planted Slevin as Nick (the man in the bus terminal) to get him close to them; Goodkat killed the bookies while Slevin killed The Boss' son. Slevin suffocates The Rabbi and The Boss by taping plastic bags over their heads, killing them the same way they killed his father. Since Lindsey photographed Goodkat while investigating Nick's disappearance, Goodkat shoots her to protect his identity.

title: Sin City: A Dame to Kill For
original_title: Sin City: A Dame to Kill For
tagline: There is no justice without sin.
overview: Some of Sin City's most hard-boiled citizens cross paths with a few of its more reviled inhabitants.
plot:
Sin City: A Dame to Kill For is a 2014 American neo-noir crime anthology film directed by Robert Rodriguez and Frank Miller and written by Miller, the follow-up to the 2005 film Sin City. Its central story adapts A Dame to Kill For, the second book of Miller's comic series, a shorter segment comes from "Just Another Saturday Night", and two tales, "The Long Bad Night" and "Nancy's Last Dance", were written for the film. Mickey Rourke, Jessica Alba, Rosario Dawson, Jaime King, Powers Boothe and Bruce Willis return, joined by Josh Brolin, Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Eva Green, Dennis Haysbert, Christopher Meloni, Jeremy Piven, Christopher Lloyd, Ray Liotta and Lady Gaga.

In the brief opening story, the brutish Marv wakes beside a wrecked police car surrounded by bodies and pieces together how he chased a group of rich college boys who had set a homeless man on fire. In "The Long Bad Night", a cocky young gambler, Johnny, wins a fortune from the ruthless Senator Roark at a backroom poker game. Roark, who recognizes him as his illegitimate son, has his fingers broken and his money taken, and later murders the waitress Johnny had taken out. Johnny scrapes together enough cash to challenge Roark again, humiliating him at the table a second time knowing the senator will kill him for it.

The title story, set before the events of the first film, follows Dwight McCarthy, a private detective struggling to keep his violent impulses in check, who is drawn back into the life of his former lover Ava Lord. Claiming that her wealthy husband, Damien, and his giant chauffeur, Manute, are abusing her, she persuades Dwight to help her, and with Marv's aid he storms the Lord estate and kills Damien, only for Ava to shoot him and reveal that she has manipulated him to gain her husband's fortune. Rescued and given a new face in Old Town with the help of Gail and the assassin Miho, Dwight returns for revenge, while Ava's seduction of a detective, Mort, ends in murder and suicide. In "Nancy's Last Dance", Nancy Callahan, haunted by the death of John Hartigan, whose ghost watches over her, scars herself and enlists Marv to help her storm Roark's compound and take her revenge.

After a premiere at Hollywood's TCL Chinese Theatre on August 19, 2014, The Weinstein Company opened it three days later. Unlike its predecessor, it was a box-office disappointment, earning about 40.7 million dollars against a production budget of around 65 million, and it received mixed reviews from critics.

As Amélie navigates her relationships with Nino and others, she begins to confront her own feelings about love, loss, and identity. In a poignant and emotional climax, Amélie must decide whether to follow her heart or stay true to herself.

The film ends on a hopeful note, with Amélie finding a sense of belonging and purpose in the world. She and Nino share a tender moment, and Amélie finally feels like she has found someone who understands her. The final shot of the film is of Amélie walking alone through the streets of Paris, but this time, she looks happy and at peace.

Overall, Amélie is a charming and whimsical film that celebrates the beauty of human connection and the power of small acts of kindness. With its stunning visuals, quirky characters, and poignant storyline, it's no wonder that Amélie has become a beloved classic around the world.

overview: The final installment finds Marty digging the trusty DeLorean out of a mineshaft and looking for Doc in the Wild West of 1885. plot:
Back to the Future Part III is a 1990 American science fiction Western directed by Robert Zemeckis and the final instalment of the Back to the Future trilogy. Picking up immediately after Part II, it sends Marty McFly to the Old West to rescue his friend Doc Brown, who is stranded in 1885 and fated to be shot by Biff's great-grandfather. Michael J. Fox, Christopher Lloyd, Mary Steenburgen, Thomas F. Wilson and Lea Thompson star.

On November 12, 1955, just after Doc vanishes in the DeLorean, Marty learns from a 70-year-old letter that his friend is living in 1885. With the help of the 1955 Doc, he recovers the car Doc hid, but nearby he finds Doc's gravestone, which records that he was shot by Buford "Mad Dog" Tannen over 80 dollars six days after writing the letter. Ignoring the warning, Marty travels to September 1885, landing amid a cavalry chase and damaging the fuel line. Knocked out while fleeing a bear, he is taken in by his Irish immigrant great-great-grandparents Seamus and Maggie, then, calling himself Clint Eastwood, rides into the young town of Hill Valley, where Doc saves him from being lynched by Buford's gang. With no gasoline to reach 88 miles per hour, Doc plans to have a steam locomotive push the DeLorean, but he falls in love with schoolteacher Clara Clayton after saving her from plunging into a ravine. Marty, provoked by Buford into accepting a duel, is warned by Doc that his rashness leads to a life-changing accident in the future. Doc reluctantly leaves Clara, who refuses to believe his story. On the morning of the showdown, Marty survives Buford's shot by wearing a stove door as armour, knocks him into a manure wagon and sees him arrested. Clara, realising Doc told the truth, races after the train; Doc saves her using Marty's hoverboard as the DeLorean reaches 88 mph and the locomotive plunges into the ravine. Back in 1985, Marty sees the car destroyed by a train, then avoids the street race that would have ruined his future. Doc arrives in a flying time-travelling locomotive with Clara and their sons, tells Marty and Jennifer their future is unwritten, and departs.

Fox plays Marty, with Lloyd as Doc, Steenburgen as Clara and Wilson as Buford. Shot back to back with Part II in 1989, it was filmed in California and Arizona on a $40 million budget. Released on May 25, 1990, it grossed about $245 million worldwide, earned 79% on Rotten Tomatoes as a sweeter finale, and won Saturn Awards for Alan Silvestri's music and Wilson.

title: Braveheart

overview: Enraged at the slaughter of Murron, his new bride and childhood love, Scottish warrior William Wallace slays a platoon of the local English lord's soldiers. This leads the village to revolt and, eventually, the entire country to rise up against English rule.
plot:
Braveheart is a historical epic film directed by and starring Mel Gibson, released in 1995. The movie is set in Scotland during the late 13th century and tells the story of William Wallace, a Scottish warrior who led a rebellion against the English army.

The film begins with a young William Wallace (played by Stellan Skarsgård) as a child, witnessing his father's brutal murder at the hands of English soldiers. This traumatic event sets the tone for Wallace's future actions and fuels his desire for revenge against the English.

As the story unfolds, we see Wallace grow into a strong and determined young man, who eventually becomes a skilled warrior and leader among the Scottish clans. He meets and falls in love with Murron (played by Sophie Marceau), a beautiful and kind-hearted woman from a neighboring clan. However, their happiness is short-lived, as English soldiers arrive at her village and brutally murder her.

This event sparks Wallace's desire for revenge against the English, whom he holds responsible for Murron's death. He becomes a key figure in the Scottish resistance movement, using his bravery and strategic thinking to rally the clans against the English army.

As the conflict escalates, Wallace faces off against the ruthless English commander, King Edward "Longshanks" (played by Patrick McGoohan). The two engage in a series of intense battles, with Wallace emerging as a formidable opponent. However, their rivalry is complicated by the fact that Longshanks is also Wallace's uncle.

Despite the odds against him, Wallace continues to fight for Scottish independence, using guerrilla tactics and clever strategies to outmaneuver his enemies. He becomes a symbol of hope for the Scottish people, who see him as a champion of freedom and self-determination.

The film's climax features an epic battle between the Scots and the English at Stirling Bridge. Wallace leads the charge against the English army, using his knowledge of the terrain to outflank and defeat them. However, he is eventually captured by Longshanks' men and put on trial for treason.

In a dramatic and emotional courtroom scene, Wallace delivers a powerful speech, condemning the English monarchy and pleading for Scottish independence. He is ultimately found guilty and sentenced to death. As he stands on the scaffold awaiting his execution, Wallace declares "Freedom!" and dies with his head held high.

The film ends with a sense of hope and renewal, as the Scottish people vow to continue their fight for freedom in the face of overwhelming odds. The final shot features a young William Wallace, who has grown up watching his father's story and is now determined to carry on his legacy.

Overall, Braveheart is a powerful and moving film that explores themes of patriotism, sacrifice, and the human spirit. Mel Gibson's performance as William Wallace is particularly noteworthy, bringing depth and nuance to the character. The film's epic scope and stunning cinematography make it a must-see for fans of historical dramas and action-adventure films.

title: Saw III

plot:
Saw III is a 2006 American horror film directed by Darren Lynn Bousman and written by Leigh Whannell and Josh Stolberg. The film stars Tobin Bell, Angus Macfadyen, Shawnee Smith, and Bahar Soomekh.

The story begins with Dr. Lawrence Gordon (Cary Elwes), a successful surgeon who is being held captive in a run-down industrial bathroom by Jigsaw (Tobin Bell). Jigsaw forces Gordon to play a deadly game of survival, where he must use his medical skills to save the life of Adam Faulkner (Angus Macfadyen), a young man with a terminal illness. The catch is that Gordon's own life is also at stake, and if he fails to save Adam's life within 60 minutes, he will die.

As the game progresses, it becomes clear that Jigsaw has set up a series of traps and puzzles for Gordon to solve in order to save Adam's life. However, things take a dark turn when it is revealed that Adam is not who he claims to be. In reality, Adam is actually Jeff Denlon (Angus Macfadyen), the son of Detective Eric Matthews (Bahar Soomekh).

Meanwhile, Detective Matthews is investigating a series of gruesome murders linked to Jigsaw's games. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Jigsaw has set up a complex web of traps and puzzles for Matthews to solve in order to rescue his son.

As the game reaches its climax, Gordon discovers that Adam is actually Jeff Denlon, and that he has been playing a deadly game with his own father. In the end, Gordon manages to save Adam's life by solving the final puzzle, but not before Jigsaw reveals that he has one last trick up his sleeve.

The film ends with Jigsaw's iconic twist: Dr. Gordon is actually the one who will die, and not Adam. The camera pans out to reveal a new game board, as Jigsaw's voiceover says "You're next." The final shot of the film shows Jigsaw's face, as he reveals that he has been manipulating events from behind the scenes all along.

Throughout the film, the tension builds as the characters navigate the deadly traps and puzzles set by Jigsaw. The film's climax is both shocking and terrifying, leaving the audience on the edge of their seats until the very end.

Overall, Saw III is a masterclass in building tension and suspense, with a complex web of plot twists and turns that keep the viewer guessing until the very end.

title: Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull
original_title: Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull
tagline: The adventure continues . . .
overview: Set during the Cold War, the Soviets—led by sword-wielding Irina Spalko—are in search of a crystal skull which has supernatural powers related to a mystical Lost City of Gold. Indy is coerced to head to Peru at the behest of a young man whose friend—and Indy's colleague—Professor Oxley has been captured for his knowledge of the skull's whereabouts.
plot:
Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull is a 2008 action-adventure film directed by Steven Spielberg, produced by George Lucas and Kathleen Kennedy, and written by David Koepp.

The movie takes place in 1957, four years after the events of Raiders of the Lost Ark (1981). Indiana Jones (Harrison Ford), now an older and wiser archaeologist, is working at Marshall College in Princeton, New Jersey. He is married to Marion Ravenwood (Karen Allen), with whom he has a son named Henry.

The story begins with a mysterious crystal skull that has been stolen from the U.S. government by Irina Spalko (Cate Blanchett), a Soviet agent who seeks to use its supposed supernatural powers to gain control over the world's nuclear arsenals. The skull is later recovered by Indy, but not before it is used in a ritual to awaken an ancient Sankara Stones' energy.

As Indy delves deeper into the mystery of the crystal skull, he discovers that it is connected to an alien spacecraft that has been hidden beneath the U.S. government's secret research facility at Area 51. The aliens, led by Mutt Williams (Shia LaBeouf), a young man who claims to be Indy's son with Marion, reveal that they have been watching Earth for centuries and are searching for a way to harness the power of the Sankara Stones.

Indy joins forces with Mutt, Marion, and a new character, Dr. Wilkins (John Hurt), an old friend of Indy's who has been working on the government project. Together, they embark on a perilous journey across the globe, from Peru to Egypt, in search of the remaining Sankara Stones.

As they navigate treacherous jungles, ancient ruins, and Soviet agents, Indy and his team face numerous challenges and obstacles. Along the way, Indy also confronts his own past and the consequences of his actions as a young adventurer.

The movie culminates in an epic showdown between Indy and Spalko at the Sankara Stones' energy source, where they engage in a fierce battle to control the power of the stones. In the end, Indy emerges victorious, but not before realizing that Mutt is indeed his son with Marion.

The film concludes with Indy returning home to his family, reflecting on his adventures and the lessons he has learned about the importance of family and responsibility. The movie ends on a hopeful note, as Indy looks forward to a new chapter in his life, one that will be filled with excitement, danger, and adventure.

Overall, Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull is an action-packed, thrilling ride that pays homage to the classic Indiana Jones films while introducing new characters and plot twists. The movie's blend of humor, adventure, and science fiction elements makes it a fun and entertaining watch for fans of the franchise and newcomers alike.

title: The Terminator
tagline: Your future is in his hands.
overview: In the post-apocalyptic future, reigning tyrannical supercomputers teleport a cyborg assassin known as the 'Terminator' back to 1984 to kill Sarah Connor, whose unborn son is destined to lead insurgents against 21st century mechanical hegemony. Meanwhile, the human-resistance movement dispatches a lone warrior to safeguard Sarah. Can he stop the virtually indestructible killing machine?
plot:
In the year 2029, Earth is a post-apocalyptic wasteland ruled by intelligent machines led by an AI called Skynet. After launching a nuclear holocaust known as Judgment Day, Skynet wages war on the remnants of humanity. The human resistance, led by a man named John Connor, manages to turn the tide. In a last-ditch effort to defeat the resistance, Skynet sends a Terminator—a nearly indestructible cyborg assassin—back in time to 1984 Los Angeles. Its mission is to kill Sarah Connor, John’s mother, before he can be born.

The Terminator, disguised as a human (played by Arnold Schwarzenegger), arrives in 1984 and begins systematically killing every woman named Sarah Connor listed in the phone book. Meanwhile, the resistance sends back one of their own, Kyle Reese (Michael Biehn), to protect the correct Sarah Connor (Linda Hamilton).

Kyle finds Sarah and explains the situation: the Terminator is a cybernetic organism designed to infiltrate and exterminate; it will never stop hunting her. Sarah, understandably skeptical, becomes convinced after witnessing the Terminator’s relentless attack. The pair go on the run, with Kyle providing knowledge of the future and Sarah beginning to accept her crucial role in humanity’s survival.

During their escape, Kyle and Sarah grow close, and she learns that John Connor deliberately chose Kyle to be sent back because Kyle is, in fact, John’s father. They conceive John during their time together.

The Terminator relentlessly pursues them, leading to a climactic showdown in a factory. Kyle sacrifices himself to destroy the Terminator by blowing it up with a pipe bomb. Though badly injured, the Terminator’s torso continues to crawl after Sarah. She manages to crush it in a hydraulic press, finally ending the threat.

In the aftermath, Sarah, now pregnant, prepares for a future that only she knows is coming. She begins recording audio tapes for her unborn son, warning him about the coming war and the role he must play. She drives into the desert, determined to survive and protect her child.

title: The Godfather
tagline: An offer you can't refuse.
overview: Spanning the years 1945 to 1955, a chronicle of the fictional Italian-American Corleone crime family. When organized crime family patriarch, Vito Corleone barely survives an attempt on his life, his youngest son, Michael steps in to take care of the would-be killers, launching a campaign of bloody revenge.
plot:
In the mid-1940s, Michael Corleone is a World War II veteran and the youngest son of Don Vito Corleone. Vito is head of the Corleone mafia family and runs it with his eldest son Santino a.k.a. Sonny and adopted son Tom Hagen, a lawyer who is the family's consigliere. At his sister Connie's wedding to Carlo Rizzi, Michael introduces his family to his girlfriend, Kay Adams. Michael tells Kay stories of his family but makes it clear that he wants no part in his family's business.
Vito fulfils the Sicilian tradition of granting favors on his daughter's wedding day to a succession of hopeful visitors. One is his godson, singer and actor Johnny Fontane, who cannot get an upcoming film role because studio owner and producer Jack Woltz has a grudge against Fontane. Vito sends Hagen to LA to persuade Woltz to relent but Woltz will not budge. Hagen departs and the next morning, Woltz wakes to find the severed head of his prized $600,000 racehorse Khartoum in his bed with him. A terrified Woltz relents and Fontane gets the role.
Approaching Christmas, Michael becomes embroiled in family affairs when Vito is gunned down by two assailants. Vito had earlier refused to offer protection to drug baron Virgil "The Turk" Sollozzo for dealing narcotics in the city. Sollozzo has the support of the Tattaglia family, who garrote notorious Corleone enforcer Luca Brasi when he attempts to become a mole in Sollozzo's operation. While Vito survives the attempt and recovers at the hospital, hot-tempered Sonny takes over the family as acting boss. He has Michael live at the house for his protection, as his successful revenge hit on Tattaglia's son Bruno has led to war between the two gangs. Michael visits his father in hospital to be told that NYPD Captain McCluskey has had Vito's bodyguards ejected from the hospital, clearing the way for a second attempt on Vito's life. Michael visits his father and, realizing his jeopardy, moves him to another hospital room then stands guard outside the hospital. He scares Sollozzo's assassins off but an angry McCluskey returns and breaks Michael's jaw for defying him. Soon after, Hagen arrives with more bodyguards and McCluskey backs down to the lawyer's demands. Being an outsider to the family business and seen as harmless, Michael later proposes a meeting between himself, Sollozzo and McCluskey at which he'll kill them both to keep his father safe. Initially amused, the family approve his plan and have a gun planted at the meeting place: a restaurant. At the meeting, Michael shoots both men dead then flees the country. He takes refuge in his family's native Sicily to escape the NYPD and the ire of the other gangs until the heat dies down. He falls in love with a local woman, Apollonia Vitelli, and marries her.
Back in New York, war has broken out between the Five Families. Sonny discovers that Connie was being abused by Carlo. At first, Sonny pummels Carlo in public and warns him never to touch Connie again.

title: Some Like It Hot
tagline: The movie too HOT for words!
overview: Two musicians witness a mob hit and struggle to find a way out of the city before they are found by the gangsters. Their only opportunity is to join an all-girl band as they leave on a tour. To make their getaway they must first disguise themselves as women, then keep their identities secret and deal with the problems this brings - such as an attractive bandmate and a very determined suitor.
plot:
Some Like It Hot is a classic American comedy film directed by Billy Wilder, released in 1959 by United Artists. The movie stars Tony Curtis, Jack Lemmon, and Marilyn Monroe.

The story begins with Joe Carter (Tony Curtis) and Jerry Parker (Jack Lemmon), two struggling musicians who are forced to flee their home after being threatened by a rival gangster, Spats Colombo (George Raft). They disguise themselves as women, with the help of a transvestite named Daphne (Joan Crawford's character in her earlier film "Mildred Pierce"), and join an all-female band on a train headed to Chicago.

In Chicago, Joe and Jerry adopt female personas, becoming Josephine and Daphne respectively. They quickly become part of the band and gain popularity as musicians. However, their new lives are threatened when Spats Colombo discovers their true identities and tries to kill them.

Meanwhile, Jerry falls in love with Sugar Kane (Marilyn Monroe), a beautiful singer who is engaged to be married to the wealthy and arrogant Osgood Fielding III (Joe E. Brown). As Jerry gets closer to Sugar, he must navigate his feelings for her while keeping his true identity hidden from her.

As the story unfolds, Joe and Jerry's disguises are put to the test as they try to avoid Spats Colombo and his henchmen. Along the way, they get into various misadventures, including a memorable scene where they accidentally join Sugar's wedding party dressed in their female attire.

In the end, Jerry must confront his feelings for Sugar and decide whether to reveal his true identity or continue living as Daphne. In a surprising twist, Joe and Jerry are able to outsmart Spats Colombo and win Sugar's heart, with Jerry ultimately choosing to leave Chicago and start a new life with Sugar.

Throughout the movie, Billy Wilder's direction and the witty dialogue by I.A.L. Diamond provide plenty of comedic moments, while Tony Curtis and Jack Lemmon deliver standout performances as the two lead characters. The film's blend of humor, romance, and music makes it a timeless classic that continues to entertain audiences to this day.

Some Like It Hot has been recognized for its cultural significance and influence on popular culture. It was selected for preservation in the National Film Registry by the Library of Congress in 1999 and has been named one of the greatest films of all time by various publications, including the American Film Institute and IMDb.
