title: Forbidden Planet
tagline: Earthmen on a fabulous, peril-journey into outer space!
overview: Starship C57D travels to planet Altair 4 in search of the crew of spaceship "Bellerophon," a scientific expedition that has been missing for 20 years, only to find themselves unwelcome by the expedition's lone survivor and warned of destruction by an invisible force if they don't turn back immediately.
plot:
Forbidden Planet is a science fiction film directed by Fred M. Wilcox, produced by Charles H. Schneer, and released by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer (MGM) in 1956.

The story begins with the crew of the spaceship C57D, led by Captain John J. Adams, receiving a distress signal from the planet Altair IV. The crew is sent to investigate and rescue any survivors. Upon arrival, they discover that the planet's surface is uninhabitable due to a toxic atmosphere. However, they soon realize that the real challenge lies within the planet's interior.

As the crew explores the planet, they come across an ancient temple dedicated to the goddess Caliban, who was once worshipped by the native inhabitants of Altair IV. The crew discovers a strange energy field surrounding the temple and decides to investigate further. They soon learn that the energy field is connected to the planet's unique properties and is believed to be the source of its deadly radiation.

The crew encounters various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, toxic gas, and malfunctioning equipment. As they delve deeper into the planet's interior, they begin to experience strange visions and hallucinations, which are later revealed to be caused by the energy field's effects on their minds.

One of the crew members, Dr. Edward Morbius, begins to exhibit unusual behavior, suggesting that he may have been affected by the energy field in a more profound way than initially thought. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Morbius has become possessed by the spirit of Caliban, who is seeking revenge against humanity for its treatment of her people.

The crew soon realizes that they must find a way to stop Morbius and escape the planet before it's too late. They discover that the only way to neutralize the energy field is to destroy the temple and sever the connection between the planet and Caliban's spirit.

In the climactic final act, the crew faces off against Morbius, who has become a vessel for Caliban's wrath. The captain and his crew must use all their skills and ingenuity to defeat Morbius and shatter the energy field, allowing them to escape the planet.

The film ends with the crew returning to Earth, where they are hailed as heroes for their bravery and ingenuity in overcoming the challenges of Altair IV. However, the ending also leaves room for interpretation, as some viewers may wonder if the crew truly escaped the planet's influence or if Morbius's spirit still lingers, waiting to be unleashed once again.

Overall, Forbidden Planet is a thought-provoking science fiction film that explores themes of identity, humanity, and the dangers of playing with forces beyond human control. The film's blend of adventure, suspense, and philosophical introspection has made it a classic of the genre, continuing to captivate audiences to this day.

title: Underworld: Evolution
tagline: My God. Brother, what have you done?
overview: As the war between the vampires and the Lycans rages on, Selene, a former member of the Death Dealers (an elite vampire special forces unit that hunts werewolves), and Michael, the werewolf hybrid, work together in an effort to unlock the secrets of their respective bloodlines.
plot:
Underworld: Evolution is a 2006 supernatural action film directed by Patrick Tatopoulos and written by Len Wiseman and Danny McBride. The movie serves as a sequel to the 2003 film Underworld, starring Kate Beckinsale as Selene, a vampire warrior.

The story begins with Selene (Kate Beckinsale) being resurrected from her death in the first film by a group of vampires who believe she is destined to fulfill an ancient prophecy. The prophecy states that Selene will be the one to bring about the end of the war between humans and vampires, as well as the destruction of both species.

As Selene awakens, she finds herself in a desolate wasteland, surrounded by a group of vampires who claim to have been sent by her maker, Kraven (Shane Brolly). They inform her that she has been chosen to fulfill the prophecy and that she must find the Lycan leader, Lucian (Scott Speedman), who is also destined for greatness.

Selene soon discovers that she is not alone in her quest. A group of humans, led by Alexander Corvinus (Tom Cruise), are also searching for Lucian, believing him to be the key to their survival. As Selene navigates this treacherous landscape, she must confront her own destiny and the true nature of her existence as a vampire.

Throughout the film, Selene encounters various characters who aid or hinder her progress. These include Michael Corvin (Scott Speedman), Alexander's son, who becomes embroiled in the conflict; Kraven, who seeks to use Selene for his own purposes; and the Lycan leader, Lucian, who is torn between his loyalty to his pack and his growing feelings for Selene.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the prophecy is more complex than initially thought. The true nature of the war between humans and vampires is revealed, as well as the motivations behind Alexander's actions. Ultimately, Selene must make a choice between her own existence and the fate of humanity, leading to a climactic showdown with Kraven and Lucian.

The film concludes with Selene emerging victorious but not without scars. She has come to terms with her destiny and is ready to face whatever challenges lie ahead. The ending sets the stage for potential future sequels, leaving audiences wondering what the future holds for this iconic vampire warrior.

Overall, Underworld: Evolution offers a thrilling and action-packed ride, exploring themes of identity, loyalty, and the blurred lines between good and evil.

title: Duel

overview: Traveling businessman David Mann angers the driver of a rusty tanker while crossing the California desert. A simple trip turns deadly, as Mann struggles to stay on the road while the tanker plays cat and mouse with his life.
plot:
Duel is a 1971 television film directed by Steven Spielberg, produced by Universal Television, and written by Richard Matheson.

The story begins with David Mann (played by Dennis Weaver), a middle-aged family man who is driving home from a business trip on the New Mexico State Highway. As he drives, he notices a black Peterbilt semi-truck following him at a distance. The truck's driver, known only as "The Driver" (played by Martin Mull), seems to be mirroring David's every move.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that The Driver is not just following David; he is also taunting and intimidating him. The Driver begins to make menacing gestures, such as flashing his headlights or making sudden stops, which causes David to become increasingly anxious and frustrated.

David tries to lose The Driver by taking various detours and changing lanes, but the truck always seems to be one step ahead of him. As the chase continues, David becomes more and more agitated, and his family back home begins to worry about his safety.

As the tension builds, it becomes clear that The Driver is not just a random driver; he has a personal vendetta against David. The Driver's actions become increasingly sinister, and David realizes that he must find a way to escape before it's too late.

In a thrilling climax, David uses his wits and resourcefulness to outsmart The Driver. He sets up a trap for the truck by driving into a narrow canyon, where The Driver is forced to slow down or risk crashing. As The Driver tries to pass David, he loses control of the truck and crashes into a rock face.

The film ends with David finally safe at home, but shaken by his terrifying experience on the road. The Driver's true identity remains a mystery, leaving the audience to wonder about the motivations behind his sinister actions.

Throughout the film, Spielberg uses suspenseful camera angles and editing techniques to create a sense of tension and unease. The film's score, composed by Lalo Schifrin, adds to the overall sense of anxiety and fear.

Overall, Duel is a masterclass in suspenseful storytelling, with a simple yet effective plot that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

title: In the Mood for Love
tagline: Feel the heat, keep the feeling burning, let the sensation explode.
overview: Hong Kong, 1962: Chow Mo-Wan and Su Li-Zhen move into neighboring apartments on the same day. Their encounters are formal and polite—until a discovery about their spouses creates an intimate bond between them.
plot:
In 1962 British Hong Kong, Shanghainese expatriates Chow Mo-wan, a journalist, and Su Li-zhen (Mrs. Chan), a secretary at a shipping company, rent rooms in adjacent apartments. Each has a spouse who often works late, leaving them alone during overtime shifts. Due to the friendly but overbearing presence of Su's Shanghainese landlady, Mrs. Suen, and their bustling, mahjong-playing neighbours, Chow and Su are frequently left alone in their rooms and rarely dine with the other tenants.
Although they are initially polite out of necessity, they grow closer as they realise their spouses are having an affair with each other. Chow notices that his wife owns a handbag available only overseas—one that Su's husband had purchased for her. Su, in turn, observes that her husband wears a tie identical to one Chow owns, a gift from Chow's wife. As they piece together the truth, they begin to reenact how the affair may have begun. While both accept that their spouses have betrayed them, they strive to avoid making the same mistake themselves.
Chow invites Su to help him write a martial arts serial. Their increased time together draws the attention of their neighbours, prompting Chow to rent a hotel room where they can work in private. As time passes, they acknowledge their growing feelings for each other. They continue reenacting scenes from their spouses' affair, but the emotional toll unsettles Su. They sometimes stop speaking, only to reconnect later. When Chow receives a job offer in Singapore, he asks Su to come with him. She agrees, but arrives at the hotel too late and breaks down in his empty room.
The following year, in Singapore, Chow tells a friend an old story: when someone had a secret, they would climb a mountain, carve a hollow in a tree, whisper the secret into it, and seal it with mud. Su later visits Chow's apartment in Singapore. She calls him but says nothing when he answers. Afterward, Chow notices a lipstick-stained cigarette butt in his ashtray and realises she had been there.
Three years later, Su visits Mrs. Suen, who is preparing to immigrate to the United States, and inquires about renting her old apartment. Some time afterward, Chow returns to Hong Kong to visit his former landlords, the Koos, who have moved to the Philippines. He asks about the Suen family next door, and the new owner informs him that a woman and her son now live there. Chow leaves.
During the Vietnam War, Chow travels to Cambodia and visits Angkor Wat. As a monk looks on, he whispers into a hollow in a wall and seals it with mud.

title: Willow
tagline: Adventure doesn't come any bigger than this.
overview: The evil Queen Bavmorda hunts the newborn princess Elora Danan, a child prophesied to bring about her downfall. When the royal infant is found by Willow, a timid farmer and aspiring sorcerer, he's entrusted with delivering her from evil.
plot:
Willow is a 1988 American high fantasy film directed by Ron Howard, produced by George Lucas, and written by Bob Dolman.

In a mystical realm, a young farmer named Willow Ufgood lives on the outskirts of a village with his adoptive family. Willow's life takes an unexpected turn when a sorceress named Madmartigan arrives at their doorstep, seeking refuge from the evil Queen Bavmorda, who is determined to destroy all newborns with magical abilities.

The queen believes that the child will grow up to be a powerful sorcerer and use his powers for evil. Willow's adoptive mother dies soon after giving birth to her son, and Willow takes on the responsibility of caring for him. However, when Madmartigan arrives, he convinces Willow to take the infant to the safety of the Sorceress Elora Danan, who is said to be able to protect the child from the queen's wrath.

As they embark on their perilous journey, Willow and Madmartigan encounter various obstacles, including fierce creatures, treacherous landscapes, and rival sorcerers. Along the way, Willow discovers his own hidden potential as a sorcerer and forms an unlikely bond with Elora Danan, who becomes a mentor to him.

Throughout their quest, Willow must confront his own identity and the true nature of his destiny. He learns that he is not just a simple farmer but a chosen one, destined to wield great power and protect the child from those who seek to harm him.

The film features a richly detailed world, memorable characters, and a narrative that explores themes of friendship, sacrifice, and self-discovery. The special effects, although dated by today's standards, still hold up remarkably well, bringing the fantastical creatures and landscapes to life in a way that immerses the viewer in the world of Willow.

Overall, Willow is a classic fantasy film that has captivated audiences for decades with its engaging story, memorable characters, and stunning visuals.

title: Black Hawk Down
tagline: Leave No Man Behind.
overview: When U.S. Rangers and an elite Delta Force team attempt to kidnap two underlings of a Somali warlord, their Black Hawk helicopters are shot down, and the Americans suffer heavy casualties, facing intense fighting from the militia on the ground.
plot:
Black Hawk Down is a 2001 war film directed by Ridley Scott, produced by Jerry Bruckheimer Films, and based on the book "Black Hawk Down: A Story of Modern War" by Mark Bowden. The film tells the true story of the Battle of Mogadishu, which took place during the Somali Civil War in October 1993.

The movie begins with a prologue that sets the stage for the events of the film. It shows the aftermath of the battle and introduces the main characters, including Delta Force operative Norm "Hoot" Gibson (played by Josh Hartnett), Sergeant First Class Mike Steele (played by Tom Sizemore), and Lieutenant Colonel Mike Steele's son, also named Mike (played by Ewan McGregor).

The story then flashes back to October 3, 1993, when a U.S. military operation aimed at capturing two top Somali warlords, Mohamed Farrah Aidid and Hassan Abdullah Hersi Gabane, goes awry. A team of U.S. soldiers from the 1st Battalion, 75th Ranger Regiment, led by Lieutenant Colonel Mike Steele, is sent to capture Aidid's bodyguards.

The operation begins with a helicopter assault, but things quickly go wrong when the Black Hawk helicopters are ambushed by Somali militiamen. The pilots, including Staff Sergeant Gary "Falcon" Gordon (played by Eric Bana), struggle to escape the city, but their aircraft are severely damaged and begin to take fire from the ground.

As the situation spirals out of control, the U.S. soldiers are forced to abandon ship and make a desperate bid for safety on foot. The movie's intense action sequences follow the soldiers as they navigate through the treacherous streets of Mogadishu, fighting off waves of Somali militiamen and trying to reach the relative safety of their extraction point.

The film's climax features an epic battle between the U.S. soldiers and the Somali militiamen, with both sides suffering heavy casualties. The movie ends with a poignant scene showing the aftermath of the battle, as the surviving soldiers are left to mourn their fallen comrades and grapple with the trauma they have experienced.

Throughout the film, Ridley Scott's direction brings a sense of realism and intensity to the action sequences, while also conveying the emotional toll that the battle takes on the soldiers. The cast delivers strong performances, particularly Josh Hartnett and Tom Sizemore, who bring depth and nuance to their characters.

Overall, Black Hawk Down is a gripping and intense war film that brings the true story of the Battle of Mogadishu to life with stunning action sequences and powerful performances.

title: The Running Man
tagline: 2019. A game nobody survives. This year might be the exception.
overview: By 2017, the global economy has collapsed and U.S. society has become a totalitarian police state, censoring all cultural activity. The government pacifies the populace by broadcasting a number of game shows in which convicted criminals fight for their lives, including the gladiator-style The Running Man, hosted by the ruthless Damon Killian, where “runners” attempt to evade “stalkers” and certain death for a chance to be pardoned and set free.
plot:
In 2017, following a worldwide economic collapse and resource scarcity, the USA has become a totalitarian police state. The government maintains control through propaganda and censorship of unsanctioned art, music, and communication. The state-controlled broadcaster ICS runs the nation's most popular program, "The Running Man," a game show in which prisoners can earn their freedom by surviving as "runners" against lethal "stalkers".
Captain Ben Richards is arrested after refusing orders to open fire on an unarmed food riot in Bakersfield. His fellow officers massacre the rioters and frame Richards for the incident, branding him the "Butcher of Bakersfield". Eighteen months later, Richards escapes from a prison labor camp with resistance fighters Harold Weiss and William Laughlin. They ask him to join their cause, but Richards declines, focused only on surviving.
Richards travels to his brother's former apartment but discovers that ICS composer Amber Mendez now lives there after his brother was taken for "re-education". Richards forces Amber to help him bypass airport security, but thinking he is the "Butcher", she alerts the authorities. After his capture, Amber sees news reports falsely claiming that Richards murdered people during the incident and begins to doubt his guilt.
Damon Killian, host of The Running Man, approaches Richards hoping to use his notoriety to revive the show's ratings. He threatens to send the recaptured Weiss and Laughlin into the game unless Richards agrees to participate. As the show begins, Killian betrays Richards by sending him, Weiss, and Laughlin into the game zone—an abandoned section of L.A.—via rocket sleds.
The group is hunted by Subzero, a hockey-themed stalker whom Richards kills, marking the first time a runner has ever killed a stalker. Meanwhile, Amber is caught retrieving the uncut Bakersfield footage and is sent into the zone. Killian sends in two more stalkers—the chainsaw-wielding Buzzsaw and the electricity-shooting Dynamo. Richards kills Buzzsaw, though Laughlin is fatally wounded. Elsewhere, Weiss discovers that the satellite uplink controlling government broadcasts is located inside the zone, and he cracks the access code for Amber to memorize before Dynamo kills him. Richards incapacitates Dynamo but refuses to kill him while he is defenseless, shocking the audience.
When Killian secretly offers Richards a job as a stalker, Richards angrily refuses. Amber later finds the corpses of the show's past "winners", realizing their victories were fabricated, and Richards kills the flamethrower-wielding Fireball. The audience begins cheering for Richards.
Richards and Amber are found by resistance leader Mic and taken to their command center. Killian tries to force retired stalker Captain Freedom to fight Richards, but he refuses unless he can fight him honorably. ICS instead fabricates footage showing Freedom killing Richards and Amber.

title: Planet of the Apes
tagline: You'll be sorry you were ever born human.
overview: After a spectacular crash-landing on an uncharted planet, brash astronaut Leo Davidson finds himself trapped in a savage world where talking apes dominate the human race. Desperate to find a way home, Leo must evade the invincible gorilla army led by Ruthless General Thade.
plot:
Planet of the Apes is a 2001 American science fiction adventure film from director Tim Burton, written by William Broyles Jr., Lawrence Konner and Mark Rosenthal. Loosely based on Pierre Boulle's 1963 novel, it remakes the 1968 film. Mark Wahlberg plays the astronaut Leo Davidson, with Tim Roth as General Thade, Helena Bonham Carter as Ari, Michael Clarke Duncan as Colonel Attar, Paul Giamatti as Limbo, Estella Warren as Daena and Kris Kristofferson.

In 2029, Leo works with apes trained for spaceflight aboard the space station Oberon. When an electromagnetic storm nears the station, his favourite chimpanzee, Pericles, is sent into it in a probe pod and vanishes. Leo follows in another pod without permission and crash-lands in the year 5021 on Ashlar, a planet where intelligent apes rule and keep humans as slaves. Ari, a chimpanzee who opposes this cruelty, buys Leo and a young woman, Daena, as servants in the house of her father, Senator Sandar. Leo breaks free and liberates other humans, taking the orangutan slave dealer Limbo prisoner to keep him quiet, while the ruthless chimpanzee General Thade and his gorilla deputy Attar lead an army in pursuit.

Leo reaches Calima, the forbidden temple of Semos, the first ape, whom the apes worship and expect to return one day. It proves to be the ancient wreck of the Oberon: Leo realises that the storm hurled him forward in time while the station, searching for him, crashed on the planet thousands of years earlier. Its logs show that the apes aboard, led by Semos, mutinied after the crash; the survivors of both species are the ancestors of the planet's people. As the apes attack the gathered humans, Leo uses the ship's remaining fuel to strike their first wave. The fighting halts when Pericles' pod descends from the sky, having also been carried through time; the apes take him for Semos and lay down their arms. Thade follows Leo into the wreck and grabs his gun, but Leo traps him on the pilot's deck. Leaving Pericles with Ari, Leo flies the pod back through the storm. Crashing in Washington, D.C., he finds the Lincoln Memorial now honours Thade, and the police and reporters who surround him are apes.

Released by 20th Century Fox on July 27, 2001, the film grossed $362.2 million worldwide, the ninth-highest total of the year. Reviews were mixed: critics faulted the screenplay and twist ending but praised Rick Baker's makeup, the visuals and the score, giving it 42% on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: Planet of the Apes
tagline: Somewhere in the Universe, there must be something better than man!
overview: Astronaut Taylor crash lands on a distant planet ruled by apes who use a primitive race of humans for experimentation and sport. Soon Taylor finds himself among the hunted, his life in the hands of a benevolent chimpanzee scientist.
plot:
Planet of the Apes is a groundbreaking science fiction film directed by Franklin J. Schaffner, released in 1968 by 20th Century Fox. The movie is set in a post-apocalyptic future where intelligent apes have evolved to become the dominant species on Earth.

The story begins with astronaut George Taylor (played by Charlton Heston), who crash-lands on a mysterious planet along with a group of astronauts, including Lieutenant Parker (James Franciscus) and Dr. Zaius (Lloyd Nolan). As they explore their surroundings, they discover that the planet is inhabited by intelligent apes, who seem to be living in a sophisticated society.

The apes are led by Zira (Kim Hunter), a scientist who is studying the human species. She is particularly interested in Taylor and his crew, as she believes they may hold the key to understanding the evolution of humanity. The apes also have a leader named Caesar (Roddy McDowall), who is intelligent and charismatic.

As Taylor and his crew try to find a way off the planet, they are captured by the apes and taken to their city. There, they meet Zira and Caesar, who reveal that the planet was once Earth but was devastated by nuclear war. The humans were wiped out, and the apes evolved from the survivors of the war.

The apes have created a complex society with their own culture, language, and customs. However, as Taylor and his crew learn more about the apes' world, they begin to realize that something is not quite right. They discover that the apes are hiding a dark secret: they have been using human embryos in their own breeding program.

Taylor becomes increasingly disillusioned with the apes' society and begins to question Zira's motives. He also forms a bond with Caesar, who is torn between his loyalty to Zira and his growing sense of humanity.

As the story unfolds, Taylor and Caesar embark on a perilous journey through the ape city, seeking answers about their past and the fate of humanity. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles and challenges, including treacherous terrain and hostile apes.

Ultimately, Taylor and Caesar reach the heart of the ape city, where they discover a shocking truth: the planet is actually a post-apocalyptic Earth, and the humans who survived the nuclear war were brought to this planet as infants and raised by the apes. The movie ends with Taylor, now an ape himself, sitting on a throne, surrounded by his new family.

The ending is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the audience to ponder the implications of the story. Is Taylor still human, or has he truly become one of them? The final shot of the movie shows a statue of a human figure with the inscription "Caesar's Head," suggesting that even in this post-apocalyptic world, humanity's legacy lives on.

Overall, Planet of the Apes is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that explores themes of identity, morality, and the nature of humanity. Its influence can still be seen in science fiction today, and it remains one of the most iconic and enduring films of all time.

title: The Best Years of Our Lives
original_title: The Best Years of Our Lives
tagline: Three wonderful loves in the best picture of the year!
overview: It's the hope that sustains the spirit of every GI: the dream of the day when he will finally return home. For three WWII veterans, the day has arrived. But for each man, the dream is about to become a nightmare.
plot:
Three returning World War II veterans meet on a flight to their midwestern hometown of Boone City. USAAF bombardier captain Fred Derry had been a drugstore soda jerk who lived with his father and stepmother on the wrong side of the tracks. Before shipping out, Fred married Marie after a whirlwind romance. Marie has since been working in a nightclub to fill her time despite receiving Fred's combat pay as an Air Force officer. U.S. Army sergeant Al Stephenson is a bank executive; he, his wife Milly and their children Peggy and Rob live in a luxury apartment. U.S. Navy petty officer Homer Parrish was a star high school athlete living with his middle-class parents and younger sister, and dating his next-door neighbor Wilma, whom he intended to marry upon his return from the war.
Each man faces challenges integrating back into civilian life. Homer lost both hands in the war; he is reluctant to return home and face his well-meaning parents and their friends, who have a hard time seeing past his disability. Homer can deftly use his mechanical hooks, but hesitates to display affection for Wilma as he cannot believe she will still want to marry him. Al, tired and jaded, returns to the bank and is given a promotion, but wrestles with alcohol. Fred suffers from PTSD flashbacks and struggles to find a job beyond menial work, befitting a military officer.
Fred arrives home and cannot locate his party girl wife, who does not expect him. The Stephensons and Peggy invite Fred to join them, bar-hopping to celebrate Al's return. An inebriated Fred keeps asking Peggy who she is; she humorously reminds him she's "Al's daughter." When Fred can't get into his apartment, the Stephensons offer him a bed for the night. Later, Peggy calms Fred during a nightmare and they develop a mutual attraction. After meeting Marie during an outing orchestrated by Peggy, she concludes Marie is shallow and materialistic. Peggy determines to break up Fred's marriage, much to Al's consternation.
Frustrated and depressed by his loss of independence; and concerned that Wilma doesn't fully understand the difficulties of being married to him, Homer demonstrates how she'll need to assist him when he removes his prosthetic hands at bedtime, leaving him helpless. Wilma reaffirms her love and vows her commitment to a grateful and emotional Homer, who finally embraces her.
Widely respected by the bank's senior management for his past business acumen, Al is admonished after approving an unsecured loan to a farmer and fellow veteran without collateral (never realizing the land the farmer wishes to purchase could be collateral for the loan). With inhibitions lowered by excessive drinking, Al gives a speech at a work banquet that satirizes requiring a veteran to provide collateral before risking his life to take a hill in battle.
With little work experience and unable to find a better job than soda jerk, Fred returns to the same drugstore and is now supervised by his former protege.

title: Bullitt

overview: Senator Walter Chalmers is aiming to take down mob boss Pete Ross with the help of testimony from the criminal's hothead brother Johnny, who is in protective custody in San Francisco under the watch of police lieutenant Frank Bullitt. plot:
Bullitt is a 1968 American action thriller film directed by Peter Yates and produced by Solar Productions. The movie stars Steve McQueen as Frank Bullitt, a tough and skilled FBI agent tasked with protecting the key witness in a murder case.

The story begins with the introduction of Frank Bullitt (Steve McQueen), an experienced and skilled FBI agent who is assigned to protect Richard "Rich" Boyer (Robert Vaughn), a wealthy businessman whose testimony could bring down notorious crime boss Samson Pope (Pat Renella). The two men are on their way to Los Angeles when they are ambushed by Pope's henchmen, resulting in the death of Boyer.

Bullitt is left shaken but determined to solve the case and bring justice to Boyer's family. He teams up with Chico Gonzalez (Estelito Aguilar), a Mexican-American informant who provides him with crucial information about Pope's organization. As Bullitt delves deeper into the case, he becomes increasingly obsessed with finding the killer.

The plot thickens as Bullitt discovers that Pope is involved in a large-scale money laundering operation and that Boyer was getting close to exposing it. With the help of Gonzalez, Bullitt sets out to track down Pope's men and bring them to justice.

As the story unfolds, Bullitt becomes more and more determined to solve the case, often putting himself in harm's way. He is aided by his partner, Lee (Robert Beatty), who provides him with support and guidance throughout the investigation.

The climax of the movie takes place during a high-speed car chase through San Francisco, where Bullitt pursues Pope's henchmen in a white Mustang. The chase is intense and suspenseful, with both drivers pushing their cars to the limit.

In the end, Bullitt finally tracks down Pope and his men, leading to a tense showdown between the two. However, just as Bullitt thinks he has solved the case, it becomes clear that there are still many loose ends. The movie ends with Bullitt reflecting on the case and the toll it has taken on him.

Throughout the movie, Steve McQueen delivers a memorable performance as Frank Bullitt, bringing depth and nuance to the character. The film's action sequences, particularly the iconic car chase, have become legendary in the world of cinema.

Overall, Bullitt is a gripping and suspenseful thriller that showcases Steve McQueen's acting abilities and Peter Yates' direction. The movie's blend of action, drama, and intrigue has made it a classic of American cinema.

Saya's next mission begins at the American Yokota Air Base, which is active in the buildup to the Vietnam War. At least one Chiropteran has managed to infiltrate the air base, and it is only a matter of time before they feed again, go into hibernation, and become untraceable. Saya is to pose as a school girl, infiltrate the high school adjacent to the base, and then track and kill the Chiropterans.
At the school, Saya runs into a meek nurse, Amino Makiho, on the eve of the school's annual Halloween party. Two of Saya's classmates, Sharon and Linda, make a visit to Makiho at the nurse's office. Suddenly, Saya bursts into the room, killing Linda and wounding Sharon, breaking her sword in the process. Both girls are revealed to be Chiropterans. Makiho goes into shock at the revelation. Meanwhile, a third Chiropteran reveals itself and begins making its way to the base. Back at the school, Makiho regains her nerve and pursues Sharon into a room full of dancing Americans in costume, where she finds Sharon transformed. Saya saves her and both flee into a nearby motor pool. The Chiropterans trap them inside and attack.
David delivers a new sword, and Saya uses it to kill Sharon. The final Chiropteran then decides to flee, attempting to stow away on a departing cargo plane. David and Saya give chase and she manages to strike the Chiropteran and mortally wound it. She then stands over the dying creature and lets some of her blood trickle into its mouth. Louis arrives and recovers Makiho before the local police reach her.
Afterward, Makiho is seen in an interview with government officials who question her about the night's events. However, it's revealed that all evidence of the battle between Saya and the Chiropterans has been covered up and both David and Saya have disappeared, leaving Makiho with nothing to prove the veracity of her story. Her interviewer then asks her to identify Saya in a picture which has a girl that looks identical to her, except the picture was taken in 1892. The only other description of the picture is the word "VAMPIRE". Makiho then returns to the school, where she narrates that she never really discovered the full truth behind Saya and the Chiropterans, and wonders if she's still out there fighting them.

title: Cars
tagline: Ahhh... it's got that new movie smell.
overview: Lightning McQueen, a hotshot rookie race car driven to succeed, discovers that life is about the journey, not the finish line, when he finds himself unexpectedly detoured in the sleepy Route 66 town of Radiator Springs. On route across the country to the big Piston Cup Championship in California to compete against two seasoned pros, McQueen gets to know the town's offbeat characters.
plot:
Cars is a computer-animated comedy-adventure film released in 2006 by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie takes place in a world where cars are living beings, and it follows the story of Lightning McQueen, a hotshot rookie race car who gets stranded in a small town called Radiator Springs.

The film begins with Lightning McQueen (voiced by Owen Wilson), a talented but arrogant racing car from North Carolina. He is on his way to California to participate in the Piston Cup Championship, a prestigious racing competition that will make him a legend in the racing world. During his journey, he gets lost due to a faulty GPS system and ends up in Radiator Springs, a small town on Route 66.

Initially, McQueen is reluctant to stay in Radiator Springs, as he believes it's not a place for high-performance cars like himself. However, he soon befriends the town's residents, including Mater (voiced by Larry the Cable Guy), a rusty but lovable tow truck; Sally Carrera (voiced by Bonnie Hunt), a sleek and sophisticated Porsche; and Doc Hudson (voiced by Paul Newman), a wise and aged Hudson Hornet.

As McQueen spends more time in Radiator Springs, he learns about the town's history and the struggles its residents have faced due to the decline of Route 66. He also discovers that his arrival has brought new life to the town, but at the cost of its former glory. McQueen decides to help the townspeople by participating in the annual "Cozy Cone" festival, which is a celebration of the town's heritage.

However, things take a turn when McQueen's rival, Chick Hicks (voiced by Michael Keaton), arrives in Radiator Springs, seeking to sabotage McQueen's chances of winning the Piston Cup. As the championship approaches, McQueen must balance his racing ambitions with his newfound friendships and sense of responsibility towards the people of Radiator Springs.

In the end, McQueen learns a valuable lesson about the importance of friendship, community, and being true to oneself. He decides to abandon his original plan to win the Piston Cup and instead focuses on helping Radiator Springs revitalize its economy and restore its former glory. The film concludes with McQueen's return to Radiator Springs as a champion, but not just for winning the championship – for being a part of a community that has become like family to him.

Throughout the movie, Cars features stunning animation, lovable characters, and a heartwarming story that explores themes of friendship, perseverance, and finding one's true purpose. The film was a critical and commercial success, grossing over $462 million worldwide and spawning two sequels, Cars 2 (2011) and Cars 3 (2017).

title: Dawn of the Dead
tagline: When there’s no more room in HELL, the dead will walk the EARTH!
overview: During an ever-growing epidemic of zombies that have risen from the dead, two Philadelphia SWAT team members, a traffic reporter, and his television-executive girlfriend seek refuge in a secluded shopping mall.
plot:
Dawn of the Dead is a 1978 zombie horror film written, directed and edited by George A. Romero and produced by Richard P. Rubinstein. An American-Italian co-production, it is the second film in Romero's series of zombie films after Night of the Living Dead (1968), and depicts a zombie apocalypse on a much larger scale. David Emge, Ken Foree, Scott Reiniger and Gaylen Ross star as survivors who barricade themselves inside a suburban shopping mall.

The dead are rising and attacking the living across the United States, and society is collapsing. At a Philadelphia television station, the traffic reporter Stephen and his pregnant girlfriend, the producer Francine, plan to escape in the station's helicopter. Across the city, a SWAT team raids a housing project whose tenants have refused to hand over their dead to the authorities, and the operation descends into a bloodbath. Disillusioned, the SWAT officer Roger, a friend of Stephen's, and Peter, an officer from another unit, decide to desert and join the couple. The four flee the city by helicopter and, after a few close calls while refueling, land on the roof of a deserted shopping mall.

Finding everything they need inside, they decide to stay. The men block the entrances with trucks and clear the building of zombies, but Roger grows reckless and is bitten. After he dies and reanimates, Peter shoots him. The survivors build a hidden refuge and settle into a comfortable but empty life of consumer abundance as emergency broadcasts end. Fran has Stephen teach her to fly the helicopter.

Months later, a gang of marauding bikers spots the helicopter and breaks into the mall to loot it, letting in hundreds of zombies. Stephen, refusing to give up what he regards as theirs, opens fire on the bikers, setting off a battle in which many of them are devoured. Stephen is shot and killed by the zombies, and after reanimating he leads the undead to the hideout. Peter kills him and prepares to take his own life, but changes his mind and fights his way to the roof, where he joins Fran in the helicopter as they fly off, low on fuel, toward an uncertain future.

Inspired by Romero's visit to the Monroeville Mall in Pennsylvania, the film was co-financed by Dario Argento, who edited his own cut featuring music by Goblin, and its gore effects launched the career of Tom Savini. Released unrated in the United States after receiving an X rating, it was acclaimed by critics, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 92% approval.

title: Dawn of the Dead
tagline: When the undead rise, civilization will fall.
overview: A group of survivors take refuge in a shopping mall after the world is taken over by aggressive, flesh-eating zombies.
plot:
Dawn of the Dead is a 2004 American zombie horror film directed by Zack Snyder, starring Ving Rhames, Mena Suvari, and Jake Weber. The movie is a remake of George A. Romero's 1978 film of the same name.

The story begins with a montage of news clips showing the rapid spread of a mysterious virus that turns people into zombies. We then see a group of survivors, including Jim (Jake Weber), Steve (Michael Kelly), and Peter (Ty Burrell), who are trying to escape the chaos in Philadelphia. They eventually find themselves at a shopping mall, where they barricade themselves inside.

As the days pass, the group tries to maintain some semblance of normalcy, with Jim attempting to hold down a job as a security guard while Steve and Peter try to scavenge for food and supplies. However, their attempts are constantly thwarted by hordes of zombies that seem to be attracted to the mall.

The group soon realizes that they are not alone in the mall. They discover a mysterious woman named Ana (Mena Suvari), who is initially hostile towards them but eventually becomes an ally. As the days turn into weeks, the group begins to experience strange and terrifying occurrences, including visions of a zombie-like creature that seems to be watching them.

As tensions rise within the group, Jim's leadership is challenged by Steve, who wants to take more drastic measures to survive. Meanwhile, Ana's past is slowly revealed, showing her to be a former model who was infected with the virus and has since become a zombie herself.

The movie takes a dark turn when the group discovers that the mall is being overrun by an even larger horde of zombies. In a desperate bid to escape, they set fire to the mall, hoping to create a diversion that will allow them to make their way out.

However, as they attempt to flee, Jim becomes increasingly unhinged, and his actions become more erratic. The group eventually splits up, with some members making it out of the mall while others are left behind.

The movie ends with Ana, who has been bitten by a zombie, being taken away by a group of survivors who have managed to escape the mall. As she is carried off into the distance, we see Jim standing alone in the ruins of the mall, his eyes fixed on the camera with a mixture of horror and despair.

Throughout the movie, Snyder's direction adds a layer of social commentary, using the zombie apocalypse as a metaphor for consumerism and the breakdown of society. The film's use of satire and irony is evident in its portrayal of the zombies as mindless consumers who are drawn to the mall like moths to a flame.

Overall, Dawn of the Dead is a tense and unsettling horror movie that explores themes of survival, leadership, and the human condition. While it received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, it has since become a cult classic and is widely regarded as one of the best zombie movies of all time.

title: Godzilla
tagline: Size does matter.
overview: French nuclear tests irradiate an iguana into a giant monster that viciously attacks freighter ships in the Pacific Ocean. A team of experts, including Niko Tatopoulos, conclude that the oversized reptile is the culprit. Before long, the giant lizard is loose in Manhattan as the US military races to destroy the monster before it reproduces and it's spawn takes over the world.
plot:
Godzilla is a 1998 American monster film directed by Roland Emmerich, who co-wrote it with producer Dean Devlin as an American reboot of Toho's Godzilla franchise. Matthew Broderick stars as the biologist Nick Tatopoulos and Jean Reno as a French secret agent, with Maria Pitillo, Hank Azaria, Kevin Dunn, Michael Lerner and Harry Shearer. The film is dedicated to Godzilla co-creator Tomoyuki Tanaka. TriStar Pictures released it on May 20, 1998, in a then-record 3,310 theatres in North America.

Fallout from French nuclear tests in Polynesia mutates an iguana nest. Years later a huge creature sinks a Japanese fishing ship, and a traumatised survivor, questioned by a mysterious Frenchman, can only repeat "Gojira". Nick Tatopoulos, studying earthworms at Chernobyl, is drafted by the US government to analyse the trail of destruction and concludes that the animal is a radiation-born mutant, not a dinosaur. The creature then comes ashore in Manhattan, flattening streets as the city is evacuated.

The army lures it out with a mountain of fish but fails to kill it. Nick discovers that the animal reproduces asexually and is about to lay eggs. He reunites with his former girlfriend Audrey Timmonds, an ambitious junior reporter, who steals a classified tape from him; her boss, Charles Caiman, claims the story and names the monster Godzilla. Nick is dismissed from the operation and recruited by Philippe Roaché, an agent of the French secret service trying to cover up France's role. Audrey and her cameraman Victor "Animal" Palotti tag along.

After a second strike, Godzilla is attacked by submarines in the Hudson and believed dead. Nick's group locates its nest inside Madison Square Garden, where hundreds of offspring hatch and attack. They broadcast a warning from the arena, escaping just before air strikes destroy it. Godzilla, still alive and enraged by the loss of its young, pursues them across Manhattan until it becomes tangled in the cables of the Brooklyn Bridge and is killed by missiles. Audrey quits her job, and Philippe departs with Animal's footage. In the ruins, one surviving egg hatches.

The film earned about 379 million dollars worldwide but was widely panned, with a 20% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, and won Golden Raspberry Awards including Worst Remake or Sequel.

However, due to climate change, the ice caps are melting, causing chaos throughout the world. The trio is forced to embark on an epic journey to reach the fabled "Paradise Falls," a lush oasis that has been hidden beneath the melting ice.

As they travel through treacherous landscapes and encounter various obstacles, Manny, Sid, and Diego begin to realize that their friendship is more important than their individual goals. Manny, Sid, and Diego must use their unique skills and work together to defeat the pirates and save Paradise Falls. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about teamwork, trust, and the importance of preserving their natural habitats.

The movie features stunning animation, witty humor, and lovable characters that have become iconic in popular culture. The voice cast, including Ray Romano, John Leguizamo, Denis Leary, and Queen Latifah, delivers memorable performances that bring the characters to life.

In the end, Manny, Sid, and Diego successfully defeat Captain Gutt and his pirates, saving Paradise Falls and restoring balance to the ecosystem. The movie concludes with a heartwarming moment of friendship and camaraderie between the three main characters as they look out upon their newly preserved home.

Overall, Ice Age: The Meltdown is a fun, action-packed adventure that explores themes of friendship, teamwork, and environmentalism. With its engaging storyline, lovable characters, and stunning animation, it's no wonder this movie has become a beloved classic among both children and adults alike.

overview: Alex the lion is the king of the urban jungle, the main attraction at New York's Central Park Zoo. plot:
Madagascar is a computer-animated comedy film released in 2005 by DreamWorks Pictures. The movie follows the story of four main characters: Alex the lion, Marty the zebra, Gloria the hippopotamus, and Melman the giraffe.

The film begins with Alex (voiced by Ben Stiller), Marty (voiced by Chris Rock), Gloria (voiced by Jada Pinkett Smith), and Melman (voiced by David Schwimmer) living in the Central Park Zoo in New York City. The animals are content with their lives, but they often fantasize about exploring the wild.

One day, a group of zoo employees plan to relocate the animals to a theme park called "Madagascar" in Africa. Alex is excited at the prospect of experiencing the wild, while Marty is more concerned about being separated from his friends. Gloria and Melman are hesitant, but ultimately agree to go along with the move.

Upon arrival in Madagascar, the animals discover that they have been transported to a remote island, far from their home in New York City. They soon realize that they must survive on their own and adapt to their new surroundings. Marty, being the curious and adventurous one, takes the lead in exploring the island and finding food.

As the group navigates their new environment, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, wild predators, and rival animals. Along the way, Alex struggles with his identity as a lion, feeling pressure to live up to his role as the "king" of the zoo. Marty, on the other hand, finds himself in a series of comedic misadventures, often getting into trouble due to his impulsive nature.

As the story unfolds, the animals form an unlikely friendship with a group of lemurs, led by King Julian (voiced by Sacha Baron Cohen). The lemurs are initially hostile towards the newcomers but eventually warm up to them. However, their friendship is put to the test when they discover that the zoo employees who brought them to Madagascar have abandoned them.

In the end, Alex and his friends must work together to survive on the island and find a way back home. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about teamwork, loyalty, and embracing their true selves. The movie culminates in a thrilling finale where the animals outsmart the zoo employees and escape the island, returning to New York City.

Throughout the film, the characters' personalities shine through, with Marty's humor and wit providing much of the comedic relief. The animation is vibrant and colorful, bringing the characters and their world to life. Overall, Madagascar is a heartwarming and entertaining film that explores themes of friendship, identity, and belonging.

title: Mission: Impossible II
tagline: Expect the impossible again.
overview: With computer genius Luther Stickell at his side and a beautiful thief on his mind, agent Ethan Hunt races across Australia and Spain to stop a former IMF agent from unleashing a genetically engineered biological weapon called Chimera. This mission, should Hunt choose to accept it, plunges him into the center of an international crisis of terrifying magnitude.
plot:
Mission: Impossible II is a 2000 action spy film directed by John Woo and starring Tom Cruise as Ethan Hunt. The movie takes place two years after the events of the first film.

The story begins with Ethan Hunt, who has been presumed dead after his last mission went awry. However, he is revealed to be alive and working undercover in the Middle East, where he infiltrates a terrorist organization known as the Syndicate. The Syndicate is led by a ruthless woman named Nyah Nordoff-Hall (Thandie Newton), who is also Ethan's love interest.

As Ethan delves deeper into the Syndicate, he discovers that they are planning to sell a deadly virus called the "Chimera" to the highest bidder. The Chimera is a genetically engineered virus that can kill millions of people and has the potential to wipe out entire cities.

Ethan soon realizes that the true mastermind behind the Syndicate is Sean Ambrose (Dougray Scott), a former CIA operative who was thought to be dead. Ambrose has been working with Nyah, who is revealed to be his sister, and together they plan to sell the Chimera virus to the highest bidder.

As Ethan navigates through the complex web of intrigue, he must also contend with the IMF (Impossible Mission Force), which is now led by Jim Phelps (Jon Voight). However, it soon becomes clear that Phelps has been compromised by Ambrose and is working against Ethan's interests.

The plot thickens as Ethan discovers that Nyah is being manipulated by her brother and that she is not what she seems. In a thrilling twist, Ethan and Nyah team up to take down the Syndicate and prevent the sale of the Chimera virus.

In the climactic final act, Ethan faces off against Ambrose in a high-stakes battle at a nightclub. The two engage in an intense fight, with Ethan using his wits and agility to outmaneuver Ambrose's henchmen.

As the dust settles, Ethan emerges victorious, but not without sacrifices. Nyah is revealed to be a double agent who was working to take down her brother from within. In the end, Ethan and Nyah share a moment of tenderness, suggesting that their relationship may have a future.

The movie concludes with Ethan returning to the IMF, where he is welcomed back as a hero. However, the film ends on a somber note, hinting that there are still many more missions ahead for Ethan Hunt.

Overall, Mission: Impossible II is an action-packed thrill ride that delivers on its promise of high-octane excitement and espionage intrigue. Tom Cruise's performance as Ethan Hunt is as charismatic as ever, and the movie's twists and turns keep viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

title: Mission: Impossible III
tagline: The mission begins 05:05:06.
overview: Retired from active duty to train new IMF agents, Ethan Hunt is called back into action to confront sadistic arms dealer, Owen Davian. Hunt must try to protect his girlfriend while working with his new team to complete the mission.

Ethan soon discovers that Davian is working with the arms dealer, August Walker (Philip Dance), to sell nuclear warheads on the black market. As Ethan delves deeper into the mission, he must navigate his complicated past and confront his own demons in order to rescue Lindsey and prevent a global catastrophe.

Throughout the film, Ethan's skills as an agent are put to the test as he faces off against Davian and Walker in a series of intense action sequences. The movie features a mix of high-stakes espionage, heart-pumping stunts, and witty banter between Ethan and his allies.

One of the standout aspects of Mission: Impossible III is its exploration of Ethan's character development. As he navigates the complex web of intrigue, he must confront his own mortality and the consequences of his actions. The film also introduces a new character, Benji Dunn (Simon Pegg), who becomes Ethan's trusted ally and provides comic relief in an otherwise tense situation.

The movie's climax features an epic showdown between Ethan and Davian, with the two agents engaging in a high-speed car chase through the streets of Paris. In the end, Ethan emerges victorious, but not without sacrifices. The film concludes on a bittersweet note, as Ethan comes to terms with his past and looks towards a uncertain future.

Overall, Mission: Impossible III is an action-packed thrill ride that delivers on its promise of high-octane espionage and heart-pumping stunts. With Tom Cruise delivering a standout performance, the movie sets the stage for the next installment in the franchise.

title: The China Syndrome
tagline: Sometimes it’s too late to tell the truth.
overview: While doing a series of reports on alternative energy sources, opportunistic reporter Kimberly Wells witnesses an accident at a nuclear power plant. Wells is determined to publicize the incident, but soon finds herself entangled in a sinister conspiracy to keep the full impact of the incident a secret.
plot:
While visiting the Ventana nuclear power plant outside Los Angeles, television news reporter Kimberly Wells, her cameraman Richard Adams and their soundman Hector Salas witness the plant going through a turbine trip and corresponding SCRAM (emergency shutdown). Shift Supervisor Jack Godell notices an unusual vibration in his cup of coffee.
In response to a gauge indicating high water levels, Godell begins removing water from the core, but the gauge remains high as operators open more valves to dump water. Another operator notices a second gauge indicating low water levels. Godell taps the first gauge, which immediately unsticks and drops to indicate very low levels. The crew urgently pumps water back in and celebrates in relief at bringing the reactor back under control.
Adams has surreptitiously filmed the incident, despite being asked not to film for security reasons. Wells' superior refuses to broadcast her report on the incident. Adams steals the footage and shows it to experts who conclude that the plant came perilously close to meltdown‍—‍‌the China syndrome.
During an inspection of the plant before it is brought back online, Godell discovers a puddle of radioactive water that has apparently leaked from a pump. He pushes to delay restarting the plant, but the plant superintendent wants nothing standing in the way of the restart.
Godell finds that a series of radiographs supposedly verifying the welds on the leaking pump are identical‍—‍‌the contractor simply kept resubmitting the same picture. He brings the evidence to the plant superintendent, who brushes him off as paranoid, stating that new radiographs would cost $20 million. Godell confronts Royce, an employee of Foster-Sullivan who built the plant, as it was he who signed off on the radiographs. Godell threatens to go to the Nuclear Regulatory Commission, but Royce threatens him; later, a pair of men from Foster-Sullivan park outside his house.
Wells and Adams confront Godell at his home and he voices his concerns. Wells and Adams ask him to testify at the NRC hearings over Foster-Sullivan's plans to build another nuclear plant. Godell agrees to obtain, through Salas, the false radiographs to take to the hearings.
Salas' car is run off the road and the radiographs are taken from him. Godell is chased by the men waiting outside his home. He takes refuge inside the plant, where he finds that the reactor is being brought up to full power. Grabbing a gun from a security guard, he forces everyone out, including his friend and co-worker Ted Spindler, and demands to be interviewed by Wells on live television. Plant management agrees to the interview in order to buy time as they try to regain control of the plant.
Minutes into the broadcast, plant technicians deliberately cause a SCRAM so they can distract Godell and retake the control room. A SWAT team forces its way in, the television cable is cut, and Godell is shot. Before dying, he feels the unusual vibration again.

title: Mulholland Drive
tagline: An actress longing to be a star. A woman searching for herself. Both worlds will collide… on Mulholland Drive.
overview: Blonde Betty Elms has only just arrived in Hollywood to become a movie star when she meets an enigmatic brunette with amnesia. Meanwhile, as the two set off to solve the second woman's identity, filmmaker Adam Kesher runs into ominous trouble while casting his latest project.
plot:
Mulholland Drive is a 2001 surrealist neo-noir mystery written and directed by David Lynch. Naomi Watts stars as Betty Elms, an aspiring actress newly arrived in Los Angeles, and Laura Harring as an amnesiac car crash survivor, with Justin Theroux as a film director, Ann Miller and Dan Hedaya. Originally conceived as a television pilot for ABC, it was shot in 1999, but after the network rejected Lynch's cut, he secured funding from the French company StudioCanal to shoot additional scenes and complete it as a feature film.

The film begins with images of jitterbug dancers and a smiling young blonde woman receiving applause. At night on Mulholland Drive, a dark-haired woman in an evening dress is about to be shot by her driver when another car crashes into theirs. Suffering from amnesia, she stumbles down into Los Angeles and hides in an empty apartment. The next morning she is discovered by Betty, a cheerful, optimistic young woman from Deep River, Ontario, who is staying in her aunt's apartment while pursuing an acting career. The stranger takes the name "Rita" from a poster of Rita Hayworth and remembers only that she is in danger. The two women become friends and find a large sum of money and a mysterious blue key in Rita's purse.

In parallel stories, a man at a diner describes a nightmare about a terrifying figure behind the building and collapses in shock when the figure appears. Adam Kesher, a film director, is pressured by sinister, mob-connected men to cast an unknown actress named Camilla Rhodes in his new film; when he refuses, his production is shut down and his life falls apart. Betty and Rita investigate Rita's identity, a search that leads them to an apartment where they find a decomposing body, and the two women fall in love. After a late-night visit to an eerie theater called Club Silencio, a blue box opened by the key transforms the story, and the film shifts into a darker reality in which the characters reappear in different roles, revealing a tale of ambition, jealousy, failure and despair in Hollywood.

Mulholland Drive initially divided some viewers with its puzzling structure but received wide critical acclaim. Lynch shared the Best Director award at the Cannes Film Festival and was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Director. The film launched Watts's career and has since been named in critics' polls as one of the greatest films of the 21st century.

title: The Leopard
tagline: Luchino Visconti's enduring romantic adventure
overview: As Garibaldi's troops begin the unification of Italy in the 1860s, an aristocratic Sicilian family grudgingly adapts to the sweeping social changes undermining their way of life. Proud but pragmatic Prince Don Fabrizio Salina allows his war hero nephew, Tancredi, to marry Angelica, the beautiful daughter of gauche, bourgeois Don Calogero, in order to maintain the family's accustomed level of comfort and political clout.
plot:
The Leopard (Italian: Il Gattopardo) is a 1963 epic historical drama directed by Luchino Visconti and adapted from Giuseppe Tomasi di Lampedusa's 1958 novel. Burt Lancaster stars as Don Fabrizio Corbera, Prince of Salina, with Alain Delon as his ambitious nephew Tancredi and Claudia Cardinale as Angelica. Paolo Stoppa plays Don Calogero Sedara. It was an Italian-French co-production between Titanus and Pathé.

In Sicily in 1860, as Garibaldi's redshirts fight the Bourbon king Francis II, the Prince tolerates his rebel nephew Tancredi with wry affection. After Garibaldi's forces take Palermo, the Prince reflects that change is inevitable: the middle class will replace the old ruling class, even if on the surface everything stays the same. He retreats to his summer palace at Donnafugata, where a plebiscite on unification passes unanimously, helped by the corruption of the town's leading citizen, Calogero. Calogero's beautiful daughter Angelica captivates both the Prince and Tancredi. Knowing Tancredi needs Calogero's money, the Prince blesses their engagement. When Tancredi switches from Garibaldi's army to the new royal army of Victor Emmanuel, the Prince recognizes him as the kind of opportunist who will thrive in the new Italy.

An envoy, Chevalley, invites the Prince to sit in the senate of the new Kingdom of Italy. He declines, saying Sicilians are too proud of their ancient heritage to want modernity, and predicts that the leopards and lions of his class will be replaced by jackals and hyenas. He suggests Calogero instead. At a lavish ball that marks Angelica's entry into high society, the melancholy Prince wanders through the rooms, disillusioned with the nouveau riche, until Angelica invites him to dance. For a moment he regains the grace of his youth, but his disenchantment soon returns. At dawn he walks home alone, pausing as a priest hurries by to give last rites, and disappears into a dark alley, a symbol of the fading past to which he belongs.

The Leopard won the Palme d'Or at the 1963 Cannes Film Festival and opened in Italy on March 28, 1963. It succeeded in Europe, but the shortened, English-dubbed version Fox released in the United States was panned by most American critics. The restored 185-minute version reached American theaters in 1983 to warm reviews, with Pauline Kael calling it intelligent and rapturous. It is now widely regarded as one of the greatest films ever made,.

title: Whale Rider
tagline: In the ways of the ancients she found a hope for the future.
overview: On the east coast of New Zealand, the Whangara people believe their presence there dates back a thousand years or more to a single ancestor, Paikea, who escaped death when his canoe capsized by riding to shore on the back of a whale. From then on, Whangara chiefs, always the first-born, always male, have been considered Paikea's direct descendants. Pai, an 11-year-old girl in a patriarchal New Zealand tribe, believes she is destined to be the new chief. But her grandfather Koro is bound by tradition to pick a male leader. Pai loves Koro more than anyone in the world, but she must fight him and a thousand years of tradition to fulfill her destiny.
plot:
The film's plot follows the story of Paikea Apirana (Pai for short). In her village, the leader is traditionally a first-born son, a direct patrilineal descendant of Paikea, the Whale Rider who rode on top of a whale from Hawaiki. Pai is originally born a twin, but her twin brother and her mother died during childbirth. Pai is female and so technically cannot inherit the leadership. While her grandfather, Koro, later forms an affectionate bond with his granddaughter, carrying her to school every day on his bicycle, he also condemns and resents her for conflicts within the tribe.
After the death of his wife and despite overwhelming pressure from Koro, Pai's father refuses to assume traditional leadership or finish the waka that he had started building for the baby son; instead, he moves to Germany to pursue a career as an artist. At one point, Paikea decides to live with her father because her grandfather says he doesn't want her. However, as they are driving away, she finds that she cannot bear to leave the sea as the whale seems to be calling her back. Pai tells her father to return her home.
Koro leads a cultural school for the village's first-born boys, hoping to find a new leader. He teaches the boys to use a taiaha (fighting stick), which is traditionally reserved for males. Pai is interested in the lessons, but is discouraged sternly by Koro for doing so. Pai feels that she can become the leader (although no woman has ever done so) and is determined to succeed. Her grandmother, Nanny, tells Pai that her second son, Pai's uncle, had won a taiaha tournament in his youth while he was still slim and so Pai secretly learns from him. She also secretly follows Koro's lessons. One of the students, Hemi, is also sympathetic towards her.
Koro is furious when he finds out, particularly when she wins a taiaha fight against Hemi. However, Koro's frustration turns to horror when none of the boys succeed at the traditional task of recovering a whale tooth (rei puta) that he threw into the ocean - the mission that would prove one of them worthy of becoming leader. With the loss of the rei puta, Koro (in despair) calls out the ancient ones: the whales. In an attempt to help, Pai also calls out to them and they hear her call.
One day Pai, her uncle, her uncle's girlfriend Shilo, and others take the boat to where Koro flung the rei puta into the sea. Pai confidently declares she'll find it and dives into the water. She finds the rei puta, which means that she is the rightful leader. Nanny does not think Koro is ready to accept this and does not tell him. Pai, in an attempt to bridge the rift that has formed, invites Koro to be her guest of honor at a concert of Māori chants that her school is putting on. Unknown to all, she had won an interschool speech contest with a touching dedication to Koro and the traditions of the village.

title: The Wind That Shakes the Barley
original_title: The Wind That Shakes the Barley
tagline: War has cost them their innocence... Freedom will cost them their blood.
overview: In 1920s Ireland young doctor Damien O'Donovan prepares to depart for a new job in a London hospital. As he says his goodbyes at a friend's farm, British Black and Tans arrive, and a young man is killed. Damien joins his brother Teddy in the Irish Republican Army, but political events are soon set in motion that tear the brothers apart.
plot:
In County Cork in Ireland, in 1920, Damien O'Donovan is about to leave his native village to practice medicine in a London hospital. Meanwhile, his brother Teddy commands the local flying column of the Irish Republican Army. After a hurling match, Damien witnesses the summary execution of his friend Micheál Ó Súilleabháin, by British Black and Tans, for refusing to say his name in English and punching an officer. Although shaken, Damien rebuffs his friends' entreaties to stay in Ireland and join the IRA, saying that the war is unwinnable. As he is leaving town, Damien witnesses the British Army vainly trying to intimidate a railway employee for refusing to permit the troops to board. In response, Damien decides to stay and is sworn into Teddy's IRA brigade.
After drilling in the mountains, the column raids the village's Royal Irish Constabulary barracks to acquire more arms, then uses them to assassinate four Auxiliaries. In the aftermath, Anglo-Irish landowner Sir John Hamilton coerces one of his servants, IRA member Chris Reilly, into passing information to the British Army's Intelligence Corps. As a result, the entire brigade is arrested. In their cell, Damien meets the train driver, Dan, a union official who shares Damien's socialist views.
Meanwhile, British officers interrogate Teddy, pulling out his fingernails when he refuses to give them the names of IRA members. Johnny Gogan, a British soldier of Irish descent, helps the prisoners escape, but three are left behind. After the actions of Sir John and Chris are revealed to the IRA's intelligence network, both are taken hostage. As Teddy is still recovering, Damien is temporarily placed in command. News arrives that the three remaining IRA prisoners have been tortured and shot. Simultaneously, the brigade receives orders to "execute the spies".
Even though Chris is a lifelong friend, Damien shoots both him and Sir John. Later, the IRA ambushes and wipes out a convoy of the Auxiliary Division, though Gogan dies as the IRA's sole casualty. Shortly after, another detachment of Auxiliaries loots and burns the farmhouse of Damien's sweetheart, Cumann na mBan member Sinéad Sullivan. Sinéad is held at gunpoint while her head is roughly shorn, her scalp being wounded in the process. Later, as Damien treats her, a messenger arrives with news of a formal ceasefire between Britain and the IRA.
After the Anglo-Irish Treaty is signed, the brigade learns that a partitioned Ireland will only be granted Dominion status within the British Empire. As a result, the brigade divides over accepting the terms of the Treaty. Teddy and his allies argue that accepting the Treaty will bring peace now while further gains can be made later. Others oppose the Treaty, proposing to continue fighting until a united Irish Republic can be obtained. Dan and Damien further demand the collectivisation of industry and agriculture.

title: The Prestige
tagline: Are You Watching Closely?
overview: A mysterious story of two magicians whose intense rivalry leads them on a life-long battle for supremacy -- full of obsession, deceit and jealousy with dangerous and deadly consequences.
plot:
Note: Though the movie contains multiple flash-forwards and flash-backs throughout, the story is told here in chronological order.
In 1890s London, Robert Angier, Alfred Borden, and Angier's wife, Julia, work as magician's assistants under the mentorship of John Cutter. During a water tank trick, Julia drowns after Borden, seemingly, incorrectly ties her wrists. Angier blames Borden, and the two men become bitter rivals.
Both men pursue separate careers in magic. Borden, a gifted inventor of illusions, marries a woman named Sarah, with whom he has a daughter named Jess, and hires an enigmatic assistant, Fallon. Angier, whose strength lies more in showmanship, continues working with Cutter and takes on a new assistant, Olivia. The feud escalates as Angier and Borden visit and sabotage each other's acts. Borden loses two fingers after being shot by Angier during a pistol trick, and Borden violently thwarts Angier's bird act in front of a live audience, harming an attendee.
Borden next debuts a spectacular illusion, The Transported Man, in which he appears to teleport from one side of the stage to the other almost instantly. Angier becomes obsessed with discovering the trick's secret and, with Cutter's help, roughly recreates the act using a lookalike named Root, a failed actor. Though Angier's version is successful, he resents remaining hidden beneath the stage while Root takes the applause. Desperate to outdo Borden, he sends Olivia to spy on him. Olivia, however, falls in love with Borden and defects, though she still passes Borden's coded diary to Angier.
After Angier kidnaps Fallon, Borden reveals to Angier that the key word, TESLA, supposedly decrypts the diary and reveals his method. Seeking answers, Angier travels to Colorado Springs to meet the inventor Nikola Tesla. Believing Tesla built a teleportation device for Borden, Angier commissions Tesla to make one. Tesla eventually delivers a working machine but warns that it will bring only misery. When used, the device creates a duplicate of its subject while leaving the original person intact. In London, Angier uses the machine in a new illusion, The Real Transported Man, which earns him acclaim. Sarah, suspicious of Borden's secrecy and affair with Olivia, hangs herself.
Determined to uncover Angier's method, Borden sneaks backstage during a performance of The Real Transported Man and witnesses Angier fall into a water tank and drown. He attempts to open the tank and save Angier, but is arrested for Angier's murder, convicted, and sentenced to death. While awaiting execution, Borden is approached by a solicitor for a wealthy Lord Caldlow, who offers to care for Borden's daughter Jess in exchange for the secret behind the original Transported Man. When Caldlow visits the prison, Borden is horrified to discover that he is actually Angier. Borden passes Angier a note revealing the secret, but Angier tears it up, leaving him to hang.

title: Dreamgirls
tagline: All you have to do is dream.
overview: A trio of female soul singers cross over to the pop charts in the early 1960s, facing their own personal struggles along the way.
plot:
In 1962 Detroit, car salesman Curtis Taylor Jr. meets a Black girl group called "The Dreamettes", consisting of lead singer Effie White and backup singers Deena Jones and Lorrell Robinson, at an R&B amateur talent show at the Detroit Theatre. Presenting himself as their new manager, he hires them as backup singers for Chitlin' Circuit R&B star Jimmy "Thunder" Early. He soon starts his own record label, Rainbow Records, out of his Cadillac dealership, appointing Effie's brother C.C. as head songwriter. When their first single "Cadillac Car" fails after white pop group "Dave and the Sweethearts" releases a cover version, Curtis, C.C., and their producer Wayne turn to payola to make "Jimmy Early & The Dreamettes" mainstream pop stars, beginning with their follow-up single "Steppin' to the Bad Side". Offstage, Effie falls in love with Curtis while the married Jimmy has an affair with Lorrell.
Jimmy's manager, Marty Madison, grows weary of Curtis' plans to make his client more pop-friendly and walks out. When Jimmy fails to connect with an all-white Miami Beach supper club audience, Curtis sends him out on the road alone, keeping The Dreamettes (whom he renames "The Dreams") behind to headline in his place. Feeling that Effie's plus size figure and distinctive, soulful voice will not attract white audiences, he appoints the slimmer, more conventionally attractive Deena as the new lead singer, as Deena's voice, although more basic and generic, is more marketable.
Aided by new songs and a new image, Curtis and C.C. transform The Dreams into a top-selling mainstream pop group. By 1965, however, Effie begins acting out, particularly when Curtis' affections also turn towards Deena. After Effie storms off during a CBS performance, Curtis decides to replace her with his secretary Michelle Morris, beginning with their 1966 New Year's Eve debut in Las Vegas as "Deena Jones & the Dreams". Effie learns she is pregnant with his child, but is fired before she can tell him. Though Effie defiantly and desperately appeals to Curtis, he, C.C., and The Dreams abandon her, forging ahead to stardom.
By 1973, Effie has become an impoverished single mother living on welfare in Detroit with her daughter Magic. To restart her music career, she appoints Marty as her manager and begins performing at a local nightclub. Meanwhile, Deena Jones & the Dreams have become superstars and Rainbow, now headquartered in Los Angeles, has become the biggest pop label in the nation. Curtis, now Deena's husband, pitches a film about Cleopatra to feature her in the title role. However, Deena clandestinely hopes the film will never be greenlit, wanting to pursue other acting gigs.
By 1974, Jimmy has become a drug addict due to Curtis's preoccupation with Deena and his rejection of Jimmy's politically charged charity single "Patience" with C.C. and Lorrell.
