title: Babel
tagline: If You Want to be Understood...Listen
overview: In Babel, a tragic incident involving an American couple in Morocco sparks a chain of events for four families in different countries throughout the world. In the struggle to overcome isolation, fear, and displacement, each character discovers that it is family that ultimately provides solace. In the remote sands of the Moroccan desert, a rifle shot rings out  detonating a chain of events that will link an American tourist couples frantic struggle to survive, two Moroccan boys involved in an accidental crime, a nanny illegally crossing into Mexico with two American children and a Japanese teen rebel whose father is sought by the police in Tokyo. Separated by clashing cultures and sprawling distances, each of these four disparate groups of people are nevertheless hurtling towards a shared destiny of isolation and grief.
plot:
Babel is a 2006 psychological drama directed by Alejandro González Iñárritu and written by Guillermo Arriaga. It completes their "Death Trilogy" after Amores perros (2000) and 21 Grams (2003). The ensemble cast includes Brad Pitt, Cate Blanchett, Gael García Bernal, Kōji Yakusho, Adriana Barraza and Rinko Kikuchi. Four interlinked stories in Morocco, the United States, Mexico and Japan are told out of chronological order.

In the Moroccan desert, a goatherd buys a rifle to protect his flock from jackals and gives it to his young sons, Yussef and Ahmed. Testing its range, Yussef fires at a passing tour bus and seriously wounds Susan, an American tourist traveling with her husband, Richard. The couple are struggling after the death of their infant son. Stranded in a remote village while the other tourists demand to leave, Richard waits desperately for help. The American government calls the shooting terrorism, and Moroccan police hunt down the family. In a shootout, Ahmed is badly hurt, and Yussef surrenders, confessing to the shooting. A helicopter finally takes Susan to a hospital in Casablanca.

In San Diego, the couple's Mexican nanny, Amelia, cannot find anyone to look after their children so she can attend her son's wedding. She takes them with her across the border to a village near Tijuana. On the way back, her drunk nephew Santiago panics at the border checkpoint, speeds off and leaves Amelia and the children in the desert. Amelia goes for help and is arrested by the Border Patrol. The children are found alive, but Amelia, who has been working illegally for years, is deported.

In Tokyo, Chieko, a deaf teenager, is lonely and grieving her mother's suicide, and she seeks attention through provocative sexual behavior. Police come to ask about her father, Yasujiro. The connection is the rifle: he had given it as a gift to his hunting guide in Morocco. Chieko tries to seduce a detective, who gently turns her down, and her father finally comforts her on their balcony.

Babel competed at the 2006 Cannes Film Festival, where González Iñárritu won Best Director. It grossed $135.3 million worldwide on a $25 million budget. It won the Golden Globe for Best Motion Picture – Drama and received seven Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture and supporting actress nominations for Barraza and Kikuchi. Gustavo Santaolalla won the Oscar for Best Original Score. Roger Ebert later added it to his Great Movies list.

title: The Queen
tagline: Our Leaders. Ourselves.
overview: The Queen is an intimate behind the scenes glimpse at the interaction between HM Elizabeth II and Prime Minister Tony Blair during their struggle, following the death of Diana, to reach a compromise between what was a private tragedy for the Royal family and the public's demand for an overt display of mourning.
plot:
The Queen is a 2006 docudrama directed by Stephen Frears and written by Peter Morgan, depicting the aftermath of the death of Diana, Princess of Wales, in 1997. While the royal family treats Diana's death as a private matter, the new prime minister Tony Blair and Prince Charles side with a public demanding an official display of grief. Helen Mirren stars as Queen Elizabeth II and Michael Sheen as Blair, with James Cromwell as Prince Philip, Helen McCrory as Cherie Blair, Alex Jennings as Prince Charles, Sylvia Syms and Roger Allam.

In 1997 Blair and the Labour Party sweep to power promising reform and modernisation, and the Queen wonders whether he intends to modernise the monarchy too. Less than four months later, Diana is killed in a car crash in a Paris tunnel, raising the question of how to honour a future king's mother who is no longer a royal. The Spencer family asks for a private funeral, and the Queen, determined to shield her grieving grandsons, stays on at Balmoral, making no public gesture. When Blair calls Diana the "People's Princess", the phrase is taken up by the press, and the nation's mourning swells into vast floral tributes outside Buckingham and Kensington Palaces.

As the royal family's popularity collapses, Blair's soars. His attempts to steer the Queen are rebuffed as giving in to hysteria, and Philip shares her disdain for the public displays of sympathy, but the private secretaries to both the Queen and Prince Charles quietly encourage Blair to keep trying. Finally he tells the Queen that seventy per cent of the country thinks her conduct is damaging the monarchy and that one in four people favour abolishing it, and urges her to fly a flag at half-mast over Buckingham Palace, pay her respects in person and address the nation. Shaken, she accepts that the country has changed during her reign and returns to London with Philip. Her live televised tribute to Diana helps calm the public mood, and the family attends the funeral at Westminster Abbey. At their next meeting, the Queen reflects with Blair on what has passed and warns him that public opinion may one day turn on him just as abruptly.

The film exceeded expectations at the box office, earning $56.4 million in the United States and Canada on a $15 million budget. Critics acclaimed it, with 97% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 91, and Mirren swept the major acting prizes, winning the Academy Award, BAFTA, Golden Globe and Screen Actors Guild Award for Best Actress.

Rocky Balboa is a 2006 American sports drama film directed by Sylvester Stallone, who also co-wrote and starred in the movie.

Rocky Balboa (Sylvester Stallone) has retired from boxing and is living a quiet life with his wife Adrian (Brenda Blethyn). As Rocky trains Tommy, he begins to see a lot of himself in the young fighter. However, when Tommy becomes disillusioned with his life under Mason's guidance, he turns against Rocky and joins forces with Mason.

Rocky is heartbroken when he discovers that Tommy has betrayed him, but he refuses to give up on his friend. He decides to come out of retirement one last time to fight for the heavyweight championship of the world against Mason Dixon.

The film's plot development revolves around Rocky's journey as he trains for the big fight. Along the way, he faces numerous challenges and setbacks, including a serious injury that leaves him unable to train. Despite this, Rocky perseveres and finds new ways to push himself to his limits.

As the fight approaches, Rocky's determination and spirit inspire those around him, including Tommy, who begins to question his loyalty to Mason. In the end, Rocky faces off against Mason in an intense and emotional battle.

The film's climax features a thrilling boxing match between Rocky and Mason, which ends with Rocky emerging victorious but at great personal cost. The movie concludes with Rocky standing alone in the ring, having given everything he has to prove that he still has what it takes to be a champion.

Throughout the film, Stallone delivers a powerful performance as Rocky Balboa, bringing depth and nuance to the character. The supporting cast, including Brenda Blethyn and Antonio Tarver, also deliver strong performances that add to the film's emotional impact.

Overall, Rocky Balboa is a heartwarming and inspiring film that explores themes of redemption, perseverance, and the power of the human spirit.

title: Ghost Rider
tagline: Hell is about to be unleashed.
overview: In order to save his dying father, young stunt cyclist Johnny Blaze sells his soul to Mephistopheles and sadly parts from the pure-hearted Roxanne Simpson, the love of his life. Years later, Johnny's path crosses again with Roxanne, now a go-getting reporter, and also with Mephistopheles, who offers to release Johnny's soul if Johnny becomes the fabled, fiery 'Ghost Rider'.
plot:
Ghost Rider is a supernatural action film directed by Mark Steven Johnson, released in 2007. The movie is based on the Marvel Comics character of the same name.

The story begins with Johnny Blaze (played by Nicolas Cage), a talented stunt motorcycle rider who makes a deal with the devil, Mephisto (played by Peter Fonda), to save his mentor's life. Unbeknownst to Johnny, this deal comes with a terrible price: his soul will be bound to a hellish contract that forces him to become the Ghost Rider, a supernatural entity with hellfire powers.

As the years pass, Johnny becomes a successful stuntman and motorcycle rider, but he is haunted by the ghost of his mentor, who appears to him as a warning. The ghost tells Johnny that Mephisto's deal has come due, and Johnny must fulfill his end of the bargain. However, when Johnny tries to break free from the contract, Mephisto reveals that he has taken over Johnny's soul, and Johnny is now doomed to become the Ghost Rider.

The Ghost Rider is a supernatural entity with hellfire powers, but also with a human conscience. He is forced to roam the earth, seeking out those who have committed evil deeds, and punishing them by setting their souls on fire. The Ghost Rider's appearance is that of a motorcycle-riding, hellish creature with flames for eyes.

As Johnny struggles to come to terms with his new identity as the Ghost Rider, he meets Roxanne Simpson (played by Eva Mendes), a beautiful and kind-hearted woman who becomes his love interest. However, Mephisto has other plans, and he uses Roxanne's life to lure Johnny into a trap.

The plot thickens when the Ghost Rider discovers that Mephisto is using an ancient artifact to gain control over the world. The Ghost Rider must stop Mephisto and break free from his contract before it's too late. Along the way, he teams up with a group of allies, including a mysterious woman named St. John (played by Sam Elliott) who claims to be able to help him.

The movie culminates in an epic showdown between the Ghost Rider and Mephisto, with the fate of the world hanging in the balance. In the end, Johnny is able to break free from his contract and defeat Mephisto, but not before he sacrifices himself to save Roxanne's soul.

In a surprising twist, it is revealed that St. John was actually a manifestation of Johnny's own subconscious, created by his guilt and regret over his deal with Mephisto. The movie ends with Roxanne finding the Ghost Rider's motorcycle, which has been left behind as a symbol of their love and connection.

Overall, Ghost Rider is an action-packed supernatural thriller that explores themes of redemption, sacrifice, and the power of love. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the movie has developed a cult following over the years, and its unique blend of horror and action has made it a fan favorite among comic book enthusiasts.

title: Letters from Iwo Jima
tagline: The battle of Iwo Jima seen through the eyes of the Japanese soldiers.
overview: The story of the battle of Iwo Jima between the United States and Imperial Japan during World War II, as told from the perspective of the Japanese who fought it.
plot:
Letters from Iwo Jima is a 2006 American war film in Japanese, directed and co-produced by Clint Eastwood and starring Ken Watanabe and Kazunari Ninomiya. It depicts the Battle of Iwo Jima from the Japanese side and serves as a companion to Eastwood's Flags of Our Fathers, which shows the same battle from the American viewpoint; the two were shot back to back.

In 2005, archaeologists on Iwo Jima dig up something buried. In 1944, Private First Class Saigo, a conscripted baker who longs for his family, is digging beach trenches when Lieutenant General Tadamichi Kuribayashi takes command of the garrison. Kuribayashi spares Saigo a beating for unpatriotic remarks and orders a network of tunnels and mountain bunkers, a strategy that he and Lieutenant Colonel Baron Nishi, an Olympic champion equestrian, defend against other officers. Dysentery spreads, and Saigo suspects a new arrival, Shimizu, of being a military police spy.

After days of bombardment, U.S. Marines land and assault Mount Suribachi. Ordered by his colonel to commit suicide rather than retreat, Saigo persuades Shimizu to flee with him, and Lieutenant Ito nearly executes them for cowardice until Kuribayashi confirms that he ordered the retreat. Ito leads a failed attack against orders and, rebuked by Nishi, sets off with land mines intending to throw himself under an American tank. Nishi reads aloud a letter found on a dying Marine, and later, blinded by shrapnel, orders a withdrawal and kills himself. Shimizu surrenders but is executed by his captors. Kuribayashi orders Saigo to stay behind and destroy documents, saving his life for a third time, then leads a final night attack in which he is gravely wounded. Ito, who never carried out his mission, is captured. When his aide is shot, Kuribayashi asks Saigo to bury him where he cannot be found and shoots himself with a pistol given to him in the United States before the war. When Saigo sees a Marine carrying that pistol he attacks, but is subdued and taken to the beach with the wounded. In the present, the archaeologists open the bag of letters Saigo had buried, and the soldiers' voices are heard.

Filmed mainly in California and Iceland, it opened in Japan on December 9, 2006, and in the United States on December 20 through Warner Bros. It was acclaimed, scoring 91% on Rotten Tomatoes and 89 on Metacritic, grossed $68.7 million on a $19 million budget, and earned four Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture, winning Best Sound Editing.

title: Notes on a Scandal
tagline: One woman's secret is another woman's power. One woman's fear is another woman's weapon. One woman's life is in another woman's hands....
overview: A veteran high school teacher befriends a younger art teacher, who is having an affair with one of her 15-year-old students. However, her intentions with this new "friend" also go well beyond platonic friendship.
plot:
Barbara Covett is a history teacher at a comprehensive school in London. She is unpopular with the students and her fellow teachers, for whom she has contempt. Having never married and nearing retirement, her only comfort is her diary. When a new art teacher, Sheba Hart, joins the staff, Barbara is immediately attracted to her and they strike up a friendship. In Barbara, this friendship quickly turns into infatuation and obsession. Sheba is married to the much older Richard, and is just re-entering the work force after devoting herself to her special needs son.
Barbara later witnesses Sheba in a sexual encounter with a 15-year-old student named Steven Connolly at the school. When Barbara confronts her, Sheba recounts all the details of her involvement with the boy, but asks Barbara not to tell the school administration until after Christmas, as she wants to be with her family. Barbara claims she has no intention of reporting her, providing Sheba ends the relationship immediately, but Barbara secretly plans to use the affair as a means of manipulating Sheba. Over the Christmas break, Barbara visits her sister, who asks her about another young teacher Barbara befriended. Barbara stiffly says that the young teacher moved away. Barbara's sister asks if she has any other female "friends", strongly implying Barbara is a lesbian; Barbara insists she has no idea what her sister is talking about.

title: Bridge to Terabithia
tagline: Close your eyes, but keep your mind wide open.
overview: Jesse Aarons trained all summer to become the fastest runner in school, so he's very upset when newcomer Leslie Burke outruns him and everyone else. Despite this and other differences, including that she's rich, he's poor, and she's a city girl, he's a country boy, the two become fast friends. Together, they create Terabithia, a land of monsters, trolls, ogres, and giants and rule as king and queen.
plot:
Bridge to Terabithia is a heart-wrenching drama film released in 2007, directed by Gábor Csupó and produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie is based on the novel of the same name by Katherine Paterson.

The story revolves around two young friends, Jesse Oliver Aarons (played by Josh Hutcherson) and Leslie Burke (played by AnnaSophia Robb), who live in rural Virginia. Jesse is an 11-year-old boy who loves to draw and paint, while Leslie is a new student in his class who has recently moved to the area with her family.

Initially, Jesse is hesitant to befriend Leslie due to his fear of rejection and his desire to fit in with his peers. However, after they meet on the first day of school, they quickly form an unlikely friendship. They discover that they share a love for fantasy and imagination, which leads them to create their own magical kingdom called Terabithia.

Terabithia is a fantastical world built by Jesse and Leslie in the woods near their homes. It's a place where they can escape the troubles of their everyday lives and be themselves without fear of judgment. The kingdom is filled with imagination, creativity, and adventure, and it becomes a sanctuary for both Jesse and Leslie.

As the story progresses, we see Jesse and Leslie grow closer, sharing their deepest secrets and fears with each other. They find comfort in each other's company, and their friendship deepens. However, their happiness is short-lived, as tragedy strikes when Leslie dies in an accident while they are playing in Terabithia.

The film takes a poignant turn as Jesse struggles to cope with the loss of his dear friend. He becomes withdrawn and isolated, unable to paint or create anything without feeling Leslie's presence. The movie shows how grief can be overwhelming, and how it can affect even the strongest relationships.

In the end, Jesse finds a way to honor Leslie's memory by creating a bridge in Terabithia, symbolizing the connection between their two worlds. The film concludes with Jesse standing on the bridge, looking out at the woods where he and Leslie shared so many adventures together.

Bridge to Terabithia is a powerful and emotional film that explores themes of friendship, loss, and the importance of imagination in our lives. The movie features outstanding performances from Josh Hutcherson and AnnaSophia Robb, who bring depth and nuance to their characters. The film's cinematography and score are also noteworthy, capturing the beauty and wonder of Terabithia.

Overall, Bridge to Terabithia is a heart-wrenching drama that will leave audiences moved and contemplative long after the credits roll.

title: Street Kings
tagline: Their city. Their rules. No prisoners.
overview: Tom Ludlow is a disillusioned L.A. Police Officer, rarely playing by the rules and haunted by the death of his wife. When evidence implicates him in the execution of a fellow officer, he is forced to go up against the cop culture he's been a part of his entire career, ultimately leading him to question the loyalties of everyone around him.
plot:
Thomas "Tom" Ludlow, an alcoholic undercover detective for the LAPD's Vice-Special unit, arranges an arms deal with Korean gangsters suspected of kidnapping two teenage girls. He provokes the gangsters into beating him and stealing his car, allowing him to track them to the gang's hideout. Ludlow storms the hideout and kills the gangsters, staging the scene to make the shootings appear justified, and rescues the captive girls.
While Captain Jack Wander and the rest of his unit congratulate him, Ludlow is confronted by his former partner, Terrence Washington, who disapproves of the unit's corrupt tactics. Ludlow is later approached by Captain James Biggs of Internal Affairs. Wander warns that Washington has reported Ludlow to Biggs.
Ludlow follows Washington to a convenience store, where they are ambushed by two gunmen under the pretense of a robbery. Accidentally shot when Ludlow returns fire, Washington is killed by the gunmen. The clerk is killed as well. Wander advises Ludlow to remove the surveillance footage, telling the press Ludlow was first on the scene but too late to save Washington. Temporarily reassigned to fielding civilian complaints, Ludlow enlists the cooperation of investigator Paul Diskant, determined to find the killers himself. Washington is implicated in stealing drugs from the evidence room and selling them to the gunmen, identified as criminals Fremont and Coates.
Joined by a reluctant Diskant, Ludlow brutalizes informants until local drug dealer Scribble leads them to the bodies of the real Fremont and Coates in a shallow grave, killed long before Washington. Giving the surveillance footage to Washington's widow, Linda, Ludlow reveals that he lost his own wife recently and vows to avenge Washington.
Ludlow and Diskant pose as dirty cops, forcing Scribble to arrange a meeting with the killers masquerading as Fremont and Coates. Diskant recognizes them, but he and Scribble are killed in the ensuing gunfight. Ludlow kills both assailants, but sees on the news that they were Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department deputies.
Declared a "cop killer", Ludlow is arrested by fellow detectives Santos and Demille, who admit to killing the real Fremont and Coates and planting evidence to frame them for Washington's murder. He realizes that Washington was actually informing on Wander, who is the one behind the evidence room theft. Before Santos and Demille can execute him, Ludlow manages to break free and kill both of them. He saves Linda from Sergeant Mike Clady, sent by Wander to recover the surveillance footage and kill her, subduing him and locking him in his trunk.
Ludlow confronts Wander at home, handcuffing him after a brawl. Wander confesses that he has incriminating evidence against high-ranking officials to use to become LAPD chief and, eventually, mayor.

title: Meet the Robinsons
tagline: Think your family's weird?
overview: Lewis, a brilliant young inventor, is keen on creating a time machine to find his mother, who abandoned him in an orphanage. Things take a turn when he meets Wilbur Robinson and his family.
plot:
Meet the Robinsons is a 2007 American animated science fiction comedy film produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie follows the story of Lewis, an orphan boy who dreams of becoming a great inventor.

The film begins with Lewis, a shy and awkward 12-year-old boy, living in an orphanage. He spends most of his time daydreaming about inventing incredible gadgets and machines that will change the world. However, his life takes a dramatic turn when he meets Wilbur, a mysterious and eccentric old man who claims to be his long-lost father.

Wilbur reveals to Lewis that he is actually the son of a brilliant inventor named Cornelius Robinson, who created a time machine called the "Time Machine 3000." The Time Machine 3000 allows its user to travel through time, but it also has a mind of its own and can be unpredictable. Wilbur warns Lewis that his father's inventions have been stolen by a rival inventor named Bowler Hat Guy, who is using them for evil purposes.

Lewis decides to embark on a journey with Wilbur to find Cornelius Robinson and retrieve the stolen inventions. Along the way, they meet a cast of eccentric characters, including Wilbur's wife, Mrs. Robinson, and their son, Lewis Jr., who becomes Lewis's rival in inventing.

As they travel through time, Lewis and his companions encounter various historical figures, including Leonardo da Vinci, Benjamin Franklin, and Albert Einstein. However, Bowler Hat Guy is always one step ahead, using the stolen inventions to alter historical events for his own gain.

The plot thickens as Lewis and his friends discover that Bowler Hat Guy's ultimate plan is to steal Cornelius Robinson's most prized invention: a machine that can create an army of robotic clones. The movie builds up to a thrilling climax as Lewis and his companions must stop Bowler Hat Guy and his minions from carrying out their evil plan.

In the end, Lewis and his friends succeed in defeating Bowler Hat Guy and restoring the timeline to its original course. Along the way, Lewis learns valuable lessons about perseverance, teamwork, and believing in himself. The movie ends with Lewis returning to the present, where he is reunited with Wilbur and becomes a confident inventor in his own right.

Throughout the film, the animation is vibrant and colorful, with a unique blend of steampunk and sci-fi elements. The characters are well-developed and quirky, adding to the movie's humor and charm. Meet the Robinsons is a heartwarming and entertaining film that celebrates the power of imagination and creativity.

title: Mr. Bean's Holiday
tagline: Disaster is just a small step away.
overview: Mr. Bean wins a trip to Cannes where he unwittingly separates a young boy from his father and must help the two reunite. On the way he discovers France, bicycling and true love, among other things.
plot:
Mr. Bean's Holiday is a 2007 comedy film directed by Steve Bendelack and produced by Universal Pictures. The movie marks the fourth installment in the Mr. Bean series, following Bean (1997) and Mr. Bean's Diner (2002), which was initially intended to be a television special but was later expanded into a feature film.

The story begins with Mr. Bean (played by Rowan Atkinson), a bumbling and eccentric British gentleman, who is on his way to Paris for a vacation. However, he soon discovers that the flight has been cancelled due to bad weather, leaving him stranded in Nice, France.

In an attempt to find a new flight to London, Mr. Bean decides to embark on a road trip across Europe with his trusty companion, Teddy (a small stuffed teddy bear). Along the way, they encounter various misadventures and cultural differences that lead to comedic misunderstandings.

As they travel through France, Italy, Austria, and Germany, Mr. Bean becomes fascinated by the idea of making it to the famous film festival in Cannes, where he hopes to meet his idol, a French actress named Fanny (played by Emma de Caunes). Believing that attending the festival will bring him fame and fortune, Mr. Bean sets out on a series of misadventures to get there.

Throughout their journey, Mr. Bean's antics cause chaos and confusion wherever they go. He gets into a series of humorous misadventures, including accidentally joining a group of Italian tourists, getting caught up in a wild goose chase through the streets of Nice, and even inadvertently causing a scene at a German beer festival.

Despite the many mishaps, Mr. Bean's determination to reach Cannes never wavers, and he eventually makes it to the film festival, where he meets Fanny and wins her heart. The movie ends with Mr. Bean returning home to London, but not before sharing a romantic moment with Fanny on the plane ride back.

Throughout the film, Rowan Atkinson's physical comedy and facial expressions provide much of the humor, as well as his ability to convey emotions without speaking. The supporting cast, including Emma de Caunes and Max Baldry, add to the comedic mayhem, making Mr. Bean's Holiday a delightful and entertaining ride for audiences.

Overall, Mr. Bean's Holiday is a lighthearted and entertaining film that showcases the beloved character's signature blend of physical comedy and wit. With its colorful European landscapes and hilarious misadventures, it's a must-see for fans of the series and comedy enthusiasts alike.

tagline: Spartans, prepare for glory!
overview: Based on Frank Miller's graphic novel, "300" is very loosely based the 480 B.C. Battle of Thermopylae, where the King of Sparta led his army against the advancing Persians; the battle is said to have inspired all of Greece to band together against the Persians, and helped usher in the world's first democracy.
plot:
In the year 480 BCE, during the Persian Empire's invasion of Greece, King Leonidas of Sparta is faced with an impossible decision: defend his city-state against the invading forces or flee and save his people.

The film opens with a prologue that sets the stage for the story. The Spartans are preparing to face the invading army, led by King Xerxes I (Rodrigo Santoro). Leonidas (Gerard Butler) is chosen to lead a small contingent of 300 Spartans against the Persian army, which is estimated to be in the hundreds of thousands.

As the battle begins, the Spartans hold their ground against the seemingly endless horde of Persians. The film's iconic "This is Sparta!" speech by King Leonidas sets the tone for the rest of the battle. Despite being vastly outnumbered, the Spartans fight with bravery and honor, using their phalanx formation to devastating effect.

Meanwhile, Queen Gorgo (Lena Headey), Leonidas' wife, tries to persuade him to reconsider his decision to lead the 300 against the Persians. She is worried about the fate of her husband and the future of Sparta.

As the battle rages on, the Spartans begin to tire. Many are killed or wounded, including several high-ranking officers. However, Leonidas remains steadfast, refusing to yield even when faced with the prospect of defeat.

The turning point of the film comes when a group of Persian warriors, led by King Xerxes' son, Xerxes II (Toby Kebbell), infiltrate the Spartan lines and kill several key officers. This allows the Persians to gain the upper hand, and it seems that all is lost for the Spartans.

However, in a stunning display of bravery and sacrifice, the 300 Spartans launch a final, desperate attack against the Persians. The film's climax features an intense and bloody battle, with the Spartans fighting valiantly against overwhelming odds.

In the end, the Spartans emerge victorious, but at great cost. King Leonidas is killed in action, and many of his men are either killed or taken prisoner. The film ends with a somber tone, as Queen Gorgo mourns the loss of her husband and the future of Sparta hangs in the balance.

Throughout the film, director Zack Snyder's use of innovative camera techniques and stunning visuals brings the epic battle to life. The film's score, composed by Tyler Bates, adds to the sense of tension and drama, perfectly capturing the mood of the film.

Overall, 300 is a gripping and intense film that explores themes of honor, duty, and sacrifice. Despite its historical inaccuracies, the film remains an exciting and visually stunning adaptation of Frank Miller's graphic novel.

title: The Dreamers
tagline: Together nothing is impossible. Together nothing is forbidden.
overview: When Isabelle and Theo invite Matthew to stay with them, what begins as a casual friendship ripens into a sensual voyage of discovery and desire in which nothing is off limits and everything is possible.
plot:
In 1968, Matthew is a shy American exchange student who has come to Paris for a year to study French. While at the Cinémathèque Française protesting the firing of its director, Henri Langlois, he meets free-spirited twins Théo and Isabelle, the children of a famous French poet and his English wife. The three bond over a shared love of film. After dinner with their parents, Théo and Isabelle invite Matthew to stay with them while their parents leave town for a month. Matthew accepts, considering them his first French friends.
Matthew becomes suspicious of Théo and Isabelle's relationship after seeing them sleeping nude together; he soon discovers that they have a liberal attitude towards nudity and sexuality. Matthew gradually accepts the twins' unusual relationship and comes to enjoy his time living with them. The three re-enact a memorable scene from Bande à part by "breaking the world record for running through the Louvre", and Matthew and Théo engage in playful arguments about Charlie Chaplin and Buster Keaton, Eric Clapton and Jimi Hendrix, as well as the subject of Maoism, which Théo fervently believes in.
After Théo loses at a trivia game, Isabelle sentences him to masturbate to a Marlene Dietrich poster in front of them. After Matthew loses at another game, Théo tells him to have sex with Isabelle in front of him, which Matthew reluctantly does. Afterwards, he realises she was a virgin, and Théo is pleased. As Matthew and Isabelle fall in love with each other, he asks her what she would do if her parents discovered the nature of her relationship with Théo; she replies that she would kill herself.
Matthew begins to pursue a relationship with Isabelle, separate from Théo. Matthew and Isabelle leave the apartment and go on a regular date, which she has never experienced before. Théo retaliates by inviting a companion up to his room, upsetting Isabelle. She distances herself from both Théo and Matthew, only to find them next to each other on Théo's bed when an argument between the two turns erotic. She then surprises them with a makeshift bedsheet fort and the three fall asleep in each other's arms.
The next morning, Théo and Isabelle's parents arrive home and find the sleeping trio naked in bed together. They are startled by what they find, but let them be, departing after leaving a cheque. Isabelle wakes up and discovers the cheque, realising that their parents have found them out. Wordlessly, she attaches a hose to the gas outlet and lies back down with the still-asleep Théo and Matthew, attempting to commit murder–suicide. Shortly afterwards, however, they are awakened by a brick being hurled through the window; they discover hundreds of students rioting in the streets.
All three of them are overjoyed and proceed to join the protesters. Théo then joins a small team of protesters preparing Molotov cocktails. Matthew tries to stop Théo by kissing him and Isabelle, arguing against violence, but he is shunned by both siblings.

title: American Psycho
tagline: I think my mask of sanity is about to slip.
overview: A wealthy New York investment banking executive hides his alternate psychopathic ego from his co-workers and friends as he escalates deeper into his illogical, gratuitous fantasies.
plot:
In 1987, New York City investment banker Patrick Bateman meticulously maintains a polished social façade while harboring violent impulses. He dines at trendy restaurants, obsesses over his physical appearance, and navigates a shallow circle of wealthy associates he secretly despises, all while engaged to Evelyn Williams. During a business meeting, he and his colleagues flaunt their business cards respective designs. Bateman is enraged by the perceived superiority of his colleague Paul Allen's card. Later, he encounters a homeless man and his dog in an alley; initially offering help, Bateman instead insults and brutally kills them.
Bateman's envy intensifies over Allen's more affluent successful lifestyle, able to easily secure reservations at Dorsia, an elite restaurant Bateman cannot access. At a Christmas party, he arranges dinner with Allen, who mistakes him for another co-worker, Marcus Halberstram. During the dinner, Allen's condescending attitude fuels Bateman's resentment. Bateman gets him drunk, lures him to his apartment, and murders him with an axe. He disposes of the body and uses Allen's keys to access his apartment, leaving a message on Allen's answering machine claiming he has gone to London. When private investigator Donald Kimball questions Bateman about Allen's disappearance, mentioning sightings of Allen in London, Bateman deflects suspicion.
Bateman hires prostitutes Christie and Sabrina, engaging in sadistic acts before paying them to leave. His violence nearly arouses colleague Luis Carruthers when he attempts to strangle him in a restaurant restroom, but Carruthers misinterprets the act as a sexual advance, horrifying Bateman, who flees. Kimball's second interview heightens Bateman's paranoia, but he continues his spree, seducing a model and later toying with killing his secretary, Jean. At his apartment, Jean narrowly escapes harm after Bateman warns her that he might lose control, unaware of the model's severed head in his refrigerator.
Kimball later informs Bateman that a colleague claims to have dined with Allen on the night of his disappearance, solidifying Bateman's alibi. Kimball dismisses the idea of Allen's murder as implausible, leaving Bateman relieved yet unnerved. Bateman rehires Christie and invites acquaintance Elizabeth for a drug-fueled encounter that turns deadly. Christie discovers corpses in his apartment while fleeing, only to be killed when Bateman drops a chainsaw on her in a stairwell.
Bateman unravels after breaking off his engagement with Evelyn. An ATM bizarrely displays "Feed me a stray cat", prompting him to nearly kill the kitten that had appeared, but he shoots a woman who intervenes instead. Fleeing from police, he shoots an officer, inexplicably blows up a patrol car, and kills more innocents before hiding in his office building. In a frantic voicemail to his lawyer, Harold Carnes, Bateman confesses to around 40 murders, including Allen, Christie, Elizabeth, and others.

title: Sex and Lucía
overview: Various lives converge on an isolated island, all connected by an author whose novel has become inextricably entwined with his own life.
plot:
Sex and Lucía (Lucía y el sexo) is a 2001 Spanish drama written and directed by Julio Medem. Paz Vega and Tristán Ulloa lead a cast that also includes Najwa Nimri, Daniel Freire, Javier Cámara, Silvia Llanos and Elena Anaya.

Lucía, a waitress, is on the phone with her boyfriend Lorenzo, a novelist sunk in a long depression, after a bitter fight. Worried, she returns home to find the apartment empty and a suicide note. When the police call, she hangs up in dread, ignores their second call, packs a bag and flees to the Balearic island Lorenzo used to talk about.

The story then moves back in time. Six years earlier, on a moonlit night, Lorenzo has a fleeting sexual encounter in the sea with Elena, a woman he has just met. She later finds she is pregnant but cannot trace him. Some time after, while Lorenzo is struggling with writer's block, Lucía approaches him in a restaurant and confesses that since reading his latest book she has followed him and fallen in love. She soon moves in with him, and the film begins to blend their life with scenes from the novel he is writing.

Lorenzo eventually learns he has a daughter, Luna, and starts watching her outside her school, where he meets her babysitter Belén. Her provocative talk feeds his fiction, which Lucía reads as pure invention. One night Belén invites him to Elena's house. While the two are having sex, Luna is killed by the family's Rottweiler. Grief-stricken, Lorenzo falls into despair, his writing turns towards death, and he anonymously sends Elena, now running an inn on the island, a consoling story about a child who loves the sea. His guilt slowly breaks down his relationship with Lucía.

In the present, Lucía befriends a diver named Carlos and then Elena, and the two women gradually realize what links them. Meanwhile, Lorenzo recovers in hospital after an "accident". When his editor says Lucía probably believes he is dead, Lorenzo guesses where she has gone and travels to the island, where the three finally face what connects them.

Sogecine produced the film, shooting in Fuerteventura and Madrid. The lighthouse at Cap de Barbaria on Formentera became a central image. Critics were generally favorable: Rotten Tomatoes' consensus said that beneath its gratuitous nudity lies a complex and visually striking film.

title: Blood Diamond
tagline: It will cost you everything.
overview: An ex-mercenary turned smuggler. A Mende fisherman. Amid the explosive civil war overtaking 1999 Sierra Leone, these men join for two desperate missions: recovering a rare pink diamond of immense value and rescuing the fisherman's son, conscripted as a child soldier into the brutal rebel forces ripping a swath of torture and bloodshed countrywide.
plot:
In 1999, Sierra Leone is ravaged by civil war. The Revolutionary United Front terrorizes the countryside and enslaves many locals to harvest diamonds, which fund their increasingly successful war effort. Solomon Vandy, a Mende fisherman from Shenge, is separated from his family and assigned to a workforce overseen by Captain Poison, a ruthless warlord.
While mining a river, Vandy discovers an enormous pink diamond. Captain Poison tries to take the stone, but the area is suddenly raided by government troops. Vandy buries the stone before being captured. Vandy and Poison are incarcerated in Freetown with Danny Archer, a white Rhodesian gunrunner and Angola War veteran jailed for trying to smuggle diamonds into Liberia. The diamonds were intended for Rudolph van de Kaap, a corrupt Afrikaner mining executive from South Africa.
Hearing of the pink diamond in prison, Archer arranges for him and Vandy to be freed. He travels to Cape Town to meet his employer: Colonel Coetzee, an Afrikaner formerly with the apartheid-era South African Defence Force (whom Archer also served under in the 32 Battalion), which now commands a private military company. Archer wants the diamond so he can sell it to Van de Kaap and retire, but Coetzee wants it as compensation for Archer's botched smuggling mission. Archer returns to Sierra Leone, locates Vandy, and offers to help him find his family if he will help recover the diamond.
The RUF conquers Freetown, while Vandy's son Dia is captured to serve as a child soldier under a liberated Captain Poison. Archer and Vandy narrowly escape to Lungi, where they plan to reach Kono with the help of an American journalist, Maddy Bowen, in exchange for Archer providing evidence of the illicit diamond trade. Maddy helps Vandy locate his remaining family at a refugee camp in Guinea. While they travel, Archer reveals to Maddy that his parents were brutally killed by Black rebels after the fall of Rhodesia (now Zimbabwe). As a child, he fled to South Africa, where he eventually joined the military and served in Angola. Eventually, the trio arrive in Kono after a harrowing journey, where Coetzee and his private army—contracted by the Sierra Leone government—prepares to repulse the rebel offensive.
While Maddy gets out with her story, the two men set out for Captain Poison's encampment. Dia, stationed with the RUF garrison there, is confronted by Vandy, but having been brainwashed he refuses to acknowledge his father. Archer radios the site's coordinates to Coetzee, who directs a combined air and ground assault on the camp. Vandy finds Captain Poison and beats him to death with a shovel as the mercenaries overwhelm the RUF defenders.
Coetzee then forces Vandy to produce the diamond, but is killed by Archer, who realizes Coetzee would eventually kill them both. Dia briefly holds the pair at gunpoint, but Vandy confronts him again and renews their familial bond.

title: Rocky IV
tagline: Get ready for the next world war.
overview: Rocky Balboa proudly holds the world heavyweight boxing championship, but a new challenger has stepped forward: Drago, a six-foot-four, 261-pound fighter who has the backing of the Soviet Union.
plot:
Rocky IV is a 1985 American sports drama film directed by Sylvester Stallone and starring Sylvester Stallone, Talia Shire, Carl Weathers, and Dolph Lundgren. The film is the fourth installment in the Rocky franchise.

The movie begins with Rocky Balboa (Sylvester Stallone) training for his upcoming fight against Ivan Drago (Dolph Lundgren), a formidable Soviet boxer who has been dominating the ring since he was a child. As Rocky prepares for the big match, he also deals with personal struggles, including the death of his friend and trainer, Mickey Goldmill's (Burgess Meredith) brother, Paulie.

Meanwhile, Ivan Drago is introduced as a ruthless and efficient fighter who is trained by the Soviet Union to crush American spirit and pride. The two fighters engage in a heated rivalry, with Rocky determined to defeat Drago and prove that he is still a force to be reckoned with in the ring.

As the fight approaches, Rocky's wife Adrian (Talia Shire) becomes increasingly concerned about his safety, while Rocky's friend Apollo Creed's (Carl Weathers) widow, Brigitte (Brigitte Nielsen), tries to persuade Rocky to retire from boxing. However, Rocky is determined to face Drago and prove that he can overcome any obstacle.

The film takes a dramatic turn when Ivan Drago kills Apollo Creed in the ring during their fight, which sparks outrage across America. Rocky sees this as an opportunity to avenge his friend's death and defeat Drago in the ring.

The climactic final fight between Rocky and Drago is intense and brutal, with both fighters giving it their all. In the end, Rocky emerges victorious, but not without suffering severe injuries. The film ends with Rocky standing over Drago's defeated body, having avenged Apollo Creed's death and proved that he still has what it takes to be a champion.

Throughout the film, Sylvester Stallone delivers a powerful performance as Rocky Balboa, bringing depth and nuance to the character. Dolph Lundgren is equally impressive as Ivan Drago, conveying the Soviet boxer's ruthless efficiency and determination. The film's themes of patriotism, loyalty, and redemption are timeless and continue to resonate with audiences today.

Overall, Rocky IV is a classic sports drama that delivers on its promise of high-octane action and emotional depth. With its iconic performances, memorable characters, and thrilling plot twists, it remains one of the most beloved films in the Rocky franchise.

title: Stalker
tagline: There's no need to speak. You must only...concentrate and recall all your past life. When a man thinks of the past, he becomes kinder.
overview: Near a gray and unnamed city is the Zone, a place guarded by barbed wire and soldiers, and where the normal laws of physics are victim to frequent anomalies. A stalker guides two men into the Zone, specifically to an area in which deep-seated desires are granted.
plot:
"The Zone" is a huge tract of open land where the normal laws of physics supposedly do not apply, containing supernatural hazards. At the heart of the Zone lies a "Room" that is said to grant the wishes of anyone who steps inside. The government has fenced off the Zone, subjecting "Stalkers", people who illegally guide others through the Zone, to harsh prison time if caught crossing the border.
One Stalker has just returned from a long prison sentence to his wife and daughter. To his wife's horror, a disaffected writer and a physics professor immediately hire the Stalker to take them through the Zone. Needing the money, he meets the Writer and Professor in a rundown bar-café, warning them that they must do what he says to survive the dangers that lie ahead. He explains that the Zone is a living thing that visitors must respect.
The trio evades the Zone's military guards by following a train through the gate, riding through the Zone's vast wilderness on a railway work car. The Zone contains such human remnants as old abandoned industrial facilities, corpses, guns, and tanks. The Stalker cautiously tests for anomalies as they painstakingly make their way toward the Room, though nothing unusual occurs.
The three men discuss their reasons for wanting to visit the Room as they travel: the Writer fears losing his inspiration, the calm Professor hopes to analyze the Zone in order to win a Nobel Prize, and the Stalker insists he has no motive beyond the altruistic aim of aiding the desperate to their desires. He mentions that his mentor, another Stalker named "Porcupine", obtained great riches by entering the Room but then hanged himself when he returned home.
The trio draw lots to determine that the Writer will go first through an especially long, dark, ominous passageway that the Stalker calls the "meat grinder". Nervously, the Writer passes through without harm, shocking the Stalker, who reveals that the meat grinder kills anyone the Zone deems morally unworthy. The Writer forges ahead and delivers a soliloquy directly to camera about the futility of knowledge and feeling overwhelmed and criticized by other people. He returns to the others, and the Stalker reveals that Porcupine sent a brother ahead of him into the meat grinder, where the brother was killed. The Stalker then recites a poem about never being satisfied, and the Writer rages at the Stalker for assuming he was morally unworthy.
Suddenly, a phone in the antechamber rings. The surprised Professor uses it to call an old enemy scientist, gloating about finding a bomb the scientist had hidden, which the Professor previously worked on. As the trio prepare to enter the Room, the Professor reveals he has brought the 20-kiloton bomb in his backpack to destroy the Room and therefore prevent evil men from abusing it for gain. He blames the Room, the Stalkers, and their clients for the recent rise of crime, political strife, and destructive science.

title: The Pursuit of Happyness
tagline: For his son, one man will reach for the impossible.
overview: A struggling salesman takes custody of his son as he's poised to begin a life-changing professional career.
plot:
The Pursuit of Happyness is a biographical drama film directed by Gabriele Muccino, released in 2006 by Columbia Pictures. The movie is based on the true story of Chris Gardner, a struggling single father who becomes homeless with his young son.

The film begins with Chris Gardner (played by Will Smith), a determined and ambitious stockbroker who has just lost his job due to the financial crisis. Despite having no income, Chris decides to move to San Francisco with his 5-year-old son Christopher (played by Jaden Smith) in order to pursue a career in finance.

Initially, Chris faces numerous challenges as he struggles to find a new job and make ends meet. He is forced to sleep on the streets, often sharing a bench or a park bench with other homeless people. Despite his hardships, Chris remains optimistic and determined to provide a better life for himself and his son.

As Chris navigates the harsh realities of homelessness, he also faces personal struggles as a single father. His relationship with Christopher is put to the test as they face poverty, hunger, and uncertainty about their future. However, Chris's love and dedication to his son keep him going, and he finds ways to make ends meet by selling blood plasma and applying for jobs.

Meanwhile, Chris meets a social worker named Dr. Seuss (played by Thandie Newton), who helps him navigate the system and find temporary housing. He also befriends a homeless man named John (played by Brian Howe), who becomes a source of inspiration and support for Chris.

As the story unfolds, Chris's determination and perseverance begin to pay off. He lands an internship at a prestigious brokerage firm, Dean Witter Reynolds, where he meets a mentor named Jim (played by Jon Voight). With Jim's guidance, Chris is able to secure a full-time job offer and eventually becomes a successful stockbroker.

The film's climax features Chris's emotional reunion with Christopher, who has been struggling to cope with his father's absence. The two share a heartwarming moment as they finally find stability and security together.

Throughout the movie, Will Smith delivers a powerful performance that showcases his range as an actor. His portrayal of Chris Gardner is both nuanced and authentic, capturing the complexity and vulnerability of a man who has faced unimaginable hardship.

The Pursuit of Happyness is a testament to the human spirit's capacity for resilience and determination. The film's themes of hope, perseverance, and the importance of family are timeless and universal, making it a must-see for audiences worldwide.

title: La Vie en Rose
tagline: The Extraordinary Story of Edith Piaf.
overview: From the mean streets of the Belleville district of Paris to the dazzling limelight of New York's most famous concert halls, Edith Piaf's life was a constant battle to sing and survive, to live and love. Raised in her grandmother's brothel, Piaf was discovered in 1935 by nightclub owner Louis Leplee, who persuaded her to sing despite her extreme nervousness. Piaf became one of France's immortal icons, her voice one of the indelible signatures of the 20th century.
plot:
The film is structured as a largely non-linear series of key events from the life of Édith Piaf. The film begins with elements from her childhood, and at the end with the events prior to and surrounding her death, poignantly juxtaposed by a performance of her song, "Non, je ne regrette rien" (No, I do not Regret Anything).
Beginning in 1918, young Édith suffers a chaotic childhood and is eventually sent to live with her paternal-grandmother, who runs a brothel in Normandy. Édith witnesses the brutal business of prostitution. When she suffers an episode of keratitis-induced blindness, a kind-hearted sex worker named Titine tenderly cares for Édith.
Édith's World War I veteran father collects her to accompany him while he works as a circus acrobat. One night, Édith sees a vision of St Thérèse in a fire eater's flames. St Thérèse says she will always be with Édith—a belief that she carries for the rest of her life. When Édith is nine years old, her father leaves the circus and performs on the streets of Paris. During a lackluster performance, a passerby asks if Édith is part of the show. She spontaneously sings "La Marseillaise" with raw emotion, mesmerizing the street crowd.
Years later, nightclub owner Louis Leplée hires Édith to sing at his club and gives her the stage surname of Piaf, a colloquialism for sparrow that is inspired by her diminutive height of only 1.47m (4 ft 8in). However, Leplée is soon shot dead and the police suspect it is due to Édith's connections to the mafia. When she next attempts a show at a cabaret, she is jeered off the stage by a hostile crowd. Things go from bad to worse when her best friend, Mômone, is forcibly taken to a convent. Desperate, Édith turns to Raymond Asso, a songwriter and accompanist. Through harsh means, he enlivens her stage presence with hand gestures, better enunciation, and other lessons.
Édith's career progresses and she achieves fame. While performing in New York City, Édith meets Marcel Cerdan, a fellow French national and a middleweight boxer competing for the World Champion title. Despite him being married, Édith believes she is falling in love with Marcel. An affair ensues and, while it is supposedly a secret, "La Vie En Rose" is played for Marcel wherever he goes. Édith persuades Marcel to fly from Paris to join her in New York, and he wakes her up in her bedroom with a kiss. She goes to get coffee and is informed by her entourage that Marcel was killed when his plane crashed. Édith hysterically searches for his ghost.
The narrative bookends scenes from Édith's middle life with repeated vignettes. One set of memories shows Édith with short curly hair, singing on stage and collapsing. She develops arthritis, as well as a severe morphine addiction. Her husband, Jacques Pills, persuades her to enter drug rehabilitation, and she travels to California with him. A now-sober but manic Édith drives around in a convertible while joking and teasing her compatriots.

title: Pan's Labyrinth
tagline: What happens when make-believe believes it's real?
overview: Living with her tyrannical stepfather in a new home with her pregnant mother, 10-year-old Ofelia feels alone until she explores a decaying labyrinth guarded by a mysterious faun who claims to know her destiny. If she wishes to return to her real father, Ofelia must complete three terrifying tasks.
plot:
Pan's Labyrinth (El laberinto del fauno) is a Spanish-language dark fantasy film of 2006 written, produced and directed by Guillermo del Toro, set in Francoist Spain in 1944. Ivana Baquero stars as Ofelia, a girl drawn into a mythical world, with Sergi López as her brutal stepfather Captain Vidal, Maribel Verdú as the housekeeper Mercedes, Doug Jones as both the Faun and the child-eating Pale Man and Ariadna Gil as Ofelia's mother Carmen.

A fable tells of Princess Moanna, daughter of the king of the underworld, who visited the human world, lost her memory in the sunlight and died as a mortal; her father built labyrinths across the world as portals for her spirit's return. Ofelia travels with her pregnant, ailing mother to a rural outpost commanded by Vidal, a fanatical Francoist officer hunting the Maquis resistance. An insect she takes for a fairy leads her to an ancient stone labyrinth, where a faun tells her she is the reincarnated princess and gives her a book revealing three tasks she must perform to return to her kingdom. Meanwhile Mercedes secretly aids her brother Pedro and the guerrillas.

Ofelia retrieves a key from the belly of a giant toad, and the faun gives her a mandrake root to keep beneath her mother's bed, easing her illness. In the second task she takes a dagger from the lair of the Pale Man but, ignoring the faun's warning, eats two grapes; the monster wakes and devours two fairies, and the furious faun abandons her. Vidal's cruelty escalates as he murders two farmers and tortures a captured guerrilla, whom Ferreiro mercifully kills before Vidal shoots the doctor. When Carmen burns the mandrake, she dies giving birth to Vidal's son. Exposed as a spy, Mercedes slashes Vidal's face and escapes. The faun returns with a final task: bring her baby brother into the labyrinth. There he asks for a drop of the infant's blood, but Ofelia refuses to harm him. Vidal, who cannot see the faun, takes the baby and shoots her. At the labyrinth's entrance he is surrounded by the Maquis; Mercedes tells him his son will never know his name, and Pedro kills him. As Ofelia dies, her blood falls onto an altar, and she awakens in a golden throne room, where her father the king tells her she passed the last test by shedding her own blood rather than an innocent's, and she takes her place beside him and her mother.

Premiering at Cannes in May 2006, the film grossed $83 million worldwide and won three Academy Awards and three BAFTAs. It scored 98 on Metacritic.

title: Breakfast on Pluto
tagline: Same world. Different planet.
overview: In the 1970s, a foundling lass, Patrick "Kitten" Braden, comes of age by leaving her Irish town for London, in part to look for her mother and in part because her transgender nature is beyond the town's understanding.
plot:
In 1958, in the fictional small Irish town of Tyrellin, County Cavan, Eily Bergin leaves her newborn baby, Patrick Braden, on the doorstep of the local parochial house, where the baby's father, Father Liam, lives. Patrick is placed with an unloving foster mother. Young Patrick dons a dress and lipstick, which angers his foster family. Patrick is accepted by his close friends Charlie, Irwin and Lawrence, as well as by Lawrence's father, who tells Patrick that Eily resembled American actress Mitzi Gaynor.
In his late teens in the 1970s, Patrick gets into trouble in school for writing an explicit story imagining how he was conceived by his parents and inquiring about where to undergo a sex change. Patrick comes out as transgender and renames herself Patricia "Kitten" Braden. In confession, she asks Father Liam about Eily but is rebuffed.
Kitten runs away from home, getting a ride with a glam rock band, Billy Hatchet and the Mohawks, and flirting with frontman Billy. He sets Kitten up in a trailer, where she discovers he is hiding guns for the IRA. Meanwhile, Irwin has begun to work with the IRA, much to his now-girlfriend Charlie's dismay. Kitten scoffs at Irwin's politics, but after Lawrence is killed by police detonating a suspected loyalist car bomb, she tosses their gun cache into a lake. Billy abandons Kitten to flee the IRA, forcing her to face the IRA men alone. Her lack of connection to their politics saves her from being murdered.
Kitten heads to London in search of Eily, but initial inquiries prove fruitless. Penniless, she finds shelter in a tiny cottage in a park, only to find that it is a Wombles children's theme park. Kitten takes a job as a singing and dancing Womble, but immediately loses it when her sponsor and co-worker punches their boss. Forced into prostitution, she is strangled by her first client, narrowly escaping by spraying Chanel No. 5 in his eyes.
At a diner, mild-mannered magician Bertie Vaughan asks Kitten what she is writing in her notebook. She explains it is a story about the mother she is seeking, whom Kitten dubs the "Phantom Lady". Intrigued, Bertie hires her as his assistant, turning her life story into a hypnosis act. One day, Bertie tries to kiss Kitten, and she explains that she is transgender, something he already knew. Soon, Charlie finds Bertie's show and takes Kitten away.
While dancing with an English soldier at a nightclub, Kitten is injured when the club is bombed by the IRA. After the police discover that Kitten is transgender and Irish, she is arrested on suspicion of terrorism. At the police station, Wallis beats her up while Routledge urges her to make a statement; Kitten fabricates a story about how she infiltrated a terrorist cell, dressed in black leather and armed with a Chanel spray bottle. Realising she is innocent, the police release her a week later.
Kitten is again forced to turn to prostitution until Wallis sympathetically brings her to a peep show, where she dons a blonde wig.

title: The Departed
tagline: Lies. Betrayal. Sacrifice. How far will you take it?
overview: To take down South Boston's Irish Mafia, the police send in one of their own to infiltrate the underworld, not realizing the syndicate has done likewise. While an undercover cop curries favor with the mob kingpin, a career criminal rises through the police ranks. But both sides soon discover there's a mole among them.
plot:
Colin Sullivan, first introduced to Boston Irish mob boss Frank Costello in the 1980s, has been groomed for years as Costello's spy inside the Massachusetts State Police (MSP). Sullivan is assigned to the Special Investigation Unit, where Captain Queenan and Sergeant Dignam assign another police academy recruit, Billy Costigan, to infiltrate Costello's organization.
Costigan, serving a prison term as cover, draws Costello's attention by committing several crimes and is recruited into Costello's gang. Costigan's mental health declines from increasing involvement in Costello's violent criminal activities, but Queenan and Dignam convince him to remain undercover. Sullivan begins dating police psychiatrist Madolyn Madden, who becomes Costigan's court-ordered therapist.
Costigan notifies the MSP that Costello will be selling stolen microprocessors to Chinese mobsters. When Sullivan helps thwart the attempted sting operation, Costello and the MSP realize they've been compromised. Costigan and Sullivan are each tasked to find the opposing mole. Costigan and Queenan learn that Costello is a protected FBI informant. Costigan begins an affair with Madden.
Costigan follows Costello and sees him pass Sullivan information on his crew. Costigan is unable to identify Sullivan, who realizes he is being followed and mistakenly stabs a passerby before fleeing. Lying to his fellow officers to have Queenan followed, Sullivan realizes Queenan is meeting with his mole and informs Costello's gang.
Costigan, fearing discovery as the mole, meets with Queenan to abort the operation. Queenan helps Costigan escape, but Costello's men arrive and throw Queenan from the building to his death. Fatally wounded in the ensuing firefight with police, Costello's henchman Timothy Delahunt tells Costigan that he knows he's the mole before dying.
Following Queenan's murder, Dignam is suspended after confronting Sullivan about cooperating with the FBI. A news report identifies Delahunt as a Boston Police Department undercover officer, but Costello suspects it's a ruse to protect the real mole. Sullivan directs the MSP to tail Costello, resulting in a gunfight that kills most of Costello's crew. Sullivan confronts a wounded Costello, who admits to being an informant before Sullivan kills him.
His assignment finished, Costigan reveals himself to Sullivan but recognizes Costello's envelope on his desk and deduces that Sullivan is Costello's mole. Costigan flees, and Sullivan realizes he has discovered the truth. Sullivan deletes Costigan's police records. Costigan leaves an envelope of evidence with Madden, who finds a recording of Sullivan's incriminating conversations with Costello.
Meeting Sullivan on the rooftop where Queenan was killed, Costigan arrests him. Trooper Brown, Costigan's police academy classmate, arrives as Costigan holds Sullivan at gunpoint, declaring he has evidence tying Sullivan to Costello.

overview: Jean-Baptiste Grenouille, born in the stench of 18th century Paris, develops a superior olfactory sense, which he uses to create the world's finest perfumes. However, his work takes a dark turn as he tries to preserve scents in the search for the ultimate perfume.
plot:
Perfume: The Story of a Murderer is a 2006 period psychological thriller film directed by Tom Tykwer, who wrote the screenplay with Andrew Birkin and Bernd Eichinger, based on Patrick Süskind's 1985 novel. Set in 18th-century France, it stars Ben Whishaw as Jean-Baptiste Grenouille, a man with an extraordinary sense of smell whose search for the perfect scent turns murderous, alongside Alan Rickman, Rachel Hurd-Wood and Dustin Hoffman.

The story unfolds in flashback from Grenouille's sentencing before a furious mob. Born amid the stalls of a Paris fish market and abandoned by his mother, who is hanged for it, he grows up in an orphanage and later works for a tanner. On a delivery into the city he becomes entranced by the scent of a young plum seller and, trying to keep her quiet, accidentally smothers her; her fading aroma haunts him. He then astonishes the declining perfumer Giuseppe Baldini with his ability to create fragrances, revives his business, and learns distillation, but discovers it cannot capture the scent of people. Baldini directs him to Grasse, where other methods are practiced. On the way Grenouille retreats to a cave and realizes that he himself has no scent at all.

In Grasse he fixes on Laure Richis, the daughter of the wealthy Antoine Richis, as the essential final note of a supreme perfume. After learning enfleurage and experimenting on murder victims, he kills a series of young women, preserving their scents while their bodies spread terror through the town. Richis flees with Laure, but Grenouille tracks her to an inn, murders her and completes his perfume before soldiers seize him. At his execution he wears the fragrance, and the crowd, overwhelmed, proclaims him innocent and falls into an orgy; even Richis embraces him. Free but realizing the perfume cannot make him love or be loved, Grenouille returns to his Paris birthplace, pours the rest over himself, and is consumed by the crowd it draws.

Eichinger acquired the rights in 2000 after Süskind long refused to sell, and the film was shot in Spain, Germany and France on a budget of about €50 million. It topped the German box office for three weeks after opening there in September 2006 and grossed about $135 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed, with 59% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 56; critics admired its visual richness while finding its antihero impossible to sympathize with.

title: Once Upon a Time in Mexico
original_title: Once Upon a Time in Mexico
tagline: The Time Has Come.
overview: Hitman "El Mariachi" becomes involved in international espionage involving a psychotic CIA agent and a corrupt Mexican general.
plot:
Once Upon a Time in Mexico is a 2003 American crime drama film directed by Robert Rodriguez, written by Robert Rodriguez and Shiny Rodriguez, and starring Antonio Banderas, Johnny Depp, and Salma Hayek.

The film takes place after the events of El Mariachi (1992) and Desperado (1995), and serves as a sequel to both films. The story follows El Mariachi (Antonio Banderas), a Mexican musician who becomes embroiled in a violent struggle between rival cartels, led by the ruthless Don Carlos (Javier Bardem).

The film begins with El Mariachi performing at a bar in Mexico City, where he is mistaken for a famous singer. He soon finds himself caught up in a complex web of violence and deception as he tries to uncover the truth about his past and the identity of the mysterious woman who has been following him.

As El Mariachi delves deeper into the world of organized crime, he becomes embroiled in a cat-and-mouse game with Don Carlos, who will stop at nothing to eliminate him. Along the way, he meets a beautiful woman named Carolina (Salma Hayek), who is being pursued by Don Carlos' henchmen.

The plot thickens as El Mariachi discovers that Carolina is actually the daughter of Don Carlos, and that she has been trying to escape her father's clutches. As the stakes grow higher, El Mariachi finds himself in a desperate bid for survival, using his wits and his musical talents to outsmart his enemies.

Meanwhile, Johnny Depp plays Jack Buechner, an American hitman who is hired by Don Carlos to eliminate El Mariachi. However, as the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Jack's true loyalties lie with Carolina, and he finds himself torn between his duty to Don Carlos and his growing feelings for the beautiful woman.

As the film hurtles towards its climax, El Mariachi and Jack engage in a series of intense battles, using everything from guns to musical instruments to try and outmaneuver each other. In the end, it is up to El Mariachi to use all his cunning and resourcefulness to defeat Don Carlos and bring peace to the troubled region.

Throughout the film, Robert Rodriguez pays homage to classic Westerns and Mexican cinema, incorporating a range of clever references and Easter eggs into the narrative. The result is a thrilling and entertaining ride that combines action, drama, and music in a way that is both unique and captivating.

Overall, Once Upon a Time in Mexico is a gripping and stylish film that showcases the talents of its cast and crew. With its intricate plot, memorable characters, and stunning visuals, it is a must-see for fans of Robert Rodriguez and anyone who loves a good action movie.

title: The Devil's Backbone
tagline: What is a ghost?
overview: Spain, 1939. In the last days of the Spanish Civil War, the young Carlos arrives at the Santa Lucía orphanage, where he will make friends and enemies as he follows the quiet footsteps of a mysterious presence eager for revenge.
plot:
The Devil's Backbone is a 2001 Spanish horror film directed by Guillermo del Toro, produced by El Deseo, and written by Guillermo del Toro and David Benioff. The film is set during the Spanish Civil War (1936-1939) and tells the story of a young boy named Carlos, who is sent to an orphanage called San Miguel de Allende.

The story begins with Carlos, a 10-year-old boy, being forced to leave his home in Madrid due to the war. He is sent to the orphanage, where he meets a mysterious and ghostly presence that seems to be connected to the death of a fellow student, Santi. As Carlos tries to adjust to his new life at the orphanage, he begins to experience strange occurrences, including finding Santi's belongings in different parts of the building.

Carlos soon discovers that the orphanage is haunted by the ghost of Santi, who died under mysterious circumstances. The ghost is believed to be a manifestation of the guilt and trauma experienced by the orphanage's caretaker, Captain Cánovas, who was responsible for Santi's death. As Carlos delves deeper into the mystery, he uncovers a dark secret about the orphanage's past and the true identity of the ghost.

Throughout the film, Carlos forms a close bond with his friend Jacinta, an older girl who is also living at the orphanage. Together, they try to uncover the truth behind Santi's death and the haunting of the orphanage. Along the way, they encounter various characters, including Captain Cánovas, who becomes increasingly unhinged as the story unfolds.

As the story progresses, Carlos learns that Santi was killed by Captain Cánovas in a fit of rage after discovering that he had been hiding a Jewish girl, Jacinta's sister, at the orphanage. The ghostly presence is revealed to be Santi's spirit, who is trapped between the world of the living and the dead.

In the climax of the film, Carlos confronts Captain Cánovas, who has become increasingly unhinged due to his guilt and paranoia. In a dramatic confrontation, Carlos exposes the truth about Santi's death and the haunting of the orphanage. The ghostly presence is finally laid to rest, and Carlos is able to find closure and move on from his experiences.

The Devil's Backbone is a haunting and atmospheric film that explores themes of trauma, guilt, and redemption. The film features stunning visuals and a powerful performance from Fernando Tielve as Carlos. The film's use of practical effects and set design creates a sense of realism and immersion, drawing the viewer into the world of the orphanage.

Overall, The Devil's Backbone is a masterful horror film that tells a haunting and atmospheric story about trauma, guilt, and redemption.

title: The Contract
tagline: Every killer meets his equal.
overview: Attempting to recover from a recent family trauma by escaping into the woods for a peaceful hiking trip, an ex-lawman and his young son stumble across a dangerous contract killer.
plot:
The Contract is a German-American action thriller of 2006 directed by Bruce Beresford and written by the television writer Stephen Katz and John Darrouzet. Morgan Freeman stars as the professional assassin Frank Carden and John Cusack as Ray Keene, a teacher who becomes entangled in Carden's latest job during a camping trip with his son. Jamie Anderson, Alice Krige, Megan Dodds and Corey Johnson co-star.

Carden has been hired to kill Lydell Hammond Sr., a reclusive billionaire and outspoken opponent of stem cell research, but his plan collapses when he is hurt in a car crash. Hospital staff find his gun, and federal marshals come for him. Meanwhile Ray, a widower, ex-cop and awkward gym teacher, takes Chris on a wilderness hike to reconnect after catching him smoking marijuana. In the same forest, Carden's men ambush the marshals' convoy; the last survivor, before he dies, asks Ray to deliver the prisoner to the authorities.

Ray and Chris set out to march Carden out of the wilderness, pursued by his crew of highly trained former soldiers. The chase draws in a couple, Sandra and Lochlan, and Lochlan is killed. In a tense standoff at a cabin, Ray agrees to release Carden, but when one of the gunmen strikes Chris, Ray kills him and Sandra shoots another. Local police rescue Ray and Sandra, but Carden escapes, taking Chris as a hostage. Miles then orders Davis, Carden's newest recruit, to kill Carden and the boy and pin the blame on Carden, and to eliminate Ray too in case he knows anything.

Back home, Ray sees a news report describing Carden as someone who removes obstacles to progress, which helps him deduce the target. He goes to the funeral of Hammond's son to intercept Carden and unwittingly saves him from Davis, whom Carden kills with his own sniper rifle. The fight costs Carden his chance at Hammond, and he hands Ray the keys to the hotel room where Chris is being held before vanishing. In Washington, D.C., Carden confronts Miles, letting her know he is aware she ordered his death and warning her to leave Ray's family alone. Two weeks later, Ray is seeing Sandra, and during a barbecue a radio bulletin reports that Hammond has died in a boating accident; Ray realizes that Carden has completed his contract.

The film was shot almost entirely in Bulgaria, with the headquarters of DSK Bank among its main sets and scenes filmed on the Vitosha mountain. Despite its cast, it went direct to video in the United States and Europe, and reviews were negative.

title: Blood: The Last Vampire
tagline: Where evil grows, she preys.
overview: On the surface, Saya is a stunning 16-year-old, but that youthful exterior hides the tormented soul of a 400-year-old "halfling". Born to a human father and a vampire mother, she has for centuries been a loner obsessed with using her samurai skills to rid the world of vampires, all the while knowing that she herself can survive only on blood like those she hunts.
plot:
In 1970s Tokyo, Saya is a 400-year-old half human-half vampire who hunts vampires. Raised by a man named Kato, she works loosely with an organisation known as "The Council", a secret society that has been hunting vampires for centuries. Saya's motivation goes beyond duty; she wants revenge: Onigen, the oldest of the vampires, murdered her father. For her next mission, she goes undercover as a student at Kanto High School on an American air base near Fussa.
When she is introduced in her class, Saya's appearance quickly attracts the negative attention of a female classmate, Sharon. The daughter of the base's general, Alice McKee, is also bothered with the attention. At her school, she finds herself being mocked. Alice is asked by her Kendo instructor Powell to stay for the Kendo practice due to her poor performance. As soon as the teacher leaves, she finds herself at the mercy of Sharon and her sidekick friend who wield sharp bladed katanas to taunt and torment her. Saya shows up just in time to stop Sharon from slashing Alice's throat. Despite Saya's effort to disguise her activity, Alice sees Sharon and her friend being butchered. However it is soon revealed that Sharon and her friend are vampires in disguise.
Because "The Council" cleans up the bodies of the demons, Alice's father does not believe her story. Determined to make her own investigation, Alice goes to the bar where her Kendo instructor usually hangs out. To her horror her instructor, as well as the rest of the people in the bar, turn out to be vampires. Once again Saya comes to her rescue and has to fight off hordes of vampires surrounding them.
General McKee investigates "The Council", who disguise themselves as CIA. Alice arrives just in time to witness her father's death. Her dying father gives her Saya's address. With nowhere else to go, Alice decides to seek Saya's help. Fortunately Saya has never sworn loyalty to "The Council" and protects Alice instead. The two of them flee the area and go off to the mountains to find and slay Onigen.
In their pursuit, Alice and Saya are run off the side of the road by an attacking demon and they fall into a ravine. When Alice and Saya awaken they are in Ancient Japan where Saya was raised. Onigen appears, reveals her true identity as Saya's mother, and fights Saya. Saya slays Onigen. Alice, who is injured during the fighting, wakes up to find herself at the wreckage of the truck and being carried into an ambulance. Later she is interviewed about the events surrounding her father's death, but her interviewer does not believe her story about the vampires or the Council. When asked about where Saya is, Alice answers that she is "searching for a way back from the other side of the looking glass".
