title: Memoirs of a Geisha
tagline: My world is as forbidden as it is fragile; without its mysteries, it cannot survive.
overview: A sweeping romantic epic set in Japan in the years before World War II, a penniless Japanese child is torn from her family to work as a maid in a geisha house.
plot:
Memoirs of a Geisha is a 2005 epic romantic drama film directed by Rob Marshall, based on the 1997 novel of the same name by Arthur Golden. The movie stars Zhang Ziyi as Chiyo Sakamoto, a young Japanese girl sold into prostitution in Gion, Kyoto, and Colin Firth as John Norman Howard, an American businessman.

The story begins in 1929 with Chiyo, a young orphaned girl who is sold to the Gion Courtesan School by her father. She is renamed Sayuri and trained in the traditional arts of geisha-hood, including music, dance, and poetry. As she grows older, Sayuri becomes a skilled geisha and attracts the attention of several wealthy clients.

One of these clients is Hatsumomo, a cruel and abusive geisha who resents Sayuri's natural beauty and talent. Despite this, Sayuri catches the eye of Nobu, a young geisha who becomes her closest friend and confidant. The two women form a strong bond, but their friendship is put to the test when they are both forced to compete for the affections of the wealthy and charming Noboru.

Noboru is a young nobleman who has recently returned from World War I and is looking for a geisha to be his companion. Sayuri is chosen as his favorite, and she becomes deeply involved in his life. However, their relationship is complicated by Hatsumomo's continued harassment of Sayuri and Nobu's own emotional baggage.

As the story unfolds, Sayuri finds herself torn between her loyalty to Nobu and her growing feelings for Noboru. Meanwhile, John Norman Howard, an American businessman, becomes a key figure in Sayuri's life, as he falls deeply in love with her. However, their social differences and cultural misunderstandings threaten to tear them apart.

The movie builds towards a tragic conclusion, as Sayuri is forced to make a choice between her two loves and the life she has built for herself. In the end, Sayuri sacrifices her own happiness for the sake of those she loves, leading to a heart-wrenching finale that will leave audiences in tears.

Throughout the film, the cinematography and costumes are stunning, capturing the beauty and elegance of traditional Japanese culture. The performances by the cast, particularly Zhang Ziyi and Colin Firth, are also noteworthy, bringing depth and nuance to their characters.

Overall, Memoirs of a Geisha is a powerful and emotional film that explores themes of love, loyalty, and sacrifice in the context of Japan's traditional geisha culture. While it has received some criticism for its portrayal of cultural stereotypes and historical inaccuracies, the movie remains a captivating and unforgettable epic romance.

title: The Sea Inside
tagline: Sensitive Drama About a Polemic Theme
overview: The Sea Inside is about Spaniard Ramón Sampedro, who fought a 30-year campaign to win the right to end his life with dignity. It is the story of Ramón’s relationships with two women: Julia a lawyer who supports his cause, and Rosa, a local woman who wants to convince him that life is worth living.
plot:
The Sea Inside is a Spanish drama film of 2004 co-written, directed, co-produced, scored and edited by Alejandro Amenábar, based on the true story of Ramón Sampedro, a man left quadriplegic by a diving accident who campaigned for decades for the right to end his life. Javier Bardem stars as Ramón, with Belén Rueda as the lawyer Julia, Lola Dueñas as Rosa, Mabel Rivera as his sister-in-law Manuela, Celso Bugallo as his brother José, Tamar Novas as his nephew Javier and Josep Maria Pou as Father Francisco.

Ramón, now in his fifties, has spent more than a quarter of a century paralysed from the neck down after a diving accident in his youth. Unable to take his own life and unwilling to involve his loved ones, who under Spanish law could be charged with murder or assisting a suicide, he fights in the courts for the right to die. Since his mother's death he has been cared for by Manuela. His elder brother José opposes his wish, while Manuela and her son Javier support him. Through Gené, who works for a right-to-die organisation, he meets Julia, a lawyer suffering from a degenerative illness who takes up his case. As he tells her about his past, he explains that he sees no dignity in living paralysed. Rosa, a local woman who has read about him, comes to persuade him that life is worth living; rebuffed, she apologises on her part-time radio show and keeps visiting with her children, and they become friends. Drawn to both women, Ramón insists he belongs to death.

Julia reads his memoir and urges him to publish it, and he dreams of flying from his bed to meet her on the beach, but she suffers a stroke and must relearn to walk, so they correspond by letter. A quadriplegic priest, Father Francisco, comes to argue for life, but since Ramón refuses to be carried downstairs, a church boy shuttles their arguments up and down until Manuela, angered, sends the priest away. Julia, whose illness will only worsen, tells Ramón she plans to die herself but wants to help him first. With Javier, Ramón designs a wheelchair so he can attend court, but his appeal is rejected. In the end each of his friends performs a small act toward his death, too slight for any one to be convicted, and Ramón films himself as he drinks a glass laced with cyanide.

The film won the Grand Jury Prize at the Venice Film Festival and the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film. Critics praised Bardem's transfixing performance, giving the film 85% on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: Sweet November
tagline: She Just Needed A Month To Change His Life Forever.
overview: Nelson is a man devoted to his advertising career in San Francisco. One day, while taking a driving test at the DMV, he meets Sara. She is very different from the other women in his life. Nelson causes her to miss out on taking the test and later that day she tracks him down. One thing leads to another and Nelson ends up living with her through a November that will change his life forever.
plot:
Sweet November is a 2001 American romantic drama directed by Pat O'Connor and set in San Francisco. A loose remake of the 1968 film written by Herman Raucher, which starred Anthony Newley and Sandy Dennis, it reunites Keanu Reeves and Charlize Theron after The Devil's Advocate (1997), with Jason Isaacs, Greg Germann and Lauren Graham in supporting roles. Warner Bros. Pictures released it on February 16, 2001.

Nelson Moss is a driven, self-absorbed advertising executive. At the Department of Motor Vehicles he tries to cheat on his driving test by asking for help from the woman next to him, Sara Deever, and it is she who is failed when the examiner thinks she is the cheat. The free-spirited Sara is intrigued by him and keeps proposing that he spend a month with her, assuring him that he will come out of it a better person. When November begins, after Nelson has lost both his job and his girlfriend on the same day, he finally agrees to stay with her.

The next day, Sara's close friend and neighbour Chaz refers to Nelson as her "November". Over the following weeks Sara draws Nelson out of his workaholic routine, and the two share a series of simple, happy experiences and gradually fall in love. Nelson begins to reflect on his life and past, and befriends Abner, a fatherless ten-year-old boy from the neighbourhood. Realising how much Sara means to him, he asks her to marry him.

Sara then reveals that she is dying of non-Hodgkin lymphoma, and Chaz's remarks make clear that Nelson is not the first man she has spent such a month with. She tells Nelson to leave, admitting to Chaz that his was the first proposal she had wanted to accept. Nelson goes, but returns over the Thanksgiving holiday with gifts recalling their happy times and covers her walls with November calendars, telling her it can always be November for them.

They spend one more night together, but in the morning Nelson finds that Sara has taken the calendars down. She runs out, and he chases her through the streets until she stops on a footbridge and begs him to let her go, so that he can remember her as she was while she returns to the family she has been avoiding. She blindfolds him, leads him to the spot of one of their first dates and kisses him goodbye, and he removes the blindfold to find himself alone.

Critics panned the film as schmaltzy and manipulative, with a 15% Rotten Tomatoes rating, and it grossed 65.8 million dollars worldwide.

title: Hulk
tagline: What if everything you were forced to keep inside was suddenly set free?
overview: Bruce Banner, a genetics researcher with a tragic past, suffers massive radiation exposure in his laboratory that causes him to transform into a raging green monster when he gets angry.
plot:
Hulk (also known as The Hulk) is a 2003 American superhero film based on the Marvel Comics character created by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby. Directed by Ang Lee and written by John Turman, James Schamus and Michael France, it stars Eric Bana as scientist Bruce Banner, with Jennifer Connelly, Sam Elliott, Josh Lucas and Nick Nolte in supporting roles. Lee himself performed some of the motion capture used to animate the computer-generated Hulk.

The story begins in the 1960s with government geneticist David Banner, who is trying to enhance human DNA. When his supervisor, Colonel Thaddeus "Thunderbolt" Ross, forbids human trials, David experiments on himself. His wife Edith later gives birth to their son Bruce, and David realizes the boy has inherited his altered genes. After Ross discovers the unauthorized research and shuts it down, David sabotages the base's gamma reactor in retaliation. Convinced his son is dangerous, he tries to kill Bruce but instead accidentally kills Edith. Ross has David committed to a psychiatric institution, and the traumatized four-year-old Bruce, who represses the memory, is placed in foster care and raised as Bruce Krenzler, believing both his parents are dead.

As an adult, Bruce works as a researcher at a Berkeley laboratory alongside his former girlfriend Betty Ross, the estranged daughter of the now General Ross. Their work attracts the interest of Glenn Talbot, a ruthless representative of the private defense company Atheon. When a lab accident exposes Bruce to a massive dose of gamma radiation, he survives unharmed, but the exposure triggers the latent changes in his DNA. Moments of rage now transform him into an enormous, green-skinned creature of immense strength. At the same time, David Banner, released and living nearby, re-enters his son's life with sinister intentions, while the military hunts the Hulk across the desert and into San Francisco.

The film's split-screen editing, which mimicked comic book panels, and its psychological focus on trauma and fathers and sons distinguished it from other superhero releases of the era. Critical reaction was mixed, with praise for its ambition and Connelly's performance tempered by complaints about its slow pacing and the appearance of the creature. Marvel Studios later rebooted the character with The Incredible Hulk in 2008.

title: The Amazing Spider-Man
tagline: The untold story begins.
overview: Peter Parker is an outcast high schooler abandoned by his parents as a boy, leaving him to be raised by his Uncle Ben and Aunt May. Like most teenagers, Peter is trying to figure out who he is and how he got to be the person he is today. As Peter discovers a mysterious briefcase that belonged to his father, he begins a quest to understand his parents' disappearance – leading him directly to Oscorp and the lab of Dr. Curt Connors, his father's former partner. As Spider-Man is set on a collision course with Connors' alter ego, The Lizard, Peter will make life-altering choices to use his powers and shape his destiny to become a hero.
plot:
After discovering that his home office has been burglarized, scientist Richard Parker and his wife Mary flee to an unknown destination, leaving their young son Peter in the care of his Aunt May and Uncle Ben.
Years later, a teenage Peter attends Midtown Science High School in New York City. He is intelligent, but socially awkward and often bullied. He has a crush on Gwen Stacy, who returns his feelings. Peter discovers his father's briefcase and learns from Ben that his father was a friend of Dr. Curt Connors, a scientist at Oscorp in the field of cross-species genetics. Hoping to learn about his father's work, Peter sneaks into a restricted laboratory at Oscorp, where a genetically modified spider bites him. He develops spider-like abilities, including superhuman strength, agility, speed, and the ability to cling to surfaces.
Connors, whose right arm has been amputated, is conducting experiments to regenerate limbs. Peter discovers the missing piece to Connors' research, the "decay rate algorithm", in his father's papers. Peter visits Connors, reveals that he is Richard's son, and gives Connors the algorithm. At home, Peter and Ben argue, and Peter leaves. While searching for Peter, Ben is killed by a thief. Under the alias Spider-Man, Peter uses his new abilities to track down criminals matching the killer's description. He creates a mask with yellow-tinted glasses and a spandex suit to hide his identity, and builds mechanical web-shooters using a web formula developed by Oscorp. At dinner with Gwen's family, he discovers her father is police captain George Stacy, who holds a grudge against Spider-Man. After arguing with Captain Stacy, Peter reveals his double identity to Gwen, and they kiss.
Connors' superior, Rajit Ratha, demands that Connors begin human trials with his formula to regrow limbs using lizard DNA. Connors refuses to rush into testing, as it could put innocent people at risk. Ratha fires Connors and decides to test the serum at a Veterans Administration hospital. Desperate, Connors tries the formula on himself, passes out, and awakens to find that his missing arm has regenerated. While trying to intercept Ratha on the Williamsburg Bridge, Connors turns into a humanoid reptilian monster and begins a violent rampage; Peter arrives and saves people from Connors' attacks. Unable to piece together a narrative for the incident, the police issue a city-wide manhunt for both the Lizard and Spider-Man.
Connors discovers that Peter is Spider-Man and attacks him at school. Peter pursues Connors into the underground sewer system, where he finds a makeshift lab. He realizes that Connors is planning to release a biochemical agent from Oscorp Tower, which will turn everyone in the city into reptilian hybrids like himself. As Peter tries to stop Connors, the police corner him, and Captain Stacy discovers his double identity. Stacy lets Peter go after Connors, while Gwen creates an antidote for Connors' chemical agent.

title: Stomp the Yard
tagline: He will challenge their traditions. Their traditions will change his life.
overview: After the death of his younger brother, a troubled 19-year-old street dancer from Los Angeles is able to bypass juvenile hall by enrolling in the historically black, Truth University in Atlanta, Georgia. But his efforts to get an education and woo the girl he likes are sidelined when he is courted by the top two campus fraternities, both of which want and need his fierce street-style dance moves to win the highly coveted national step show competition.
plot:
Stomp the Yard is a 2007 American musical drama film directed by Chris Stokes and written by Chris Stokes and John Langley. The movie stars Columbus Short, Meagan Good, Rob Brown, and Idris Elba.

The story takes place at the historically black college, Lincoln University, in Jefferson City, Missouri. The plot revolves around Huxtable "Hype" Hollingsworth (Columbus Short), a young and talented dancer who is struggling to find his place on campus. Hype is a freshman who has just transferred from a high school for troubled youth, where he was forced to drop out due to disciplinary issues.

Upon arrival at Lincoln University, Hype discovers that the school's dance team, led by the charismatic and confident captain, Darnell "D-Town" Turner (Rob Brown), is in disarray. The team has been banned from performing for a year after a violent incident involving rival college teams. The university administration believes that the team's behavior was unacceptable and that they need to be reformed.

Hype sees an opportunity to prove himself and earn respect by joining the dance team, despite initial reservations from D-Town and other team members. As Hype becomes more involved with the team, he learns about their struggles and the pressures of being a part of a high-profile performance group.

Throughout the film, Hype faces various challenges, including his own personal demons, rivalries with other dancers, and conflicts with the university administration. He also develops relationships with his teammates, particularly D-Town's sister, April (Meagan Good), who becomes a source of support and encouragement for him.

As the story unfolds, Hype and the dance team work together to prepare for an upcoming competition against rival colleges. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about teamwork, discipline, and perseverance. The film culminates in a high-energy performance at the national dance competition, where the Lincoln University team faces off against their toughest opponents yet.

Ultimately, Hype and the team succeed in overcoming their challenges and delivering an outstanding performance that showcases their talents and dedication. The movie ends on a triumphant note, with Hype having found his place on campus and earning the respect of his peers.

Throughout the film, the music plays a significant role, as the dance team incorporates various styles and genres into their performances. The soundtrack features a mix of hip-hop, R&B, and pop tracks that reflect the characters' personalities and emotions.

Overall, Stomp the Yard is a heartwarming and inspiring film that explores themes of perseverance, teamwork, and self-discovery. With its energetic dance sequences and memorable characters, the movie has become a beloved favorite among fans of musical dramas.

title: The Others
tagline: Sooner or later they’ll find you.
overview: Grace is a religious woman who lives in an old house kept dark because her two children, Anne and Nicholas, have a rare sensitivity to light. When the family begins to suspect the house is haunted, Grace fights to protect her children at any cost in the face of strange events and disturbing visions.
plot:
The Others is a Gothic psychological horror film of 2001 written, directed and scored by Alejandro Amenábar, set on the island of Jersey in 1945. Nicole Kidman stars as Grace Stewart, a mother living in an isolated manor with her two children, with Fionnula Flanagan as the housekeeper Bertha Mills, Christopher Eccleston as Charles, Alakina Mann and James Bentley as the children Anne and Nicholas, Eric Sykes as the gardener Edmund Tuttle and Elaine Cassidy as the mute maid Lydia.

Grace lives in a remote house on Jersey, recently freed from German occupation. Because Anne and Nicholas suffer from an extreme sensitivity to light, she keeps the house in constant gloom behind heavy curtains. Grace hires three servants who arrive seeking work, learning that they served in the house years before. Anne insists that she has seen a boy called Victor, his parents and a blind old woman. Grace dismisses this as fantasy until she hears footsteps and voices herself and orders a search for intruders. In a storeroom she finds a nineteenth-century album of photographs of the dead, and Mrs Mills mentions that many people left the house during a tuberculosis outbreak in 1891.

Torn between her fears and her Catholic faith, Grace becomes convinced the house is haunted when a piano plays by itself, and sets out to fetch a priest, while Mrs Mills has Tuttle cover a set of gravestones with leaves. In the woods she instead finds Charles, whom she believed killed in the war and brings him home, but he soon departs again for the front, though she insists the war is over. Grace sees an old woman in Anne's communion dress speaking with her daughter's voice and attacks her, only to find she has struck Anne. When every curtain in the house vanishes, exposing the children to daylight, Grace throws out the servants, but the children discover their names on the hidden graves, and Grace finds a post-mortem photograph of the three, who all died in 1891. At a séance, Grace learns the truth: the blind woman is a medium contacted by Victor's living family, and Grace, in despair after Charles's death, smothered her children and then shot herself. She, the children and the servants are the ghosts. Victor's family moves out, the children enjoy sunlight for the first time, and Grace declares that the house is theirs and they will never leave.

The film grossed $210 million worldwide on a $17 million budget. It won eight Goya Awards, including Best Film, a first for a film with no Spanish dialogue.

title: Zodiac
tagline: There's more than one way to lose your life to a killer.
overview: A cartoonist teams up with an ace reporter and a law enforcement officer to track down an elusive serial killer.
plot:
On July 4, 1969, an unknown man attacks Darlene Ferrin and Mike Mageau with a handgun at a lovers' lane in Vallejo, California. Only Mike survives and later disappears from the public eye. One month later, the San Francisco Chronicle receives encrypted letters written by the killer, calling himself "Zodiac", who threatens to kill a dozen people, unless his coded message containing his identity is published.
Political cartoonist Robert Graysmith, who correctly guesses that his identity is not in the message, is not taken seriously by crime reporter Paul Avery or the editors and is excluded from the initial details about the killings. When the newspaper publishes the letters, a married couple deciphers one, revealing it indeed did not contain the killer's name. On September 27, the killer stabs law student, Bryan Hartnell and Cecelia Shepard at Lake Berryessa in Napa County; Cecelia dies two days later.
At the office, Avery makes fun of Graysmith before they discuss the coded letters. Graysmith interprets the letter, which Avery finds helpful, and he begins sharing information. One of Graysmith's insights about the letters is that Zodiac's reference to man as, "the most dangerous animal of them all," is a reference to the 1932 film The Most Dangerous Game, which features the villainous Count Zaroff, a man who hunts live human prey.
On October 11, San Francisco taxicab driver Paul Stine is shot and killed in the city's Presidio Heights district. The Zodiac killer mails pieces of Stine's bloodstained shirt to the Chronicle along with a taunting letter. San Francisco police inspectors Dave Toschi and his partner, Bill Armstrong, are assigned to the case by Captain Marty Lee, and work closely with Vallejo's Jack Mulanax and Captain Ken Narlow in Napa. Someone claiming to be Zodiac continues to send taunting letters and speaks on the phone with lawyer, Melvin Belli, on the KGO-TV morning talk show, hosted by Jim Dunbar.
On August 4, 1971, Detectives Toschi, Armstrong, and Mulanax question Arthur Leigh Allen, a suspect in the Vallejo case. They notice that he wears a Zodiac wristwatch, with the same logo used by the killer, and Toschi thinks he is the killer. However, a handwriting expert Sherwood insists that Allen did not write the Zodiac letters, even though Allen is said to be ambidextrous.
Avery receives a letter threatening his life; becoming paranoid, he turns to drugs and alcohol. He shares information with the Riverside Police Department that the killer might have been active before the initial killings, angering Toschi and Armstrong. The case's notoriety weighs on Toschi, who cannot sit through a Hollywood film, Dirty Harry, loosely based on the Zodiac case.
In 1976, Avery moves to the Sacramento Bee. Graysmith persistently contacts Toschi about the Zodiac murders, and eventually impresses him with his knowledge of the case.

title: Lucky You
tagline: Change your game. Change your life.
overview: A professional poker player whose astounding luck at the table fails to translate into his lonesome love life attempts to win the World Series of Poker while simultaneously earning the affections of a beautiful Las Vegas singer.
plot:
In 2003, Huck Cheever is a young and talented poker player in Las Vegas haunted by his relationship with his estranged father, L.C. Cheever, a two-time World Series of Poker Champion. Huck is a regular in Vegas poker rooms but needs $10,000 to get a seat in the World Series of Poker Main Event.
After a good night at the Bellagio hotel's poker room, Huck goes to a party and meets aspiring singer Billie Offer, who has just arrived in town. Billie's older sister Suzanne warns her that Huck is "hustle 10, commitment zero." Back at the Bellagio, Huck is doing well at the tables before L.C. returns to town from the South of France. Huck greets his father coldly. The two play heads-up.
Loan shark Roy Durucher tells Huck that he plays poker as well as anybody, except for his reputation as a "blaster" (not patient enough) who always goes for broke. Roy proposes to stake Huck in the $10,000 main event with a 60% (Roy) — 40% (Huck) split of any winnings, but Huck refuses. After failing to borrow money from his friend Jack, Huck goes to Suzanne's place hoping for a loan. Instead, he runs into Billie, who gets a call confirming that she has landed a job singing at a club.
Huck proposes a celebration and at Binion's Horseshoe he shows her how to play poker. L.C. arrives and shows Huck a wedding ring of Huck's late mother's that Huck had pawned and that L.C. has redeemed. Huck loses his winnings. Over dinner, he explains to Billie that his father stole from his mother before leaving her. Huck says his father taught him how to play on the kitchen table with "pennies, nickels, and dimes." They make love after dinner. As Billie sleeps, Huck steals money from Billie's purse.
Huck plays in a "super satellite" to enter the main event. He appears to have the seat won, but a misdeal costs him. Roy agrees to stake Huck and even gives him an extra $1200 so that he can repay Billie. He apologizes to her, saying he feels they have a chance at something special. They later run into L.C., who wins all of Huck's stake money for the World Series in a quick game of guts.
Billie holds the stopwatch in a golfing marathon that Huck must complete in 3 hours to win a bet. She declines to cheat for him when he finishes two seconds too late. Huck gets a black eye when Roy's thugs toss him into his empty pool. They warn him to return the $11,200 stake that he owes to Roy or get a seat in the World Series within 48 hours. When Huck goes to Suzanne's apartment looking for Billie, he learns Billie has gone home to Bakersfield. Huck sells the wedding ring to his father for $500 and makes the 10 grand playing poker in one night to buy a seat in the World Series. Huck travels to Bakersfield to tell Billie that he meant what he said when he felt they had a chance at something special.
Back in Vegas, having found the entry money, Huck enters the World Series. He and his father both advance to the final table of nine. Billie looks on from the audience as Huck and L.C. have a showdown.

title: The Butterfly Effect
tagline: Change one thing. Change everything.
overview: A young man struggles to access sublimated childhood memories. He finds a technique that allows him to travel back into the past, to occupy his childhood body and change history. However, he soon finds that every change he makes has unexpected consequences.
plot:
The Butterfly Effect is a psychological science fiction film directed by Eric Bress and J. Mackye Gruber, released in 2004 by New Line Cinema.

The movie follows the story of Evan Treborn (played by Ashton Kutcher), a young man who suffers from dissociative identity disorder (DID). As a child, Evan was physically and emotionally abused by his mother, and he developed multiple personalities to cope with her abuse. The film begins with Evan as an adult, struggling to come to terms with his past traumas.

Evan discovers that small changes in the past can have significant effects on his present and future. He starts experimenting with altering events from his childhood, using a technique called "butterfly effect," where even the tiniest change can cause a ripple effect leading to unpredictable outcomes.

Initially, Evan's attempts at changing the past are met with success, but he soon realizes that each alteration has unintended consequences on his present and future. He starts to experience strange visions and nightmares, hinting at the existence of alternate timelines or parallel universes.

As Evan continues to experiment with time travel, he becomes increasingly obsessed with altering a traumatic event from his childhood, where he was bullied by a group of kids. He decides to go back in time and prevent the bullying, but this decision sets off a chain reaction of events that lead to devastating consequences.

Evan's actions start to affect those around him, including his friends and family. His relationships become strained, and he starts to question his own identity. The film takes a dark turn as Evan realizes that changing the past has made him lose touch with his true self.

The movie builds up to a climactic finale where Evan must confront the consequences of his actions. He discovers that altering the past has created multiple timelines, each with their own version of reality. In the end, Evan is forced to make a choice between preserving his original timeline or embracing the new reality he has created.

Throughout the film, the director explores themes of trauma, identity, and the consequences of playing with time. The movie raises questions about the nature of reality and the butterfly effect, leaving the audience to ponder the implications of Evan's actions.

The Butterfly Effect received mixed reviews from critics but was a commercial success, grossing over $187 million worldwide. Ashton Kutcher's performance as Evan Treborn was praised for its intensity and emotional depth. The film's unique blend of science fiction and psychological drama has made it a cult classic among fans of the genre.

title: Enough
tagline: Everyone has a limit.
overview: Working-class waitress Slim thought she was entering a life of domestic bliss when she married Mitch, the man of her dreams. After the arrival of their first child, her picture perfect life is shattered when she discovers Mitch's hidden possessive dark side, a controlling and abusive alter ego that can turn trust, love and tranquility into terror. plot:
Enough is a 2002 American psychological thriller directed by Michael Apted and written by Nicholas Kazan, based on Anna Quindlen's 1998 bestselling novel Black and Blue. Jennifer Lopez stars as Slim, a woman who escapes an abusive marriage and eventually learns to fight back, with Billy Campbell as her husband Mitch and Juliette Lewis, Noah Wyle, Dan Futterman and Fred Ward in supporting roles.

Slim is working as a waitress at a Los Angeles diner when a wealthy customer, Mitch Hiller, comes to her defence against a man pestering her on a bet. They marry, have a daughter, Gracie, and settle into a comfortable home. Six years on, Slim learns that Mitch has been cheating on her without remorse, and when she threatens to leave he beats her and declares that, as the provider, he can do as he pleases. His mother hints at a history of abuse; the police cannot help. After a first escape attempt is foiled at gunpoint, Slim flees with Gracie, but Mitch drains and freezes her accounts and tracks her to a cheap motel. She moves on to Seattle, where her former boyfriend Joe is intimidated by men posing as FBI agents, and turns to her rich, estranged father, Jupiter, who initially dismisses her as a gold digger. Once Mitch's associates threaten him as well, Jupiter sends her enough money to start a new life under a new name in Michigan.

Mitch finds her again with the help of Robbie, a corrupt police officer who, it turns out, was the man in the staged diner incident; the two had been running such cons to seduce women. Slim escapes an attack and a car chase, and a lawyer warns her that the law offers little protection and that a custody hearing may be a trap. Hiding Gracie away, she trains in Krav Maga in San Francisco, recruits a lookalike as a decoy, and breaks into Mitch's new house, hiding his guns and disabling the phone. When he returns, she defeats him in a brutal fight that ends with him falling from a balcony to his death, and the police rule it self-defense.

Sandra Bullock was originally attached to the lead before scheduling conflicts intervened. Filming began on May 21, 2001, and the release, first planned for September 2001, was moved to May 24, 2002. Made for $38 million, the film earned about $40 million in North America and $51.8 million worldwide. Critics were largely negative, with 22% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 25, though audiences gave it an "A−" CinemaScore. Lopez received a Golden Raspberry nomination for Worst Actress.

title: Alexander
tagline: The greatest legend of all was real
overview: Alexander, the King of Macedonia, leads his legions against the giant Persian Empire. After defeating the Persians, he leads his army across the then known world, venturing farther than any westerner had ever gone, all the way to India.
plot:
Around 285 BC, Ptolemy I Soter, basileus and pharaoh of Ptolemaic Egypt, narrates the life of Alexander. Alexander grows up with his mother Olympias and his tutor Aristotle, where he finds interest in love, honor, music, exploration, poetry and military combat. His relationship with his father, Philip II of Macedon, is destroyed when Philip marries Attalus's niece, Eurydice. Alexander insults Philip after disowning Attalus as his kinsman, which results in Alexander's banishment from Philip's palace.
After Philip is assassinated, Alexander becomes King of Macedonia. Ptolemy mentions Alexander's punitive campaign in which he razes Thebes, also referring to the later burning of Persepolis, then gives an overview of Alexander's west-Persian campaign, including his declaration as the son of Zeus by the Oracle of Amun at Siwa Oasis, his great battle against the Persian Emperor Darius III in the Battle of Gaugamela, and his eight-year campaign across Asia.
Alexander's most private relationships are these with his childhood friends; Glaucos (who receives a mercy killing from Alexander when wounded at Gaugamela), Hephaestion, Bagoas, and later his wife, Roxana. Hephaestion compares Alexander to Achilles, to which Alexander replies that Hephaestion must be his Patroclus (Achilles's friend and possible lover). When Hephaestion mentions that Patroclus died first, Alexander pledges that, if Hephaestion should die first, he will follow him into the afterlife (as Achilles had done for Patroclus). Hephaestion shows extensive jealousy when Alexander marries Roxana, going so far as to attempt to keep her away from him after Alexander murders Cleitus the Black in India during a drunken rage.
After initial objection from his soldiers, Alexander convinces them to join him in his final and bloodiest battle, the Battle of Hydaspes. He is severely injured with an arrow but survives and is celebrated. Later on, Hephaestion succumbs to typhus carried with him from India, and dies, deeply saddening Alexander. During a symposium in Babylon, Alexander falls unconscious after downing a large bowl of wine. On his deathbed, Bagoas grieves as Alexander's generals begin to split up his kingdom and fight over the ownership of his body.
In 285 BC, Ptolemy admits to his scribe that he, along with all the other officers, had indeed poisoned Alexander just to spare themselves from any future conquests or consequences. However, he has it recorded that Alexander died due to illness compounding his overall weakened condition. He then goes on to end his memoirs with praise to Alexander.
Ptolemy's memoirs of Alexander were eventually burned, lost forever with other scrolls of the Library of Alexandria by the end of the Roman Empire.

title: The Grudge
tagline: It never forgives. It never forgets.
overview: An American nurse living and working in Tokyo is exposed to a mysterious supernatural curse, one that locks a person in a powerful rage before claiming their life and spreading to another victim.
plot:
The Grudge is a curse, born when someone dies in extreme rage or sorrow and lingers where the person dies. Those who encounter it will die, and the curse is reborn repeatedly, passing from victim to victim in an endless growing chain of horror.
In 2001, Kayako Saeki, a housewife in Tokyo, is in love with her college professor, Peter Kirk, obsessively writing about him in a diary. Her jealous husband Takeo discovers the diary and believes Kayako is having an affair. In a fit of rage, he brutally murders her, their young son Toshio, and their pet cat Mar. After Takeo hides the bodies in the house, Kayako's ghost hangs him with her hair. After receiving a letter from Kayako, Peter visits the Saeki house only to find her and Takeo's corpses and Toshio's ghost. Shocked and horrified, he flees the scene and commits suicide the next day. The remainder of the Saeki family rises again as restless ghosts due to the curse, notably Kayako, who appears as an onryō.
In 2004, the Williams family from America moved into the Saeki house for Matt's job. While Matt is thrilled with the house, his wife Jennifer and dementia-ridden mother Emma feel uncomfortable, the former experiencing culture shock and feeling lost as she can't speak Japanese, and the latter sensing that something is wrong with the house. The curse quickly consumes Matt and Jennifer. Matt's sister Susan is also haunted as the curse follows her back into her apartment. Yoko, a care worker, arrives at the house to find Emma alone before she encounters Kayako, who drags her up into the attic. Concerned about Yoko's disappearance, her employer, Alex, sends another care worker, Karen Davis, to take over the care of Emma. Karen discovers Toshio sealed up in a wardrobe at the house and later witnesses Kayako's spirit descending from the ceilings to claim Emma.
Alex arrives at the house and finds Emma dead and Karen in shock. He calls the police, who come with Detective Nakagawa. In the attic, Nakagawa and his partner Igarashi find Matt and Jennifer's bodies, along with a human's lower jaw. Meanwhile, Susan is pursued by Kayako around her office building. At home, Kayako attacks her, and she vanishes. While leaving work, Alex is killed by Yoko's jawless corpse. Kayako begins haunting Karen, who informs her boyfriend, Doug, of the situation.
Karen researches the house, eventually confronting Nakagawa, who explains that the curse consumed three of his colleagues investigating the Saeki deaths. That night, Nakagawa carries gasoline into the house to burn it down but is killed by Takeo. Karen races there after learning Doug has ventured to the Saeki house to look for her. She finds Doug paralyzed and attempts to flee with him. Kayako crawls down the stairs and latches onto Doug, who dies of shock. As Kayako closes in, Karen sees the gasoline and ignites it. Karen survives, and in the hospital, she learns that the house also survived the fire. Visiting Doug's body, Karen realizes that Kayako still haunts her.

title: Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer

tagline: Discover the secret of the Surfer.
overview: The Fantastic Four return to the big screen as a new and all powerful enemy threatens the Earth. The seemingly unstoppable 'Silver Surfer', but all is not what it seems and there are old and new enemies that pose a greater threat than the intrepid superheroes realize.
plot:
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer is a 2007 superhero film based on Marvel Comics' Fantastic Four and the sequel to Fantastic Four (2005). Directed by Tim Story from a screenplay by Don Payne and Mark Frost, it stars Ioan Gruffudd as Reed Richards, Jessica Alba as Sue Storm, Chris Evans as Johnny Storm and Michael Chiklis as Ben Grimm, with Julian McMahon as Victor Von Doom, and Doug Jones as the Silver Surfer, voiced by Laurence Fishburne.

The U.S. government asks Reed to track a mysterious object that is gouging craters across the globe and causing freak weather and power outages, just as he and Sue are preparing for their wedding and considering leaving the team. When the phenomenon disrupts the ceremony in New York, Johnny chases it and finds a silver alien riding a flying surfboard, who overpowers him. The encounter leaves Johnny able to swap powers with his teammates on contact. Reed discovers that every planet the Surfer has visited has been destroyed and predicts his next strike in London, where the team fails to stop him from draining the River Thames. The Surfer's passage also frees Doom from his frozen state in Latveria, and after a clash with the Surfer restores his human form, Doom persuades the U.S. military to make the team work with him.

Realizing the Surfer's board is the source of his power, Reed builds a pulse generator to separate them. In the Black Forest, the Surfer tells Sue that he is not the one seeking to destroy Earth before the pulse strips him of his board, and he is taken to Siberia and tortured by the military. Sue learns that he serves Galactus, a colossal cosmic entity that consumes inhabited planets, in exchange for sparing his own world, and that the board is guiding Galactus to Earth. Doom steals the board and flees to China, and in a battle in Shanghai he impales Sue. Johnny absorbs all the team's powers and, helped by Ben, defeats Doom and recovers the board. Reunited with it and moved by Sue's humanity, the Surfer revives her and flies off to confront Galactus, vanishing in a vast explosion. Reed and Sue choose to stay with the team and marry in Japan, and a mid-credits scene shows the Surfer coming back to life in space.

Released in the United States on June 15, 2007, the film opened at number one and grossed $301.9 million worldwide on a budget of $120–130 million, below its predecessor's total. Reviews were mixed, though many saw an improvement; Rotten Tomatoes gave it 38% approval.

title: The Constant Gardener
tagline: Love. At any cost.
overview: Justin Quayle is a low-level British diplomat who has always gone about his work very quietly, not causing any problems. But after his radical wife Tessa is killed he becomes determined to find out why, thrusting himself into the middle of a very dangerous conspiracy.
plot:
British diplomat and avid horticulturalist Justin Quayle is confronted by Amnesty International activist Tessa during a lecture in London. They strike up a romance, and marry after she accompanies him to his posting in Kenya. She befriends Belgian doctor Arnold Bluhm, leading to rumours of an affair. Tessa has no qualms confronting corruption, to the chagrin of Justin's superiors, and she loses a child late in pregnancy.
Tessa and Arnold connect recent local deaths to drug trials being conducted by the Kenyan-based company Three Bees using the drug Dypraxa. They write a damaging report on the drug and Tessa gives it to Justin's colleague Sandy Woodrow, the British High Commissioner, who sends it to Sir Bernard Pellegrin, head of the Africa Desk at the Foreign Office. Pellegrin responds with an incriminating letter to Sandy, which Tessa persuades him to show her, and she steals it before departing for Lokichogio with Arnold.
Sandy informs Justin that a white woman and black driver have been killed near Lake Turkana, and that Tessa and Arnold shared a room at Lodwar before hiring a car. Justin and Sandy identify Tessa's mutilated body, but Arnold's whereabouts remain unknown. Police confiscate Tessa's computer and files, but Justin finds her keepsake box, containing a letter from Sandy declaring his love for her and asking her to return Pellegrin's letter, and records of Three Bees' tests.
After Tessa's burial, Justin learns from his colleague Ghita that Tessa kept Arnold's secret that he was gay, as homosexuality is illegal in Kenya. Pursuing the truth about his wife's murder, he follows the trail of her report. Justin is briefly detained by police and confronts Three Bees' CEO Kenny Curtiss, but receives no answers.
Returning to London, Justin's passport is confiscated. He dines with Pellegrin, who lies that Arnold must have murdered Tessa, and believes that Justin has his incriminating letter. Justin meets with Tessa's cousin and lawyer Ham, and they access her computer files to reveal her investigation into Dypraxa and its manufacturer, Swiss-Canadian pharmaceutical conglomerate KDH, which hired Three Bees to test the drug on unsuspecting Kenyans as a treatment for tuberculosis.
Justin receives a threatening note and Ham provides him with a fake passport to travel to Germany to meet with Tessa's contact Birgit. She is part of a pharmaceutical watchdog group and is reluctant to speak due to the targeting of her group. Justin is attacked in his hotel room and warned to stop investigating. Arnold's body is found having been tortured to death, while the announcement of a safe Dypraxa causes KDH's share price to soar.
Returning to Kenya, Justin confronts Sandy, who admits that Tessa's report was silenced to save KDH from spending millions redeveloping the drug. Justin is approached by Curtiss, who has been betrayed by KDH, and brought to a mass grave of Dypraxa test subjects.

title: My Blueberry Nights
tagline: How do you say goodbye to someone you can't imagine living without?
overview: Elizabeth has just been through a particularly nasty breakup, and now she's ready to leave her friends and memories behind as she chases her dreams across the country. In order to support herself on her journey, Elizabeth picks up a series of waitress jobs along the way. As Elizabeth crosses paths with a series of lost souls whose yearnings are even greater than her own, their emotional turmoil ultimately helps her gain a greater understanding of her own problems...
plot:
Jeremy, an émigré from Manchester, owns a small New York City café. He provides customer Elizabeth with clues that reveal her boyfriend is cheating on her. Devastated, she breaks up with him and becomes a regular at the diner, arriving late at night for blueberry pie and to share stories with Jeremy. One night, after they are assaulted in separate incidents, Elizabeth falls asleep at the counter. Jeremy sneaks a kiss while she sleeps and she subtly smiles. Later that night, Elizabeth stands on a curb and sadly watches her ex-boyfriend and his new girlfriend through their apartment window.
Elizabeth, now calling herself Lizzie, drifts to Memphis, Tennessee. She takes two jobs, waitress by day and bartender by night, to earn enough money to eventually purchase a car. She regularly sends postcards to Jeremy without revealing where exactly she lives or works. He tries to locate her by calling and sending postcards to all the restaurants in the area, but to no avail.
One of Elizabeth's regulars at both jobs is local police officer Arnie Copeland, an alcoholic who cannot accept that his wife, Sue Lynne, has left him. She openly flaunts her new relationship with a younger man, deepening Arnie's sorrow. He shows Elizabeth his pocketful of AA sobriety tokens and recounts his many attempts at sobriety.
One night, while off duty in Elizabeth's bar, Arnie drunkenly threatens Sue Lynne with his gun if she leaves, but he doesn't shoot her. Later on, he drives drunk, crashes into a pole and dies. Elizabeth comforts Sue Lynne at the crash site, where she had first met him, suggesting he may have committed suicide. Before both women say goodbye to the town, Sue Lynne gives her Arnie's tab money, admitting she had made a mistake and she misses him.
Heading west, Elizabeth – now Beth – gets another server job at a casino in a small town in Nevada. She meets Leslie, an inveterate poker player who has lost all her money. Elizabeth lends her $2,200 in exchange for the money back, plus a third of her winnings. However, if she loses, then Elizabeth gets Leslie's car, a new Jaguar XK. When Leslie does lose, she fulfills her promise, but asks for a lift to Las Vegas to borrow money from her estranged father.
En route, a Vegas hospital calls to inform Leslie that her father has been admitted and is dying. She believes the call is a ruse to lure her back, but upon arrival she discovers that he actually died the previous night. Leslie announces she's keeping the car, which she had stolen from her father. He had sent her the vehicle's title and registration, despite their estrangement. She confesses she actually won the poker game and subsequently helps Elizabeth negotiate the purchase of her dream car.
Elizabeth returns to Manhattan and the café, where Jeremy has kept a stool at the counter reserved for her ever since she left. As she eats a slice of blueberry pie, Elizabeth realizes her feelings for him are reciprocated.

plot:
Planet Terror is a 2007 American exploitation horror film written and directed by Quentin Tarantino and Robert Rodriguez. The film stars Rose McGowan, Freddy Rodríguez, Josh Brolin, Bruce Dern, and Kim Darby.

The story begins with Cherry Darling (Rose McGowan), a young woman who lives in El Paso, Texas, with her boyfriend, Meg (Jordana Brewster). After being diagnosed with terminal cancer, Cherry decides to have her leg amputated. She then becomes involved with a group of women who are also having their limbs removed as part of an experimental treatment.

The story takes a dark turn when Cherry's boyfriend is killed by a group of Nazi scientists led by General Kilgore (Bruce Dern) and his accomplice, Dr. Wiesner (Willem Dafoe). The Nazis have been experimenting on women to create super-soldiers, and they plan to use the treated women as part of their army.

Cherry escapes from the Nazis and joins a group of survivors, including El Wey (Danny Trejo), a Mexican revolutionary who is also being pursued by the Nazis. Together, they embark on a mission to take down General Kilgore and his men.

As Cherry navigates her new reality, she meets Otis Driftwood (Freddy Rodríguez), a wheelchair-bound mechanic who becomes her love interest. The two form an unlikely bond as they work together to survive the Nazi threat.

The film's plot is interspersed with scenes of other characters, including El Wey and his men, who are fighting against the Nazis in Mexico. These scenes provide a sense of scope and scale to the story, highlighting the global reach of the Nazi threat.

Throughout the film, Tarantino and Rodriguez pay homage to classic exploitation films of the 1970s, incorporating elements such as over-the-top violence, graphic gore, and campy humor. The result is a film that is both a loving tribute to the genre and a fresh take on the exploitation horror subgenre.

As the story unfolds, Cherry and Otis find themselves in a series of increasingly absurd and violent situations, including a showdown with General Kilgore's men at a nightclub. In the end, Cherry and her allies manage to defeat the Nazis, but not before suffering significant losses.

The film ends with Cherry and Otis riding off into the sunset on motorcycles, ready to face whatever challenges come their way next. The final shot is of Cherry's prosthetic leg, which has become a symbol of her newfound strength and independence.

Overall, Planet Terror is a wildly entertaining and unapologetically violent film that is sure to appeal to fans of exploitation horror. With its over-the-top action sequences, graphic gore, and campy humor, it is a true classic of the genre.

title: Lara Croft: Tomb Raider
tagline: Born into Wealth. Groomed by the Elite. Trained for Combat.
overview: English aristocrat Lara Croft is skilled in hand-to-hand combat and in the middle of a battle with a secret society. The shapely archaeologist moonlights as a tomb raider to recover lost antiquities and meets her match in the evil Powell, who's in search of a powerful relic.
plot:
Lara Croft: Tomb Raider is a 2001 action-adventure film directed by Simon West, starring Angelina Jolie as the titular character. The movie is based on the popular video game series of the same name.

The film begins with Lara Croft (Angelina Jolie), a brilliant and fearless archaeologist, competing in an expedition to find the legendary Scion of Atlantis. However, she loses out to her rival, Walter Croft (Ciarán Hinds), who is revealed to be her father. The movie then cuts to 15 years later, where Lara is now a recluse, living off the grid and avoiding the media.

The story takes a turn when Lara's father dies under mysterious circumstances, and she receives a cryptic message from an unknown sender, claiming that he has hidden his most valuable treasure, the Scion of Atlantis. Believing her father was murdered to get to the treasure first, Lara sets out on a perilous journey to find it.

As Lara delves deeper into the mystery, she encounters a group of mercenaries led by the ruthless Rudi Brooks (Jon Voight), who are also after the Scion. Along the way, she meets Terry Sheridan (Noah Taylor), an American adventurer and friend of her father's, who joins her on her quest.

The plot thickens as Lara uncovers clues that suggest her father was not just a treasure hunter but also a spy working for a secret organization known as the Trinity. The more Lara learns about her father's past, the more she realizes that she is in grave danger and must use all her skills to stay one step ahead of her enemies.

As the story unfolds, Lara faces numerous challenges, including treacherous jungle terrain, deadly traps, and rival treasure hunters. She also discovers that the Scion of Atlantis holds the key to a powerful technology that could change the course of human history.

In the climactic final act, Lara confronts Rudi Brooks and his team in an epic battle at the temple where the Scion is hidden. With her wits, bravery, and athleticism, she outsmarts and outmaneuvers her foes, claiming the treasure and uncovering a shocking secret about her father's past.

The movie concludes with Lara emerging victorious but scarred by her experiences. She realizes that her father's legacy is not just about treasure hunting but also about protecting the world from those who would misuse powerful technologies. The film ends on a hopeful note, as Lara sets out to continue her father's work and make a difference in the world.

Overall, Lara Croft: Tomb Raider is an action-packed adventure that showcases Angelina Jolie's physicality and charisma as the iconic video game character. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the film has become a cult classic among fans of the franchise and action-adventure movies in general.

title: Lara Croft: Tomb Raider - The Cradle of Life
original_title: Lara Croft: Tomb Raider - The Cradle of Life
tagline: The lady returns.
overview: Lara Croft is tasked by MI6 to find the mythological Pandora's Box, an object from ancient legends which supposedly contains one of the deadliest plagues on Earth, before evil Nobel Prize-winning scientist turned bioterrorist Jonathan Reiss can get his hands on it. Lara ventures to an underwater temple in search of a magical luminous orb, the key to finding Pandora's Box, but after securing it, it is promptly stolen by the villainous leader of a Chinese crime syndicate who in turn plans to sell the orb to Reiss. Lara must recover the box before evil mastermind Reiss uses it to construct a weapon of catastrophic capabilities.
plot:
Lara Croft: Tomb Raider – The Cradle of Life is a 2003 action adventure film directed by Jan de Bont and written by Dean Georgaris, based on Core Design's Tomb Raider video games. It is the sequel to Lara Croft: Tomb Raider (2001). Angelina Jolie returns as Lara Croft, with Gerard Butler as Terry Sheridan, Ciarán Hinds as Jonathan Reiss, Djimon Hounsou as Kosa, Simon Yam as Chen Lo, Til Schweiger as Sean, Noah Taylor as Bryce and Chris Barrie as Hillary.

An earthquake on Santorini uncovers the Luna Temple of Alexander the Great, which holds a glowing orb etched with a code. Lara finds it, but her team is ambushed and killed by the Shay Ling crime syndicate, led by the brothers Chen Lo and Xien, who steal the orb. MI6 then tells her that the orb is a map to the legendary Cradle of Life, where Pandora's box, said to contain a deadly plague, is hidden. Chen plans to sell the orb to Reiss, a Nobel Prize-winning scientist turned bioweapons dealer. Lara agrees to help if MI6 frees her former lover Terry, an ex-Marine mercenary who knows Chen's operation.

Raiding Chen's lair, where he smuggles Terracotta Army figures, they learn the orb is bound for Shanghai. There Reiss takes the orb and executes Xien, but Lara tags the crate with a tracker. She and Terry find the orb in Reiss's Hong Kong lab. Captured, Lara learns Reiss plans to unleash the plague and spare only those he deems worthy, but Terry rescues her and they flee with the orb in wingsuits. Lara decodes it and locates the Cradle near Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania, but Reiss's men abduct her assistants Bryce and Hillary. In Africa, Lara joins her friend Kosa, but Reiss's mercenaries massacre their tribal escort and force Lara to lead them to a crater guarded by creatures called the Shadow Guardians. Placing the orb in a keyhole stops the creatures and opens the Cradle, a crystalline labyrinth where the laws of physics break down. Pandora's box floats there in a pool of acid. Lara throws Reiss into the acid, then shoots Terry when he refuses to give up the box, and returns it to the pool.

Made for $95 million, it was shot in Hong Kong, Santorini, Wales, Kenya and Britain. Paramount released it on July 25, 2003. It grossed $160.1 million worldwide, well below the first film. Paramount blamed the weak video game The Angel of Darkness. Critics found it better than the first film and praised Jolie, though Rotten Tomatoes reported 24% approval. A third film was abandoned when Jolie chose not to return.

title: Two Brothers
tagline: Two infant tiger cubs, separated from their parents and each other.
overview: Two tigers are separated as cubs and taken into captivity, only to be reunited years later as enemies by an explorer (Pearce) who inadvertently forces them to fight each other.
plot:
Two Brothers (French: Deux frères) is a 2004 adventure drama directed by Jean-Jacques Annaud about two Indochinese tiger cubs, Kumal and Sangha, who are separated from their parents and from each other, then reunited a year later as adults and find their way back home. Guy Pearce plays the adventurer and hunter Aidan McRory and Freddie Highmore plays Raoul Normandin, the young son of a French colonial administrator, with Jean-Claude Dreyfus as his father and Oanh Nguyen as a local prince. Pathé distributed the film in Europe and Universal in the United States.

The story is set in French colonial Cambodia in the 1920s. The cubs are born to a protective tigress and a tiger that McRory later kills. When the brothers are separated, their lives take very different paths. Kumal is caught by villagers and sold to a cruel circus run by Zerbino and Saladin, where abusive training forces him to perform dangerous tricks. Sangha is adopted for a time by eight-year-old Raoul, son of the administrator Eugene Normandin, but after a clash with the family dog he is sent to the menagerie of a palace.

McRory, a morally ambiguous figure, becomes tangled up in the fates of both tigers. After failing to satisfy the vain prince with a counterfeit tiger skin taken from the circus's elderly tiger, Caesar, he learns that the prince's prized fighting tiger is Sangha. The prince stages a fight between Sangha and Kumal as a public spectacle. The brothers attack each other at first but recognise one another in the middle of the fight and fall back into the playful games of their cubhood. When their handlers try to provoke them, chaos breaks out and the two tigers escape together into the wilderness, causing havoc in nearby villages as they go. McRory and Raoul set off to track them down. Raoul persuades Sangha to go back to the jungle, away from the dangers posed by people, and Kumal, remembering McRory's past kindness, spares the hunter. The brothers return to their ancestral temple and are reunited with their mother, whom they recognise by the bullet wound McRory once left in her ear.

Around 30 tigers were used in the film, most from French zoos and others from Thailand. Two Brothers opened in the United States on 25 June 2004 and earned about $62 million worldwide. Reviews were generally positive, with 79% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and audiences polled by CinemaScore gave it an "A−".

title: In the Bedroom
tagline: A young man. An older woman. Her ex-husband. Things are about to explode...
overview: Summertime on the coast of Maine, "In the Bedroom" centers on the inner dynamics of a family in transition. Matt Fowler is a doctor practicing in his native Maine and is married to New York born Ruth Fowler, a music teacher. His son is involved in a love affair with a local single mother. As the beauty of Maine's brief and fleeting summer comes to an end, these characters find themselves in the midst of unimaginable tragedy.
plot:
In coastal Rockport, Maine, Matt and Ruth Fowler enjoy a happy marriage and a good relationship with their son Frank, a recent college graduate home for the summer. Frank has fallen in love with a divorced older woman with children, Natalie Strout; Ruth is concerned about the relationship, while Matt thinks it is only a fling. The family struggles to communicate their feelings to one another, especially regarding Frank's relationship and schooling.
Frank is about to begin graduate school for architecture but is considering staying in town to continue working as a fisherman and to be near Natalie and her kids. Natalie's ex-husband, Richard Strout, tries to find a way into his ex-wife and children's lives, going to increasingly violent lengths to get his intentions across to Natalie, including assaulting Frank.
Frank rushes to Natalie's home one evening after receiving a frightened phone call from one of her children. He arrives to find the living room trashed and Natalie in distress. She tells him Richard just left, but he returns almost immediately. Natalie takes the boys upstairs, and Frank insists through the locked front door that Richard leave. He feigns doing so, only to break in through the back door with a handgun; in the ensuing scuffle, Frank is shot and killed.
Though equally devastated, Matt and Ruth grieve in different ways, with Matt putting on a brave face and quickly returning to work, while Ruth becomes reclusive and quiet. The couple retreat with friends Willis and Katie Grinnel to a secluded cottage for a weekend, but Ruth is distant and Matt begins to drink heavily.
At Richard's bail hearing, Natalie is pressed by his lawyer over whether she saw the shooting, as she initially testified when police arrived on the scene, and she tearfully shakes her head, as she only heard what happened. The tension between Matt and Ruth increases when their lawyer informs them that because of the change from Natalie's original testimony, Richard was allowed out on bail, and his defense will argue that Frank's death was an accident, meaning Richard will most likely be charged with accidental manslaughter and only serve five to ten years in prison. The couple begin to see Richard around town.
Matt approaches Natalie at work to check in on her and the two have a well-intentioned but strained conversation. Matt takes the boat out to catch lobsters to feel a connection with Frank, but he struggles with it and is pinched by a lobster, leaving a bleeding wound on one finger which Matt bandages. Natalie approaches Ruth at work and attempts to apologize, but Ruth slaps her before dismissively returning to her work. Natalie leaves in tears. Later that day, Ruth runs into Richard at the grocery store.

title: We Own the Night
tagline: Two brothers on opposite sides of the law. Beyond their differences lies loyalty.
overview: A New York nightclub manager tries to save his brother and father from Russian mafia hitmen.
plot:
In November 1988 in Brooklyn, New York, Robert "Bobby" Grusinsky is the manager of the El Caribe nightclub in Brighton Beach, which is owned by his boss, fur importer Marat Buzhayev, whose nephew, drug lord Vadim Nezhinski, is a patron of the joint. Estranged from both his father Albert ("Burt"), an NYPD Deputy Chief, and brother Joseph, a newly minted Captain, Bobby uses the maiden name of his late mother, Carol Green, as a part of his work alias and opts for a life of pleasure with his girlfriend Amada Juarez and best friend Louis "Jumbo" Falsetti, with a plan to soon run his own club in Manhattan. Joseph, who has just been named to be the head of a new anti-drug unit, warns Bobby that he will soon lead a bust on the spot with the aim of netting Vadim.
Bobby is jailed for drug possession and resisting arrest in the wake of the raid on November 22, souring his ties with Burt and Joseph, who both bail him out of jail the next day; he and Joseph later engage in a harsh feud. That evening, a masked Vadim shoots Joseph in the face outside his house and firebombs his car, causing him to be confined at Jamaica Hospital Medical Center for 4 months. A remorseful Bobby agrees to the request of Michael Solo, a comrade of Burt, to go inside Vadim's drug operation behind Burt's back. When the transceiver hidden in his lighter is exposed, he evades death as Vadim is nabbed by the police.
The bond between Bobby and Amada decays while they are hiding at the Kew Motor Inn, and they prep for a move to the Corona Hotel after Vadim flees from Rikers Island on March 20, 1989. In the midst of a heavy deluge, his men ambush the three-car escort, one of whom fatally wounds Burt with a shot to the neck. Bobby passes out in the rain upon seeing his body, wakes up a few hours later atop a bed in a suite at the Sheraton near Kennedy Airport, and breaks down when Joseph tells him that Burt is dead. At the funeral, Jack Shapiro, a colleague of Burt, donates Burt's Korean War combat ribbon to Joseph, and Michael informs him of a Russian cocaine shipment that is set to arrive in the area in the next week.
Amada breaks up with Bobby once he chooses to join the NYPD to avenge the death of his father, upset because he neglected to ask for her input or consent prior to pursuing such a risky change of career. Sworn into the force due to his special knowledge, provided that he will undergo training at the Police Academy once the case is wrapped up, he questions Jumbo outside El Caribe on the night of April 2, 1989; Jumbo admits that he was coerced into betraying Bobby by leaking word from Amada regarding the pair's location to Marat and Vadim. The brothers plan a final sting set for that Tuesday, as he recounts that per Jumbo, Marat's grandchildren, whom he takes to Floyd Bennett Field on Tuesdays, act as his couriers. During the sting, Joseph is numbed by his prior injury and is thus unable to proceed, and so Bobby chases Vadim into the reed beds.

title: Persepolis
tagline: The film Iran didn't want the world to see.
overview: In 1970s Iran, Marjane 'Marji' Statrapi watches events through her young eyes and her idealistic family of a long dream being fulfilled of the hated Shah's defeat in the Iranian Revolution of 1979. However as Marji grows up, she witnesses first hand how the new Iran, now ruled by Islamic fundamentalists, has become a repressive tyranny on its own.
plot:
At Orly Airport in Paris, Marjane "Marji" Satrapi prepares to board a plane to Tehran, but changes her mind at the last moment. She spends the whole day at the airport, reflecting on her life before her departure from France.
During the 1979 Islamic Revolution against Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi, Marji's upper-middle-class family participates in the rallies, though she is forbidden from attending. Marji's uncle Anoosh comes to dinner upon release from prison, inspiring Marji with stories of his life on the run from the government. The Shah is deposed, and elections for a new leading power commence; Islamic fundamentalists win the elections and impose strict Islamic law, forcing women to dress "modestly" and wear headscarves. Anoosh is rearrested and executed for his political beliefs. Over time, many Iranians escape abroad.
The Iran–Iraq War breaks out and the Iranian government takes away even more social freedoms. Marji's uncle Taher suffers a heart attack and must go to England for surgery, but only those approved by the Board of Health can leave the country. When Marji's aunt seeks permission, she finds that the hospital director is her former window washer, who is incompetent and submissive to religion. Marji and her father visit Khosro for a fake passport. Khosro is sheltering Niloufar, a woman wanted for her Communist beliefs. When Niloufar is caught and executed, Khosro flees. Taher dies afterward.
As she grows up, Marji buys heavy metal music on the black market and wears Western clothing. When she rebuts a teacher's lies about government abuses, she is expelled. Fearing her arrest, her parents send her to a French lycée in Vienna to live with her mother's best friend. Marjane is later sent to live in a boarding house with Catholic nuns. Marji makes few friends and feels isolated. After she insults a nun, she is thrown out. She moves from house to house until she rents a room from Dr. Frau Schloss, a former teacher with an unstable personality.
One night, as she leaves a party where she lies about being French, Marji hears her grandmother's voice telling her to stay true to herself. She develops a relationship with Markus, but it ends after she catches him cheating on her with another woman. Schloss accuses Marji of stealing, and Marji leaves. She spends the day on a park bench, reflecting upon her actions and realizing she has nowhere to go. After living on the street for a few months, she contracts bronchitis and almost dies. She awakens in a Viennese hospital, where she is allowed to make a phone call home.
Marji returns to Iran with her family's hopes that the end of the war will improve their lives. She grows depressed, and attempts suicide by overdosing on medication. She dreams of meeting God, who insists that her time is not over. Jolted out of her depression, she attends university and starts dating fellow student Reza.

title: No Good Deed
tagline: HE was more than a cop. SHE was more than a thief.
overview: While doing a friend a favor and searching for a runaway teenager, a police detective stumbles upon a bizarre band of criminals about to pull off a bank robbery.
plot:
No Good Deed, also known as The House on Turk Street, is an American crime thriller of 2002 directed by Bob Rafelson, his last feature film. Christopher Cannan and Steve Barancik wrote the screenplay, updating Dashiell Hammett's 1924 story "The House in Turk Street". Samuel L. Jackson stars as the police detective Jack Friar, with Milla Jovovich as Erin, Stellan Skarsgård as the gang leader Tyrone, Doug Hutchison as the volatile Hoop and Joss Ackland and Grace Zabriskie as the Quarres.

Jack, a diabetic auto-theft detective and amateur cellist, is about to leave for a week of music-making when a neighbor begs him to bring home her runaway teenage daughter. His search leads him to a house on Turk Street, where he stumbles by chance onto a crew in the final stages of a bank robbery: a multimillion-dollar computer heist masterminded by the meticulous Tyrone. The gang's hideout is fronted by a harmless-looking older couple, the Quarres, and the plan depends on David, a bank official who believes Erin is in love with him. The criminals tie Jack to a chair.

Erin, Tyrone's glamorous girlfriend, turns out to be a skilled manipulator who quietly plays the men in her life against one another. Hoop imagines they will ditch Tyrone and take the money. When the others leave to carry out the robbery, Erin is left alone to guard Jack. The two share secrets; Tyrone, he learns, brought her from Russia, where she was a piano prodigy. When Jack slips into a diabetic coma, she fetches insulin from his house and brings back his cello, and later unties him for an intimate, erotically charged cello lesson. Tied up again, he tries to burn through his bonds over a flame on the kitchen stove. Meanwhile Mr. Quarre waits to fly the robbers away. The heist proceeds until David refuses to hand over a password-protected disk holding the transfer data unless he sees Erin, and Hoop reacts violently. Caught between her loyalty to her partners and her growing feelings for the captive, Erin keeps all three men guessing, and Jack cannot tell whether she is sincere or manipulating him too. The ending strikes the cynical, unsentimental note of classic film noir.

The film was screened at the 24th Moscow International Film Festival in June 2002, opened first in Italy that autumn and reached American theaters in September 2003. Made for about $12 million, it grossed about $1.4 million. Reviews were mostly negative; Roger Ebert, however, called it an absorbing, atmospheric noir.

title: The Wedding Planner
tagline: His big day is her big problem.
overview: San Francisco's premiere wedding planner, Mary Fiore is rescued from an accident by the man of her dreams, paediatrician Steve Edison, only to find he is the fiancé of her latest client. As Mary continues making the wedding arrangements, she and Steve are put into a string of uncomfortable situations that force them to face their mutual attraction.
plot:
Ambitious San Francisco wedding planner Mary Fiore is reintroduced to childhood acquaintance Massimo by her father Salvatore, who wants them to marry, but Mary declines. She hopes that her boss, Geri, will make her a partner at their company, and is hired to plan heiress Fran Donolly's society wedding to long-term boyfriend Eddie. While reporting her success to colleague Penny on the phone, Mary gets her shoe heel stuck in a manhole cover. plot:
The Patriot is a historical drama film directed by Roland Emmerich, released in 2000 by Columbia Pictures.

The movie takes place during the American Revolutionary War and follows the story of Benjamin Martin (played by Mel Gibson), a widowed farmer who lives on his plantation in South Carolina with his two sons, Gabriel (Heath Ledger) and William (Jason Isaacs). The family is struggling to survive due to the British occupation of their land.

When the British army arrives at the Martin farm, they demand that Benjamin's sons join the British Army as loyalists. However, Benjamin refuses to send his sons, citing his loyalty to the American cause. Gabriel, who has been trained in combat by Benjamin, is particularly resistant to joining the British Army and instead decides to fight for the Americans.

As tensions rise between the British and the Americans, Benjamin's farm becomes a target for British raids. The family is forced to flee their home, and Benjamin's sons are captured by the British. Gabriel is eventually killed in battle, while William is taken prisoner and later executed by the British for his involvement with the American resistance.

Consumed by grief and anger, Benjamin sets out on a mission of revenge against the British army that killed his son. He joins the Continental Army and becomes a key figure in the war effort, using his knowledge of the land and his combat skills to help the Americans defeat the British.

As the war rages on, Benjamin's actions become increasingly radicalized, leading him to take drastic measures to protect his fellow soldiers and avenge his son's death. The movie culminates with a dramatic battle between the Continental Army and the British at Cowpens, where Benjamin plays a crucial role in the American victory.

Throughout the film, Mel Gibson delivers a powerful performance as Benjamin Martin, bringing depth and nuance to the character. The supporting cast, including Jason Isaacs and Miranda Richardson, also deliver strong performances that add to the overall tension and drama of the movie.

Overall, The Patriot is a gripping historical drama that explores themes of loyalty, sacrifice, and revenge in the context of the American Revolutionary War. With its stunning action sequences, memorable characters, and epic scope, it's no wonder that this film has become a classic of the genre.

title: Hostage
tagline: Every second counts.
overview: When a mafia accountant is taken hostage on his beat, a police officer – wracked by guilt from a prior stint as a negotiator – must negotiate the standoff, even as his own family is held captive by the mob.
plot:
Hostage is a 2005 American action thriller film directed by Florent Emilio Siri and starring Bruce Willis, Kevin Pollak, and Radha Mitchell.

The movie begins with U.S. Marshal Andy Fiddler (Bruce Willis) who is tasked with protecting the President of the United States, James Marshall (Kevin Pollak), during his visit to Los Angeles. However, things take a turn for the worse when a group of heavily armed terrorists, led by the ruthless and cunning Emil Rottmayer (Peter Stormare), take several people hostage at a bank in downtown LA.

The terrorists demand that the President be released from his protective detail and handed over to them, or else they will kill their hostages. The situation escalates when Andy Fiddler is forced to make an impossible choice: either he can save the President's life by releasing Rottmayer and his men, or he can try to rescue the hostages.

As the standoff unfolds, we see flashbacks of Andy's troubled past, including a traumatic event that led him to become a U.S. Marshal. We also learn about his complicated relationship with his wife, Julia (Radha Mitchell), who is struggling to cope with her husband's absence and emotional distance.

Meanwhile, Rottmayer reveals that he has a personal vendetta against the President, who had previously thwarted one of his previous plans. The situation becomes increasingly tense as the hours tick by, and Andy must use all his skills and experience to try and defuse the situation without putting anyone in harm's way.

As the standoff reaches its climax, Andy comes up with a plan to rescue the hostages and take down Rottmayer and his men. In a heart-pumping action sequence, Andy faces off against Rottmayer in a desperate bid to save the day.

In the end, Andy successfully rescues the hostages, but not without sustaining serious injuries himself. The movie ends with Andy returning home to Julia, who has finally begun to understand the depth of his emotional scars and is willing to work through them together.

Throughout the film, Bruce Willis delivers a strong performance as the stoic and determined U.S. Marshal Andy Fiddler, while Kevin Pollak shines as the President, bringing a sense of vulnerability and humanity to the role. The supporting cast, including Radha Mitchell and Peter Stormare, add depth and complexity to the story.

Overall, Hostage is a tense and thrilling action movie that explores themes of duty, loyalty, and redemption. With its strong performances, clever plot twists, and heart-pumping action sequences, it's a must-see for fans of the genre.
