title: The Chronicles of Narnia: Prince Caspian
original_title: The Chronicles of Narnia: Prince Caspian
tagline: Everything you know is about to change forever.
overview: One year after their incredible adventures in the Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe, Peter, Edmund, Lucy and Susan Pevensie return to Narnia to aid a young prince whose life has been threatened by the evil King Miraz. Now, with the help of a colorful cast of new characters, including Trufflehunter the badger and Nikabrik the dwarf, the Pevensie clan embarks on an incredible quest to ensure that Narnia is returned to its rightful heir.
plot:
The Chronicles of Narnia: Prince Caspian is a 2008 high fantasy film directed by Andrew Adamson and written by Adamson, Christopher Markus and Stephen McFeely. Based on Prince Caspian (1951), the second published novel in C. S. Lewis's series, it is the second installment in The Chronicles of Narnia film series. Ben Barnes stars as Caspian, with Georgie Henley, Skandar Keynes, William Moseley and Anna Popplewell reprising their roles as the Pevensie children, Sergio Castellitto as King Miraz, Peter Dinklage as Trumpkin, and Liam Neeson voicing Aslan.

Nearly 1,300 Narnian years after the Pevensie siblings ruled as kings and queens and returned to their own world, Narnia has been conquered by the Telmarines. Caspian, a young Telmarine prince, is woken one night by his tutor, Doctor Cornelius, who warns him that his uncle, Lord Miraz, has just had a son and now intends to kill Caspian to secure the throne for his own heir. Cornelius gives him an ancient magical horn that once belonged to Queen Susan and tells him to use it only in great need. Fleeing into the woods, Caspian is rescued by surviving Narnians, the dwarfs Trumpkin and Nikabrik and the talking badger Trufflehunter; Trumpkin is captured by soldiers. Caspian blows the horn.

In wartime England, a year after their first adventure, the four Pevensies are waiting on a London Underground platform when they are suddenly pulled back into Narnia. They find their castle, Cair Paravel, in ruins and rescue Trumpkin from execution, learning how much time has passed. Lucy glimpses Aslan pointing the way, but her older siblings do not believe her. The Pevensies join Caspian and the Narnians, who have taken refuge at Aslan's How, and tensions arise between Peter and Caspian over leadership. A disastrous night raid on Miraz's castle leaves many Narnians dead, and Nikabrik's plot to summon the White Witch is narrowly thwarted. As Miraz's army advances, Peter challenges him to single combat to buy time, while Lucy sets out to find Aslan and bring help.

The film received generally positive reviews, though many considered it darker and less charming than the first film. It grossed about $419 million worldwide, a significant decline from its predecessor, which prompted Disney to withdraw from the series before the third film was made with 20th Century Fox.

title: The Bourne Identity
tagline: He was the perfect weapon until he became the target.
overview: Wounded to the brink of death and suffering from amnesia, Jason Bourne is rescued at sea by a fisherman. With nothing to go on but a Swiss bank account number, he starts to reconstruct his life, but finds that many people he encounters want him dead. However, Bourne realizes that he has the combat and mental skills of a world-class spy—but who does he work for?
plot:
In the Mediterranean Sea, Italian fishermen rescue an American man adrift with gunshot wounds in his back. Tending to his wounds, they find he has amnesia but shows fluency in several languages. A tiny laser projector found implanted in his hip gives the number of a safe deposit box in Zurich. While investigating this, he discovers he is highly trained in hand-to-hand combat after incapacitating two Zurich police officers.
In the deposit box he finds various currencies, passports, IDs with different names, and a handgun. The man takes everything but the gun and starts using the name on the American passport, Jason Bourne. After Bourne's departure, a bank employee contacts Operation Treadstone, a CIA black ops program. Its head, Alexander Conklin, issues alerts to police to capture Bourne and assigns three agents – codenamed Castel, Manheim, and the Professor – to kill him.
CIA director of operations Ward Abbott contacts Conklin about a failed assassination attempt against exiled African dictator Wombosi and promises to deal with the agent responsible. Bourne evades the Swiss police by using his U.S. passport to enter the American consulate but is pursued by Marine guards.
Bourne escapes after offering $20,000 to Marie Kreutz, a 26-year-old German woman he saw at the consulate, to drive him to an address in Paris. From the apartment, Bourne contacts a hotel to inquire about the names on his passports. A "John Michael Kane" was registered but died two weeks before in a car crash. Castel ambushes Bourne and Marie in the apartment, but Bourne gets the upper hand. Instead of allowing himself to be interrogated, Castel throws himself from a window to his death.
While searching through Castel's belongings, Marie finds wanted posters of Bourne and herself. Frightened, she agrees to help him. After they evade the police in Marie's car, they spend the night in a Paris hotel.
Wombosi obsesses over the attempt on his life. Conklin, having anticipated this, has planted a body identified as John Michael Kane in a Paris morgue to appear to be the assailant. Wombosi is unconvinced and threatens to report the CIA's actions to the media. The Professor assassinates Wombosi on Conklin's orders.
Bourne, posing as Kane, learns about the failed assassination attempt on Wombosi's yacht, and that the assassin was shot twice in the back during the escape, ultimately realizing that he was responsible. He and Marie take refuge in the French countryside home of Marie's half-brother Eamon and his children.
Under pressure from Abbott to handle the matter, Conklin tracks Bourne's location and sends the Professor to kill him. Bourne mortally wounds the Professor, who reveals their shared connection to Treadstone before dying. Bourne sends Marie, Eamon, and the children away for their protection. He contacts Conklin via the Professor's phone, and they agree to meet alone in Paris.

title: The Bourne Supremacy
tagline: They should have left him alone.
overview: When a CIA operation to purchase classified Russian documents is blown by a rival agent, who then shows up in the sleepy seaside village where Bourne and Marie have been living. The pair run for their lives and Bourne, who promised retaliation should anyone from his former life attempt contact, is forced to once again take up his life as a trained assassin to survive.
plot:
The Bourne Supremacy is a 2004 action-thriller film directed by Paul Greengrass, starring Matt Damon as Jason Bourne. The movie is the sequel to The Bourne Identity and the second installment in the Bourne series.

The film begins with Jason Bourne (Matt Damon) living under an assumed identity in Paris, France. He has been trying to piece together his past, but his memories are fragmented and unclear. Bourne's life is disrupted when he discovers that his current identity is not genuine, and he must flee the city to avoid being caught.

Bourne's search for answers leads him to a mysterious woman named Marie Kreutz (Franka Potente), who claims to be an old friend from his past. She provides him with information about his true identity and the circumstances surrounding his amnesia. However, their conversation is interrupted by a group of assassins sent by the CIA, led by Noah Vosen (David Strathairn).

As Bourne navigates through Paris, he uncovers evidence that suggests the CIA is involved in a conspiracy to kill him. He also discovers that his memories are being manipulated and altered by the agency. The more Bourne learns, the more he realizes that his entire life has been fabricated.

Bourne's investigation takes him to Washington D.C., where he encounters Pamela Landy (Joan Allen), a CIA agent who is initially tasked with capturing him. However, as she delves deeper into the conspiracy, she begins to question her own allegiances and ultimately joins forces with Bourne.

The plot thickens when Bourne discovers that his memories are being manipulated by the CIA's black ops program, Operation Outcome. He also learns that he was involved in a failed assassination attempt on a Russian diplomat, which led to his amnesia. The more Bourne learns about his past, the more he realizes that he is not just an ordinary man but a highly trained assassin.

As the story unfolds, Bourne and Landy work together to uncover the truth behind Operation Outcome and the conspiracy surrounding his identity. They are pursued by Vosen and his team of assassins, who will stop at nothing to eliminate Bourne.

The film's climax features an intense car chase through the streets of Washington D.C., followed by a confrontation between Bourne and Vosen in a hotel room. In the end, Bourne manages to outsmart Vosen and escape, but not before discovering that his memories are still fragmented and unclear.

The Bourne Supremacy received widespread critical acclaim for its gripping storyline, well-developed characters, and intense action sequences. The film's success can be attributed to Matt Damon's performance as Jason Bourne, who brought depth and nuance to the character. The movie's themes of identity, loyalty, and deception are timeless and continue to captivate audiences to this day.

Overall, The Bourne Supremacy is a masterclass in storytelling, with a complex plot that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats. The film's success paved the way for future installments in the Bourne series, cementing Jason Bourne's place as one of the most iconic action heroes in cinema history.

title: The Bourne Ultimatum
tagline: Remember everything. Forgive nothing.
overview: Bourne is brought out of hiding once again by reporter Simon Ross who is trying to unveil Operation Blackbriar, an upgrade to Project Treadstone, in a series of newspaper columns. Information from the reporter stirs a new set of memories, and Bourne must finally uncover his dark past while dodging The Company's best efforts to eradicate him.
plot:
The Bourne Ultimatum is a 2007 action-thriller film directed by Paul Greengrass, starring Matt Damon as Jason Bourne. The movie is the third installment in the Bourne series and concludes the story of the amnesiac assassin.

Beginning:
The film opens with Jason Bourne (Matt Damon) on the run from the CIA, who are trying to capture him for his alleged crimes. Bourne is haunted by fragmented memories of his past, which he struggles to piece together. He encounters Nicky Parsons (Julia Stiles), a former CIA operative who helps him uncover more about his identity.

Plot Development:
As Bourne delves deeper into his past, he discovers that the CIA has been experimenting on him using advanced techniques such as memory erasure and implantation. He also learns that he was created by the Treadstone program, a secret black ops organization within the CIA. The program's goal was to create super-soldiers through mind control and conditioning.

Bourne's investigation leads him to uncover a conspiracy involving the CIA's attempts to cover up their involvement in the assassination of several world leaders, including the President of Russia. He also discovers that his memories are false and that he is not who he thinks he is.

As Bourne gets closer to the truth, he is pursued by the CIA and other agents, including Noah Vosen (David Strathairn), a ruthless agent tasked with capturing him. Bourne's only ally is Pamela Landy (Joan Allen), a senior CIA officer who begins to question her agency's motives.

Ending:
The film culminates in an intense action sequence where Bourne confronts Vosen and the CIA's attempts to silence him. In a thrilling finale, Bourne outsmarts his pursuers and escapes, but not before discovering that he is still being hunted by the CIA.

In a surprising twist, it is revealed that Bourne has been playing into the hands of the CIA all along, using his skills to gather intelligence on their operations. The film ends with Bourne walking away from the chaos, leaving the audience wondering what will happen next in his journey.

Overall, The Bourne Ultimatum is a gripping and intense thriller that explores themes of identity, loyalty, and the blurred lines between good and evil. Matt Damon's performance as Jason Bourne cements his status as one of Hollywood's most iconic action heroes.

title: Spanglish
tagline: Every family has a hero.
overview: Mexican immigrant and single mother Flor Moreno finds housekeeping work with Deborah and John Clasky, a well-off couple with two children of their own. When Flor admits she can't handle the schedule because of her daughter, Cristina, Deborah decides they should move into the Clasky home. Cultures clash and tensions run high as Flor and the Claskys struggle to share space while raising their children on their own, and very different, terms.
plot:
In Cristina Moreno's Princeton University application essay, she tells the story of a year from her childhood and how it shaped who she is today.
In 1992, Flor Moreno, a Mexican single mother, moved to the United States ("economy class," according to Cristina's letter) to seek a better life for her and her daughter. Settling in a Latino community in Los Angeles, Flor has no need to learn English, though Cristina does.
Flor works two jobs to support them, but, as Cristina blossoms, realizes she needs to watch her more closely. So she gets a job as a housekeeper for John and Deborah Clasky; their children Bernice and Georgie; and Deborah's mother, Evelyn Wright.
John is a chef and easy-going family man. Deborah is a businesswoman who was laid off, so is now a stay-at-home mother. Evelyn is a retired singer who tends to drink to excess. Deborah is uptight, neurotic and insecure. She body-shames Bernice and bullies John by demanding he always back her up. He is torn between defending his kids' mental health and his domineering wife. Flor tries to build Bernice's self-confidence with small acts of kindness, especially when Deborah is harsh.
Flor gets on well with the Claskys despite the language barrier. When Deborah rents a house for the summer, she demands Flor live in while they are there, as commuting from LA to Malibu by bus is unfeasible. Faced with losing her job, Flor reluctantly agrees to bring Cristina to live with the Claskys for the summer. Cristina is instantly dazzled by the Claskys' wealthy lifestyle.
Deborah quickly attaches to the beautiful and personable Cristina, ignoring Bernice. Flor does not approve of the attention. John unwittingly angers Flor when he offers to pay the children a set amount for each bit of sea glass they find on the beach. Cristina earnestly searches for hours, earning $640 for her efforts.
Flor and John argue, with Cristina as an interpreter. Flor wants to leave because of the awkward family dynamic. To Cristina's delight, he convinces her to stay, and Flor starts an English course so she can better communicate with them. Deborah begins an affair with a real estate agent.
John is tipped off to a critic visiting his restaurant; not wanting the additional social pressures of being famed for his cooking, he unsuccessfully attempts to offer a good but not great dish. When John's restaurant subsequently receives an enthusiastic review, he stresses about maintaining standards, but Deborah is allegedly so happy with the news she has sex with John. She also secures Cristina a scholarship to Bernice's private school, upsetting Flor, who is concerned her daughter might become an outcast or lose her individuality there. As Cristina begs to attend the school, Flor agrees but feels that Deborah is overstepping her bounds and voices her concerns to John, who tells her he empathizes as Bernice's own mother does not support her.

title: The Aviator
tagline: The way of the future
overview: A biopic depicting the life of filmmaker and aviation pioneer Howard Hughes from 1927 to 1947, during which time he became a successful film producer and an aviation magnate, while simultaneously growing more unstable due to severe obsessive-compulsive disorder.
plot:
In 1913 Houston, eight-year-old Howard Hughes's mother gives him a bath and teaches him to spell "quarantine", warning him about the recent cholera outbreak. Fourteen years later, in 1927, he begins to direct his film Hell's Angels, and hires Noah Dietrich to manage the day-to-day operations of his business empire.
After the release of The Jazz Singer (1927), the first partially talking film, Hughes becomes obsessed with shooting his film realistically, and decides to convert the movie to a sound film. Despite the film being a hit, Hughes remains unsatisfied with the result and orders it to be recut after its Hollywood premiere. He becomes romantically involved with actress Katharine Hepburn, who helps to ease the symptoms of his worsening obsessive–compulsive disorder (OCD) and germaphobia.
In 1935, Hughes test-flies the H-1 Racer, pushing it to a new speed record despite having to crash-land into a beet field when the aircraft runs out of fuel. Three years later, he flies around the world in four days, breaking the world record. He subsequently purchases majority interest in Transcontinental & Western Air (TWA).
Juan Trippe, company rival and chairman of Pan Am, asks his crony, Senator Ralph Owen Brewster, to introduce the Community Airline Bill, which would give Pan Am exclusivity on international air travel. Hepburn grows tired of Hughes's eccentricity and workaholism, and leaves him for fellow actor Spencer Tracy. Hughes quickly finds a new love interest with 15-year-old Faith Domergue, and later actress Ava Gardner. However, he still has feelings for Hepburn, and bribes a reporter to keep reports about her affair with the married Tracy out of the press.
In the mid-1940s, Hughes contracts two projects with the Army Air Forces, one for a spy aircraft, and another for a troop transport unit for use in World War II.
In 1946, with the H-4 Hercules flying boat still in construction, Hughes finishes the XF-11 reconnaissance aircraft and takes it for a test flight. However, one of the engines fails midflight; he crashes in Beverly Hills and is severely injured, but miraculously survives. The army cancels its order for the H-4 Hercules, although Hughes still continues the development with his own money. Dietrich informs Hughes that he must choose between funding the airlines or his flying boat. Hughes orders Dietrich to mortgage the TWA assets so he can continue the development.
By 1947, his OCD worsens and Hughes becomes increasingly paranoid, planting microphones and tapping Gardner's phone lines to keep track of her, until she kicks him out of her house. The FBI searches his home for incriminating evidence of war profiteering, searching through his possessions.
Brewster privately offers to drop the charges if Hughes sells TWA to Trippe, but Hughes refuses. Hughes's OCD symptoms become extreme, and he retreats into an isolated "germ-free zone" for three months.

title: Shopgirl
overview: Mirabelle is a disenchanted salesgirl and aspiring artist who sells gloves and accessories at a department store. She has two men in her life: wealthy divorcée Ray Porter and struggling musician Jeremy. Mirabelle falls in love with the glamorous Ray, and her life takes a magical turn, but eventually she realizes that she must empower herself and make a choice between them.
plot:
Shopgirl is a 2005 American romantic comedy-drama film directed by Anand Tucker from a screenplay by Steve Martin, based on his 2000 novella. It follows a complicated love triangle between a disenchanted salesgirl, a wealthy older man and an aimless young man. Claire Danes stars as Mirabelle Buttersfield, Martin as Ray Porter and Jason Schwartzman as Jeremy, with Bridgette Wilson and Frances Conroy also in the cast.

Mirabelle, a young aspiring artist from Vermont, works behind the women's glove counter at Saks Fifth Avenue in Beverly Hills. Depressed and lonely, she finds herself courted by two very different men. Jeremy, a socially inept, penniless graphic designer and would-be typographer, meets her in a laundromat, but she loses interest after an awkward first date and a failed attempt at sex. Ray, a suave, wealthy and divorced older man, buys a pair of gloves from her and has them delivered to her apartment with a dinner invitation. After several dates they sleep together, and the next morning Ray explains that he does not want anything serious because he constantly travels between Los Angeles and Seattle, but she believes he wants to commit. As their affair continues, Jeremy leaves as a roadie for the band Hot Tears, where he discovers self-help tapes about relating to women. Ray lavishes Mirabelle with gifts and pays off her student loans rather than offering real affection, and when she stops taking her antidepressants, he takes her to a psychiatrist and cares for her. After Ray confesses to sleeping with a former girlfriend on a business trip, Mirabelle ends things, but she later accepts his apology and joins him in New York, where she feels lost at a lavish party. Back in Los Angeles, when Ray mentions that he is looking for a larger apartment in New York in case he meets someone and wants children, Mirabelle leaves him for good. She quits Saks to work as a receptionist at an art gallery, and Jeremy, now pursuing her properly, wins her love. At her own exhibition at the gallery, Ray apologizes and admits he did love her before she runs into Jeremy's arms.

Released by Buena Vista Pictures on October 21, 2005, Shopgirl grossed $11.7 million worldwide and received positive reviews, with critics singling out Danes. It was nominated for four Satellite Awards, including Best Picture – Musical or Comedy.

title: Return to Me
tagline: A comedy straight from the heart
overview: It took a lot of cajoling to get Bob, a recently widowed architect, to go on a blind date at a quirky Irish-Italian eatery. Once there, he's smitten instantly not with his date but with the sharp-witted waitress. Everything seems to be going great until an unbelievable truth is revealed, one that could easily break both of their hearts for good.
plot:
Bob and Elizabeth Rueland live and work in Chicago. Bob is an architect and Elizabeth is a zoologist at Lincoln Park Zoo.
On the night of her fundraiser for a new primate house, Bob promises Elizabeth that he will finish the building. However, she is killed in a car accident leaving the fundraiser, and her heart is transplanted to artist Grace Briggs, who has suffered from heart disease since the age of 14 and is near death.
The surgery is successful, and Grace is able to live a normal life for the first time. She plans to take her first airplane trip to Italy to paint. Grace's best friend Megan Dayton encourages her to start dating in spite of her self-consciousness about the long surgical scar on her chest.
Grace writes a letter to the donor's family after the surgery, thanking them for the heart she received, but it takes her more than a year to find the courage to mail the letter. Bob works to build the primate house for which Elizabeth raised money, but he is still depressed a year after her death and recognizes that he must resume his life.
A friend organizes a blind date for Bob that goes badly, as his date is very obnoxious, petty and self-absorbed. However, Bob is drawn to the waitress, Grace, who is also the granddaughter of the restaurant's owner.
Although they are both unaware of the connection they have through Elizabeth's heart, Bob and Grace begin to date. As they grow closer together, she is reluctant to share her medical history. After several months of dating, Grace finally decides to tell Bob about the transplant. However, before she can do so, she finds the letter that she had sent several months earlier in Bob's house.
Horrified by the discovery, Grace flees and tells Megan what has happened. Megan's husband Joe becomes infuriated because he has misunderstood Grace's panic and thinks Bob must be married. Megan then shouts at Joe, "Grace has Bob's dead wife's heart!" When Grace meets Bob again, she tells him the truth, leaving him speechless.
Against Megan's advice to face the situation, Grace travels to Italy alone. Back at home, Bob realizes that although he will always miss Elizabeth, he pines for Grace, so he reunites with her in Italy. They return to Chicago for the dedication of the new primate house.
The characters, including a pregnant Megan, dance at a wedding reception.

title: Two Weeks Notice
tagline: Over. Done. Finished. A comedy about love at last glance.
overview: Dedicated environmental lawyer Lucy Kelson goes to work for billionaire George Wade as part of a deal to preserve a community center. plot:
Lucy Kelson is a lawyer, who specializes in historic preservation, environmental law, and pro bono cases in New York City. George Wade is a real estate developer and playboy who has grown up in a life of luxury. Lucy's hard work and devotion to others contrasts sharply with George's childish recklessness and insensitivity to others. George is the face of his company and works alongside his greedy brother Howard, who is more responsible and mature.
Lucy meets George in an attempt to stop the destruction of the Coney Island community center she grew up with. Learning that she graduated from the prestigious Harvard Law School, he asks to hire her to replace his old Chief Counsel, overlooking their opposing views of real estate development. She decides the benefits he offers in discretionary funding for causes she supports outweigh the negatives, especially as he promises to protect the community center.

After Lucy is disrupted at a friend's wedding by George's latest "emergency" (what to wear to an event he is attending), she gives him two weeks' notice of resignation.

Eventually, he admits defeat and she offers to help him find a replacement, unaware of how close and interdependent they have become. Lucy's boyfriend Ansel, who is always away with Greenpeace, breaks up with her over the phone and she is consoled by George on his private yacht. At a business event, June kisses George and they go to his room. Lucy learns that despite George's promise, the community center is going to be demolished in favour of a new real estate project, so goes to confront him on his apparent betrayal. Arriving at his hotel, she finds George and June in his suite in their underclothes during a game of "strip chess". George confronts Lucy the next day, her last day at work, where she reminds him he promised her to spare the community center and storms out.

title: House of 1000 Corpses
tagline: The Most Shocking Tale of Carnage Ever Seen
overview: Two teenage couples traveling across the backwoods of Texas searching for urban legends of serial killers end up as prisoners of a bizarre and sadistic backwater family of serial killers.
plot:
House of 1000 Corpses is a 2003 American horror film written and directed by Rob Zombie. The film follows a group of young friends who embark on a road trip to visit the legendary Captain Spaulding's Museum of Monsters, which is supposedly located in rural California.

The story begins with Jerry Goldsmith (Chris Hardwick), a comic book store clerk, who is obsessed with the legend of Captain Spaulding. He convinces his friends, Tom (Matthew McGrory), Baby Firefly (Bill Moseley), and Dennis (Sid Haig), to join him on a road trip to find the museum. Along the way, they pick up two more passengers, Mary (Sheri Moon Zombie) and Otis (William Forsythe).

As they drive through the desert, they become lost and stumble upon a dilapidated house with a sign that reads "House of 1000 Corpses." The group decides to investigate the house, which leads them into a world of horror and terror. They soon discover that the house is inhabited by a family of serial killers, led by Captain Spaulding (Sid Haig), who are known for their gruesome murders.

The group tries to escape, but they are captured by the family and subjected to various forms of torture and abuse. Baby Firefly, who has a fascination with death and violence, becomes particularly enthralled with the family's activities. As the night wears on, the group is forced to participate in a series of gruesome and disturbing rituals.

Meanwhile, Jerry begins to realize that he may have made a terrible mistake by bringing his friends to this place. He tries to escape, but it's too late. The group is eventually killed off one by one, with some being subjected to particularly brutal forms of torture.

In the end, only Mary is left alive, and she manages to escape from the house by setting fire to it. As she flees into the night, she is seen walking away from the burning house, symbolizing her survival and freedom.

Throughout the film, Rob Zombie pays homage to classic horror movies, such as EC Comics and exploitation films of the 1960s and 1970s. The film's graphic violence, gore, and dark humor have made it a cult classic among horror fans. However, some critics have argued that the film's tone is inconsistent and that it relies too heavily on shock value.

Overall, House of 1000 Corpses is a gruesome and unsettling horror film that explores themes of death, violence, and the darker aspects of human nature. While it may not be to everyone's taste, it has become a beloved cult classic among horror fans.

title: Ringu
tagline: One curse, one cure, one week to find it
overview: A mysterious video has been linked to a number of deaths, and when an inquisitive journalist finds the tape and views it herself, she sets in motion a chain of events that puts her own life in danger.
plot:
Ring (Ringu) is a 1998 Japanese supernatural psychological horror film directed by Hideo Nakata and written by Hiroshi Takahashi, adapted from Koji Suzuki's 1991 novel. Nanako Matsushima, Miki Nakatani and Hiroyuki Sanada star in the story of a reporter racing to unravel a cursed videotape that kills its viewers seven days after they watch it. Released in North America as Ringu, it was shot back to back with the sequel Spiral and the two films opened together in Japan.

At a sleepover, schoolgirl Tomoko tells her friend Masami about a legend of a videotape that dooms its viewers to die a week after a mysterious phone call, then admits that she and her friends watched such a tape a week earlier. Moments later the television switches itself on and Tomoko is killed by an unseen presence. Her aunt, journalist Reiko Asakawa, learns that the three friends who watched with her all died at the same moment. At a resort cabin in Izu where the group stayed, Reiko finds an unlabeled tape of disjointed images and screeching sounds ending with a shot of a well. After watching it she sees an apparition and receives a phone call carrying the same sounds.

Reiko turns to her psychic ex-husband, Ryūji Takayama, who studies a copy and finds a message in the dialect of Ōshima island. Before they leave, Reiko catches their son, Yōichi, watching the tape. On Ōshima they learn of Shizuko Yamamura, a psychic who became notorious after a public demonstration arranged by her lover, researcher Dr. Heihachiro Ikuma, before her suicide, and a vision reveals that her young daughter, Sadako, psychically killed a journalist who mocked her mother. Returning to the Izu cabin, they discover a sealed well beneath it and learn through another vision that Ikuma trapped Sadako inside it. Concluding that her rage gave birth to the curse, they drain the well and recover her remains. When Reiko survives her deadline, they believe the curse is lifted, but the next day Sadako crawls out of Ryūji's television and kills him. Reiko realizes that she was spared because she copied the tape and showed it to someone else, and she drives to her father's house to make him watch it and save Yōichi.

Distributed by Toho, Ring became the highest-grossing horror film in Japan, earning about ¥1.7 billion there. Critics praised its atmosphere and themes, giving it 98% on Rotten Tomatoes. It spawned a franchise and English-language remakes beginning with The Ring (2002) and helped spark a wave of Japanese horror.

title: Signs
tagline: It's not like they didn't warn us.
overview: A family living on a farm finds mysterious crop circles in their fields which suggests something more frightening to come.
plot:
Signs is a 2002 American science fiction thriller film directed by M. Night Shyamalan, produced by The Kennedy/Marshall Company, and written by M. Night Shyamalan.

The story begins with Graham Hess (played by Mel Gibson), a former priest who has lost his faith after the death of his wife in a car accident. He lives on a farm in rural Pennsylvania with his two children, Bo (played by Abigail Breslin) and Morgan (played by Rory Culkin). The family is struggling to cope with their grief.

One day, strange crop circles begin to appear in the fields around Graham's farm, which he initially dismisses as a prank. However, when more circles appear, he becomes increasingly concerned. As the circles grow larger and more complex, Graham starts to suspect that something supernatural is at play.

As the situation escalates, Graham's children become more and more frightened by the strange occurrences. They begin to experience bizarre events, such as finding dead animals in their fields and witnessing unexplained lights in the sky. Graham becomes convinced that an alien invasion is underway, but his skepticism is challenged when he discovers a message scrawled on one of the crop circles.

The family soon realizes that they are not alone on the farm. A group of aliens, who appear to be studying the Earth's crops, have arrived on the scene. The aliens seem to be drawn to the crops, and Graham becomes convinced that they are connected to his wife's death.

As the story unfolds, Graham's faith is tested as he grapples with the possibility of an alien invasion. He begins to question whether God has abandoned him or if there is a higher purpose at play. The family must work together to survive the alien threat and uncover the truth behind their presence on Earth.

The film builds towards a tense and suspenseful climax as Graham and his children face off against the aliens in a desperate bid for survival. In the end, Graham emerges victorious, but not without scars. He has come to terms with his faith and found a new sense of purpose in protecting his family.

Throughout the film, Shyamalan explores themes of grief, faith, and redemption. The movie's slow-burning tension and suspenseful plot twists keep the audience on the edge of their seats as they follow Graham's journey from skepticism to conviction.

title: Z
tagline: He is alive!
overview: Amidst a heated political climate, the opposition leader is killed in what appears to be a traffic accident. When a magistrate finds evidence of a government cover-up, witnesses start to get targeted. A thinly-fictionalized account of the events surrounding the assassination of Greek politician Grigoris Lambrakis in 1963, Z captures the outrage about the military junta that ruled Greece at the time.
plot:
Z is a 1969 political thriller directed by Costa-Gavras from a screenplay he co-wrote with Jorge Semprún, based on Vassilis Vassilikos's 1967 novel. A thinly disguised account of the 1963 assassination of the Greek left-wing politician Grigoris Lambrakis and its aftermath, it reflects the director's anger at the military junta then ruling Greece. A French and Algerian co-production, it stars Jean-Louis Trintignant as the investigating magistrate and Yves Montand as the deputy, with Irene Papas, Jacques Perrin and Charles Denner. Its title evokes a Greek protest slogan meaning "he lives".

In an unnamed Mediterranean country, the opposition organises a rally at which a popular deputy is to speak in favour of nuclear disarmament. The authorities obstruct it at every turn, pressuring venues to refuse them and allowing thugs to tear down posters and harass supporters. Warned of a plot against the deputy's life, his colleagues alert officials, who brush the threat aside. After the speech, as he crosses the street, a man on the back of a speeding delivery truck strikes him on the head with a club. The General commanding the police claims he was hit by a drunk driver, but the deputy dies of his injuries.

The young examining magistrate assigned to the case finds that the autopsy points to blows to the skull rather than a traffic accident. Witnesses are threatened or attacked, but a determined photojournalist and the magistrate gradually expose the truth. The magistrate tricks one of the assailants into revealing that he belongs to a secret far-right group, the Christian Royalist Organization against Communism, which is protected by senior police and military officers who had bribed the killers.

Despite pressure from his superiors to limit the case to the hired thugs, the magistrate charges the high-ranking officers. But an epilogue reveals that justice is undone: the magistrate is removed, witnesses die in suspicious circumstances, the assassins receive light sentences, the officers escape with reprimands and the journalist is jailed. A military coup follows, and the new regime bans a long list of things, including modern music, many writers and philosophers, and the letter Z.

Z won the Academy Awards for Best Foreign Language Film and Best Film Editing and was also nominated for Best Picture, while Trintignant was named Best Actor at Cannes. Roger Ebert named it the best film of 1969.

title: Postal
tagline: Some comedies go too far... others start there.
overview: The story begins with a regular Joe who tries desperately to seek employment, but embarks on a violent rampage when he teams up with cult leader Uncle Dave. Their first act is to heist an amusement park, only to learn that the Taliban are planning the same heist as well. Chaos ensues, and now the Postal Dude must not only take on terrorists but also political figures.
plot:
Postal is a 2007 action comedy based on the Postal video game series, directed by Uwe Boll, who co-wrote the screenplay. It stars Zack Ward as the Postal Dude, Dave Foley as his Uncle Dave, Chris Coppola, Jackie Tohn as Faith, J. K. Simmons, Verne Troyer as himself, Larry Thomas as Osama bin Laden, David Huddleston and Seymour Cassel. Known for its deliberately offensive humor, the film satirizes terrorism, religion, politics and Boll's own reputation, with the director appearing as himself.

The film opens with a provocative parody of the September 11 attacks. Five years later, in the dead-end town of Paradise, Arizona, the Postal Dude is thrown out of the unemployment office and discovers that his wife is cheating on him. Desperate to leave town, he teams up with his slovenly Uncle Dave, a con artist turned doomsday cult leader who owes the government more than a million dollars in back taxes.

The Dude comes up with a plan to hijack a shipment of Krotchy Dolls, a rare and highly sought-after plush toy, so that his uncle can resell them online. Unknown to them, Osama bin Laden and a band of al-Qaeda operatives have been hiding in Paradise since 9/11 and plan to steal the same shipment, infect the dolls with avian influenza and distribute them to American children. When both groups converge on Little Germany, a German-themed amusement park where the dolls are being delivered, the result is a massive shootout. Escaping with the dolls and the park's guest of honor, Verne Troyer, the Dude and the cult are pursued by terrorists, police and an angry mob. After betrayal within the cult, the Dude and a barista named Faith set out on a violent rampage against everyone who wants them dead.

Boll framed the film as a political satire attacking all sides, mixing slapstick, shock humor and graphic violence in the anarchic spirit of the games.

Postal was released in Germany on October 18, 2007, and in the United States on May 23, 2008. It was a box office flop, earning about 146,000 dollars against a 15 million dollar budget, and holds 9 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it a witless satire, though one of Boll's more successful films, and a Metacritic score of 22.

title: About Schmidt
tagline: Schmidt Happens.
overview: A recently retired man embarks on a journey to his estranged daughter's wedding, only to discover more about himself and life than he ever expected.
plot:
Warren Schmidt is retiring from his position as an actuary with Woodmen of the World, a life insurance company in Omaha, Nebraska. He looks with depression at the clock in his office and waits until exactly five to leave with no fanfare. He attends a paint by the numbers retirement dinner where people give generic remarks and empty well wishes. During the dinner, he ducks out and heads to the bar alone, finding it hard to adjust to his new life, feeling useless.
Schmidt sees a television advertisement about a foster program for African children, Childreach, and decides to sponsor a child. He soon receives an information package with a photo of his foster child, a small Tanzanian boy named Ndugu Umbo, to whom he relates his life in a series of letters.
Schmidt visits his young successor at the life insurance company to offer his help, but he is politely declined. As he leaves the building, he sees the contents and files of his office set out for the garbage. He describes to Ndugu his resentment towards his successor, implying that he was forced into retirement against his will. He describes to Ndugu his longtime alienation from Helen, his wife, who dies from a blood clot in her brain just after their purchase of a Winnebago Adventurer motor home.
Jeannie, their daughter, and her fiancé, Randall Hertzel, a waterbed salesman, arrive from Denver. Consoling him at the funeral, she later berates him for taking his wife for granted, refusing to fully pay for the Winnebago, and getting her a cheap casket. He asks her to move back to take care of him, but she refuses. Meanwhile, Randall tries to rope him into a pyramid scheme.
Schmidt feels that his daughter could do better than Randall. After they leave, he is overcome by loneliness. When he discovers hidden love letters disclosing Helen's long-ago affair with Ray, a mutual friend, Schmidt collects all her possessions and dumps them next to a clothing donations bin. He then confronts Ray for his betrayal.
Deciding to take a journey in the new Winnebago to visit his daughter and convince her not to marry Randall, he tells her he is coming early for the wedding. She makes it clear she does not want him there until right before the ceremony, so Schmidt visits places from his past including his college (University of Kansas), his childhood home (now a tire store) and other museums and points of interest.
At a trailer campground, he is invited to dinner by a friendly and sympathetic couple, John and Vicki Rusk. When John goes for beer, Schmidt makes a pass at Vicki, who tells him to leave. He attempts to call Ray and repair their relationship, but his voicemail is deleted during the call and he decides to let it go. Sitting on the roof of his RV on a starry night, Schmidt forgives his departed wife for her affair, apologizing to her for his own failings. At that moment, he is amazed to see a meteor streak across the sky, taking it as a possible sign from Helen.

The main plot point of the movie centers around a summer vacation that the friends plan together. They rent a lake house in Michigan, where they spend their days partying and engaging in various misadventures. However, things take a turn when Oz's family reveals that they are planning to sell the lake house, which would mean the end of the friends' annual tradition.

As the summer progresses, the friends face various challenges, including romantic relationships, family conflicts, and personal growth. Along the way, they also encounter new characters, such as Stifler's father (Paul Gleason), who becomes a recurring figure in the series.

Throughout the movie, the friends learn valuable lessons about friendship, loyalty, and growing up. They come to realize that their relationships with each other are more important than any romantic relationship or personal achievement. The movie ends on a positive note, with the friends having learned to appreciate the importance of their friendships and the value of spending time together.

Overall, American Pie 2 is a lighthearted and entertaining comedy that explores themes of friendship, growing up, and self-discovery. While it may not be as groundbreaking as its predecessor, the movie delivers on its promise of raunchy humor and memorable characters.

title: Asterix & Obelix: Mission Cleopatra
tagline: The funniest film in ancient history!
overview: The Egyptian Queen Cleopatra bets against the Roman Emperor, Julius Caesar, that her people are still great, even if the times of the Pharaohs has long passed. She vows (against all logic) to build a new palace for Caesar within three months. Since all her architects are either busy otherwise or too conservative in style, this ambivalent honor falls to Edifis. He is to build the palace and be covered in gold or, if not, his fate is to be eaten by crocodiles. Edifis calls upon an old friend to help him out: The fabulous Druid Getafix from Gaul, who brews a fantastic potion that gives supernatural strength. In order to help and protect the old Druid, Asterix and Obelix accompany him on his journey to Egypt. When Julius Caesar gets wind of the project succeeding, he has the building site attacked by his troops in order to win the bet and not lose face. But just like the local pirates, he hasn't counted on Asterix and Obelix.
plot:
Asterix & Obelix: Mission Cleopatra is a 2002 French-Italian comedy film directed by Robert Guédiguian, produced by Renn Productions, and written by Robert Guédiguian. The movie is the fourth installment in the Asterix series, based on the comic book characters created by René Goscinny and Albert Uderzo.

The story begins with Asterix (Gérard Depardieu) and Obelix (Christian Clavier), two ancient Celtic warriors who live in the village of Indomiti. The villagers are preparing for a grand festival to celebrate their victory over the Romans, but they soon discover that Cleopatra (Monica Bellucci), the last pharaoh of Ancient Egypt, has arrived in their village.

Cleopatra is on a mission to find the legendary Golden Egg, which she believes will grant her immense power and help her reclaim her throne. However, she is being pursued by Julius Caesar's (Gérard Depardieu) nephew, Octavius (Vincent Cassel), who seeks to capture Cleopatra and claim the Golden Egg for himself.

Asterix and Obelix are recruited by a group of Egyptian warriors to help Cleopatra on her quest. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous landscapes, ferocious beasts, and Octavius's henchmen. The duo also befriends a young Egyptian warrior named Irini (Monica Bellucci), who becomes Obelix's love interest.

As the journey progresses, Asterix and Obelix face numerous challenges, from navigating treacherous tombs to battling giant spiders. Meanwhile, Cleopatra's true intentions are revealed, and it is discovered that she has been using her charm and beauty to manipulate those around her in order to achieve her goals.

In the end, Asterix and Obelix successfully retrieve the Golden Egg, but not before Octavius and his men arrive on the scene. A fierce battle ensues, with Asterix and Obelix fighting valiantly to protect Cleopatra and the Golden Egg. In the heat of the battle, Irini sacrifices herself to save Obelix, and Cleopatra is forced to flee.

The movie ends with Asterix and Obelix returning to their village, where they are greeted as heroes. However, the film's final scene reveals that Octavius has survived and is planning his revenge against Asterix and Obelix.

Overall, Asterix & Obelix: Mission Cleopatra is a lighthearted and entertaining comedy that combines action, adventure, and humor. The movie features impressive stunts, witty dialogue, and memorable characters, making it a fun watch for fans of the Asterix series.

title: License to Wed
tagline: First came love... then came Reverend Frank.
overview: Newly engaged, Ben and Sadie can't wait to start their life together and live happily ever after. However Sadie's family church's Reverend Frank won't bless their union until they pass his patented, "foolproof" marriage prep course consisting of outrageous classes, outlandish homework assignments and some outright invasion of privacy.
plot:
Sadie Jones longs to marry her lifetime companion Ben Murphy in her family church. Although her lifelong dream has been to do so in her childhood church, St. Augustine's the next available wedding slot is two years away. This is unless they take advantage of a cancellation, meaning the wedding must be held in three weeks.
The church's eccentric minister, Reverend Frank Littleton, will only wed the couple if they agree to pass his prenuptial course (shortened, due to the wedding date, from three months to three weeks). As the big day draws near, Sadie and Ben must now follow all of Reverend Frank's rules, attend his unusual classes, and complete a series of homework assignments These are designed specifically to test their relationship, to confirm that theirs is not puppy love and to ensure the union will have a sound foundation.
In one part of the course, the couple must care for twin robot babies to simulate parenting. Due to a technical issue, they get on Ben's nerves so he damages one, to the horror of bystanders in a department store. To Ben's dismay, one of Frank's rules is no premarital sex. To ensure compliance, Frank has a bug planted in the couple's bedroom, so he can listen to all conversations. Ben eventually discovers the transmitter but does not tell Sadie, fearing she would not believe him.
Problems gradually begin to develop between the couple. Ben begins an investigation into Frank and eventually discovers that he was once married to a woman named Maria Gonzalez. Shortly before the wedding, Sadie starts to have doubts, in part due to Ben not preparing his marriage vows as required. Instead, he creates a cartoon flip book of a truck.
Ben confronts Frank about Maria Gonzalez, believing him to be a hypocrite. However, he reveals that the marriage was done to allow Maria, an immigrant and member of Frank's congregation, to stay in the U.S. Upset that Ben has wasted his time on this investigation rather than write his vows, Sadie calls off the wedding, leaving Ben devastated. On Frank's advice, Sadie goes on vacation with her whole family to Jamaica, the couple's intended honeymoon destination.
Ben seeks advice from his friend Joel, who advises him to give up on Sadie, as there are other "fish in the sea". He, however, disagrees with this so decides to go to Jamaica. Frank and his assistant also travel there shortly after.
Ben attempts to call Sadie, but she refuses to listen. Her parents assure her that all marriages have problems, and even her friend Carlisle tells her that Ben may just want someone who relies on him, allowing her to forgive Ben more easily. Ben writes his vows on the sand of the beach, they reconcile, and Frank weds them there.

title: Becoming Jane
tagline: Her own life is her greatest inspiration.
overview: A biographical portrait of a pre-fame Jane Austen and her romance with a young Irishman.
plot:
Jane Austen is the youngest daughter of Reverend George Austen and his wife Cassandra, who have yet to find a suitable husband for her. She aspires to be a writer, to the dismay of her mother and proud delight of her father.
Thomas Lefroy is a promising lawyer with a bad reputation, which he describes as "typical" for lawyers, and is sent to live in the country by his uncle to calm him down. There he makes a terrible first impression upon meeting Jane, when he nearly falls asleep while she gives a reading of her work. Overhearing his subsequent criticism, Jane cannot stand the arrogant Irishman.
Meanwhile, Jane turns down the affections of other men, including Mr. Wisley, the nephew and heir of the wealthy Lady Gresham. He proposes but she ultimately rejects him due to her lack of affection for him. The mischievous Tom encounters Jane again; they argue but increasingly take interest in each other and he demonstrates that he takes Jane's literary aspirations seriously. In time they fall in love.
Tom, Jane, her brother Henry and Jane's rich widowed cousin Eliza, Comtesse de Feullide, conspire to receive an invitation from Tom's great uncle and benefactor, the Lord Chief Judge Langlois, for the rich "Madame La Comtesse" and her friends. This visit to London is meant to be a short break in their journey to see Jane's brother Edward, and would allow Judge Langlois to get to know Jane and give a blessing for their marriage.
Full of hope, Jane cannot sleep during the night at the Judge's place. In a flow of inspiration, she then begins writing First Impressions, the manuscript that will become Pride and Prejudice. However, Judge Langlois receives a letter informing him of the genteel poverty of Jane's family.
The judge refuses to give Tom his blessing, declaring that he would rather he be the whoremonger he had been than allow him to live in poverty due to a bad marriage. When Tom tells Jane that he cannot marry her she is crushed, not knowing that Tom has a legitimate reason; his family depends on him financially.
Jane returns home and soon learns that Tom has become engaged to someone else, arranged by his family. Her sister Cassandra learns that her fiancé Robert Fowler has died of yellow fever while stationed abroad. Then Jane accepts the marriage proposal of Mr. Wisley, who had not lost hope that she would change her mind.
Later, Tom realises he cannot live without Jane and returns, asking Jane to run away with him, for "What value will there be in life, if we are not together?" Jane agrees, and they leave, with only Jane's older sister, Cassandra, knowing they plan to elope. On the way, Jane stumbles upon a letter from Tom's mother, and realizes his situation: he sends money he receives from his uncle back to his parents and siblings, and they cannot survive without it.
Jane tells Tom that they cannot elope, not with so many people depending upon him. He insists they must marry, promising he will earn money.

tagline: The only demons in room 1408 are those within you.
overview: A man who specializes in debunking paranormal occurrences checks into the fabled room 1408 in the Dolphin Hotel. Soon after settling in, he confronts genuine terror.
plot:
1408 is an American supernatural psychological horror film of 2007 directed by Mikael Håfström and adapted from Stephen King's short story of 1999 by Matt Greenberg, Scott Alexander and Larry Karaszewski. John Cusack stars as the writer Mike Enslin, with Samuel L. Jackson as hotel manager Gerald Olin, Mary McCormack as Mike's estranged wife Lily, Jasmine Jessica Anthony as their late daughter Katie, Len Cariou as Mike's father and Tony Shalhoub as Sam Farrell.

Mike is a cynical author of guidebooks to supposedly haunted places, none of which he believes in. While promoting his latest book in California, he receives an anonymous postcard of the Dolphin, a hotel on Lexington Avenue in New York, warning him not to enter room 1408. Taking it as a dare, he demands the room. Olin tries everything to stop him, explaining that in 95 years no guest has survived more than an hour there and that 56 people have died, but relents when Mike threatens legal action.

At first Mike dictates notes on the room's ordinariness into his tape recorder, until the clock radio begins playing "We've Only Just Begun" and its display starts counting down from sixty minutes. He sees the ghosts of past victims and visions of Katie, who died young, and of his dying father, and every attempt to escape fails. He reaches Lily over his laptop, but a double of Mike appears on the video call urging her to come to the hotel. A painting of a storm-tossed ship floods the room, and Mike seems to wake in hospital after a surfing accident, reconciling with Lily and writing up his ordeal as a nightmare, until workmen at a post office turn out to be hotel staff and tear down the walls to reveal he never left 1408. When the countdown ends, the room resets. A voice on the phone tells him he may relive the hour forever or take the express checkout, and a noose appears. Refusing, Mike builds a Molotov cocktail and sets the room ablaze. Firefighters rescue him and he reunites with the doubtful Lily, but when he repairs his damaged tape recorder, they both hear Katie's voice on it, confirming his story.

Shot partly at the Roosevelt Hotel in New York and the Reform Club in London, the film was released by MGM and The Weinstein Company in June 2007. Made for $25 million, it grossed $132 million worldwide, and critics praised its psychological tension and Cusack's lead performance, giving it 80% on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: Night Watch
tagline: All That Stands Between Light And Darkness Is The Night Watch.
overview: Among normal humans live the "Others" possessing various supernatural powers. They are divided up into the forces of light and the forces of the dark, who signed a truce several centuries ago to end a devastating battle. Ever since, the forces of light govern the day while the night belongs to their dark opponents. In modern day Moscow the dark Others actually roam the night as vampires while a "Night Watch" of light forces, among them Anton, the movie's protagonist, try to control them and limit their outrage
plot:
Night Watch (Russian: Nochnoy dozor) is a 2004 Russian urban fantasy thriller directed by Timur Bekmambetov, who wrote the screenplay with Laeta Kalogridis, loosely based on Sergei Lukyanenko's 1998 novel The Night Watch. Channel One bought the adaptation rights and hired Bekmambetov after an earlier, low-budget attempt stalled. Made for about $4.2 million, it was the first big-budget Russian supernatural film and one of the first blockbusters after the collapse of the Soviet film industry, with effects shots made by 16 Russian studios.

Since ancient times, humans with supernatural powers, known as Others, have been split between Light and Dark. After a medieval battle ended in stalemate, the leaders Geser and Zavulon agreed a truce policed by the Night Watch, which monitors the Dark, and the Day Watch, which monitors the Light. In Moscow in 1992, Anton Gorodetsky pays a witch to win back his wife, agreeing that the spell will make her lose the child she is carrying, which he believes is another man's. Two agents burst in to stop the ritual and realize that Anton can see them, revealing that he is an Other himself.

Twelve years later, Anton works for the Night Watch. Geser tells him that a series of omens point to an ancient prophecy of an immensely powerful Other who will break the balance between Light and Dark and is more likely to choose the Dark. Anton's investigations lead him to Svetlana, a nurse around whom disasters seem to gather, and to a young boy, Yegor. Realizing that Svetlana is an Other, Anton prevents a storm from leveling Moscow and begins teaching her to control her power. But he then discovers that Yegor is his own son, the child his wife was carrying in 1992. Learning that his father once tried to have him killed before birth, Yegor, the prophesied Other, turns away from Anton toward Zavulon, as Zavulon had planned. Anton strikes him in rage, vowing not to give up despite the Dark's apparent victory.

Konstantin Khabensky plays Anton, with Vladimir Menshov as Geser, Viktor Verzhbitsky as Zavulon, Mariya Poroshina as Svetlana and Dmitry Martynov as Yegor. Premiering at the Moscow Film Festival on 27 June 2004, it became the highest-grossing Russian release to date, earning $16.7 million at home. Fox Searchlight bought the international rights, releasing a re-edited version with animated subtitles. Reviews were mixed, with 59% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and a sequel, Day Watch, followed in 2006.

title: Basic Instinct 2
tagline: Everything interesting begins in the mind
overview: Novelist Catherine Tramell is once again in trouble with the law, and Scotland Yard appoints psychiatrist Dr. Michael Glass to evaluate her. Though, like Detective Nick Curran before him, Glass is entranced by Tramell and lured into a seductive game.
plot:
Basic Instinct 2 (released in some markets as Basic Instinct 2: Risk Addiction) is an erotic thriller from 2006, directed by Michael Caton-Jones and written by Leora Barish and Henry Bean, the sequel to Basic Instinct (1992). Sharon Stone reprises her role as the crime novelist Catherine Tramell, opposite David Morrissey as the psychiatrist Dr. Michael Glass, with Charlotte Rampling and David Thewlis.

In London, Catherine is speeding through the city at night with her companion, the football star Kevin Franks, when she loses control during a reckless sexual encounter and plunges the car into the West India Docks. She gets out, but Franks dies, and she coolly tells police that her own life mattered more to her than his. Detective Superintendent Roy Washburn of Scotland Yard reveals that a paralysing drug was found in both the car and the dead man's body and that Franks had stopped breathing before the crash, but Catherine denies the drug dealer's claim that he sold it to her.

Dr. Glass, who assessed her for the court and judged her a narcissist, begins treating her. She toys with him, and he becomes frustrated and fascinated, even though he has just begun dating a fellow psychiatrist, Michelle. Then people in his life start dying: the journalist boyfriend of his ex-wife, Denise, who had been writing a critical article about one of Glass's old cases, is strangled; Denise and Catherine's dealer are murdered too. As police suspicion turns toward Glass, Washburn tells him Catherine is the killer and is setting him up. Glass confronts her, they sleep together, and she hands him the manuscript of her new novel, The Analyst, which turns recent events into fiction and names a character based on his colleague Dr. Milena Gardosh as the next victim. Racing to Gardosh's flat, he finds Catherine already there; Gardosh tells him she has taken over Catherine's case and that his licence will be revoked. In the struggle he knocks Gardosh out, seizes Catherine's gun and shoots Washburn when the detective arrives. Later, visiting Glass in a psychiatric hospital, Catherine suggests that he committed the murders himself and is feigning madness, leaves him a signed copy of her bestseller, and walks out as he smiles.

The film was cut to avoid an NC-17 rating. It was a notorious flop, grossing $38.6 million worldwide on a $70 million budget, and was savaged by critics, with 6% on Rotten Tomatoes. It won four Golden Raspberry Awards, including Worst Picture and Worst Actress.

title: Gangs of New York
tagline: America was born in the streets.
overview: It's 1863. Amsterdam Vallon returns to the Five Points of America to seek vengeance against the psychotic gangland kingpin, Bill the Butcher, who murdered his father years earlier. With an eager pickpocket by his side and a whole new army, Vallon fights his way to seek vengeance on the Butcher and restore peace in the area.
plot:
In the 1846 slum of the Five Points, two rival gangs, the Confederation of American Natives, a nativist Protestant faction led by William "Bill the Butcher" Cutting, and the Dead Rabbits, an Irish Catholic immigrant gang led by "Priest" Vallon, engage in their final turf war outside the Old Brewery, the Dead Rabbits domain, to determine which faction will hold power over the Five Points. During the street brawl, Cutting kills Vallon, orders Vallon's body to remain untouched, and declares the Dead Rabbits outlawed. Having witnessed this, Vallon's young son hides the knife that killed his father before being taken to the Hellgate Orphanage on Blackwell's Island.
16 years later, in 1862, Vallon's son "Amsterdam" returns to the Five Points seeking revenge and retrieves the knife while the Metropolitan Police evict the Irish from the Old Brewery. An old acquaintance, Johnny Sirocco, familiarizes him with the local gang clans, all of whom pay tribute to Cutting, who still controls the Five Points. Amsterdam helps Sirocco loot a burning house one night, during which Cutting takes notice of them. Amsterdam is introduced to Cutting but keeps his past a secret as he seeks recruitment into the gang. He learns many of his father's former lieutenants—particularly "Happy" Jack Mulraney, who has become a corrupt policeman, and McGloin—are now in Cutting's employ, despite his deep anti-Irish and racist views.
Each year, Cutting celebrates the anniversary of his victory over the Dead Rabbits. Amsterdam secretly plans to kill him publicly during this celebration. Amsterdam soon becomes attracted to pickpocket and grifter Jenny Everdeane, with whom Sirocco is also infatuated. Amsterdam gains Cutting's confidence and becomes his protégé, which draws him into the dealings of corrupt Tammany Hall politician William M. Tweed. His first test was to help Sirocco and his crew loot a ship in the harbor, only to find that the Daybreak Boys had already hit the ship and killed everyone aboard.
An assassination attempt takes place against Cutting. He is wounded, but Amsterdam saves his life. Amsterdam encounters Walter 'Monk' McGinn, a former Dead Rabbit, who is aware of Amsterdam's true identity and was behind the assassination plot. He later discovers that Everdeane was once a ward and consort for Cutting until she had an abortion that left her scarred. Sirocco, jealous of Everdeane's affection for Amsterdam and Amsterdam's newfound popularity, reveals his true identity and intentions to Cutting. Cutting baits Amsterdam with a knife throwing act involving Everdeane. As Cutting toasts Priest Vallon, Amsterdam throws his knife, but it is deflected, and Amsterdam is wounded by a counter throw. Cutting then beats him and burns his cheek with a hot blade before banishing him, believing Amsterdam to not be worthy of a death by his hand.
Everdeane implores Amsterdam to escape with her to San Francisco.

title: Good Night, and Good Luck.
tagline: They took on the Government with nothing but the truth.
overview: The story of journalist Edward R. Murrow's stand against Senator Joseph McCarthy's anti-communist witch-hunts in the early 1950s.
plot:
Good Night, and Good Luck. is a 2005 American historical drama film directed by George Clooney, who co-wrote it with producer Grant Heslov. It stars David Strathairn as the veteran CBS broadcaster Edward R. Murrow, alongside Patricia Clarkson, Clooney, Jeff Daniels, Robert Downey Jr. and Frank Langella, and dramatizes Murrow's conflict with Senator Joseph McCarthy of Wisconsin. Shot on color stock on a grayscale set and converted to black and white, it explores media responsibility and journalism's role in voicing dissent.

The film opens in 1958 at a tribute dinner where Murrow begins a speech, then flashes back to October 1953 at CBS, as McCarthy claims that over 200 communists work in the government. Murrow and his producer, Fred Friendly, decide to cover the case of Milo Radulovich, an Air Force officer discharged because his father and sister were accused of communist sympathies, on evidence kept in a sealed envelope. Despite objections from CBS executive Sig Mickelson and pressure from military officers, the segment airs on See It Now, and the team turns its attention to McCarthy himself, exposing his questioning methods and falsehoods and inviting him onto the program to respond. The Air Force reinstates Radulovich.

On April 6, 1954, McCarthy appears on the show and accuses Murrow of being a communist, as Murrow expected. In his reply, Murrow flatly denies the charge and points out that anyone who opposes the senator's methods is branded a communist. The tide then turns against McCarthy, who faces investigation over charges brought by the Army, but the newsroom's celebration is cut short by the suicide of colleague Don Hollenbeck, who had been smeared as a "pinko" by a columnist. After the Army-McCarthy hearings, CBS chief Paley, having lost a major sponsor, cuts See It Now to five more episodes in a Sunday afternoon slot and orders layoffs; Joe Wershba, secretly married to colleague Shirley in breach of company policy, volunteers to leave. Returning to 1958, Murrow warns that television can inform and enlighten only if used for that purpose, or it is "merely wires and lights in a box."

The film was a box office success and was widely acclaimed for Clooney's direction, the writing, cinematography, production design and performances, especially Strathairn's. Rotten Tomatoes reported 93% approval and Metacritic a score of 80. It received six Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture, Best Director and Best Actor.

title: Dirty Pretty Things
tagline: Every dream has its price.
overview: An undocumented immigrant finds a human heart in one of the toilets of the west London hotel where he works with other undocumented immigrants.
plot:
Okwe, a doctor in his home country (not initially named) who was forced to flee after being falsely accused of murdering his wife, lives in the United Kingdom as an undocumented immigrant. He drives a cab in London during the day and works at the front desk of a hotel at night, which is staffed by other immigrants, both documented and undocumented. He is pressed to treat other poor immigrants, including fellow cab drivers with venereal diseases, with scarce supplies provided by his friend Guo Yi, an employee at a hospital mortuary.
Juliette, a sex worker who regularly conducts her business at the hotel, informs Okwe about a blocked toilet in one of the rooms, and he fishes out a human heart. The manager of the hotel, Juan, runs an illegal operation at the hotel wherein immigrants swap kidneys for forged passports. After learning of Okwe's past as a doctor, Juan pressures him to join his operation as a surgeon, but Okwe refuses.
Senay is a Turkish Muslim seeking asylum who also works at the hotel as a cleaner. Her immigration status allows her to stay in the UK, provided she does not work; the hotel is a perfect cover because she is not named on its books. She allows Okwe to sleep on her sofa when she is not home, as she is from a conservative culture where men and women who are not married do not spend the night together under the same roof. After Senay is visited by Immigration Services, who inspect the hotel after finding a book of matches in her flat, Okwe prevents the officials from intercepting her.
No longer able to work at the hotel, Senay begins working in a sweatshop making clothes, which is also raided by officials looking for undocumented immigrants, who the manager gets rid of. The manager offers to allow Senay to keep her job and not report her to the authorities in return for performing oral sex on him; she initially complies before biting him. Okwe finds her a place to stay at the hospital mortuary, while Senay asks him to accept Juan's proposition in his organ business to raise money to travel to America.
In desperation, Senay offers her kidney to Juan for a passport; Juan accepts the deal on condition he takes her virginity as well. Senay is later provided with a morning-after pill by Juliette. After learning of Senay's plan, Okwe agrees to perform the operation to ensure her safety, but only if Juan provides them both with passports under different names. After Juan delivers the passports, Okwe and Senay drug him, surgically remove his kidney, and sell it to Juan's contact.
Okwe plans to use his new identity to return to his young daughter in Nigeria, and Senay plans to start a new life in New York. Before they part at Stansted Airport, they mouth the words "I love you" to each other, and she gives him her cousin's address in New York. Senay boards her plane, and Okwe calls his daughter long-distance to tell her he is finally coming home.

title: 88 Minutes
tagline: He has 88 minutes to solve a murder. His own.
overview: A college professor who moonlights as a forensic psychiatrist for the FBI, receives a death threat claiming he has only 88 minutes to live.
plot:
88 Minutes is a 2007 thriller directed by Jon Avnet. Al Pacino stars as Dr. Jack Gramm, a forensic psychiatrist and renowned profiler, with Alicia Witt as his teaching assistant Kim Cummings, Leelee Sobieski as his student Lauren Douglas, Amy Brenneman as his assistant Shelly, William Forsythe as FBI agent Frank Parks, Deborah Kara Unger as Dean Carol Johnson, Benjamin McKenzie as the student Mike Stempt and Neal McDonough as the convicted killer Jon Forster. It was filmed around Vancouver in late 2005.

In 1997 Gramm's testimony helps convict Forster of a brutal attack on twin sisters, one of whom was drugged, hung upside down and murdered. As the verdict is read, Forster taunts him with the words "Tick-tock, Doc." Nine years later, with Forster's execution approaching, near-identical murders begin. Gramm, now teaching at the University of Washington, learns that the latest victim was a former student of his. On his way to class, a caller using a voice changer tells him he has eighty-eight minutes to live, the exact time it took for his own sister Kate to be murdered decades earlier after he left her alone.

The threats multiply. A bomb scare empties his lecture hall, messages appear on his projector and vandalized car, and Lauren is attacked in a stairwell. At his condo Gramm receives a tape of Kate's final cries, taken from his secure files, before Kim's ex-husband is shot dead there by a helmeted assailant and Gramm's car explodes. A woman he spent the previous night with is found murdered amid evidence pointing to him, and suspicion shifts between Carol, Kim and his students. Through prison visiting records Gramm realizes that Forster's appeals lawyer is Lauren under a false name. She has Carol dangling from a balcony and Kim bound at gunpoint, and forces Gramm to record a confession that he lied at the trial. Agent Parks shoots her and she falls to her death, and Gramm keeps the recording as he gives Forster the news.

The film was released in Europe in 2007 before Sony acquired it for North America, where it opened fourth and earned about $32.6 million worldwide. It was panned: just 5% of 122 reviews on Rotten Tomatoes are positive, and its Metacritic score is 17. Pacino and Sobieski were each nominated for Golden Raspberry Awards.

title: Lady Chatterley
overview: In the Chatterley’s country estate, monotonous days follow one after the other for Constance, trapped by her marriage and her sense of duty. During spring, deep in the heart of Wragby forest, she encounters Parkin, the estate’s gamekeeper. A tale of an encounter, a difficult apprenticeship, a slow awakening to sensuality for her, a long return to life for him. Or how love is but one with experience and transformation.
plot:
Lady Chatterley is a 2006 film adaptation of the novel by D.H. Lawrence, directed by Laurence Dunmore and produced by ARTE France Cinéma. The movie explores the complex and tumultuous relationship between Lady Constance Chatterley, a young woman from a wealthy family, and Oliver Mellors, her husband's gamekeeper.

At its core, Lady Chatterley is a film about the struggle for identity, autonomy, and self-discovery in a society that restricts women's choices and desires. The movie delves into the themes of class, privilege, and the constraints placed on individuals by their social status. Lady Constance, trapped in a loveless marriage with the wealthy but emotionally distant Sir Clifford Chatterley, must navigate her own desires and sense of self-worth.

The film also explores the tension between nature and civilization, as embodied by the contrast between Oliver Mellors' connection to the natural world and Lady Constance's confinement within the stifling social norms of her family. Through their relationship, Lawrence critiques the societal expectations placed on women, highlighting the ways in which they are forced to choose between conformity and authenticity.

Furthermore, Lady Chatterley is a powerful exploration of the human need for intimacy, connection, and physical expression. The movie's portrayal of Oliver Mellors' passion and sensuality serves as a counterpoint to the stifling emotional repression of Lady Constance's marriage, highlighting the importance of embracing one's desires and needs.

Ultimately, the film presents a nuanced and complex exploration of the human experience, one that challenges societal norms and expectations while celebrating the beauty and power of individual desire.
