title: Armored
tagline: To protect and serve yourself.
overview: A crew of officers at an armored transport security firm risk their lives when they embark on the ultimate heist against their own company. Armed with a seemingly fool-proof plan, the men plan on making off with a fortune with harm to none. But when an unexpected witness interferes, the plan quickly unravels and all bets are off.
plot:
Armored is a 2009 American heist action thriller directed by Nimród Antal from a script by James V. Simpson. Columbus Short leads a cast that includes Matt Dillon, Laurence Fishburne, Jean Reno, Skeet Ulrich, Amaury Nolasco, Milo Ventimiglia and Fred Ward. It was released on December 4, 2009.

Ty Hackett is a military veteran who now works on an armored transport crew for the security firm Eagle Shield. Since their parents died he has been raising his younger brother Jimmy, but the bills are piling up: the bank is threatening to foreclose on the house, and social services are considering placing the truant Jimmy in foster care. Mike Cochrane, Ty's godfather and colleague, lets him in on a plan to rob two of their own trucks of the $42 million they are carrying from the Federal Reserve to local banks. Ty initially refuses, but agrees after Mike promises that nobody will get hurt.

The six guards unload the first truck at an abandoned steel mill, but a homeless man living there sees them, and Baines shoots him dead. Horrified, Ty locks himself inside the second truck with the remaining $21 million. When he cannot drive away, he trips the alarm, drawing sheriff's deputy Jake Eckehart to the mill. Baines shoots the deputy, and Ty pulls the wounded man into the truck while the others try to knock out the door hinges. Dobbs wavers and secretly tries to replace an engine fuse Mike removed, but Palmer catches and kills him; later, after Ty persuades Palmer that the robbery is wrong, Palmer, consumed by guilt, takes his own life. The surviving robbers then reveal that they have kidnapped Jimmy, and Ty is forced to cooperate. Quinn and Baines are killed by a booby trap rigged to the cash, and Mike, chasing Ty in the other truck, crashes into a pit and dies. Recovering in hospital, Jake tells Duncan Ashcroft how Ty tried to stop the thieves, a reward is mentioned, and the brothers go home.

Screen Gems bought Simpson's spec script in 2006, Dillon and Short were announced as leads in 2007, and the film was shot in Los Angeles. It was not screened for critics in advance and drew mostly negative reviews, scoring 42% on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus faulted plot holes and a messy finale despite the good cast; CinemaScore audiences gave it a "B−". A. O. Scott of The New York Times was kinder, calling it a basic, brutal and sometimes clumsy B movie that was far from dumb, and praising Andrzej Sekuła's cinematography.

title: Raising Helen
tagline: Her uptown life gets turned inside out!
overview: Helen Harris has a glamorous, big-city life working for one of New York's hottest modeling agencies. But suddenly her free-spirited life gets turned upside down when she must chose between the life she's always loved, and the new loves of her life!
plot:
Helen, Jenny, and Lindsay Harris are close sisters living in New York; the eldest Jenny raised the other two after their mother died when they were young. Jenny and Lindsay are responsible stay-at-home mothers while Helen, an executive assistant to the CEO of one of Manhattan's most prestigious modeling agencies, enjoys a lavish, carefree lifestyle.
One morning, Helen receives a call from Jenny who tells her Lindsay and her husband Paul have died in a car accident, leaving behind their three children, 15-year-old Audrey, 10-year-old Henry, and 5-year-old Sarah. At an appointment with Lindsay's attorney, Helen and Jenny are shocked to discover Lindsay has appointed Helen the guardian of the children. Both sisters are given a letter that Lindsay had left for them.
Forced to give up her wild lifestyle and move to Queens, Helen initially struggles to raise the children on her own. As time goes by, her concentration at work begins to slip and she is fired as a result, leading her to become a receptionist at a car dealership. Helen and Jenny get into a fight about how best to raise the children and they stop talking. Things later start to improve for Helen after she begins dating Dan Parker, the children's school principal and pastor, who helps her bond with them.
Audrey starts to fall in with the wrong crowd at school and gets an older boyfriend called BZ. When she disappears after prom, Helen is forced to call Jenny for backup, too scared to take control of the situation on her own in fear that Audrey will hate her if confronted. Audrey is found at a motel with BZ, and Helen later turns the children over to Jenny's custody, much to their dismay.
Helen goes back to work and slowly returns to her previous way of living, but soon realizes she is not happy. She goes to Jenny's to take the children back, adamant she is ready to put her foot down and be a mother, but Jenny asks her to leave and think about it some more. Later that night, as Helen sits alone in the nearby park, Jenny appears and allows Helen to read her letter from Lindsay; in it, Lindsay explains she chose Helen to care for her children because their personalities are so similar and she wanted the children to have a mother figure who reminds them of her.
Finally having accepted Helen can cope, Jenny returns the children to her the following morning, and they happily begin to settle into their new family life.

title: Hot Fuzz
tagline: Big cops. Small town. Moderate violence.
overview: As a former London constable, Nicholas Angel finds it difficult to adapt to his new assignment in the sleepy British village of Sandford. Not only does he miss the excitement of the big city, but he also has a well-meaning oaf for a partner. However, when a series of grisly accidents rocks Sandford, Angel smells something rotten in the idyllic village.
plot:
Hot Fuzz is a 2007 action comedy film directed by Edgar Wright and written by Wright and Simon Pegg. The movie stars Pegg, Nick Frost, Timothy Dalton, and Jim Broadbent.

The film follows the story of Nicholas Angel (Pegg), a top-notch police officer in London who is known for his exceptional skills and bravery. However, after solving a high-profile case involving a serial killer, Angel becomes an embarrassment to the Metropolitan Police Service due to his unorthodox methods. As a result, he is transferred to the small town of Sandford, where crime rates are low and the police department is understaffed.

Upon arrival in Sandford, Angel meets his new partner, Danny Butterman (Frost), who is an enthusiastic but awkward local cop. The two men quickly clash due to their vastly different approaches to policing, with Angel's by-the-book methods contrasting with Butterman's more relaxed and intuitive approach.

As the story unfolds, a series of bizarre and gruesome murders takes place in Sandford, which Angel initially dismisses as a prank gone wrong. However, when the bodies start piling up, Angel realizes that something sinister is at play. He begins to investigate the murders, working closely with Butterman to uncover the truth behind the killings.

Throughout the investigation, Angel's fish-out-of-water experience in Sandford provides plenty of comedic moments, as he struggles to adapt to the town's eccentricities and the local police department's ineptitude. Meanwhile, Butterman's enthusiasm and loyalty provide a heartwarming counterpoint to Angel's cynicism.

As the plot thickens, Angel and Butterman uncover a shocking conspiracy involving a corrupt politician, a sinister plot to cover up the murders, and a surprising connection between the victims. The film builds towards an action-packed climax as Angel and Butterman confront the mastermind behind the killings in a thrilling showdown.

One of the standout aspects of Hot Fuzz is its clever subversion of action movie tropes, with Wright and Pegg paying homage to classic films like Die Hard and Beverly Hills Cop while also cleverly deconstructing them. The film's witty dialogue, memorable characters, and expertly choreographed action sequences make it a joy to watch.

Ultimately, Hot Fuzz is a hilarious and entertaining ride that balances humor and suspense with ease. With its talented cast, clever writing, and Edgar Wright's masterful direction, the film has become a cult classic and a staple of 2000s British comedy.

title: Read It and Weep
overview: A young girl turns into an A-List celebrity over night when her private journal is accidently published and becomes a best-seller.
plot:
Read It and Weep is a 2006 American comedy-drama Disney Channel Original Movie, which premiered on July 21, 2006. Based on Julia DeVillers's novel How My Private, Personal Journal Became a Bestseller, it stars real-life sisters Kay Panabaker as the ninth-grader Jamie Bartlett and Danielle Panabaker as Isabella, or "Is", the confident heroine of Jamie's imagination. Jason Dolley, Alexandra Krosney, Allison Scagliotti, Nick Whitaker and Robin Riker co-star, and DeVillers makes a cameo in a pizza parlour scene.

Jamie is a freshman with three close friends, Connor, Lindsay and Harmony, a brother named Lenny, and a rival, the popular Sawyer Sullivan, whose boyfriend Marco Vega is Jamie's crush. On her tablet computer she keeps a daily journal starring Is, a glamorous girl with remarkable powers who stands up to a nasty classmate named Myrna. The stories are a fanciful version of Jamie's own life, and Myrna is clearly modelled on Sawyer. When her printer breaks on the day an English essay is due, Jamie emails the file to Lindsay to print, but sends the journal by mistake. Lindsay hands it in, the journal wins a writing contest, and it is published as a novel.

The book becomes a bestseller and Jamie a celebrity, touring signings and talk shows and meeting stars she has long admired. Fame goes to her head: she grows materialistic and dismissive, quits her job at her father's struggling pizza restaurant, mocks Lenny's guitar playing and neglects her friends. During a television interview she lets slip that the villain is based on Sawyer and that the book draws on real school dramas, and her classmates turn against her, hurt by what she has written about them.

Shunned by her friends, Jamie sets out to repair the damage. She apologises to Lenny and encourages him to play again, learns that her parents may have to close the restaurant, and finally confronts Is, telling her imaginary alter ego to stop steering her life. At the ocean-themed school dance her classmates gradually accept that the journal was never meant to be published. Jamie discovers that the poems she admired in class were written by Connor, not Marco, and the two share a kiss while Lenny performs a song for her. Afterwards a mishap with seaweed on the restaurant's pizzas proves a hit with customers, giving the family business a way to survive.

title: Across the Universe
tagline: All you need is love.
overview: When young dockworker Jude leaves Liverpool to find his estranged father in the United States, he is swept up by the waves of change that are re-shaping the nation. Jude falls in love with Lucy, who joins the growing anti-war movement. plot:
In the 1960s, Jude Feeney, a young shipyard worker in Liverpool, heads to the US to find his G.I. father who conceived him during World War II, whom he has never met. He promises his girlfriend Molly he will stay in touch while he is away.
Meanwhile, in New Jersey, Lucy Carrigan worries about her boyfriend Daniel, who is headed for service in the Vietnam War. In Dayton, Ohio, cheerleader Prudence pines for another member of her all-female cheerleader squad in high school. Prudence then drops out of school in shame.
Jude meets his father Wes, a janitor at Princeton University. Son does not particularly bond with father as Jude just wanted to let him know that he exists, but Wes assures him he would have been there for him if he had known about him.
While on the Princeton campus, Jude meets and befriends slacker student Max, who brings him home for Thanksgiving. Max introduces Jude to his family, including his younger sister Lucy. Max drops out of college; he and Jude move into a bohemian enclave in Greenwich Village run by a singer, Sadie. Jude becomes a freelance artist, and Max is a cab driver. Daniel is killed in Vietnam, and Lucy attends his funeral.
In Detroit, a young African-American boy is killed in the 1967 riot. His adult brother Jo-Jo, a guitarist, moves to New York for a change of scenery and auditions for Sadie's band. They are soon joined by Prudence, who had hitchhiked to New York.
Lucy goes to Max in New York for a visit before she starts college. Soon, she and Jude fall in love. Max, initially displeased upon learning they slept together, gives them his blessing when he realizes Jude is in love with Lucy. Later, Max is drafted into the army and sent to Vietnam, as he is no longer a college student protected from the draft. Prudence is attracted to Sadie and becomes depressed when Sadie and Jo-Jo begin a relationship.
Lucy becomes increasingly involved in the anti-war movement. Jude remains comparatively apolitical but devoted to her. Sadie is offered a chance to go on a solo tour as a headliner, leading to a bitter breakup between her, Jo-Jo, and her original band. Jude dislikes the increasing amount of time Lucy spends with the Students for a Democratic Republic, led by activist Paco, as he suspects that Paco is attempting to seduce her.
Jude storms into the SDR office, leading to an argument with Lucy and a fight with Paco, after which Jude is thrown out. Lucy breaks up with him. Some time later, Jude follows her to an anti-war demonstration at Columbia University. When the police arrest Lucy, Paco, and the other activists, Jude's attempts to reach her lead to his arrest as well.
With Jude facing deportation, Lucy contacts his father. Wes visits Jude in jail, but has no legal proof that Jude is his son and thus an American citizen. As a result, Jude is sent back to England.

title: Sympathy for Mr. Vengeance
tagline: Revenge Was Never This Sweet
overview: A deaf man and his girlfriend resort to desperate measures in order to fund a kidney transplant for his sister. Things go horribly wrong, and the situation spirals rapidly into a cycle of violence and revenge.
plot:
Ryu is a deaf-mute man who works in a factory. His ailing sister is in desperate need of a kidney transplant. Unfortunately Ryu's blood type is not a match. After he loses his job, Ryu contacts a group of black market organ dealers to exchange one of his kidneys as well as ₩10 million (about $7,200 US) for one that his sister can use. However, the dealers disappear after taking Ryu's kidney and severance money. A legitimate kidney donor is found, but after having been conned by the organ dealers, Ryu is unable to afford the operation. To raise money, Yeong-mi, Ryu's radical anarchist girlfriend, suggests kidnapping the daughter of the executive who fired Ryu. They observe the executive with company president Park Dong-jin arriving at the latter's home one day, where one of Dong-jin's former employees, Peng, attempts to commit suicide in front of them. Ryu and Yeong-mi change their plan, deciding to kidnap Dong-jin's young daughter Yu-sun instead.
Yu-sun stays with Ryu's sister, who believes that Ryu is babysitting Yu-sun. Ryu, his sister, and Yeong-Mi treat Yu-Sun with kindness while she is with her kidnappers, and when Yu-Sun reveals that her mom left the house after her parents' divorce, Ryu makes a necklace for Yu-Sun adorned with beads and seashells. While Ryu's sister blow-dries Yu-Sun's hair, she asks her to come visit her again and gives her a note with her phone number. She then discovers Ryu's job termination paper in his pants pocket while doing laundry and calls Ryu's employer to inquire. Meanwhile, Ryu and Yeong-mi send a request for ransom to Dong-jin, and he obliges.
Upon returning home with the ransom money, Ryu discovers that his sister learned that Yu-sun was kidnapped and, not wanting to be a burden any longer, killed herself in the bathtub. Ryu takes Yu-sun and his sister's body to a riverbed they frequented as children to bury her. Distracted by the burial and unable to hear, Ryu is unaware when Yu-sun slips into the river, where she drowns. A disabled wanderer steals Yu-Sun's necklace.
After Yu-sun's body is discovered by the authorities, a deeply mournful Dong-jin hires the detective on the case to find her kidnappers with bribe money from selling his company and house. The detective finds Ryu's sister's note on Yu-Sun and searches their apartment, but the place is abandoned and they cannot link the murder. Dong-Jin suspects that Peng is behind the murder, but they find Peng and his family dead by suicide in their home. Dong-Jin realizes one of their children is barely alive and takes him to the hospital, hoping to save him.
Dong-Jin returns to Ryu's apartment and overhears a local radio program where the host reads a letter Ryu has sent about the painful death of his sister. Dong-Jin visits the radio station and sees a painting that Ryu has sent along with the letter depicting his sister's burial and Yu-Sun's death.

title: Southland Tales
tagline: Have a nice apocalypse.
overview: Set in the futuristic landscape of Los Angeles on July 4, 2008, as it stands on the brink of social, economic and environmental disaster. Boxer Santaros is an action star who's stricken with amnesia. His life intertwines with Krysta Now, an adult film star developing her own reality television project, and Ronald Taverner, a Hermosa Beach police officer who holds the key to a vast conspiracy.
plot:
Southland Tales is a 2006 dystopian black comedy thriller written and directed by Richard Kelly, with an ensemble cast including Dwayne Johnson, Seann William Scott, Sarah Michelle Gellar, Mandy Moore, Justin Timberlake, Will Sasso and Wallace Shawn, and music by Moby. Set in the then-near future of 2008, it is a sprawling satirical portrait of Los Angeles and a commentary on the military-industrial complex, surveillance and the infotainment industry.

On July 4, 2005, nuclear attacks destroy the Texas cities of El Paso and Abilene, plunging the world into a third world war. The United States reinstates the draft and creates US-IDENT, a vast surveillance agency. Amid a fuel crisis, the company Treer unveils Fluid Karma, a seemingly limitless energy source generated by ocean currents, while its scientist Baron von Westphalen harbors grander ambitions.

In Los Angeles in 2008, the action star Boxer Santaros, married to the daughter of a Republican vice-presidential candidate, wakes up with amnesia in the desert and begins an affair with Krysta Now, a former adult film star turned would-be talk show host. Together they have written a screenplay that seems to predict the apocalypse. A cell of neo-Marxist radicals plots to discredit the government by staging a fake act of police brutality, involving Boxer and the police officer Roland Taverner, whose apparent twin brother Ronald is to be dressed in his uniform. But a rogue officer turns the staged killing into a real one, and the leaked footage ignites riots across the city.

As Los Angeles erupts, the elite gather aboard von Westphalen's giant zeppelin to celebrate the launch of Fluid Karma. Boxer learns that Treer's experiments have torn a rift in time, that he is a future version of himself who traveled back an instant, and that contact between two versions of the same person could bring about the apocalypse. Roland and Ronald are likewise the same man from two timelines. When they finally clasp hands, they rise into the air as a rift opens in the sky, and a missile destroys the zeppelin with Boxer aboard. The narrator, Iraq war veteran Pilot Abilene, describes the dawning of a new age.

The film premiered in competition at the 2006 Cannes Film Festival, where it was poorly received, and was re-edited before its US release on November 14, 2007. Critics were divided by its length and chaotic structure despite its intriguing vision; it grossed under $400,000 but has since developed a cult following.

title: Cassandra's Dream
tagline: Family is family. Blood is blood.
overview: The tale of two brothers with serious financial woes. When a third party proposes they turn to crime, things go bad and the two become enemies.
plot:
Cassandra's Dream is a 2007 crime thriller drama written and directed by Woody Allen, starring Colin Farrell, Ewan McGregor, Hayley Atwell, Sally Hawkins and Tom Wilkinson. Shot in England as a co-production between the United States, France and the United Kingdom, it was the third of Allen's London-set films of the period, following Match Point and Scoop, and it features an original score by Philip Glass.

Brothers Ian and Terry live in South London. Their father runs a struggling restaurant, while their mother has always encouraged them to look up to her brother Howard, a wealthy plastic surgeon whose business has expanded to clinics abroad. Using money Terry won on a greyhound named Cassandra's Dream, the brothers buy a bargain sailboat and name it after the dog. Ian, ambitious and restless, falls for Angela Stark, a glamorous young actress, and dreams of investing in California hotels to build a new life with her. Terry, a mechanic with a gambling problem, sinks deeper and deeper into debt after a disastrous run at cards.

Desperate, the brothers turn to Uncle Howard when he visits from abroad. He agrees to help them, but asks a terrible favor in return: they must kill Martin Burns, a former business associate who is prepared to testify against Howard and could send him to prison. After initial horror, both brothers agree. Their first attempt, using homemade untraceable guns, is abandoned when Burns comes home with a companion, but the next day they follow him and carry out the killing. Ian is able to move on, but Terry is consumed by guilt, turning to alcohol and pills and talking of confessing to the police. Ian and Howard conclude that Terry must be silenced. During an outing on the boat, Ian plans to poison his brother but cannot go through with it; a violent struggle breaks out and Terry accidentally kills Ian. The police later find the boat adrift and conclude that Terry killed his brother before drowning himself.

The film premiered at the 64th Venice International Film Festival in September 2007 after an unannounced screening in Avilés, Spain, and was released in the United States in January 2008. Critical opinion was sharply divided. Some reviewers dismissed it as a clichéd morality play and among Allen's weakest films, while others praised it as a modern tale of temptation; The New Yorker's Richard Brody named it one of the best films of the decade.

title: Ghost Dog: The Way of the Samurai
original_title: Ghost Dog: The Way of the Samurai
tagline: Live by the code. Die by the code.
overview: An African-American Mafia hit man who models himself after the samurai of old finds himself targeted for death by the mob. Jarmusch's spiritual gangster film tells the story of an inner-city hit man (Whitaker) who lives on a rooftop, training himself as a samurai in the strictest sense. plot:
Ghost Dog: The Way of the Samurai is a 1999 crime drama written, produced and directed by Jim Jarmusch. Forest Whitaker stars as Ghost Dog, a hitman for the Mafia who lives by the ancient code of the samurai as set out in the Hagakure, the collection of sayings attributed to Yamamoto Tsunetomo. Cliff Gorman, Henry Silva, Isaach de Bankolé, Victor Argo and Camille Winbush appear in supporting roles, and RZA of the Wu-Tang Clan, who composed the score, makes his film debut. An international co-production between the United States, France, Germany and Japan, the film competed for the Palme d'Or at the 1999 Cannes Film Festival.

Ghost Dog lives alone on a rooftop in an unnamed American city with a flock of homing pigeons, which he uses to communicate. He considers himself the retainer of Louie, a small-time mobster who saved his life years earlier, and he has served him faithfully as a contract killer ever since, applying the wisdom of the Hagakure, which is quoted throughout the film, to his everyday existence.

Louie orders him to kill Handsome Frank, a gangster who has been sleeping with the daughter of the mob boss Vargo. Ghost Dog carries out the hit, but discovers that the young woman is also in the room. He spares her, and she gives him a copy of the book Rashōmon. To avoid blame for the murder of a made man, Vargo and his associates decide that Ghost Dog must be eliminated. Since Louie knows almost nothing about his retainer, the mobsters track him down by searching the city's pigeon coops, and they kill his birds. Ghost Dog realises that he must strike back against Vargo's crew, even while remaining loyal to Louie. Meanwhile, he spends time with his best friend Raymond, a French-speaking ice-cream vendor with whom he shares no common language, and befriends Pearline, a young girl with whom he exchanges books.

Jarmusch blends the gangster film with samurai cinema and hip-hop culture, drawing on influences such as Jean-Pierre Melville's Le Samouraï, and treats the aging Mafia figures as men clinging to a fading code of their own.

Ghost Dog received largely positive reviews, with an approval rating of about 84 percent on Rotten Tomatoes, and critics praised Whitaker's performance, the film's offbeat humour and RZA's score.

title: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button
original_title: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button
tagline: Life isn't measured in minutes, but in moments.
overview: I was born under unusual circumstances. And so begins The Curious Case of Benjamin Button, adapted from the 1920s story by F. Scott Fitzgerald about a man who is born in his eighties and ages backwards: a man, like any of us, who is unable to stop time. We follow his story, set in New Orleans, from the end of World War I in 1918 into the 21st century, following his journey that is as unusual as any man's life can be. Benjamin Button, is a grand tale of a not-so-ordinary man and the people and places he discovers along the way, the loves he finds, the joys of life and the sadness of death, and what lasts beyond time.
plot:
The Curious Case of Benjamin Button is a 2008 American fantasy drama directed by David Fincher, adapted by Eric Roth and Robin Swicord from F. Scott Fitzgerald's 1922 short story. Brad Pitt stars as a man who ages in reverse and Cate Blanchett as Daisy, the love of his life, with Taraji P. Henson, Julia Ormond, Jason Flemyng, Elias Koteas and Tilda Swinton. After decades in development, it was released by Paramount Pictures in North America and Warner Bros. internationally on 25 December 2008.

In August 2005, as Hurricane Katrina approaches, the elderly Daisy Fuller lies dying in a New Orleans hospital. She tells her daughter Caroline about a blind clockmaker who built a station clock that ran backward, in memory of the young men, including his own son, killed in the First World War. Daisy then asks Caroline to read aloud from the diary of Benjamin Button. On the night of 11 November 1918, a baby is born with the appearance and ailments of a very old man. His mother dies after the birth, and his father, the wealthy button manufacturer Thomas Button, abandons him on the steps of a nursing home. Queenie, a caretaker there, raises him as her own and names him Benjamin.

Benjamin grows older in mind but younger in body, moving from a wheelchair to crutches and learning to walk. In 1930 he meets seven-year-old Daisy, whose grandmother lives at the home, and they form an immediate bond. As a young-looking old man, he goes to work on a tugboat captained by Mike Clark and travels the world, sending postcards to Daisy, who becomes a dancer in New York. In Murmansk he has an affair with Elizabeth Abbott, the wife of a British official, and during the Second World War his tugboat is drawn into combat. Returning home, he reunites with his dying father, who has revealed himself, and inherits his fortune. Benjamin and Daisy's paths cross repeatedly as they move in opposite directions through time, until in middle age they finally meet in the same moment of their lives and fall in love, knowing their time together is fleeting.

The film received generally positive reviews and grossed over $335 million worldwide. It received thirteen Academy Award nominations, the most of that year, including Best Picture, Best Director and Best Actor for Pitt, and won three, for Best Art Direction, Best Makeup and Best Visual Effects.

title: Howl's Moving Castle
tagline: The two lived there.
overview: When Sophie, a shy young woman, is cursed with an old body by a spiteful witch, her only chance of breaking the spell lies with a self-indulgent yet insecure young wizard and his companions in his legged, walking castle.
plot:
Howl's Moving Castle (Japanese: ハウルの動く城) is a 2004 Japanese animated fantasy film written and directed by Hayao Miyazaki, loosely based on Diana Wynne Jones's 1986 novel. Produced by Toshio Suzuki at Studio Ghibli and distributed by Toho, it features the voices of Chieko Baisho, Takuya Kimura and Akihiro Miwa. Set in a fictional kingdom where magic coexists with early 20th-century technology during a war, it reflects Miyazaki's opposition to the Iraq War.

Sophie, a shy young hatmaker, is rescued from two soldiers by a mysterious wizard, Howl. That evening, the jealous Witch of the Waste enters Sophie's shop and curses her, transforming her into a ninety-year-old woman who cannot speak of the spell. Sophie leaves home and wanders into the hills, where she befriends an enchanted scarecrow she names Turnip Head, who leads her to Howl's huge walking castle. Inside, she meets Howl's young apprentice, Markl, and Calcifer, a fire demon bound to Howl by a contract and the source of the castle's power. Calcifer promises to break her curse if she frees him, and she becomes the castle's cleaning lady.

The king summons Howl to aid in the war, but Howl sends Sophie, posing as his mother, to declare him a coward. At the palace, Madame Suliman, the royal sorceress and Howl's former teacher, strips the Witch of the Waste of her powers, reducing her to a harmless old woman, and threatens Howl with the same fate. Howl rescues Sophie, and they escape with the Witch and Suliman's dog. Sophie learns that Howl has been transforming into a bird-like creature to fight against both sides of the war, at the risk of losing his humanity, and her feelings for him grow.

When the town is bombed, Howl leaves to protect his household. To save him, Sophie removes Calcifer from the hearth, collapsing the castle. Through a magic ring, she travels into Howl's past and sees him as a boy swallowing a falling star, Calcifer, and giving the demon his heart. She returns Howl's heart to him, freeing Calcifer and breaking her own curse. Her kiss transforms Turnip Head back into a missing prince of the enemy kingdom, who sets off to end the war, and Sophie and Howl fly off together in a rebuilt castle.

Howl's Moving Castle premiered at the Venice Film Festival and became one of Japan's most successful films, grossing about $236 million worldwide. It received critical acclaim and was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature.

title: Leatherheads
tagline: If Love Is a Game, Who'll Make the First Pass?
overview: A light hearted comedy about the beginnings of Professional American Football. When a decorated war hero and college all star is tempted into playing professional football. Everyone see the chance to make some big money, but when a reporter digs up some dirt on the war hero... everyone could lose out.
plot:
Leatherheads is a 2008 American sports comedy directed by George Clooney, who also stars, written by Duncan Brantley and Rick Reilly. Set in the early years of professional American football, it co-stars Renée Zellweger, John Krasinski, Jonathan Pryce, Stephen Root and Wayne Duvall. Universal Pictures released it on 4 April 2008.

In 1925, Jimmy "Dodge" Connelly, an aging player, captains the Duluth Bulldogs, a struggling professional football team. With the professional game on the verge of collapse and players unpaid, Dodge persuades Carter "the Bullet" Rutherford, a star player at Princeton and a celebrated First World War hero, to join the Bulldogs, hoping that his fame will draw crowds. Carter's arrival transforms the team's fortunes, and the games attract huge audiences.

Lexie Littleton, a fast-talking reporter for the Chicago Tribune, is assigned to prove that Carter's wartime heroics, which supposedly involved capturing a group of German soldiers single-handedly, are a fabrication. As she travels with the team, she finds herself caught in a love triangle with Dodge and Carter. Carter eventually confesses to her that the German platoon surrendered to him by mistake, but he also discovers her assignment and learns that she has shared a kiss with Dodge. Pressured by threats from Carter's slick manager, Lexie publishes the story, while the manager uses underhanded tactics, including bribing a key witness, to discredit her. Meanwhile, a commissioner appointed to clean up the sport introduces formal rules that threaten the improvised tricks on which Dodge relies. When public opinion turns against Lexie, Dodge intervenes at a hearing, forcing the truth into the open, and the story builds toward a muddy, decisive game between the Bulldogs and Carter's new team in Chicago, in which Dodge must use all his cunning to win.

Leatherheads received mixed reviews; critics appreciated its affectionate homage to the screwball comedies of the 1930s and its period atmosphere but found it uneven and slow. It grossed about $41 million worldwide against a budget of $58 million.

overview: World War I has left golfer Rannulph Junuh a poker-playing alcoholic, his perfect swing gone. Now, however, he needs to get it back to play in a tournament to save the financially ravaged golf course of a long-ago sweetheart. Help arrives in the form of mysterious caddy Bagger Vance.
plot:
The Legend of Bagger Vance is a 2000 American sports drama film directed by Robert Redford. The movie tells the story of Rannulph Junuh, a young golfer from Georgia who seeks the advice of an enigmatic caddie named Bagger Vance to help him win a high-stakes golf tournament.

At its core, The Legend of Bagger Vance is a film about redemption and self-discovery. Rannulph's journey is one of coming to terms with his past mistakes and finding forgiveness from himself and others. Through his interactions with Bagger Vance, who embodies the values of humility, integrity, and respect for nature, Rannulph learns to let go of his ego and find a deeper connection with the game of golf.

The film also explores themes of friendship and loyalty, as Rannulph forms a bond with Bagger Vance, who becomes like a mentor to him. The movie highlights the importance of relationships in our lives and how they can help us grow and learn from our experiences.

Furthermore, The Legend of Bagger Vance is a story about finding one's true purpose and identity. Rannulph's journey is not just about winning a golf tournament, but about discovering who he is as a person and what truly matters to him in life. Through his experiences, he learns to appreciate the simple things in life and finds a sense of peace and contentment.

Overall, The Legend of Bagger Vance is a film that celebrates the beauty of nature, the importance of relationships, and the power of self-discovery and redemption.

title: The International
tagline: Is your money making a killing?
overview: An interpol agent and an attorney are determined to bring one of the world's most powerful banks to justice. Uncovering money laundering, arms trading, and conspiracy to destabilize world governments, their investigation takes them from Berlin, Milan, New York and Istanbul. Finding themselves in a chase across the globe, their relentless tenacity puts their own lives at risk.
plot:
Louis Salinger, an Interpol detective, and Eleanor Whitman, an Assistant District Attorney from Manhattan, are assigned to investigate the International Bank of Business and Credit (IBBC), which funds criminal activities such as money laundering, terrorism, arms trading, and the destabilization of governments. Salinger's and Whitman's investigation takes them to Milan, where the IBBC assassinates Umberto Calvini, an arms manufacturer and Italian prime ministerial candidate. The assassin diverts suspicion to a local assassin with political connections to the Red Brigades, who is then promptly killed by a corrupt policeman. Salinger and Whitman get a lead on the second assassin, but the policeman confronts the two and orders them out of the country. At the airport, they are able to check the security camera footage for clues on the whereabouts of the bank's assassin, and follow a suspect to New York City.
In New York, Salinger and Whitman are met by two New York Police Department detectives, Iggy Ornelas and Bernie Ward, who have a photograph of the assassin's face. Salinger, Ornelas, and Ward locate Dr. Isaacson to whose practice the assassin's leg brace has been traced, and they are able to locate him at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum.
Jonas Skarssen, the chairman of the IBBC, reveals to his lawyer White and security adviser Wexler that Calvini was killed so they could have his sons purchase missile guidance systems in which the bank has invested. Since the bank understands that Salinger and Whitman are close to finding their assassin, they send a team of hitmen to kill him, while Wexler is arrested by Ornelas. As Salinger and Ward speak to the assassin and attempt to arrest him, a massive shootout at the Guggenheim erupts when a number of gunmen attack them. Ward is killed in the chaos, and Salinger is forced to team up with the assassin to fight off the gunmen. However, the assassin is mortally wounded during their escape and dies of his injuries.
When Salinger goes to interrogate Wexler, a veteran Stasi officer, the latter reveals that the IBBC is practically untouchable due to its connections to terrorist organizations, drug cartels, governments, and powerful corporations, though Wexler indicates a willingness to help Salinger take down the IBBC. Meanwhile, Salinger persuades Whitman to let him continue alone.
In Italy, Salinger tells Calvini's sons of the IBBC's responsibility for their father's murder, prompting them to cancel the deal with the bank and order White to be killed. Salinger then accompanies Wexler to Istanbul, where Skarssen is buying the guidance systems from their only other manufacturer, Ahmet Sunay. Salinger attempts to record the conversation so that he can obstruct the deal by proving to the buyers that the missiles will be useless, but he ultimately fails. Both Wexler and Skarssen are then killed by a hitman contracted by the Calvinis to avenge their father's murder.

plot:
The Green Butchers (Danish: De grønne slagtere) is a 2003 Danish black comedy written and directed by Anders Thomas Jensen. It stars Mads Mikkelsen as Svend, nicknamed "Sweat", and Nikolaj Lie Kaas in the dual roles of the butcher Bjarne and his twin brother Eigil, with Line Kruse as Astrid. The film follows two misfit butchers whose new business becomes a runaway success thanks to a gruesome secret ingredient.

Svend and Bjarne work in a butcher shop under their arrogant and condescending boss, Holger, who mocks Svend's pride and joy, his special marinade. Insecure and desperate for recognition, Svend persuades the withdrawn Bjarne to go into business with him, and they open their own shop in a small Danish town. Bjarne has his own reason for needing money: his intellectually disabled twin brother Eigil, left brain-damaged by a car accident that killed their parents and Bjarne's wife, has been kept on life support for years, and Bjarne is ready to claim his inheritance.

On opening day no customers come. Then Svend accidentally locks an electrician in the cold store overnight, and the man freezes to death. In panic, Svend disposes of the body by turning it into meat, marinating it and selling it, and the new product, which he calls "chicky-wickies", becomes a sensation, drawing long queues of customers. Bjarne is horrified but reluctantly goes along with the scheme as business booms. To keep up with demand, Svend must find more ingredients, while Bjarne's life is complicated by his relationship with Astrid, a kind young woman who works at the local church, and by Eigil, an innocent, animal-loving man who unexpectedly wakes up when his life support is switched off and turns up at the shop.

Jensen's comedy uses its grotesque premise to explore loneliness, insecurity, grief and the desire for acceptance, mixing deadpan humor with surprising tenderness.

The Green Butchers won several European awards, including the 2003 Méliès d'Or. It holds an approval rating of about 63 percent on Rotten Tomatoes, and later reappraisals, such as a 2023 Collider review, praised the nuance of both the script and Mikkelsen's performance.

title: Vicky Cristina Barcelona
tagline: Life is the ultimate work of art.
overview: Two girlfriends on a summer holiday in Spain become enamored with the same painter, unaware that his ex-wife, with whom he has a tempestuous relationship, is about to re-enter the picture.
plot:
Vicky Cristina Barcelona is a 2008 romantic comedy-drama film written and directed by Woody Allen. Rebecca Hall and Scarlett Johansson star as Vicky and Cristina, two young American women spending a summer in Spain, with Javier Bardem as the painter Juan Antonio and Penélope Cruz as his volatile ex-wife, María Elena, with Patricia Clarkson, Kevin Dunn and Chris Messina in supporting roles and Christopher Evan Welch as the narrator. Filmed in Barcelona, Avilés and Oviedo, it premiered at the 2008 Cannes Film Festival.

Vicky and Cristina, close friends with very different attitudes toward love, spend a summer in Barcelona staying with Vicky's relative Judy and her husband, Mark. Vicky, practical and conventional, is engaged to the dependable Doug, while Cristina sees herself as a free spirit but is uncertain about what she wants. At an art exhibition, they notice Juan Antonio, an attractive painter rumored to have had a violent relationship with his former wife. He boldly invites both women to fly with him to Oviedo for a weekend of sightseeing, food, wine and, he frankly hopes, lovemaking. Cristina is immediately enthusiastic; Vicky, unimpressed, comes along to keep an eye on her friend.

When Cristina falls ill with food poisoning on the first night, Vicky and Juan Antonio spend the weekend together, and despite her resistance she is charmed and sleeps with him, an experience that leaves her shaken. Back in Barcelona, Cristina begins a relationship with Juan Antonio and moves into his home, while Vicky, troubled by her feelings, goes ahead with her marriage to Doug. Then María Elena, a brilliant but unstable artist, arrives after a suicide attempt, and Juan Antonio takes her in. Instead of driving Cristina away, the situation evolves into a passionate three-way relationship in which Cristina finds inspiration for her photography. As the summer progresses, however, Cristina grows restless, Vicky remains drawn to Juan Antonio, and the tangled relationships come to a head in a dramatic confrontation that sends the two Americans home changed, if not wiser.

The film received widespread acclaim, particularly for Cruz's fiery performance and Bardem's charm, and was one of Allen's biggest late-career successes, grossing nearly $100 million worldwide. Cruz won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress, and the film won the Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy.

title: The Sugarland Express
tagline: Every cop in the state was after her. Everybody else was behind her.
overview: Married small-time crooks Lou-Jean and Clovis Poplin lose their baby to the state of Texas and resolve to do whatever it takes to get him back. Lou-Jean gets Clovis out of jail, and the two steal their son from his foster home, in addition to taking a highway patrolman hostage. As a massive dragnet starts to pursue them across Texas, the couple become unlikely folk heroes and even start to bond with the captive policeman.
plot:
The Sugarland Express is an American crime drama of 1974 and Steven Spielberg's first theatrical feature as director, following his television film Duel. Hal Barwood and Matthew Robbins wrote the screenplay from a story they developed with Spielberg. Based on real events, it stars Goldie Hawn as Lou Jean Poplin and William Atherton as her husband Clovis, who take a state trooper hostage and flee across Texas to reclaim their child, with Michael Sacks as the trooper Maxwell Slide and Ben Johnson as Captain Tanner. It began his partnership with John Williams.

In April 1969, Lou Jean visits Clovis in prison to tell him that their young son is about to be placed with foster parents. Although he is only four months from release, she persuades him to escape and help her get the boy back. The pair hitch a ride away from the prison with a couple, but when Patrolman Slide of the Texas Department of Public Safety pulls the car over, they make off in it. After the car crashes, they overpower Slide and take him hostage in his own patrol car.

What follows is a slow-moving chase across Texas, with the fugitives and their captive at the head of an ever-growing convoy, first of police cars and later of news vans, helicopters and ordinary citizens who join in. Holding Slide allows the couple to keep refueling and to obtain food and supplies, some from sympathetic locals, and over the long journey the three come to like and respect one another. When the trio stop at a used car lot to commandeer a camper, local vigilantes attack them, but Tanner lets the Poplins drive on after further bargaining.

When they reach Sugarland, Tanner urges Clovis to give himself up, but he refuses. Slide, and then Clovis, sense that something is wrong at the foster parents' house, yet Lou Jean insists that her husband go in for their son. Two Texas Rangers shoot Clovis, mortally wounding him, and after a further chase Lou Jean is arrested; Slide is found unharmed. A closing epilogue explains that Lou Jean served fifteen months of a five-year sentence and later won the right to live with her son.

Parts of the film were shot in Sugar Land, where some of the real events took place, and around San Antonio and other Texas towns. It won the award for Best Screenplay at the 1974 Cannes Film Festival and drew positive reviews, but with a worldwide gross of about $12 million it remains the lowest-grossing film of Spielberg's career, and Universal pulled it from theaters after two weeks.

plot:
August Rush is a musical drama film released in 2007 by Warner Bros. Pictures. The movie tells the story of an adopted boy named Evan Taylor, who discovers his birth parents and embarks on a journey to find his roots.

The film begins with Evan (played by Freddie Highmore), a talented young musician who lives with his foster parents, Robert and Lily Taylor (played by Jonathan Rhys Meyers and Keri Russell). Despite their love for him, Evan feels like an outsider in his family. He is haunted by strange memories of music and a sense of belonging he can't explain.

As Evan grows older, he begins to experience vivid dreams and visions that seem to be connected to the music he hears. He becomes obsessed with finding the source of these sounds, which lead him on a journey to New York City. There, he meets a street musician named Gus (played by Jason Schwartzman), who claims to have known Evan's biological father.

Evan soon discovers that his birth parents were both musicians who were part of a famous jazz band in the 1950s. He learns that his mother, Lyla (played by Marcia Gay Harden), was a singer and songwriter, while his father, Robert Lewis (played by Terence Stamp), was a pianist and composer.

As Evan delves deeper into his family's past, he meets his biological siblings, Charlie (played by James Carnes) and Isabel (played by Fiona Shaw). Together, they form a band and begin to perform music that is a fusion of their different styles. Through this process, Evan comes to terms with his identity and finds a sense of belonging.

However, the journey is not without its challenges. Evan's biological father, Robert Lewis, had abandoned his family years ago, leaving behind a legacy of unfinished business. As Evan gets to know him, he learns about the sacrifices his father made for his music and the pain he caused by leaving his family.

The film builds towards a emotional climax as Evan confronts his past and makes amends with his father. In the end, Evan finds a sense of peace and belonging, not just through his music but also through his connection to his biological family.

Overall, August Rush is a heartwarming story about identity, family, and the power of music to bring people together. The film features a talented cast, beautiful music, and a poignant storyline that will leave audiences feeling uplifted and inspired.

title: The Astronaut Farmer
overview: Texan Charles Farmer left the Air Force as a young man to save the family ranch when his dad died. Like most American ranchers, he owes his bank. plot:
Charles Farmer is a former United States Air Force fighter pilot and astronaut-in-training who reluctantly resigned from the space program and was discharged from the military before he could fulfill his dream of becoming a vital part of NASA. He did so in order to take over his family's failing ranch in Texas after his financially strapped father's suicide prior to the ranch being foreclosed on.
Having missed the opportunity to travel into space, he decides to build a working replica of the historic Mercury-Atlas rocket and spacecraft in the barn on his secluded ranch in the fictional town of Story, Texas, using all his assets and facing his own foreclosure of the ranch as a result. But he has done so with the ongoing support of his wife Audrey, his teenage son Shepard, and young daughters Stanley and Sunshine. When he begins making inquiries about purchasing rocket fuel, the FBI and FAA step in to investigate, and the ensuing publicity thrusts Farmer into the spotlight and makes him a media darling.
Farmer's launch is delayed by endless red tape created by U.S. government officials from the FAA, FBI, CIA, NASA and the Department of Defense, who seek to stall him beyond his deadline and force his creditors to foreclose on the farm. Farmer was counting on publicity to help him financially. He is denied the hydrazine fuel he requires, with government officials claiming he is a security risk and that it is too dangerous to allow a private citizen to launch a space vehicle. Facing financial ruin, he panics, climbs aboard, and, using a less-than-optimal substitute fuel, somehow launches the rocket. However, after only a foot or two of vertical lift, the rocket descends back down, falls over, and horizontally blasts out of the old wooden barn where it was constructed.
Farmer nearly dies from head trauma and other injuries after his capsule is thrown from the rocket. News media, spectators and all their vehicles are nearly crushed in the process. During the months he spends recuperating, public interest in his project wanes, and while he recovers slowly, he is depressed at the failure of the project and of his dream.
An inheritance from her father, Hal, is unexpectedly left to Audrey after his death, which allows them to bring their debts current. Audrey, realizing how much Charles' dream means to the entire family, encourages Charles to construct another rocket, financing it with the rest of her inheritance. He is able to do so in relative privacy.
Using a ruse to distract snooping government officials, Charles succeeds in launching the rocket The Dreamer, while the FAA claims no such thing has occurred. As the rocket rises out of the barn, the locals and law enforcement authorities in the area are amazed to watch it rise into space.

overview: After a botched assassination attempt, the mismatched duo finds themselves in Paris, struggling to retrieve a precious list of names, as the murderous crime syndicate's henchmen try their best to stop them. plot:
Rush Hour 3 is a 2007 action comedy film directed by Brett Ratner and starring Jackie Chan and Chris Tucker as the main characters, Inspector Lee and Detective James Carter. The movie takes place three years after the events of Rush Hour 2.

The story begins with Inspector Lee (Jackie Chan) being summoned to Paris by his friend, Inspector Soo-Yong (Ken Leung), who is now working for Interpol. Soo-Yong informs Lee that a valuable artifact, the "Dragon's Blood" diamond, has been stolen from a museum in Paris. The thief plans to sell it on the black market, and Soo-Yong needs Lee's help to track him down.

Upon arrival in Paris, Lee meets up with his old friend, Detective James Carter (Chris Tucker), who is now working for Interpol as well. Carter is initially reluctant to work with Lee again, but eventually agrees to help him solve the case.

As they begin their investigation, Lee and Carter discover that the thief is a wealthy businessman named Yuen (Yuen Wah), who has connections to the Triads. They also learn that Yuen plans to sell the diamond to a mysterious buyer in Dubai.

Lee and Carter's investigation takes them from Paris to Hong Kong, where they encounter various obstacles and challenges along the way. Along the way, Lee must confront his own personal demons and learn to trust Carter again.

As the story unfolds, Lee and Carter discover that Yuen is working with a group of Triad members who are seeking revenge against the Chinese government for their treatment of them in Hong Kong. The group plans to use the diamond to fund their operations and exact revenge on China.

In the climactic final act, Lee and Carter track down Yuen and his accomplices to Dubai, where they engage in a high-stakes battle to recover the stolen diamond. In the end, Lee and Carter successfully foil the plot, but not before Yuen is killed by one of his own accomplices.

The movie ends with Lee and Carter returning to Hong Kong as heroes, where they are greeted with parades and celebrations. The film concludes on a positive note, with Lee and Carter's friendship stronger than ever.

Overall, Rush Hour 3 received mixed reviews from critics, but was still a commercial success, grossing over $250 million worldwide. While it did not live up to the expectations of some fans, the movie still delivered plenty of action, humor, and excitement, making it a satisfying conclusion to the Rush Hour trilogy.

title: 3:10 to Yuma
tagline: Time waits for one man.
overview: In Arizona in the late 1800s, infamous outlaw Ben Wade and his vicious gang of thieves and murderers have plagued the Southern Railroad. When Wade is captured, Civil War veteran Dan Evans, struggling to survive on his drought-plagued ranch, volunteers to deliver him alive to the "3:10 to Yuma", a train that will take the killer to trial.
plot:
3:10 to Yuma is a 2007 American Western action drama directed by James Mangold and produced by Cathy Konrad. The second screen adaptation of Elmore Leonard's 1953 short story "Three-Ten to Yuma", following the 1957 film, it casts Christian Bale as a drought-stricken rancher who takes on the perilous job of escorting a notorious outlaw, played by Russell Crowe, to justice. It was filmed at various locations in New Mexico, premiered in Los Angeles in August 2007 and was released by Lionsgate on September 7.

In the Arizona Territory of 1884, Dan Evans, a struggling rancher and Civil War veteran, is in debt to Glen Hollander, whose men burn his barn. Searching for his scattered cattle with his two sons, Evans witnesses Ben Wade's gang rob a stagecoach guarded by Pinkertons. Wade takes the family's horses but leaves them alive, and Evans rescues the only surviving guard, Pinkerton agent Byron McElroy. In the town of Bisbee, Wade lingers with a barmaid and is arrested. Railroad agent Grayson Butterfield assembles a posse, including McElroy, the veterinarian Doc Potter and Hollander's man Tucker, to take Wade to Contention and put him on the 3:10 train to Yuma Territorial Prison, and Evans signs on for $200 to save his ranch.

On the journey, Wade kills Tucker with a stolen fork and throws McElroy off a cliff. Evans's elder son, William, follows and helps stop an escape. After an Apache attack, Wade flees to a camp of Chinese laborers whose foreman bears a grudge against him, and Potter is killed in the ensuing gunfight. In Contention, Wade's vicious lieutenant, Charlie Prince, offers $200 to anyone who kills a captor; the marshals desert, and Butterfield gives up. Evans refuses to quit, demanding better terms for his family and declaring that the task is now about honor; he reveals that he lost part of his leg after being accidentally shot by one of his own men during a retreat. Wade, who has escaped Yuma twice, helps Evans dodge the gunfire and boards the train, but Prince shoots Evans. Wade kills Prince and the rest of his gang, then surrenders his weapon as William comforts his dying father. As the train pulls away, Wade whistles and his horse gallops after it.

Crowe plays Wade and Bale plays Evans, with Peter Fonda as McElroy, Ben Foster as Prince, Logan Lerman as William, Dallas Roberts as Butterfield and Gretchen Mol as Alice Evans. Critics were enthusiastic, with 89% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and it grossed $71.2 million on a $48–55 million budget.

title: The Polar Express
tagline: This holiday season... believe.
overview: When a doubting young boy takes an extraordinary train ride to the North Pole, he embarks on a journey of self-discovery that shows him that the wonder of life never fades for those who believe.
plot:
The Polar Express is a 2004 animated film directed by Robert Zemeckis, produced by Castle Rock Entertainment, and based on the children's book of the same name by Chris Van Allsburg.

The story follows a young boy who lives in a small town with his parents. On Christmas Eve, he lies awake in bed, feeling lonely and disconnected from the magic of the holiday season. As he drifts off to sleep, he is visited by a mysterious train called the Polar Express, which arrives at his house and whisks him away on an adventure.

The boy boards the train, where he meets other children who are also traveling to the North Pole. They are greeted by the conductor, who welcomes them aboard with a warm smile. As they journey through the night, the boy experiences incredible sights and sensations: snow-covered landscapes, sparkling stars, and even a visit from Santa Claus himself.

However, not all of the passengers on the train are what they seem. One boy is revealed to be a "bad boy" who has been naughty throughout the year, and he is punished by being forced to sit in a cold, dark room with no toys or treats. The other children, including our protagonist, are rewarded for their good behavior.

As the journey continues, the boy begins to question whether the entire experience was just a dream. He wonders if he really did board the Polar Express, or if it was all just his imagination. But as he looks out the window of the train, he sees the Northern Lights dancing in the sky, and he knows that something magical is real.

The film's climax features a heartwarming moment when Santa Claus presents each child with a special gift: a golden ticket to ride on the Polar Express forever. The boy returns home, feeling transformed by his experience and filled with a newfound sense of wonder and joy.

Throughout the film, Zemeckis uses innovative visual effects to bring the world of the Polar Express to life. The animation is stunning, with beautifully rendered landscapes and characters that seem almost real. The voice cast, including Tom Hanks as the narrator and several other notable actors, adds depth and warmth to the story.

Overall, The Polar Express is a timeless tale of childhood wonder and the magic of the holiday season. It's a film that will leave audiences of all ages feeling inspired and uplifted, with its themes of kindness, generosity, and the power of imagination.

title: Chaos
tagline: When the system breaks down... someone is about to get rich.
overview: In Seattle, detective Quentin Conners is unfairly suspended and his partner Jason York leaves the police force after a tragic shooting on Pearl Street Bridge, when the hostage and the criminal die. During a bank heist with a hostage situation, Conners is assigned in charge of the operation with the rookie Shane Dekker as his partner. plot:
Chaos is a 2005 crime action thriller written and directed by Tony Giglio, starring Jason Statham, Ryan Phillippe and Wesley Snipes, with Henry Czerny and Justine Waddell in supporting roles. Distribution disputes delayed its release for years: it premiered in the United Arab Emirates in December 2005, but did not reach North America until it appeared on DVD in February 2008.

Seattle detective Quentin Conners and his partner Jason York are disgraced after a botched standoff on a bridge in which York accidentally kills a hostage taken by the carjacker John Curtis, and Conners then kills Curtis. A fellow officer testifies against them; Conners is suspended and York is fired. Some time later a gang led by a man calling himself Lorenz takes hostages in a bank and insists on negotiating with Conners, who is reinstated and paired with a fresh-faced rookie, Shane Dekker. The robbers escape amid an explosion, and Dekker notes that Lorenz kept alluding to chaos theory.

The investigation uncovers a series of puzzles. One captured robber's girlfriend has banknotes scented with a chemical police use to mark evidence, traced to cash signed out of police storage by the officer who testified against Conners, who is soon found dead with evidence linking him to the heist. Bank footage reveals that the robbery was a cover for a hacker who planted a virus to siphon a billion dollars through thousands of tiny transactions; the hacker is murdered before he can talk. The captured robber identifies Lorenz as Scott Curtis, the dead carjacker's brother. A raid on Scott's house ends in a deadly shootout and a bomb blast with Conners inside.

Dekker learns that the evidence log was forged and that "Scott Curtis" is in fact York. He tracks York to a diner and kills him in self-defence. Paying for his coffee, he notices that a ten-dollar bill he received from Conners carries the evidence scent, and he realises that Conners, who faked his own death in the blast, masterminded the whole scheme. Finding a copy of James Gleick's book Chaos at Conners' home, Dekker races to the airport, but Conners phones him to explain that he only killed those who deserved it, before escaping on a private jet.

Reviews were generally unenthusiastic; critics acknowledged the late twist and some solid car chases but found the plot reliant on implausible coincidences and stock action clichés.

title: Fred Claus
tagline: Everybody has that one relative who can't help but cause problems over the holidays. Even Santa.
overview: Fred Claus and Santa Claus have been estranged brothers for many years. Now Fred must reconcile his differences with his brother whom he believes overshadows him. When an efficiency expert assesses the workings at the North Pole and threatens to shut Santa down, Fred must help his brother to save Christmas.
plot:
Fred Claus is a Christmas comedy film released in 2007 by Warner Bros. Pictures. The movie stars Vince Vaughn as Fred Claus, the brother of Santa Claus (played by Kevin Spacey), and Paul Giamatti as Nick Claus, also known as Santa's half-brother.

The story begins with Fred Claus, a grumpy and irresponsible man who has been living in his own personal hell since being kicked out of his family's home. He is forced to move back into the family's old house after being evicted from his apartment. Unbeknownst to Fred, Santa is struggling to find a suitable replacement for his deceased wife, Mrs. Claus (played by Mary Steenburgen), and has been searching for someone with the right qualities to take over her role.

Upon arrival at the North Pole, Fred discovers that Santa's search for a new Mrs. Claus has led him to Nick Claus, a bitter and resentful man who feels he was unfairly passed over for the role. The two brothers are forced to work together to find a suitable replacement for Mrs. Claus, with hilarious results.

As the story unfolds, Fred and Nick embark on a series of misadventures, including a disastrous Christmas Eve delivery and a chaotic attempt to find a new Mrs. Claus. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about family, forgiveness, and the true meaning of Christmas.

Throughout the movie, Vince Vaughn shines as the lovable but flawed Fred Claus, bringing his signature wit and charm to the role. Paul Giamatti provides excellent comedic relief as Nick Claus, playing off Vaughn's antics with ease.

The film's climax features a heartwarming moment where Fred and Nick come together to save Christmas, and in doing so, find redemption and forgiveness for past mistakes. The movie ends on a high note, with Fred finding a new sense of purpose and belonging at the North Pole, and Santa finally finding a suitable replacement for Mrs. Claus.

Overall, Fred Claus is a fun and lighthearted holiday film that explores themes of family, forgiveness, and redemption. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and hilarious antics, it's sure to bring a smile to your face during the holiday season.

title: Cruel Intentions 2
tagline: Seduce and destroy.
overview: After his precocious behavior has gotten him bounced out of one more in a string of exclusive private schools, 16-year old Sebastian Valmont has arrived in New York City to live with his father and stepmother. The cunning and handsome Sebastian may have met his match, however in his equally manipulative and beautiful stepsister Kathryn Merteuil.
plot:
Cruel Intentions 2, also known as Cruel Intentions 2: Manchester Prep, is a 2000 American direct-to-video teen drama film written and directed by Roger Kumble. A prequel to Cruel Intentions (1999) and the second installment in the franchise, it stars Robin Dunne, Sarah Thompson, Keri Lynn Pratt and Amy Adams. The film began life as Manchester Prep, a television series for which Fox ordered 13 episodes for the 1999–2000 season with Kumble writing and executive producing. After conflicts between Columbia TriStar Television and the network, and executives' discomfort with its themes of teen sexuality, the series was canceled with only two episodes filmed. The studio's home video division then edited those episodes into a film, shooting additional scenes to turn the story into a prequel, give it an ending and add sexual content, while cutting some subplots and characters.

Sebastian Valmont, a troublemaking student, moves to New York City after his father marries a wealthy divorcée. Before leaving, he takes revenge on his old principal, who insists on forwarding his permanent record, by publishing a nude photo of the principal's wife in the yearbook, and he secretly swaps the record for a glowing one so that he can start fresh at the exclusive Manchester Prep. In his new home he meets his scheming and ambitious stepsister, Kathryn Merteuil, who quickly warns him not to interfere with her privileged life,, and the two become bickering step-siblings. At school Sebastian meets and falls for Danielle Sherman, the headmaster's daughter. Kathryn presides over a secret society of elite students that judges the newcomers, and she embarks on a vendetta against Cherie, a new girl whose family turns out to be richer than hers and who accidentally humiliated her at an assembly. As Sebastian's romance with Danielle develops, Kathryn tries to lure him away, tempting him with a pair of identical twins who tell him that Danielle is the only virgin at the school. Meanwhile Sebastian discovers his father cheating on Kathryn's mother, and Kathryn's mother orders her to befriend Cherie in the hope of securing a large donation to the school. When Sebastian finally declares his love for Danielle, he learns that the manipulation around him runs deeper than he suspected, and he must decide whether to fight the game or join it.

Released on home video in 2001, Cruel Intentions 2 received generally negative reviews, with an 18% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on 11 critics.

title: Battlefield Earth
tagline: Take Back The Planet
overview: In the year 3000, man is no match for the Psychlos, a greedy, manipulative race of aliens on a quest for ultimate profit. Led by the powerful Terl, the Psychlos are stripping Earth clean of its natural resources, using the broken remnants of humanity as slaves. What is left of the human race has descended into a near primitive state. After being captured, it is up to Tyler to save mankind.
plot:
In 3000 AD, Jonnie Goodboy Tyler lives in the Rocky Mountains with a band of cave-dwellers who fear the "demons" that rule Earth. Jonnie doubts their stories and rides into the lowlands, where hunters Carlo and Rock show him a desolate and overgrown city. While exploring it, he and Carlo are captured by the demons, a cruel alien race called Psychlos, and taken as slaves to a base in the ruins of Denver. The base is covered with an enormous dome that provides the Psychlos with a breathable atmosphere. Jonnie shows resourcefulness, drawing the respect of the other human slaves and the interest of Terl, the high-born Earth security chief.
Terl learns from a visiting supervisor that his temporary assignment on Earth will be extended indefinitely as punishment for offending a politician. Desperate to leave, he hatches a plan with his assistant Ker. They know about a recently exposed gold deposit in an area with elevated radiation levels. Gold is valuable to the Psychlos, who have been reporting losses from their mining operations, but radiation causes their air mixture to explode. Terl and Ker will train humans to mine the gold, and Terl will use part of it to bribe his way off the planet.
Terl places Jonnie in a learning machine that rapidly teaches him Psychlo language and technology. Jonnie shares his knowledge with other slaves while hiding it from Terl and Ker. After Jonnie stages an unsuccessful escape attempt, Terl takes him to the Denver Library hoping to impress him that human knowledge is no match for the Psychlos. Jonnie reads the Declaration of Independence and is inspired to seek not only escape but reconquest. Jonnie's fiancée Chrissy is captured while searching for him and fitted with an explosive collar. Terl tells Jonnie that she will be killed if he does not obey, also making an example out of a fellow slave, Sammy.
Believing that the slaves are subdued, Terl blackmails the planet administrator into letting him order the gold mining operation. Jonnie receives further training to pilot aircraft and is sent to the mining site with a team. He leaves half of them to pretend to work while the other half gather abandoned human weapons and take gold from Fort Knox to pass off as mining production. Ker tries to blackmail Terl for a greater share of the gold at Jonnie's urging, but Terl detects the attempt and shoots off Ker's hand.
The humans launch their revolt, assaulting the base while using Harrier jets to combat the Psychlo air defenses and explosives to rupture the dome. Terl orders the execution of all humans and alerts the Psychlo homeworld to teleport an extermination force. As the teleporter activates, Jonnie fights with Terl, reattaching Chrissy's collar to his arm and tricking him into detonating it. Sammy's brother Mickey rides the teleporter to the homeworld with a nuclear weapon. The fallout from the weapon incinerates the atmosphere, causing the entire planet to explode.

title: The Fugitive
tagline: A murdered wife. A one-armed man. An obsessed detective. The chase begins.
overview: Wrongfully convicted of murdering his wife and sentenced to death, Richard Kimble escapes from the law in an attempt to find the real killer and clear his name.
plot:
The Fugitive is a 1993 American thriller film directed by Andrew Davis and starring Harrison Ford as Dr. Richard Kimble, a man wrongly accused of murdering his wife.

The movie begins with Dr. Richard Kimble (Harrison Ford), a successful surgeon who lives in Chicago with his wife, Helen (Kelly McGillis). On the day of their 10-year anniversary, Helen is found dead on a train track, and Richard is arrested and charged with her murder. The police investigation reveals that Richard was at the scene of the crime, but he claims he was framed.

The film's opening scene shows the brutal murder of Helen, followed by Richard's arrest and subsequent escape from custody while being transported to his trial. The U.S. Marshal who is transporting him, Samuel Gerard ( Tommy Lee Jones), is determined to bring Richard back to justice.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Richard was indeed innocent of the crime, but he has been on the run for 15 years, evading capture and trying to clear his name. Along the way, he meets a young woman named Emma (Juliette Lewis), who helps him evade the authorities.

Throughout the film, Richard's determination to prove his innocence drives the plot forward. He uses his medical skills to help those in need, while also staying one step ahead of Gerard and his team. The cat-and-mouse game between Richard and the law is intense, with both sides using clever tactics to outmaneuver each other.

As the story reaches its climax, Richard discovers a crucial piece of evidence that could prove his innocence: a fingerprint on a train car that matches one found at the crime scene. However, Gerard is hot on his heels, and a thrilling chase ensues as they pursue each other across the country.

In the end, Richard finally proves his innocence by revealing the true killer: a former patient who had been seeking revenge against him. The film concludes with Richard's exoneration, and he is reunited with Emma, who has fallen in love with him.

The Fugitive was a critical and commercial success, earning several Academy Award nominations, including Best Actor for Harrison Ford. The film's tense plot and memorable performances made it a classic thriller of the 1990s.

title: The Ladykillers
tagline: The greatest criminal minds of all time have finally met their match.
overview: An eccentric, if not charming Southern professor and his crew pose as a band in order to rob a casino, all under the nose of his unsuspecting landlord – a sharp old woman.
plot:
The Ladykillers is a 2004 American black comedy crime film written, directed, produced and edited by Joel and Ethan Coen, a remake of the 1955 Ealing comedy written by William Rose. It is the Coens' first remake and their only film with Tom Hanks. Hanks stars as Professor G. H. Dorr, with Irma P. Hall as Marva Munson, Marlon Wayans as Gawain MacSam, J. K. Simmons as Garth Pancake, Tzi Ma as the General and Ryan Hurst as Lump.

Mrs. Munson, a devout, strict elderly widow, rents a room to Dorr, a self-styled classics professor who asks to use her root cellar for rehearsals of his early music ensemble. The musicians are actually criminals. Lump is a dim former football player, Pancake is a demolitions expert with irritable bowel syndrome, MacSam is a foul-mouthed janitor and the gang's inside man at a riverboat casino, and the General is a silent, chain-smoking tunneling expert. They plan to dig from the cellar into the casino's underground vault, dumping the dirt each night onto a garbage barge passing under a nearby bridge. Despite mishaps, including Pancake blowing off a finger that Mrs. Munson's cat carries away, they reach the vault and take the money.

Mrs. Munson discovers the plot and demands that Dorr return the money and come to church, or she will call the police. Dorr's arguments fail. The gang decides she must die and draws straws. MacSam cannot go through with it because she reminds him of his mother, and in the ensuing fight with Pancake he is shot dead. Pancake then tries to escape with the loot and his girlfriend, Mountain Girl, but the General strangles them both. Preparing to kill Mrs. Munson in her sleep, the General is startled by a cuckoo clock, swallows his cigarette, trips over the cat and falls to his death. Lump decides to do as Mrs. Munson says, but he accidentally shoots himself while trying to shoot Dorr. Dorr is knocked off the bridge by a falling piece of gargoyle and dies when his cloak catches on the railing. All of their bodies land on the barge. Mrs. Munson finds the money, and when the police laugh off her story, she gives it to Bob Jones University.

The barge replaces the original's freight train. Buena Vista released it on March 26, 2004, and it grossed $76 million worldwide. Many critics considered it a lesser Coen film. Rotten Tomatoes reported 54% approval, calling Hanks's performance inspired but the film minor. Roger Ebert gave it two and a half stars, singling out Hall as its most successful performer.

overview: Barry B. Benson, a bee who has just graduated from college, is disillusioned at his lone career choice: making honey.
