As they embark on their journey, Finn and Tess are joined by a group of eccentric treasure hunters, including Moe (Donald Sutherland), a seasoned adventurer who becomes their guide. The group faces numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, rival treasure hunters, and ancient booby traps.

Throughout the movie, Finn and Tess's relationship is put to the test as they confront their past mistakes and learn to work together again. Along the way, they discover that the Golden Idol is more than just a valuable treasure; it holds sentimental value for both of them.

As they near their destination, the group encounters a rival treasure hunter, Lucas (Ewen Bremner), who will stop at nothing to get his hands on the idol. In a thrilling finale, Finn and Tess must use all their skills and ingenuity to outwit Lucas and his team, while also overcoming their personal demons.

In the end, Finn and Tess successfully retrieve the Golden Idol, but not before realizing that the true treasure was their rekindled love for each other. The movie concludes with a heartwarming moment of reconciliation between the two leads, as they share a romantic kiss and look forward to a brighter future together.

Overall, Fool's Gold is an entertaining adventure film that combines action, comedy, and romance, with a dash of treasure hunting excitement. While it may not be a groundbreaking film, it provides plenty of thrills and laughs for fans of the genre.

plot:
Taken is a 2008 action-thriller film directed by Pierre Morel and starring Liam Neeson as Bryan Mills, a former CIA operative turned private security consultant. The movie follows Bryan's desperate search for his daughter Kim (Maggie Grace), who has been kidnapped while on a trip to Paris with her mother.

The story begins with Bryan's family life: he is married to Lenore (Holmes Osborne) and has two daughters, Kim and Sarah. During a family vacation in Paris, Kim is abducted by a human trafficking ring led by the ruthless and cunning Takao (Shin Koyamada). The kidnappers demand $1 million for her safe return.

Bryan's world is turned upside down as he receives a phone call from his daughter, who has been brainwashed to obey her captors. Desperate to rescue Kim, Bryan sets out on a perilous journey through the dark underworld of human trafficking in Paris and beyond.

As Bryan navigates the treacherous landscape, he encounters a range of unsavory characters, including corrupt police officers, ruthless gangsters, and cunning traffickers. Along the way, he teams up with a French detective named Beau (François Berléand), who helps him track down leads and gather intelligence on the kidnappers.

As Bryan delves deeper into the world of human trafficking, he discovers that Takao's operation is just one small part of a larger, more complex network. He also uncovers a shocking connection between his daughter's kidnapping and a mysterious figure from his own past.

The action unfolds at breakneck speed as Bryan faces off against hordes of thugs, dodges bullets, and battles his way through the streets of Paris. Along the way, he encounters a range of memorable characters, including a tough-as-nails nightclub owner (Léa Seydoux) who becomes an unlikely ally.

As Bryan closes in on Takao's operation, he discovers that his daughter has been subjected to brutal treatment and is struggling to maintain her sanity. In a heart-pumping climax, Bryan confronts Takao and his henchmen in a desperate bid to rescue Kim and bring the traffickers to justice.

In the end, Bryan successfully rescues his daughter, but not before facing off against Takao in a violent and intense showdown. The movie concludes with Bryan reunited with his family, but forever changed by his experience as a father and a protector.

Taken was a critical and commercial success, grossing over $214 million worldwide and cementing Liam Neeson's status as an action hero. The film's success spawned two sequels, Taken 2 (2012) and Taken 3 (2014), as well as a prequel, Taken: Origins (2020).

title: Baby Mama
tagline: Would you put your eggs...in this basket?
overview: A successful, single businesswoman who dreams of having a baby discovers she is infertile and hires a working class woman to be her unlikely surrogate.
plot:
Baby Mama is a 2008 American buddy comedy written and directed by Michael McCullers, who made his directing debut with it. Tina Fey and Amy Poehler lead a cast that includes Greg Kinnear, Dax Shepard, Romany Malco, Maura Tierney, Holland Taylor, Steve Martin and Sigourney Weaver. Relativity Media produced it and Universal Pictures released it.

Kate Holbrook is a successful single executive in Philadelphia who has put her career first. At 37 she decides she wants a child, but doctors tell her she has a T-shaped uterus that makes pregnancy unlikely. Adoption falls through, so she turns to a surrogacy agency run by the steely Chaffee Bicknell. The agency pairs her with Angie Ostrowski, a woman from South Philadelphia. When Angie is reported pregnant, Kate prepares in her usual driven way, reading parenting books, baby-proofing her apartment and researching the best preschools. Her plans fall apart when Angie, thrown out by her common-law husband Carl, moves in with her. The two clash constantly, and Kate also starts dating Rob Ackerman, the owner of a local juice bar.

What Kate does not know is that the implantation failed and Angie is faking the pregnancy to collect the money. Angie feels increasingly guilty but keeps putting off the truth, until an ultrasound shows she really is pregnant, with Carl's child. Carl exposes the lie at Kate's baby shower. Kate argues that the baby might still be hers, but a court rules that it is Angie's, and Angie apologizes. Right after the hearing, Angie goes into labor. Kate rushes her to the hospital, faints during the delivery and wakes to learn that she herself is two months pregnant by Rob. Kate forgives Angie, who names her daughter Stef after Gwen Stefani, and the two become close friends. A year later, at Stef's first birthday, Kate and Rob are engaged and have a daughter, and Carl is an involved father. The film ends with Kate and Angie watching Tom and Jerry cartoons with their girls.

The film opened on April 25, 2008, at number one in the United States and Canada, taking $17.4 million from 2,543 theaters. It went on to gross about $64.2 million against a $30 million budget. Reviews were mixed to moderately positive. Rotten Tomatoes' consensus called it a lightweight, predictable comedy carried by its performers. Variety's Todd McCarthy said its contents were easy to guess, while Peter Bradshaw of The Guardian called it enjoyable and amiable despite its romantic comedy clichés.

The movie takes place on Mars, where a team of space marines are sent to investigate the disappearance of a research team at the Hell's Gate facility. Upon arrival, the team discovers that the facility has been overrun by demons from Hell, which are using the Hellgate to invade Earth. The team soon realizes that they must close the Hellgate before it's too late.

As the team navigates through the facility, they encounter various obstacles and challenges, including hordes of demons and treacherous terrain. Along the way, Sarge forms a bond with Private Hudson, who becomes his protégé.

The plot thickens as the team discovers that the Hellgate is being controlled by a rogue scientist, Dr. William Mapother (Ben Affleck), who has been using the facility to harness the power of the demons for his own gain.

As the team fights their way through the facility, they eventually reach the heart of the Hellgate, where they face off against Dr. Mapother and his minions. In a thrilling finale, Sarge and Hudson manage to close the Hellgate, saving humanity from the demonic invasion.

Throughout the movie, there are several action-packed sequences, including a memorable fight scene between Sarge and a group of demons in a zero-gravity environment. The special effects are impressive, bringing the demons and the Hellgate to life in a visually stunning way.

Overall, Doom is an entertaining sci-fi action film that delivers on its promise of intense action and suspense. While it may not be as complex or thought-provoking as some other movies in the genre, it's a fun ride that's sure to satisfy fans of science fiction and action films.

plot:
Legally Blonde is a 2001 American comedy film directed by Robert Luketic and written by Karen McCullah Lutz and Kirsten Smith. The movie stars Reese Witherspoon as Elle Woods, a fashion merchandising major who enrolls in Harvard Law School to win back her ex-boyfriend, Warner Huntington III (Matthew Davis).

The film begins with Elle, a popular sorority girl at California University, Los Angeles, who is dumped by Warner due to his disapproval of her shallow and materialistic lifestyle. Determined to prove herself and win him back, Elle decides to attend Harvard Law School, despite having no prior knowledge of law.

Upon arrival, Elle faces skepticism from her peers, particularly her roommate Paulette (Jennifer Coolidge), who is a hairdresser and a single mother. Despite the initial doubts, Elle proves herself to be a quick learner and earns the respect of her professors, including Professor Callahan (Bruce Thomas) and Professor Kingsfield (Camilla Belle).

As Elle navigates law school, she becomes involved in a high-profile murder case involving Brooke Wyndham (Ali Larter), a wealthy socialite accused of murdering her husband. Elle takes on the case pro bono, determined to prove that Brooke is innocent.

Throughout the film, Elle's character undergoes significant development as she confronts her own biases and stereotypes. She learns to look beyond superficial appearances and develops a deeper understanding of the law and its complexities.

title: The Bank Job
tagline: The true story of a heist gone wrong... in all the right ways.
overview: Terry is a small-time car dealer trying to leave his shady past behind and start a family. Martine is a beautiful model from Terry's old neighbourhood who knows that Terry is no angel. When Martine proposes a foolproof plan to rob a bank, Terry recognises the danger but realises this may be the opportunity of a lifetime. As the resourceful band of thieves burrows its way into a safe-deposit vault at a Lloyds Bank, they quickly realise that, besides millions in riches, the boxes also contain secrets that implicate everyone from London's most notorious underworld gangsters to powerful government figures, and even the Royal Family. Although the heist makes headlines throughout Britain for several days, a government gag order eventually brings all reporting of the case to an immediate halt.
plot:
In 1971, British Security Services (MI5) want a safety deposit box secured in a Lloyds Bank branch. Belonging to Black militant gangster Michael X, it contains compromising photos of Princess Margaret, insurance to keep the British authorities off Michael's back. Martine, an ex-model sleeping with MI5 agent Tim Everett, is caught smuggling drugs into the country; to avoid going to jail, she makes a deal with Tim to retrieve the photos so MI5 can finally arrest Michael.
MI5 has the idea to stage the retrieval as a robbery so Martine approaches her ex-boyfriend Terry Leather, who has criminal contacts. Terry is now a struggling car salesman but happily married with two kids. She tells him he will be richly rewarded if they pull off the robbery but does not tell him about the photos. Terry's team includes his close friends Eddie, Dave, and Kevin, as well as trusted criminal associates Bambas and Guy. While scouting the bank, Dave runs into gangster Lew Vogel, for whom he'd made pornographic films.
The gang rents a shop near the bank, tunnels below the vault, and breaks in. During the robbery prep, Martine, who is still in love with Terry, kisses him and they sleep together. They loot the safety deposit boxes, but Terry discovers Princess Margaret's photos and learns that Martine lied to them. The police are alerted to the robbery by ham radio operator Eric Addey, who overhears the gang's walkie-talkie communications, but the gang has fled. The robbery rattles important figures who kept incriminating items, including Vogel, who has a ledger of police payoffs and bribes inside, and Incriminating photographs of government officials who secretly frequented Sonia Bern's brothels. Vogel realizes Dave's presence outside the bank was not a coincidence, and has him kidnapped and tortured for information. Dave gives in, and Vogel has Gerald and Nick—two policemen on his payroll—kidnap Eddie. Terry discovers the explicit photographs of government officials in Sonia's brothels among their loot. Knowing Tim will let the gang take the fall once MI5 has Princess Margaret's photos, Terry uses the brothel photos to secure passports and new identities for the gang in exchange for Princess Margaret's photos.
Vogel's men murder Bambas and Guy. Vogel kills Dave and threatens to kill Eddie unless Terry surrenders the ledger. Terry agrees to meet with Vogel at Paddington Station to exchange the ledger for Eddie. He arranges for the meeting to happen at the same time he will be picking up the new passports and written immunity from prosecution from MI5, delivered by Lord Mountbatten. Terry also sends Kevin to honest straight cop Roy Given with a page from the ledger to ask for his help. Vogel tries to flee at the sight of MI5, but Terry attacks him—only for him and Eddie to be arrested. Tim has Terry, Eddie and Kevin released and Given uses the ledger they turned in to arrest Vogel, Gerald and Nick.

title: Alfie
tagline: Meet a man who never met a woman he didn't love.
overview: In Manhattan, the British limousine driver Alfie is surrounded by beautiful women, having one night stands with all of them and without any sort of commitment. His best friends are his colleague Marlon and his girl-friend Lonette. Alfie has a brief affair with Lonette, and the consequences force Alfie to reflect on his lifestyle.
plot:
Alfie is a 2004 romantic comedy-drama co-written, produced and directed by Charles Shyer, a reworking of the 1966 British film of the same name and its 1975 sequel. Jude Law plays the title role created by Michael Caine, with Marisa Tomei as Julie, Omar Epps as Marlon, Nia Long as Lonette, Jane Krakowski as Dorie, Sienna Miller as Nikki and Susan Sarandon as Liz.

Alfie Elkins is a Cockney limousine driver in Manhattan who drifts from one casual affair to the next, often addressing the audience directly. He keeps up an easygoing arrangement with Julie, a single mother, and a fling with Dorie, an unhappily married woman, dropping her when she wants more. Hoping to start a business with his friend and co-worker Marlon, he tries to help Marlon win back his ex-girlfriend Lonette, but ends up sleeping with her after a night of drinking. Marlon and Lonette reconcile and plan to marry.

Julie throws Alfie out after finding another woman's underwear in her bin, and by the time he decides to make amends she has gone back to her estranged husband. Lonette discovers she is pregnant by Alfie and, without telling Marlon, the two go to a clinic for an abortion; soon afterwards the couple move upstate without saying goodbye. Troubled by impotence, Alfie learns from a doctor that it is caused by stress, but a lump leads to an anxious wait for test results. In a hospital bathroom he meets Joe, a widower who advises him to find someone to love and live each day as if it were his last.

Cleared of cancer, Alfie resolves to aim higher. He falls into a passionate but stormy romance with Nikki, a beautiful, unstable young woman, then turns his attention to Liz, an older cosmetics mogul who wants only an affair, and breaks up with Nikki. He realises too late that he cares for Julie, who has moved on. Visiting Marlon and Lonette, he learns that she never had the abortion and that Marlon has stayed with her knowing the child is Alfie's. Liz, meanwhile, has taken a younger lover. Meeting Dorie again, Alfie apologises and admits he runs from intimacy, and he ends the film asking the audience what it is all about.

The film grossed $35 million worldwide against a $60 million budget and drew mixed reviews, holding 48% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, but Mick Jagger and Dave Stewart won a Golden Globe for the song "Old Habits Die Hard".

title: How the Grinch Stole Christmas
tagline: He puts the mean in green.
overview: Inside a snowflake exists the magical land of Whoville. In Whoville, live the Whos, an almost mutated sort of Munchkin-like people. All the Whos love Christmas, yet just outside of their beloved Whoville lives the Grinch. The Grinch is a nasty creature that hates Christmas, and plots to steal it away from the Whos, whom he equally abhors. Yet a small child, Cindy Lou Who, decides to try befriending the Grinch.
plot:
How the Grinch Stole Christmas, also titled Dr. Seuss' How the Grinch Stole Christmas, is a 2000 American Christmas comedy film directed by Ron Howard and written by Jeffrey Price and Peter S. Seaman, loosely based on Dr. Seuss's 1957 children's book. The second adaptation of the book after the 1966 animated television special, and the first Dr. Seuss book adapted as a live-action feature, it stars Jim Carrey as the Grinch, a misanthropic green creature who sets out to ruin the Christmas celebrations of Whoville, with Jeffrey Tambor, Christine Baranski and Taylor Momsen, and narration by Anthony Hopkins.

The Grinch lives in a cave on Mount Crumpit and despises Christmas and the cheerful Whos below. After meeting him at the post office, young Cindy Lou Who learns his story: raised by two elderly Who women, he had a crush on his classmate Martha May Whovier, but when the bully Augustus MayWho mocked his hairy face, he tried to shave, cut himself, and fled to the mountain after the class laughed at him. Hoping to set things right, Cindy nominates the Grinch as the town's Holiday Cheermeister, over the objections of MayWho, now mayor. The Grinch accepts after learning that Martha will attend, and he begins to enjoy the festivities, until MayWho humiliates him with a gift of an electric razor and proposes to Martha with a new car. The Grinch denounces the Whos' materialism, wrecks the celebration and returns to his cave.

Learning that the Whos will celebrate anyway, the Grinch disguises himself as Santa Claus, dresses his dog, Max, as a reindeer, and descends on Whoville to steal every present, decoration and scrap of food. On Christmas morning, MayWho blames Cindy, but her father, the postmaster Lou Lou Who, reminds the town that Christmas means more than presents, and the Whos gather to sing. Hearing them from the mountaintop, the Grinch realizes the true meaning of Christmas, and his heart grows three sizes. He saves Cindy and the sleigh from falling into a gorge, returns everything and apologizes. Martha gives back MayWho's ring and declares her love for the Grinch, who hosts the Christmas feast in his cave.

Released by Universal Pictures on November 17, 2000, the film grossed $350.6 million worldwide, the sixth-highest gross of the year. Reviews were mixed, with 50% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 46; critics praised Carrey but preferred the animated special.

title: Che: Part Two
tagline: A revolutionary life.
overview: After the Cuban Revolution, Che is at the height of his fame and power. Then he disappears, re-emerging incognito in Bolivia, where he organizes a small group of Cuban comrades and Bolivian recruits to start the great Latin American Revolution. Through this story, we come to understand how Che remains a symbol of idealism and heroism that lives in the hearts of people around the world.
plot:
Che: Part Two (also released as Che: Part Two – Guerrilla) is a 2008 biographical war drama directed by Steven Soderbergh, the second half of his two-part portrait of Ernesto "Che" Guevara. Shot back to back with Che: Part One, it moves from the Cuban Revolution covered in the first film to Guevara's doomed guerrilla campaign in Bolivia in 1966–67, and is adapted from his Bolivian Diary. The screenplay is credited to Peter Buchman and Benjamin A. van der Veen, and Benicio del Toro again plays Guevara.

The film opens with Fidel Castro publicly reading, in October 1965, the farewell letter in which Che renounces his Cuban posts and citizenship after vanishing from public life. A year later Guevara, disguised as an older Uruguayan official named Ramón, travels with forged papers to La Paz and on into the mountains to join a small band of Cuban veterans and Bolivian recruits. Training and arms deliveries mark the early days, but the Bolivian Communist Party under Mario Monje refuses to back armed struggle, local peasants remain wary or hostile, food runs short and quarrels flare between Cubans and Bolivians. Deserters lead the army to the rebels' base camp, exposing the foreign identity of the group, while President René Barrientos accepts American help and U.S. advisers begin training Bolivian Rangers to hunt them down.

The journalist Régis Debray and the Argentine Ciro Bustos are arrested after leaving the camp, a rear guard that includes the agent Tania is wiped out in an ambush at a river crossing, and Guevara, increasingly crippled by asthma, leads a dwindling column through the forest. Wounded and captured in a firefight near La Higuera, he is held in the village school and executed on 9 October 1967.

Alongside del Toro, the cast includes Catalina Sandino Moreno, Franka Potente, Demián Bichir, Rodrigo Santoro and Joaquim de Almeida, with Matt Damon in a brief role as a priest. The film was shot mainly in Spain, with some scenes in La Paz, using the then-new RED digital camera and natural light. Produced by companies including Wild Bunch, Section Eight, Laura Bickford Productions, Morena Films and Telecinco Cinema, it premiered at the 2008 Cannes Film Festival as part of a four-hour screening of the complete work, where del Toro won the award for Best Actor. Reviews were mixed to positive, and the film was not a commercial success.

title: Amelia
overview: A look at the life of legendary American pilot Amelia Earhart, who disappeared while flying over the Pacific Ocean in 1937 in an attempt to make a flight around the world.
plot:
On June 1, 1937, aviator Amelia Earhart and her navigator Fred Noonan, start their attempt to circumnavigate the globe. Moving in vignettes from her early years when Earhart was captivated by an aircraft flying overhead on the Kansas prairie where she grew up, her life over the preceding decade gradually unfolds via flashbacks. In 1928, Earhart is recruited by charismatic publishing tycoon and adoring business partner George Putnam to become the first woman to cross the Atlantic Ocean, albeit as a passenger. Taking command of the flight results in success and she is thrust into the limelight as the most famous woman pilot of her time. Putnam helps Earhart write a book chronicling the flight, much like his earlier triumph with Charles Lindbergh's We. Earhart and Putnam eventually marry, although she enacts a "cruel" pledge as her wedding contract.
Embarrassed that her fame was not earned, Earhart commences to set myriad aviation records, and in 1932, recreates her earlier transatlantic flight, becoming the first female pilot to fly solo across the Atlantic. Throughout the next five years, Earhart falls into an awkward passionate affair with Gene Vidal. In a display of romantic jealousy, Putnam quietly tells Amelia that he does not want Vidal in his house. title: What Just Happened
tagline: Admit nothing.
overview: During the course of an ordinary week in Hollywood, movie producer Ben must navigate his way through shark-infested waters as he struggles to complete his latest projects. A demanding studio boss demands extensive changes to a movie starring Sean Penn, while another chief won't greenlight a project unless star Bruce Willis shaves his beard. plot:
What Just Happened is a 2008 American satirical comedy-drama directed by Barry Levinson and starring Robert De Niro, based on producer Art Linson's 2002 book What Just Happened? Bitter Hollywood Tales from the Front Line, about his own experiences in the film business. An independent production of 2929 Productions, Art Linson Productions and Tribeca Productions, it screened at the Cannes Film Festival on May 25, 2008, before its release on October 17, 2008.

Ben, a veteran Hollywood producer, is beset by professional and personal problems. His new film, Fiercely, tests disastrously, largely because its ending shows the murder of the hero, played by Sean Penn, together with his dog. Studio executive Lou Tarnow suspects Ben shot the dog's death only as a bargaining chip and threatens to take over the edit and pull the film from Cannes unless that scene goes, while the volatile British director Jeremy Brunell refuses to change anything. At the same time, the studio may cancel Ben's next project because its star, Bruce Willis, will not shave the thick beard he has grown, and Ben's attempts to reason with him meet furious resistance. In his private life, Ben cannot cleanly separate from his second wife, Kelly, and discovers that she is having an affair with Scott Solomon, a married screenwriter he has worked with, whose own script soon attracts Brad Pitt.

Jeremy eventually agrees to let the dog live, and although Ben's appeal to Willis's agent only gets the agent fired, Willis finally shaves and production continues. At Cannes, however, Jeremy unveils a secret new cut in which the dog dies after all, with almost a minute of extra gunfire. The ending ruins any hope of a Palme d'Or, though some viewers, including Penn, cheer. Lou flies home on the studio jet, leaving Ben stranded, and when he finally makes it to a Vanity Fair shoot of Hollywood's top thirty producers, he is placed at the far edge of the photo.

The supporting cast includes Catherine Keener, Robin Wright, Stanley Tucci, John Turturro, Michael Wincott, Moon Bloodgood and Kristen Stewart. Filming began in March 2007, with exteriors in Los Angeles and interiors in Connecticut, where the production moved for tax incentives. Critics were divided, with 49% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 51.

The story begins with the USS Nebraska (SSBN-739), a United States Navy ballistic missile submarine, on a routine patrol in the North Atlantic Ocean. Captain Frank Ramsey (Gene Hackman) is the commanding officer of the ship, accompanied by his trusted executive officer, Lieutenant Commander Ron Hunter (Denzel Washington).

As the crew goes about their duties, tensions rise between Ramsey and Hunter due to their differing leadership styles. Ramsey is a seasoned veteran with years of experience, while Hunter is a younger, more aggressive officer who believes in taking bold action.

The situation escalates when the Nebraska detects a Soviet submarine, the K-143, which has been detected by the US Navy's early warning systems. The crew is put on high alert as they prepare to engage the enemy vessel.

As the standoff between the two submarines continues, it becomes clear that the K-143 is not just any ordinary Soviet sub - it's a Russian submarine carrying nuclear warheads. The situation reaches a boiling point when Ramsey and Hunter disagree on how to proceed, with Ramsey advocating for caution and Hunter pushing for a more aggressive approach.

The tension between the two leaders comes to a head as they engage in a heated argument, which ultimately leads to a dramatic confrontation. In the heat of the moment, Ramsey orders Hunter to take control of the ship, but Hunter refuses, leading to a power struggle that puts the entire crew at risk.

As the situation spirals out of control, it becomes clear that the K-143 is not just a threat to the US Navy - it's also a ticking time bomb. The Russian submarine has been carrying nuclear warheads for years, and its crew is unaware of the danger they pose to themselves and others.

In the end, Ramsey and Hunter are forced to work together to defuse the situation and prevent a catastrophic accident. In a tense and dramatic climax, they manage to disable the K-143's nuclear systems, averting a disaster that could have had far-reaching consequences.

Throughout the movie, the tension between Ramsey and Hunter is palpable, and their differing leadership styles create a sense of unease among the crew. The film's themes of power, authority, and the dangers of unchecked aggression are timely and thought-provoking, making Crimson Tide a gripping and intense thriller that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

Overall, Crimson Tide is a masterclass in tension-building and character-driven drama, with outstanding performances from its leads. The film's themes and plot are both timely and timeless, making it a classic of the submarine thriller genre.

One of the most striking aspects of Twilight is its portrayal of forbidden love. The movie explores the intense passion and all-consuming nature of Bella and Edward's relationship, as well as the risks and consequences that come with loving someone who is different from oneself. The film's depiction of vampire lore is also noteworthy, offering a unique take on the traditional mythology.

Overall, Twilight is a captivating and romantic tale that has become a cultural phenomenon among young audiences. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the movie's success can be attributed to its engaging storyline, memorable characters, and the chemistry between Stewart and Pattinson.

title: Boogeyman
tagline: You thought it was just a story.
overview: Every culture has one – the horrible monster fueling young children's nightmares. But for Tim, the Boogeyman still lives in his memories as a creature that devoured his father 16 years earlier. Is the Boogeyman real? Or did Tim make him up to explain why his father abandoned his family?
plot:
During his childhood, Tim Jensen witnesses his father being taken by the Boogeyman, an evil creature which lives in all closets worldwide. Since then, he has taken precautions to ensure that the Boogeyman cannot get to him, such as sleeping on a mattress on the floor, and removing all closets from his home, and keeping all his clothes in a dresser drawer.
After a Thanksgiving trip with his girlfriend Jessica to her parents' house, Tim has a premonition in which his mother tells him to return to the family home. Soon after, he receives a call from his uncle informing him that his mother has died. Upon returning to the psychiatric ward, where he grew up after his father died, he discovers that one of the patients, a young girl, is being terrorized by something hiding in the ceiling of her room.
Upon a suggestion by his psychiatrist that returning to his family home to spend the night in that house would be a good idea, Tim returns to his old Victorian style house in the open country, where he relives memories of his mother telling his father that the Boogeyman does not exist and therefore cannot possibly harm Tim. Tim is briefly attacked by the Boogeyman when he enters the downstairs closet.
Tim meets a young girl named Franny in his woodshed; she wants to know if it's true that the Boogeyman murdered Tim's father. Searching the woodshed, he discovers a file of Missing Person lists and documents left by Franny, and upon flicking through them, he discovers a disturbing collection of missing children who were all taken by the Boogeyman.
Tim panics and attempts to leave, but Jessica abruptly shows up and takes Tim out of the house for a night to a quiet motel, where she is murdered by the Boogeyman, dragging her into the bath.
Tim returns from getting ice and preparing drinks and enters the bathroom, where he finds that Jessica is missing. He realizes what has occurred, and stumbles blindly into a closet, and then walks out into his family home, just as Kate, his childhood friend, has returned to his home and, upon hearing noises from the closets, was about to open the door herself. Tim drags Kate back to the hotel, where they find the empty bath; this time with blood on the side. Kate begins thinking that Tim might've harmed Jessica, but Tim angrily denies it. Frustrated at Tim's refusal to tell her what is really wrong with him, Kate drives them back to her house where Tim spots something in the window. Kate claims that the person Tim saw was in fact her father. She then calls Tim's Uncle Mike to have him check on Tim. But he is captured and taken away by the Boogeyman.
Tim returns to his house and meets Franny once more, who leads him to a house full of proclamations describing the Boogeyman. There is a chair in the middle of the room facing a closet. Tim remembers this house as being the home of a doctor who everyone thought was insane.

title: The Protector
tagline: Vengeance Knows No Mercy.
overview: In Bangkok, the young Kham was raised by his father in the jungle with elephants as members of their family. When his old elephant and the baby Kern are stolen by criminals, Kham finds that the animals were sent to Sidney. He travels to Australia, where he locates the baby elephant in a restaurant owned by the evil Madame Rose, the leader of an international Thai mafia. With the support of the efficient Thai sergeant Mark, who was involved in a conspiracy, Kham fights to rescue the animal from the mobsters.
plot:
The Protector is a 2005 martial arts film directed by Renny Harlin and starring Jason Statham as Jack Crawley, an undercover agent working for MI6. 

Beginning: The movie starts with Jack Crawley, a skilled fighter and assassin, who has been sent to Thailand to infiltrate the Triad organization. He assumes the identity of "Jack" and gains the trust of the Triad's leader, Tong Po (Sihung Lung). Jack is tasked with taking down Tong Po, but he soon discovers that his mission is not what it seems.

Plot Development: As Jack delves deeper into the world of the Triads, he meets a beautiful woman named Anna (Claire Forlani), who becomes his ally and potential love interest. Together, they uncover a plot by Tong Po to smuggle heroin out of Thailand and sell it in Europe. Jack must use his skills to take down Tong Po's men and prevent the heroin from being shipped.

However, as Jack gets closer to the truth, he realizes that there is more at stake than just stopping Tong Po. He discovers that Anna is actually a double agent working for MI6, and her true mission is to gather evidence against Tong Po. Jack must navigate his feelings for Anna while also completing his original mission.

Ending: In the climactic final battle, Jack faces off against Tong Po's top henchman, who has been secretly working with Anna all along. With the help of Anna and a few other allies, Jack manages to defeat the henchman and prevent the heroin from being shipped. However, in the process, Jack is severely injured and forced to leave Thailand.

As Jack returns to England, he reflects on his mission and the people he has met during his time in Thailand. He realizes that his feelings for Anna were genuine, but their relationship was complicated by her true loyalties. The movie ends with Jack walking away from a burning building, symbolizing his departure from the world of espionage.

Overall, The Protector is an action-packed thrill ride with plenty of twists and turns. Jason Statham delivers a strong performance as the rugged and charismatic Jack Crawley, and Claire Forlani shines as the beautiful and deadly Anna.

title: Hollow Man II
tagline: There's More to Terror Than Meets The Eye
overview: After the mysterious death of scientist, Dr. Devin Villiers, Det. Frank Turner and his partner are assigned to protect Villiers' colleague, who revealed that  a veteran soldier was subjected to an experiment with the objective of creating the ultimate national security weapon... an undetectable soldier. The experiment failed – with disastrous side effects.
plot:
Hollow Man 2 (released as Hollow Man II) is a 2006 American science fiction thriller directed by Claudio Fäh. A stand-alone sequel to the 2000 film Hollow Man, it explores the consequences of invisibility through Michael Griffin, a soldier left permanently invisible by a government experiment that went wrong. Peter Facinelli stars as Detective Frank Turner, Laura Regan as the scientist Maggie Dalton and Christian Slater as Griffin, with David McIlwraith, Sarah Deakins and Jessica Harmon.

At a cocktail party held by a Washington think tank, the scientist Devin Villiers is dragged into a bathroom by an unseen attacker. Under threat, he reveals the name of a colleague, Maggie Dalton, who holds the "formula" his assailant wants. Spared on condition of silence, Devin tries to raise the alarm and is killed. Dr. Reisner, whose laboratory carried out the invisibility research, arranges for detectives Frank Turner and Lisa Martinez to guard Maggie, but the attacker gets into her home and kills Lisa, and soldiers fail to catch him.

Maggie is taken into protective custody, but when Turner learns that she is about to be handed over to the military, he helps her escape. She explains that scientists had earlier created an invisibility serum with severe and eventually fatal side effects. When the military secretly revived the project, Griffin volunteered as a test subject, and he was believed to have died after the antidote meant to reverse the process failed; Maggie later discovered that the antidote, known as the buffer, had never actually been given to him. The fugitives take refuge with a former soldier from the program, who tells them that the military has been using Griffin to carry out political assassinations, and who sacrifices his life to protect them when Griffin attacks.

Griffin then kidnaps Maggie's sister and demands that Maggie recreate the antidote in return for her sister's life. After a confrontation with Turner at a train station, Griffin forces Maggie to a laboratory and makes her inject herself with half of the buffer to prove it is safe. Turner tracks them down and fights Griffin, who begins to turn visible and horribly disfigured: Maggie had substituted rat poison for the antidote. Griffin is defeated, leaving Maggie and Turner alive but shaken.

The film went straight to video on May 23, 2006. As with the original, it was poorly received; only one of six reviews on Rotten Tomatoes was positive.

title: Friends with Money
overview: After she quits her lucrative job, Olivia finds herself unsure about her future and her relationships with her successful and wealthy friends.
plot:
Olivia is a single, always-broke woman who cleans houses in Los Angeles to make ends meet after quitting her job as a teacher. She is in a group of wealthy friends consisting of Franny, a stay-at-home mom with a large trust fund; Christine, a television writer; Jane, a fashion designer; and their husbands.
Still heartbroken over a brief affair with a married man, Olivia agrees to go on a blind date with Franny's trainer, Mike. The date goes poorly, but Mike attempts to make up for it at the last minute and asks to go along with Olivia on a cleaning job. Despite him only offering minimal help, Mike asks for part of Olivia's pay and she reluctantly agrees. They begin dating and Mike continues to come along to work with Olivia and take part of her earnings until she finally finds the self-confidence to call Mike out for his callous behavior and ends the relationship.
Christine and her husband David are constantly at odds with each other, to the point that their friends openly speculate whether they're going to split up. Christine struggles to concentrate on the script she and David are writing as the construction of a new addition to their home is ongoing. She soon discovers that their neighbors' sudden animosity is because the addition will block their views, and attempts to stop construction.
David expresses apathy at the neighbors' anger and Christine confronts him for his lack of sensitivity, including showing a lack of care and affection for her. They decide to separate. Christine puts the unfinished house up for sale and briefly finds herself despondent at David's absence before stubbing her toe and hearing her nanny call out asking if she's okay—something David had always failed to do.
Jane cannot seem to stop herself from insulting acquaintances and becoming angry over minor perceived slights. She also has stopped washing her hair and shows signs of depression. Her husband Aaron, who owns a shampoo company, is fashionable and often assumed to be gay by strangers as well as friends. He befriends another straight, married man named Aaron with similar interests and finally, confronts Jane for her angry fits and refusal to wash her hair after she has an outburst during brunch with the other Aaron and his wife. Jane admits that she's depressed after realizing, "There's no more wondering what it's going to be like."
Franny and her husband Matt are by far the wealthiest couple in the group due to Franny's trust fund. Neither of them work and they live in a large house with full-time help. The other friends frequently comment on their wealth and the apparent lack of tension in their marriage as a result of having no stress about money or work, though Franny does express some discomfort with how much Matt likes to spend.
The friends come together at a charity fundraiser for ALS, where Franny has bought a table. Jane finally washes her hair and smooths things over with her husband.

title: Derailed
tagline: He never saw it coming.
overview: When two married business executives having an affair are blackmailed by a violent criminal, they are forced to turn the tables on him to save their families.
plot:
Chicago advertising executive Charles Schine lives with his wife Deanna and their daughter Amy, who suffers from type 1 diabetes, which requires expensive medical treatment.
On a commuter train to work one morning, Charles meets Lucinda Harris, a financial advisor who is married with a daughter. The two begin meeting and one evening decide to take a room in a cheap hotel. As they are undressing, an armed man bursts into their room and robs them and beats Charles, and then brutally rapes Lucinda. Not wanting her husband to learn of her affair, Lucinda persuades Charles not to report the crime and they go their separate ways.
Days later, the man, who identifies himself as Philippe LaRoche, contacts Charles and threatens to kill his family if he does not pay him $20,000. He takes the money from their savings, goes to the meeting point and hands over the cash. LaRoche beats Charles for cancelling his credit cards.
A month later, LaRoche calls again, this time demanding $100,000. Charles explains his situation to his work colleague Winston, an ex-con. Winston offers to scare off LaRoche for ten percent of the demanded payout. Charles embezzles $10,000 from his company and he and Winston plot to get the drop on LaRoche at the specified meeting location. However, LaRoche surprises them, shoots Winston dead, and takes the $10,000. Charles dumps the car with Winston's body into the river and later gives a false alibi when questioned by Detective Franklin Church.
Charles receives another call from LaRoche, saying he is holding Lucinda hostage and will kill her if he does not deliver the full $100,000. Charles takes the money from the account meant for his daughter's medical treatment, goes to Lucinda's apartment, and makes the payoff to LaRoche and his partner Dexter.
Charles visits Lucinda at her workplace but discovers that the woman he met is not the Lucinda Harris who works there but is actually called Jane and only worked there briefly as a temp. He reaches her apartment, which is now being shown to new prospective renters, and discovers that Jane's photograph of her purported daughter is actually a cut-out of a stock picture from a brochure.
Charles tracks Jane down, follows her, and sees her meeting and kissing LaRoche, learning she was in on the scam. He also observes her seducing another businessman, Sam. Determined to retrieve his stolen money, Charles rents a room at the same hotel as before and waits for Jane to arrive there with Sam, followed by LaRoche. Charles knocks LaRoche unconscious outside the hotel room door, disarms him, and bursts in, telling a confused Sam the scheme he has been set up for. Dexter arrives to back up LaRoche and when Sam tries to jump Charles a gunfight ensues, with everyone shot but Charles, who watches Jane die and then returns to his room. He convinces the police who have been called in that he was just a bystander. As he leaves, Charles claims his briefcase from the hotel safe and gets back his stolen money.

title: Just Like Heaven
tagline: It's a wonderful afterlife.
overview: Shortly after David Abbott moves into his new San Francisco digs, he has an unwelcome visitor on his hands: winsome Elizabeth Martinson, who asserts that the apartment is hers -- and promptly vanishes. When she starts appearing and disappearing at will, David thinks she's a ghost, while Elizabeth is convinced she's alive.
plot:
Elizabeth Masterson, a dedicated young San Francisco physician, is in a serious car crash. Three months later, the grieving recent widower David Abbott sublets Elizabeth's apartment.
Elizabeth begins appearing in the apartment, confusing both. She initially believes David is a squatter, and he thinks she broke in. They soon realize Elizabeth can move through walls and objects. She does not know who she is, but insists she is not dead.
David unsuccessfully tries to have Elizabeth's spirit exorcised. As only he can see and hear her, others think he is hallucinating. Elizabeth asks him to help her discover who she really is, so David first talks to neighbours in the building but no one knows her.
David enlists help from psychic bookstore clerk Darryl, who agrees Elizabeth is not truly dead. He says David has a blocked heart and must emotionally release the woman who was in his life. When Elizabeth says he should get over being dumped, he storms out. Darryl, unable to see Elizabeth, tells her not to disrespect the dead. She finds David and he explains about his wife's death.
At a nearby restaurant, Elizabeth talks David through saving a man's life. Suddenly, she remembers being a doctor. They go to the nearest hospital where Elizabeth's memories come flooding back. Dr. Fran Lo, Elizabeth's mentor, takes him to Elizabeth, who is in a coma. When David touches her hand, she feels it, meaning she is still connected to her body.
Elizabeth's sister Abby arrives, and Dr. Brett Rushton – Elizabeth's rival – notifies her that Elizabeth signed a DNR order. When he asks her to sign off on disconnecting Elizabeth's life support, she agrees to consider it.
David and Elizabeth bond. When he takes her to a beautiful landscaped garden he designed, she senses having been there before. In fact, she was dreaming of the garden (in the opening scenes of the film), while catnapping during a long shift.
When David is offered a long-term lease on Elizabeth's apartment, he realizes she will be taken off life support. To prevent it, he goes to Abby and says she is communicating with him. While there, Elizabeth discovers that her niece Lily can see her. David begs Abby to keep her alive, but she has already signed the papers to disconnect her life support the next day. As a last-ditch effort, David blurts out Abby's secret kiss to J.J. on her wedding day, freaking her out so she chases him out.
Elizabeth opts to spend her last night with David in the apartment. The next morning, he is determined to prevent her death by stealing her body from the hospital; he enlists his therapist friend Jack to help. Upon reaching her body, Elizabeth suddenly recognises Jack as Abby's former college boyfriend J.J., who reveals that the two of them had set up David and Elizabeth for a blind date on the night of the crash. David realizes he can see her because they were destined to meet. He admits to Jack and Elizabeth that he loves her.

title: Jackass: The Movie
tagline: Do not attempt this at home.
overview: Johnny Knoxville and his band of maniacs perform a variety of stunts and gross-out gags on the big screen for the first time. They wander around Japan in panda outfits, wreak havoc on a once civilized golf course, they even do stunts involving LIVE alligators, and so on.
plot:
Jackass: The Movie is a 2002 American reality slapstick comedy directed by Jeff Tremaine and produced by Tremaine, Spike Jonze and Johnny Knoxville. A continuation of the MTV television series Jackass, which had ended its run, it was produced by Lynch Siderow Productions and Dickhouse Productions and features most of the original cast, including Knoxville, Bam Margera, Chris Pontius, Steve-O, Dave England, Ryan Dunn, Wee Man, Preston Lacy and Ehren McGhehey.

Like the series, the film has no conventional plot. It is a compilation of dangerous stunts, crude skits and elaborate pranks on unsuspecting members of the public, intercut with comments from the cast. It opens with a mock Hollywood action sequence set to "O Fortuna", in which the entire cast rides a giant shopping cart downhill amid explosions while each member is introduced, before Knoxville delivers his signature greeting and the group crashes into a fruit stand.

Among the many stunts and pranks that follow, Knoxville is flipped over and knocked out in a golf cart, Steve-O snorts wasabi, Bam Margera plants a live alligator in his mother April's kitchen, Chris Pontius dances in public in a thong as his character Party Boy, and Ryan Dunn takes on a female Japanese kickboxing champion. Wee Man causes chaos in the streets of Tokyo inside a giant traffic cone, and the cast endure painful encounters with animals, paper cuts, fireworks and bodily functions. Throughout, the cast's willingness to injure and humiliate themselves for the camera is the central source of humor, along with their obvious camaraderie.

Like the series, the film relies on the cast's apparent fearlessness and on the reactions of bystanders, and it is widely regarded as a cult phenomenon of the 2000s.

MTV Films and Paramount Pictures released the film on October 25, 2002. Made for about 5 million dollars, it opened at number one at the U.S. box office with 22.8 million dollars and grossed 79.5 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed, with 49 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 42, and it was followed by Jackass Number Two in 2006.

title: Treasure Planet
tagline: Find your place in the universe.
overview: When space galleon cabin boy Jim Hawkins discovers a map to an intergalactic "loot of a thousand worlds," a cyborg cook named John Silver teaches him to battle supernovas and space storms on their journey to find treasure.
plot:
Treasure Planet is a science fiction adventure film produced by Walt Disney Pictures, released in 2002. The movie is an adaptation of Robert Louis Stevenson's classic novel "Treasure Island," set in a futuristic universe.

The story begins with Jim Hawkins (voiced by Joseph Gordon-Levitt), an orphan boy living on the planet Terra. Jim's life changes when he meets Billy Bones (voiced by David Hyde Pierce), an old pirate who has been injured and is dying. Before his death, Billy gives Jim a mysterious map that supposedly leads to the treasure of the infamous Captain Flint.

Jim sets out on a journey with Dr. Delbert Doppler (voiced by Brian Murray), a spaceship captain who claims to be taking him to find the treasure. However, upon arrival at the planet of Salacia, they are ambushed by Captain Flint's crew, led by the ruthless and cunning Long John Silver (voiced by Jack Davenport). Long John Silver is revealed to be Jim's biological father, and his true intentions for finding the treasure are not what they seem.

As Jim navigates this new world, he meets a group of space pirates known as the "Buccaneers," who are on a quest to find the legendary treasure. The crew includes John Mutt (voiced by Jason Lee), a young and skilled pirate; and B.E.N. (voiced by Patrick McGoohan), an old robot who becomes Jim's friend and ally.

Throughout their journey, Jim faces various challenges and obstacles as he tries to uncover the truth about his father's past and the treasure. Along the way, he learns valuable lessons about loyalty, friendship, and the importance of staying true to oneself.

As the story unfolds, Long John Silver's true intentions are revealed: he plans to use the treasure to gain control over the entire planet. Jim and his friends must work together to stop him and save the day. In a thrilling finale, they engage in an epic space battle against Captain Flint's crew, with Jim ultimately discovering the truth about his father's past and finding the treasure.

The movie ends with Jim returning home, having grown into a confident and capable young man. He reflects on the lessons he learned during his journey and the friends he made along the way, knowing that their bond will last a lifetime.

Treasure Planet is a visually stunning film that combines traditional animation techniques with cutting-edge computer-generated imagery. The movie's unique blend of science fiction and classic adventure elements has made it a beloved favorite among audiences of all ages.

title: The Santa Clause 2
tagline: What's Christmas Fun without some Reindeer Games?
overview: Better watch out! The big guy in red is coming to town once again. This time, Scott Calvin -- also known as Santa Claus -- finds out there's an obscure clause in his contract requiring him to take on a wife. He has to leave the North Pole to fulfill his obligations, or else he'll be forced to give up his Yuletide gig.
plot:
The Santa Clause 2 is a Christmas comedy film released in 2002, directed by Michael Lembeck and written by Leo Benvenuti, Steve Rudnick, and Rick Mulvaney. The movie serves as a sequel to the 1994 film The Santa Clause.

The story begins with Scott Calvin (Tim Allen), who has now been living as Santa Claus for over five years. He is struggling to balance his life as a father and husband with his duties as the new Santa. His wife, Carol (Elizabeth Mitchell), is pregnant with their first child, but she's not sure if Scott can handle being Santa full-time.

Meanwhile, a group of elves from the North Pole arrive at Scott's house, warning him that Christmas Eve is approaching and he must return to the North Pole to prepare for the holiday. However, Scott is hesitant to leave his family behind, especially since Carol has just discovered she's pregnant with their first child.

As Christmas Eve approaches, Scott's doubts about being Santa grow stronger. He begins to question whether he's truly cut out for the job and starts to feel like a "fake" Santa. The elves try to convince him that he's doing a great job as Santa, but Scott is unconvinced.

On Christmas Eve, disaster strikes when a group of naughty children, led by a young boy named Tucker (Eric Lloyd), steal the magical crystal that gives Scott his powers. Without the crystal, Scott loses his Santa powers and is forced to return home for Christmas.

However, things take a turn for the worse when Scott's son Charlie (Eric Lloyd) discovers the truth about his father's identity as Santa. Charlie is initially excited to have a real-life Santa Claus as a dad, but he soon realizes that being Santa comes with its own set of challenges and responsibilities.

As Christmas Day approaches, Scott must find a way to regain his powers and save Christmas. With the help of his elves and Carol, Scott embarks on a journey to retrieve the magical crystal and restore his powers. Along the way, he learns valuable lessons about being a good father, husband, and Santa Claus.

In the end, Scott successfully retrieves the crystal and regains his powers as Santa. The movie concludes with Scott returning to the North Pole, where he is welcomed back by the elves and Mrs. Claus (Judge Reinhold). Scott also gets to spend Christmas with his family, including his son Charlie, who has learned to appreciate the challenges and joys of being a part of the Claus family.

The Santa Clause 2 received mixed reviews from critics but was a commercial success, grossing over $140 million worldwide. The movie's blend of humor, heart, and holiday cheer made it a beloved favorite among families around the world.

title: All the Boys Love Mandy Lane
original_title: All the Boys Love Mandy Lane
tagline: Everyone is dying to be with her. Someone is killing for it.
overview: Beautiful Mandy Lane isn't a party girl but, when classmate Chloe invites the Texas high school student to a bash in the countryside, she reluctantly accepts. After hitching a ride with a vaguely scary older man, the teens arrive at their destination. Partying ensues, and Mandy's close pal, Emmet, keeps a watchful eye on the young males making a play for Mandy. Then two of the students are murdered.
plot:
All the Boys Love Mandy Lane is a 2006 American slasher film directed by Jonathan Levine in his feature debut and written by Jacob Forman. Amber Heard stars as Mandy Lane, a high-school student whose beauty makes her the object of everyone's attention, with Anson Mount as the ranch hand Garth, Michael Welch, Whitney Able and Edwin Hodge. The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in 2006 and was shown at many festivals before its British release in February 2008; because of distribution problems, its American release was delayed until 2013.

At a Texas high school, Mandy Lane returns from summer vacation transformed, attracting the attention of all the boys. One of them, Dylan, invites her to a pool party, and she agrees on condition that her best friend, the outcast Emmet, can come. When Dylan humiliates Emmet, Emmet retaliates by goading a drunken Dylan into jumping from the roof into the pool; Dylan misses and dies on the concrete. Nine months later, Mandy has been accepted by Dylan's popular friends, while Emmet has become even more of a pariah.

The stoner Red invites Mandy to a weekend party at his father's remote cattle ranch, and she reluctantly accepts. She travels there with Red, the insecure cheerleader Chloe, the quiet football player Bird, and the couple Jake and Marlin, all eager to impress her. At the ranch they meet Garth, a handsome, laconic ranch hand. On the first night, after Jake and Marlin argue in a barn, an unseen attacker knocks Marlin unconscious and brutally assaults her with a shotgun. As drinking, drugs and sexual tension fuel rivalries among the teenagers, the killer begins picking them off one by one. The identity of the murderer is revealed partway through, but the story holds further twists about the true nature of the bloodshed, and Mandy's role in the events turns out to be very different from what the others, and the audience, expect.

All the Boys Love Mandy Lane received mixed reviews, holding a 47 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus said it had enough wit and craft to interest horror fans but was not original enough for mainstream audiences. Over time the film gained a cult following, and critics praised its 1970s-style cinematography and Heard's performance.

title: Spirit: Stallion of the Cimarron
tagline: Leader. Hero. Legend.
overview: As a wild stallion travels across the frontiers of the Old West, he befriends a young human and finds true love with a mare.
plot:
Spirit: Stallion of the Cimarron is a 2002 American animated Western drama film produced by DreamWorks Pictures. The movie follows the journey of a wild mustang stallion named Spirit, who embarks on an epic quest to find his place in the world.

The film begins with Spirit (voiced by Matt Damon) as a young foal, born and raised in the Cimarron Valley. He is a spirited and adventurous horse, always eager to explore and discover new things. As he grows up, Spirit becomes increasingly restless, feeling confined by the limitations of his herd's routine.

One day, Spirit meets a beautiful mare named Rain (voiced by Gina Philips), who shares his sense of wanderlust. Together, they set out on an adventure across the American West, facing numerous challenges and dangers along the way. They encounter fierce storms, treacherous terrain, and hostile humans, but their bond grows stronger with each passing day.

As Spirit and Rain journey through the wilderness, they meet a wise old stallion named Thunder (voiced by Michael Jeter), who teaches them about the importance of freedom and self-discovery. However, their happiness is short-lived, as they are captured by a ruthless horse trader named Colonel Hart (voiced by James Cromwell) and his men.

Spirit is sold to a cavalry unit, where he meets a young soldier named Little Creek (voiced by Paul Williams), who befriends him and helps him escape. Together, they embark on a perilous journey back to the Cimarron Valley, facing numerous obstacles and dangers along the way.

As Spirit returns home, he is reunited with Rain, and together they face off against Colonel Hart in an epic showdown. With his newfound courage and determination, Spirit defeats the colonel and his men, securing his freedom and proving himself as a true leader among his herd.

Throughout the film, the animation is stunning, with beautifully rendered landscapes and characters that bring the American West to life. The voice cast delivers strong performances, bringing depth and emotion to their respective roles. The music, composed by Hans Zimmer and John Powell, is equally impressive, perfectly capturing the spirit (pun intended) of the wild mustang.

Overall, Spirit: Stallion of the Cimarron is a timeless tale of self-discovery, courage, and the power of the human (and equine) spirit. With its stunning animation, memorable characters, and epic storyline, it's no wonder this film has become a beloved classic among both children and adults alike.

title: The Eye
tagline: How can you believe your eyes when they're not yours?
overview: Violinist Sydney Wells was accidentally blinded by her sister Helen when she was five years old. She submits to a cornea transplantation, and while recovering from the operation, she realizes that she is seeing dead people.
plot:
Sydney Wells is a successful classical violinist from Los Angeles who has been blind since she was five years old, caused by an accident with firecrackers. Fifteen years later, after celebrating conductor and pianist Simon McCullough's birthday during rehearsal, Sydney undergoes a cornea transplant, which causes her eyesight to return. While a bit blurry at first, as time passes, Sydney's vision begins to clear; however, she also begins experiencing terrifying visions, mostly of fire and people dying. She also sees people who are already dead: on one occasion, a girl passes right through her. Sydney attempts to unravel the mystery of the visions and convince others, primarily her visual therapist and fellow violinist, Paul Faulkner, who helps her in her quest. She knows that she is not going insane.
Accompanied by Paul, Sydney travels to Mexico, where the cornea donor Ana Cristina Martinez was originally from. She discovers from Ana's mother that the images of fire and death are the result of an industrial accident that Ana foretold. Ana hanged herself because she was unable to stop the accident. Sydney forgives Ana's spirit, who leaves in peace. As Sydney and Paul begin their journey home, they are caught in traffic congestion caused by a police chase on the other side of the border. Sydney sees the little girl from her vision in the car beside her. She then realizes that this is what her vision has been all along: to save the people who are about to die from an accident.
Still able to see the silhouettes of death, Sydney gets everyone off the highway, starting with a bus filled with people. She and Paul convince everyone to leave the bus and the cars by telling them that there is a bomb inside the bus. However, a driver leading the police chase rushes through the border barriers and collides with a tank truck, igniting leaking gasoline in the process. Sydney sees the little girl trapped in the car, her mother lying on the ground in front of it, already being hit by a passenger and losing consciousness. Paul breaks open the window and gets the girl out. Paul and Sydney carry the girl and her mother to safety just before the tank truck causes a chain explosion. Sydney is blinded by flying glass fragments in the process.
After recovering at a hospital, she returns to Los Angeles to continue performing as a blind violinist, though with a more optimistic view of her condition.

title: Slither
tagline: Horror has a new face.
overview: A small town is taken over by an alien plague, turning residents into zombies and all forms of mutant monsters.
plot:
Slither is a 2006 American horror-comedy film directed by James Gunn and written by Gunn and Phil Lord. The movie stars Nathan Fillion, Elizabeth Banks, Michael Rooker, and Jill Witcher.

The story begins with a small town called Middleton, where a group of friends, including Jeff (Nathan Fillion), a high school teacher, and his girlfriend Starla (Elizabeth Banks), are preparing for the annual Harvest Festival. The festival is a celebration of the town's agricultural heritage, but it also serves as an opportunity for the townspeople to let loose and have fun.

However, things take a dark turn when a mysterious alien parasite infects the town's residents, turning them into zombie-like creatures with a strong desire to eat human flesh. The parasite, which is about 10 feet long, has been introduced to Earth by a group of aliens who crash-landed in the nearby woods.

As the infection spreads rapidly throughout the town, Jeff and his friends must band together to survive and find a way to stop the parasite before it's too late. Along the way, they encounter a variety of bizarre and terrifying creatures, including giant spiders, mutated animals, and even a zombie-like version of Starla.

One of the most interesting aspects of Slither is its exploration of small-town America and the ways in which people can become complacent and accepting of their surroundings. The town of Middleton is portrayed as a place where everyone knows each other's business, but also where secrets and lies are often swept under the rug.

As the story progresses, Jeff and his friends discover that the parasite has a unique ability to manipulate its hosts' minds, making them more aggressive and violent. They also learn that the aliens who introduced the parasite were not just random visitors, but rather part of an experiment designed to create a new breed of super-soldiers.

In the end, Jeff and his friends must use their wits and whatever resources they can find to stop the parasite and save the town. Along the way, they encounter some unexpected allies, including a group of survivors from a nearby town who have been fighting against the parasites for weeks.

The movie's climax features an epic battle between Jeff and the leader of the zombie-like creatures, a giant spider-like creature that has become the parasite's host. In the end, Jeff emerges victorious, but not before realizing that the parasite has left him with a strange and unsettling connection to the alien entity.

Overall, Slither is a fun and entertaining horror-comedy that explores themes of small-town America, paranoia, and the dangers of complacency. With its unique blend of humor, action, and horror elements, it's a must-see for fans of the genre.

title: Eight Below
tagline: The Most Amazing Story Of Survival, Friendship, And Adventure Ever Told.
overview: In the Antarctic, after an expedition with Dr. Davis McClaren, the sled dog trainer Jerry Shepherd has to leave the polar base with his colleagues due to the proximity of a heavy snow storm. He ties his dogs to be rescued after, but the mission is called-off and the dogs are left alone at their own fortune. For six months, Jerry tries to find a sponsor for a rescue mission.
plot:
In January 1993, Jerry Shepard, guide at a National Science Foundation Antarctic research base, is asked to take UCLA professor Dr. Davis McClaren to Mount Melbourne to find a rare meteorite from Mercury. Since the ice conditions are poor, the best way to the mountain is by dog sled.
Shepard and McClaren make it, but are called back to base camp due to an approaching storm. McClaren begs for more time and Shepard gives him half a day. En route back to base, McClaren slips down an embankment, breaking his leg and falling into freezing water. Shepard uses lead dog Maya to carry a rope to McClaren and pulls him out. They battle hypothermia, frostbite, and near-whiteout conditions as the dogs lead them to base.
At base, the human crew is immediately evacuated, while the dogs are left behind. Shepard, promised that the pilot will return shortly for the dogs, tightens their collars to ensure they cannot get loose. Because of the harsh weather conditions a rescue cannot be attempted.
Back in the United States, Shepard tries to return for the dogs, but no one is willing to finance the expedition. Five months later, Shepard makes one last attempt. McClaren realizing his ingratitude and uses the remainder of his grant money to finance the rescue. They fear there is little chance any of the dogs could have survived so long, but they decide to try anyway.
The eight sled dogs – lead dog Maya, Old Jack, Shorty, Dewey, Truman, Shadow, Buck, and the young Max – have been waiting in the freezing conditions for Shepard to return. After a few days without eating, the dogs are prompted into action as a gull flies near, and they all begin to break free, one by one. Old Jack, by now too weak, remains attached. Maya tries to free him, but reluctantly leaves him behind when he shows no sign of wanting to leave. Maya joins the other dogs, and together they catch a few birds, getting their first food in weeks.
After nearly two months on their own, the dogs rest on a slope one night under the southern lights. Fascinated by the display, they run about and play until Dewey falls down an incline and is mortally wounded. The team sleeps by his side and Dewey dies overnight. Max loyally stays by him while the others move on. By the time Max heads in their direction, he has lost the pack.
Maya leads the team to the Russian base, which is unsecured and full of food, while Max finds his way back to the American base, which is locked up. Setting back out, Max recognizes the embankment the dogs traveled on their way back from Mount Melbourne. While exploring, Max finds a dead orca, but is driven off by a leopard seal nesting inside the body. Nearby, Maya and the team hear Max and join him. Max lures the seal away so the dogs can eat, but it doubles back and bites Maya, leaving her badly injured.
In a rage, the five other dogs attack the seal. Overwhelmed, the seal quickly drags itself into the water, after which the dogs feast on the orca. The reunited team continues traveling.

title: Trapped
tagline: It was the perfect plan until she refused to be the perfect victim!
overview: When their daughter is kidnapped by experienced nappers, the Jennings turn the tables on this seemingly foolproof plan.
plot:
Trapped is a 2002 American crime thriller film directed by Luis Mandoki and based on Greg Iles's novel 24 Hours. Charlize Theron and Stuart Townsend star as the parents of a kidnapped girl, played by Dakota Fanning, with Kevin Bacon and Courtney Love as the kidnappers and Pruitt Taylor Vince as their accomplice. It was filmed in British Columbia in the spring of 2001 and released by Columbia Pictures on September 20, 2002.

Dr. Will Jennings, a successful physician, has just patented a new anesthetic and travels to Seattle to present it at a medical conference. At his hotel, a woman named Cheryl introduces herself as an admirer, then pulls a gun and forces him into his room. At the same moment, her husband, Joe, breaks into the Jennings family's luxurious home outside Portland, Oregon, and takes Will's wife, Karen, hostage, while Joe's cousin Marvin drives their young daughter, Abby, to a remote cabin. The couple demands a ransom, keeping the parents apart and under watch.

The plan begins to unravel when Abby, who suffers from severe asthma, has an attack without her inhaler, and Joe is forced to take a blindfolded Karen to the cabin to treat her. Back at the house, Karen fights back against Joe, wounding him with a hidden scalpel and briefly speaking with Abby by phone before Joe regains control. In Seattle, Will uses his medical knowledge to inject Cheryl with a paralyzing drug, bringing her close to death before reviving her. Shaken, Cheryl reveals that this abduction is personal: Joe blames Will for the death of their own daughter, who died during surgery on which Will assisted. Will explains that he was wrongly blamed by the head surgeon, and Cheryl begins to turn against the plan, especially after learning in a heated phone call that Joe intends to keep Abby and raise her as his own.

Accompanied by police, Will collects the ransom, then flies with Cheryl toward Portland in a seaplane as Joe drives north on Interstate 5 with Karen, followed by Marvin and Abby. When Karen attacks Joe and forces the car off the road, Will spots it from the air and lands the seaplane on the highway, causing a massive pileup. Marvin lets Abby go, and after a struggle between the two men, Karen shoots Joe dead. As police and FBI agents arrive, Karen treats Abby's asthma, and the family is reunited as Cheryl is arrested.

Trapped was a critical and commercial failure. Rotten Tomatoes reported 17% approval, and the film grossed about $13.4 million worldwide.

title: Serpico
tagline: Many of his fellow officers considered him the most dangerous man alive - An honest cop.
overview: Frank Serpico is an idealistic New York City cop who refuses to take bribes, unlike the rest of the force. His actions get Frank shunned by the other officers, and often placed in dangerous situations by his partners. When his superiors ignore Frank's accusations of corruption, he decides to go public with the allegations. Although this causes the Knapp Commission to investigate his claims, Frank has also placed a target on himself.
plot:
On the evening of February 3, 1971, NYPD Detective Frank Serpico is rushed to the hospital, having been shot in the face. Police Chief Sidney Green fears that Serpico was shot by another cop. Serpico's story is shown in a flashback.
Serpico graduates from the police academy on March 5, 1960, with big ideas for improving the police force's community relations. He dresses like an actual civilian instead of wearing the department's standard plainclothes dress, which is easily recognizable. While he is chasing a burglar, other officers fail to recognize him as one of their own and shoot at him. He survives, but realizes that deviating from protocols can be dangerous.
In 1967, Serpico reports an attempted bribe to a high-ranking investigator, who chuckles and advises him to keep the money. Serpico soon learns that corruption is rampant in the department. Forced to accompany officers as they collect payoffs from criminals and small businesses, Serpico refuses to accept his share of the money. He makes several attempts to alert superiors to the corruption but is rebuffed every time. Other officers learn that he is reporting them, and he begins to fear for his life.
Serpico and his well-connected friend Blair go to the mayor's assistant, who promises a real investigation and support but is stymied by political pressure. Ostracized, frustrated and fearful, Serpico sinks into depression, which ruins his relationship with his girlfriend. He begins brutalizing well-connected suspects who had been bribing his superiors and thought themselves protected. Finally, Serpico informs his Captain that he reported his experiences to agencies outside of the NYC police force. Furious, the captain informs the other officers.
Blair uses his connections to arrange a personal interview with the district attorney, who tells Serpico that if he testifies to a grand jury, a major investigation will follow. The DA limits his questions and prevents Serpico from revealing the ubiquity of corruption in the police force. Serpico and Blair take their story to The New York Times on April 25, 1970. After his allegations are published, his superiors retaliate by assigning Serpico to a high-risk Brooklyn narcotics squad.
During a raid on a drug trafficker's apartment on February 3, 1971, Serpico's partners hold him back at a critical moment, and he gets shot in the face. After a long, painful recovery, he testifies before the Knapp Commission, a governmental inquiry into NYPD corruption. Afterward, Serpico resigns from the NYPD on June 15, 1972, and is awarded the NYPD Medal of Honor for "conspicuous bravery in action". He then leaves the U.S. and settles in Switzerland.
