title: King Arthur
tagline: Rule Your Fate.
overview: The story of the Arthurian legend, based on the 'Sarmatian hypothesis' which contends that the legend has a historical nucleus in the Sarmatian heavy cavalry troops stationed in Britain, and that the Roman-British military commander, Lucius Artorius Castus is the historical person behind the legend.
plot:
King Arthur is an epic historical adventure film of 2004 directed by Antoine Fuqua and written by David Franzoni, which recasts the legendary king as a Roman officer in fifth-century Britain rather than a medieval knight. Clive Owen stars as Arthur, with Ioan Gruffudd as Lancelot, Keira Knightley as Guinevere, Mads Mikkelsen as Tristan, Ray Winstone as Bors, Stephen Dillane as Merlin, Stellan Skarsgård as the Saxon leader Cerdic and Til Schweiger as his son Cynric.

As the declining Roman Empire withdraws from Britain, the native Woads, led by Merlin, wage an insurgency. Arthur, the half-British commander Artorius Castus, and his Sarmatian knights have completed fifteen years of compulsory service for Rome and are ready to go home. Instead Bishop Germanus orders one last mission: to rescue an important Roman family living north of Hadrian's Wall before an invading Saxon army under Cerdic and Cynric arrives, whose son Alecto may one day be pope. Arthur and his surviving knights, Lancelot, Tristan, Galahad, Bors, Gawain and Dagonet, reluctantly agree.

At the estate they find that the patriarch Marius, who refuses to leave, has enslaved the local people. Arthur frees two tortured Woad prisoners, Guinevere and her young brother, and forces Marius to leave. As the convoy flees through the mountains with the Saxons in pursuit, Marius attempts a revolt and is killed by Guinevere. Learning from Alecto that Germanus and the bishops had his beloved mentor Pelagius executed for heresy, Arthur grows disillusioned with Rome, while Guinevere and Merlin remind him of his bond with Britain through his Celtic mother. On a frozen lake Arthur's men confront Cynric's troops, and Dagonet gives his life breaking the ice with his axe to halt them. The knights deliver Alecto and his mother safely to the Wall and receive their discharge, but Arthur resolves to stay and fight with his mother's people. After a night with Guinevere, he confronts Cerdic under a flag of truce, and his knights return to fight beside him. At the Battle of Badon Hill, Lancelot kills Cynric but is mortally wounded, Cerdic kills Tristan and Arthur slays Cerdic, breaking the Saxon assault. Arthur marries Guinevere, Merlin proclaims him king of the Britons.

Released in July 2004, the film grossed $203.6 million worldwide against a $120 million budget. Critics were largely unimpressed, giving it 30% on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it a dreary, generic action movie.

title: The Nightmare Before Christmas
tagline: This is Halloween, everybody make a scene!
overview: Tired of scaring humans every October 31 with the same old bag of tricks, Jack Skellington, the spindly king of Halloween Town, kidnaps Santa Claus and plans to deliver shrunken heads and other ghoulish gifts to children on Christmas morning. But as Christmas approaches, Jack's rag-doll girlfriend, Sally, tries to foil his misguided plans.
plot:
The Nightmare Before Christmas is a stop-motion animated musical fantasy film directed by Henry Selick, produced by Tim Burton, and released by Walt Disney Pictures in 1993.

In the town of Halloween Town, Jack Skellington, the Pumpkin King, has grown tired of the same annual routine of Halloween celebrations. One day, while exploring the woods, he stumbles upon a portal to Christmas Town, a holiday-themed town filled with joy and cheer. Intrigued by this new discovery, Jack becomes obsessed with learning about Christmas and decides to take over the holiday himself.

Jack's attempts to understand Christmas lead him to recruit Santa Claus's elves to help him prepare for Christmas Eve. However, things quickly go awry as Jack's Halloween-themed ideas clash with the traditional Christmas customs. The result is a series of chaotic events that put both Halloween Town and Christmas Town in jeopardy.

Meanwhile, Sally, Jack's rag doll creation, tries to warn him about the dangers of meddling with other holidays. She also develops feelings for Jack, but her emotions are unrequited due to his infatuation with Christmas.

As Christmas Eve approaches, Jack's obsession with Christmas reaches a boiling point, and he decides to deliver presents to children all around the world on Christmas Eve. However, things don't go as planned, and Jack's attempts at gift-giving lead to a series of hilarious and disastrous consequences.

In the end, Jack realizes that Halloween and Christmas are two separate holidays with their own unique traditions and values. He also comes to appreciate Sally's love and acceptance for him. The film concludes with Jack returning to Halloween Town, where he is welcomed back as the Pumpkin King, and Sally finds happiness in her own right.

The Nightmare Before Christmas is a timeless tale of self-discovery, friendship, and the importance of embracing one's true identity. With its unique blend of stop-motion animation, catchy musical numbers, and memorable characters, this film has become a beloved classic among both children and adults alike.

title: Daredevil
tagline: A Guardian Devil
overview: A man blinded in a childhood accident fights crime using his superhumanly-elevated remaining senses.
plot:
Daredevil is a 2003 American superhero film written and directed by Mark Steven Johnson, based on the Marvel Comics character created by Stan Lee and Bill Everett. Ben Affleck stars as Matt Murdock, a blind lawyer who fights for justice in the courtroom by day and on the streets of New York as the masked vigilante Daredevil by night. Jennifer Garner plays Elektra Natchios, Michael Clarke Duncan plays Wilson Fisk, Colin Farrell plays the assassin Bullseye, and Joe Pantoliano, Jon Favreau and David Keith complete the main cast.

In 1982, young Matt Murdock is blinded in an accident involving radioactive waste, shortly after discovering that his father, the washed-up boxer Jack "The Devil" Murdock, has been working as an enforcer for a local mobster. Although he loses his sight, his remaining senses are heightened to superhuman levels, giving him a sonar-like ability to perceive his surroundings. Feeling responsible for his son's accident, Jack abandons crime and makes a boxing comeback, unaware that his victories have been arranged. When he refuses to throw a fight, he is murdered.

Twenty years later, Matt works as an attorney in Hell's Kitchen with his friend Foggy Nelson, representing clients he believes to be innocent, often for free. At night he dons a red costume to punish criminals who escape justice. Ben Urich, a newspaper reporter investigating Daredevil, is also pursuing stories about the Kingpin, a mysterious figure said to control organised crime in the city, who is in reality Wilson Fisk, a ruthless crime boss posing as a respectable businessman. Matt falls for Elektra, the daughter of a wealthy businessman linked to Fisk. When her father tries to break away, the Kingpin hires Bullseye, an Irish assassin who never misses, to kill him and frame Daredevil, setting Elektra on a quest for revenge against the man she loves and leading to a confrontation with both Bullseye and the Kingpin.

The film adopts a dark, brooding tone and explores the conflict between justice and vengeance, as well as Matt's Catholic faith and guilt.

Daredevil received mixed reviews but was a commercial success. An extended R-rated director's cut released in 2004 was considered an improvement, and a spin-off, Elektra, followed in 2005.

title: Johnny English
tagline: He knows no fear. He knows no danger. He knows nothing.
overview: A lowly pencil pusher working for MI7, Johnny English is suddenly promoted to super spy after Agent One is assassinated and every other agent is blown up at his funeral. When a billionaire entrepreneur sponsors the exhibition of the Crown Jewels—and the valuable gems disappear on the opening night and on English's watch—the newly-designated agent must jump into action to find the thief and recover the missing gems.
plot:
Johnny English is a 2003 spy comedy film directed by Rob Sitch and starring Rowan Atkinson as the titular character. The movie follows the story of Johnny English, a bumbling but lovable British secret agent working for MI7, the British intelligence agency.

The film begins with Johnny English (Rowan Atkinson) being introduced to his new boss, Pemberley (John Malkovich), who is impressed by Johnny's skills and assigns him to stop a plot by the villainous Vesper Lynd (Natalie Imbruglia). However, things quickly go awry as Johnny discovers that he has been replaced by a more competent agent, Johnny English Jr. (Ben Miller).

Despite his initial setbacks, Johnny English perseveres and sets out to stop Vesper's plan, which involves stealing the world's most expensive diamond, the "Regent Diamond." Along the way, he encounters a beautiful and intelligent woman named Natalie (Natalie Imbruglia), who becomes his love interest.

As Johnny English navigates through various obstacles and mishaps, he must also contend with his own ineptitude and the skepticism of his colleagues. However, with the help of his trusty sidekick, Bough (Simon Pegg), and a series of hilarious gadgets and disguises, Johnny is able to stay one step ahead of Vesper's henchmen.

Throughout the film, Rowan Atkinson's physical comedy and timing are on full display as he brings Johnny English to life. The movie's humor is clever and witty, with plenty of references to James Bond and other spy movies.

In the end, Johnny English successfully foils Vesper's plan and saves the Regent Diamond. Along the way, he also wins over Natalie's heart and proves himself to be a worthy secret agent in his own right.

Overall, Johnny English is a hilarious and entertaining film that showcases Rowan Atkinson's unique brand of comedy. With its clever plot, witty humor, and plenty of physical comedy, it's no wonder that the movie became a box office hit and spawned two sequels.

title: Spy Kids 2: The Island of Lost Dreams
original_title: Spy Kids 2: The Island of Lost Dreams
tagline: Little Spies. Big Attitudes.
overview: Exploring the further adventures of Carmen and Juni Cortez, who have now joined the family spy business as Level 2 OSS agents. Their new mission is to save the world from a mad scientist living on a volcanic island populated by an imaginative menagerie of creatures. On this bizarre island, none of the Cortez's gadgets work and they must rely on their wits--and each other--to survive and save the day.
plot:
Spy Kids 2: The Island of Lost Dreams is a 2002 American spy action comedy written, directed, shot, edited and co-scored by Robert Rodriguez, the sequel to Spy Kids. Alexa Vega and Daryl Sabara return as Carmen and Juni Cortez, with Antonio Banderas and Carla Gugino as their parents Gregorio and Ingrid, Mike Judge as Donnagon Giggles, Ricardo Montalbán and Holland Taylor as their grandparents, Cheech Marin, and Steve Buscemi as the scientist Romero. Matt O'Leary and Emily Osment, in her film debut, play the rival agents Gary and Gerti Giggles.

Carmen and Juni are now full-time agents in the new Spy Kids division of the OSS, where they face fierce competition from Gary and Gerti, the children of Donnagon Giggles. After the Giggles siblings outshine them on a mission at the Troublemakers theme park, Donnagon manipulates his way into being named director of the OSS instead of Gregorio. Soon a group of Magna Men steals the Transmooker, a device capable of shutting down every electronic device in the world, and Gary frames Juni for the loss, getting him fired.

Carmen hacks into the agency's database, reinstates her brother and assigns them the mission of recovering the Transmooker, which takes them to a mysterious island where no electronics work. There they meet Romero, a reclusive scientist who tried to create miniature hybrid animals to sell but accidentally made them gigantic, and who now hides in his lab in fear of his own creations. Romero reveals that the stolen device was only a prototype and that the real Transmooker lies on the island. As Carmen and Juni brave strange creatures, from flying pigs to spider-monkeys, Gary and Gerti close in, and Gregorio and Ingrid, joined by Ingrid's parents, set out to find their missing children.

The film celebrates family, inventiveness and loyalty, and pays homage to stop-motion creature films such as those of Ray Harryhausen with its imaginative monsters.

Released by Dimension Films on August 7, 2002, the film opened in third place and grossed about 85.8 million dollars domestically. It received generally favorable reviews, with 75 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 66, and Roger Ebert gave it three out of four stars.

title: Kung Fu Panda
tagline: Prepare for awesomeness.
overview: When the Valley of Peace is threatened, lazy Po the panda discovers his destiny as the "chosen one" and trains to become a kung fu hero, but transforming the unsleek slacker into a brave warrior won't be easy. It's up to Master Shifu and the Furious Five -- Tigress, Crane, Mantis, Viper and Monkey -- to give it a try.
plot:
Kung Fu Panda is a 2008 computer-animated action comedy film produced by DreamWorks Animation. The movie follows the story of Po, a lazy and overweight panda who dreams of becoming a kung fu master.

The film begins with Po (voiced by Jack Black) living in the Valley of Peace, a serene and idyllic valley inhabited by various animals. Po is a food enthusiast and spends most of his days eating and lounging around. However, his life takes an unexpected turn when he is unexpectedly chosen by Master Oogway (voiced by Randall Duk Kim), a wise old tortoise, to be the Dragon Warrior.

According to legend, the Dragon Warrior is destined to bring balance to the Valley of Peace and defeat the evil snow leopard, Tai Lung. Po is initially hesitant and uninterested in taking on the challenge, but Master Oogway convinces him that he has what it takes to become a kung fu master.

Po begins his training with Master Shifu (voiced by Dustin Hoffman), a strict and demanding kung fu master who teaches him the ways of kung fu. However, Po struggles to keep up with the other students, including Tigress (voiced by Angelina Jolie), Monkey (voiced by Jackie Chan), Viper (voiced by Lucy Liu), and Crane (voiced by David Cross).

As Po's training progresses, he faces numerous challenges and setbacks, including a series of humiliating defeats at the hands of Tai Lung. Despite his struggles, Po perseveres and eventually discovers his own unique kung fu style, which combines humor, wit, and heart.

Meanwhile, Tai Lung escapes from prison and begins to wreak havoc on the Valley of Peace, threatening its inhabitants and destroying its harmony. Po must confront his fears and doubts in order to face Tai Lung and save the valley.

The final battle between Po and Tai Lung is an epic showdown that showcases Po's growth and development as a kung fu master. With the help of his friends and Master Shifu, Po defeats Tai Lung and brings balance back to the Valley of Peace.

Throughout the film, Kung Fu Panda explores themes of identity, perseverance, and self-acceptance. Po's journey is a metaphor for finding one's true purpose and embracing one's uniqueness. The movie also features stunning animation, witty humor, and memorable characters that have become iconic in modern animation.

Overall, Kung Fu Panda is a heartwarming and entertaining film that celebrates the power of friendship, teamwork, and believing in oneself.

title: Pope Joan
overview: A 9th century woman of English extraction born in the German city of Ingelheim disguises herself as a man and rises through the Vatican ranks.
plot:
Pope Joan (German: Die Päpstin) is a 2009 epic historical drama film directed by Sönke Wortmann and produced by Bernd Eichinger, based on Donna Woolfolk Cross's novel about the legendary female pope. It stars Johanna Wokalek as Johanna, David Wenham as her lover, Count Gerold, and John Goodman as Pope Sergius II.

Shortly after Charlemagne's death, Johanna is born in Ingelheim am Rhein, the daughter of a harsh village priest. Studying the Bible behind her father's back, she proves far more gifted than her brother Johannes when the scholar Aesculapius visits, and he tutors her against her father's wishes. When a bishop's messenger comes for her, her father sends Johannes instead, but Johanna runs away, joins her brother and reaches the cathedral school at Dorestad, where a reluctant teacher accepts her. Count Gerold takes her into his household and falls in love with her. While he is away fighting for Lothair I, his jealous wife arranges Johanna's marriage, but Vikings attack during the wedding, killing Johannes. Disguised as a man, Johanna enters the Benedictine monastery at Fulda as Brother Johannes Anglicus. Her father, discovering her identity, dies of a stroke while trying to expose her, and when fever strikes the monastery, an old monk who knows her secret helps her avoid examination before she flees, finding shelter with Arn, whose daughter, Arnalda, she tutors.

Resuming her disguise, Johanna travels to Rome as a physician, cures Sergius II of gout and becomes his doctor and later his nomenclator. When Lothair marches on Rome, a hydraulic device swings the palace door shut as if by divine will, and his soldiers kneel. Gerold, in Lothair's army, recognizes Johanna, and she is torn between her two identities. After Lothair's ally Anastasius has Sergius murdered, the people acclaim Johanna as pope. She rules charitably, helping women and children, and makes Gerold head of the papal army, but she becomes pregnant. Gerold is killed by Anastasius's conspirators during the Easter procession, and Johanna dies in childbirth that day. Anastasius succeeds her but is soon deposed and exiled, and in revenge omits her from his history of the popes. Years later her story is revealed by Bishop Arnaldo, who is really Arnalda.

The film premiered in Berlin on 19 October 2009 and opened in Germany three days later. It reached the Italian box office top ten, but drew Vatican criticism, and the Italian bishops' newspaper Avvenire called it extremely limited in vision.

title: Anger Management
tagline: Feel the Love.
overview: After a small misunderstanding aboard an airplane escalates out of control, timid businessman Dave Buznik is ordered by the court to undergo anger management therapy at the hands of specialist Dr. Buddy Rydell. But when Buddy steps up his aggressive treatment by moving in, Dave goes from mild to wild as the unorthodox treatment wreaks havoc with his life.
plot:
Anger Management is a 2003 American comedy film directed by Peter Segal, starring Adam Sandler as Dave Buznik, a man with anger management issues. The movie follows the story of Dave, who is sentenced to anger management classes after he loses his temper in court.

The film begins with Dave, a successful dentist, getting into an argument with his boss, George (Peter Greene), over a parking spot. This incident lands him in jail, where he meets a fellow inmate, Jack (Joe Viterelli). After being released on bail, Dave is forced to attend anger management classes, which are led by Dr. Buddy Rydell (Jack Nicholson).

Initially, Dave struggles with the classes, as his anger issues make it difficult for him to follow the rules and behave in a calm manner. However, he eventually warms up to Dr. Rydell's unorthodox methods, which include using hypnosis and meditation to manage anger.

As Dave progresses through the program, he begins to develop feelings for his instructor, Dr. Rydell's assistant, Miss Jones (Kate Beckinsale). Meanwhile, Jack becomes a source of support and guidance for Dave, helping him to navigate the challenges of anger management.

Throughout the film, Dave faces various situations that test his newfound skills, including a confrontation with George at work and a run-in with a group of thugs. With the help of Dr. Rydell's classes and Jack's advice, Dave is able to manage his anger and develop healthier coping mechanisms.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Dr. Rydell has ulterior motives for running the anger management program. He is using the classes as a way to gather information on his patients' personal lives, which he can use to blackmail them into doing his bidding.

In the end, Dave discovers Dr. Rydell's true intentions and must find a way to stop him. With the help of Jack and Miss Jones, Dave is able to outsmart Dr. Rydell and bring him to justice.

Overall, Anger Management is a lighthearted comedy that explores themes of anger management, relationships, and personal growth. The film features strong performances from Adam Sandler and Jack Nicholson, as well as supporting turns from Kate Beckinsale and Joe Viterelli.

title: Man on Fire
tagline: Creasy's art is death, and he is about to paint his masterpiece.
overview: Jaded ex-CIA operative John Creasy reluctantly accepts a job as the bodyguard for a 10-year-old girl in Mexico City. They clash at first, but eventually bond, and when she's kidnapped he's consumed by fury and will stop at nothing to save her life.
plot:
Man on Fire is a 2004 action-drama film directed by Tony Scott, starring Denzel Washington as John Creasy, a former CIA operative turned private security contractor. The movie follows the story of a man who forms an unlikely bond with a young girl and must fight to protect her from those who seek to harm her.

title: Chopper
tagline: Never let the truth get in the way of a good yarn.
overview: The true and infamous story of Australia's notorious criminal Mark 'Chopper' Read and his years of crime, interest in violence, drugs and prostitutes.
plot:
Chopper is a 2000 Australian crime drama film written and directed by Andrew Dominik in his feature debut, based on the autobiographical books of the criminal turned author Mark "Chopper" Read. It stars Eric Bana as Read, with Vince Colosimo, Simon Lyndon and Kate Beahan. Read himself suggested Bana for the role after seeing him on the sketch comedy series Full Frontal.

In 1978, Read is an inmate at Pentridge Prison in Victoria, serving a sixteen-and-a-half-year sentence for attempting to abduct a judge in a bid to free his friend Jimmy Loughnan. When a fellow prisoner, Keithy George, warns him not to cross a line in the yard marking the territory of the Painters and Dockers gang, Read crosses it the next day and stabs him repeatedly. The gang puts a $10,000 contract on his life. Read recruits Bluey Barnes and Jimmy to help him wage war on the gang, but Jimmy, wanting no part in the suicidal plan, stabs Read and cuts his own arm to claim self-defense. Read recovers and is moved to a separate cell. When the prison board refuses to transfer him for his safety, he has his ears cut off so that he will be sent to a psychiatric wing, where he finishes his sentence.

Released, Read reunites with his girlfriend, Tanya. At a nightclub he flies into a jealous rage and fires a handgun, and when he later catches Tanya on the phone with Neville Bartos, played by Colosimo, he beats both her and her mother. Learning that Neville is a wealthy supplier of amphetamines to Melbourne's western suburbs, Read demands money and shoots him in the stomach when he refuses. He then visits Jimmy, who lives with his pregnant fiancée, Mandy, and their young daughter, claims that the police have given him a green light to shoot criminals, and confronts Jimmy at gunpoint about the contracts on his life before apologizing and giving him money. In the Bojangles car park, an associate called Sammy the Turk says he wants to show Read something, and after an argument, Read shoots him in the eye with a sawn-off shotgun. Mandy, who witnessed the killing, becomes a Crown witness. It emerges that Sammy had been leading Read into a trap for Jimmy to collect the contract but chose the wrong car park. Read is acquitted of murder but convicted of wounding Neville and sentenced to five years.

The film opened at number one in Australia in August 2000. It grossed A$5.9 million locally and received positive reviews, with critics singling out Bana's performance; it has since gained a cult following.

title: A Prairie Home Companion
tagline: Radio like you've never seen it before.
overview: A look at what goes on backstage during the last broadcast of America's most celebrated radio show, where singing cowboys Dusty and Lefty, a country music siren, and a host of others hold court.
plot:
A Prairie Home Companion is a 2006 American musical comedy film directed by Robert Altman, his final film before his death later that year. Written by Garrison Keillor, it presents a fictional behind-the-scenes look at the long-running public radio variety show of the same name, which Keillor created and hosted. The ensemble cast includes Woody Harrelson, Tommy Lee Jones, Keillor himself, Kevin Kline, Lindsay Lohan, Virginia Madsen, John C. Reilly, Maya Rudolph, Meryl Streep and Lily Tomlin.

In Saint Paul, Minnesota, the cast and crew of A Prairie Home Companion gather at the historic Fitzgerald Theater for what turns out to be the show's final broadcast, although the listening audience does not know it. A Texas corporation has bought the radio station and plans to demolish the theater, and it has sent a representative known only as "the Axeman" to oversee the closure. The story unfolds in real time over the course of the evening, as the live show proceeds between songs, comic sketches and fake commercials while the performers mingle backstage.

The evening is watched over by Guy Noir, a bumbling private detective turned security man, a character taken from a recurring segment of the real show. Among the performers are the singing Johnson sisters, Yolanda and Rhonda, who reminisce about their family's days on the gospel circuit, and Yolanda's moody daughter Lola, who writes poems about suicide; the bawdy singing cowboys Dusty and Lefty; and an aging country singer, Chuck Akers. Keillor, known as GK, calmly refuses to acknowledge that this is the last show. A mysterious woman in a white trench coat drifts through the theater; she is revealed to be the spirit of a listener who died in a car accident while laughing at a joke on the program, and who has returned as an angel to bring comfort and to escort someone away. The film reflects gently on mortality, tradition and the passing of an old-fashioned form of entertainment.

The film received mostly positive reviews and was a moderate box-office success on a small budget. Critics praised its relaxed, affectionate mood, its musical performances, which the actors sang themselves, and the ensemble, especially Streep and Tomlin. Because Altman died a few months after its release, many reviewers came to see its meditation on endings as a fitting farewell from the director.

plot:
Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time is a 2010 action fantasy film directed by Mike Newell from a screenplay by Boaz Yakin, Doug Miro and Carlo Bernard, based on a story by Jordan Mechner, creator of the Prince of Persia video game series. Adapted from the 2003 Ubisoft game of the same name, with elements from its sequels Warrior Within and The Two Thrones, it stars Jake Gyllenhaal, Ben Kingsley, Gemma Arterton and Alfred Molina.

Dastan, a Persian street urchin, is adopted by King Sharaman after showing courage. Fifteen years later, the king's brother Nizam presents the princes, Dastan and the king's sons Tus and Garsiv, with evidence that the holy city of Alamut is forging weapons for Persia's enemies, and Tus leads an attack. During the assault, Dastan takes a sacred dagger from a guard. Princess Tamina of Alamut denies that her city makes weapons and agrees to marry Tus only after seeing the dagger in Dastan's hands. At the victory banquet, a robe Dastan presents to the king turns out to be poisoned, killing Sharaman, and Dastan is accused of murder. He escapes with Tamina and discovers that the dagger lets its wielder turn back time.

Hoping to clear his name, Dastan reaches Nizam, sees burns on his hands and realizes that he poisoned the king. Nizam sends the Hassansins, secret assassins, after the dagger. Tamina explains that the gods once sent a sandstorm to destroy humanity but, moved by a girl's offer of sacrifice, sealed the Sands of Time in a giant sandglass that the dagger can pierce, and that Nizam means to go back to his youth, let Sharaman die in a lion attack and claim the throne. With the help of the opportunistic Sheik Amar, Dastan and Tamina head to a sanctuary to seal the dagger, but Garsiv is killed in an ambush and the dagger is lost. Dastan recovers it in Alamut and convinces Tus of the truth before Nizam kills Tus and seizes it. Beneath the city, Tamina sacrifices herself so that Dastan can fight on, and as Nizam plunges the dagger into the sandglass, Dastan grips it with him, rewinding time to the moment he first found the dagger. He exposes Nizam, who is killed by Tus. Tus proposes a marriage between Tamina and Dastan to unite the two nations.

Released by Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures in May 2010, the film grossed over $336 million on a budget of $150–200 million, then the highest-grossing video game film. Critics were mixed, with 36% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 50.

plot:
Tears of the Sun is a 2003 American war drama film directed by Antoine Fuqua and starring Bruce Willis, Monica Bellucci, and Dennis Quaid. The movie follows a team of Navy SEALs on a mission to rescue a group of women who are being held captive in Nigeria.

The story begins with Lieutenant A.K. Waters (Bruce Willis), the leader of an elite Navy SEAL team, who is tasked by the President of the United States to lead a team of operatives into Nigeria to rescue a group of American aid workers who have been kidnapped by a ruthless warlord named General Medu (Oscar Isaac). The aid workers, including Dr. Lena Kendricks (Monica Bellucci), are being held captive in a remote village and are subjected to brutal treatment.

As the SEAL team, which includes Lieutenant Waters' second-in-command, Chief Mike Banning (Dennis Quaid), and other operatives, infiltrate Nigeria, they face numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, enemy soldiers, and local villagers who are hostile towards them. The team also encounters a group of Nigerian rebels who are fighting against the corrupt government.

Upon arrival at the village, the SEALs discover that the aid workers have been subjected to brutal treatment by General Medu's men, including being forced to undergo female genital mutilation. The SEALs launch a daring rescue mission, using their skills and training to take down the enemy soldiers and free the aid workers.

As the team fights to complete their mission, they also begin to form bonds with the aid workers, who are struggling to cope with their ordeal. Dr. Kendricks, in particular, forms a close relationship with Lieutenant Waters, which adds an emotional depth to the story.

The movie's climax features an intense and action-packed battle between the SEALs and General Medu's men, as well as a dramatic confrontation between Lieutenant Waters and the warlord himself. In the end, the SEALs successfully complete their mission, rescuing the aid workers and killing General Medu in the process.

Throughout the movie, Fuqua uses stunning cinematography to capture the beauty of Nigeria's landscapes and the brutality of its conflicts. The film also features a powerful score by James Horner, which adds to the emotional impact of the story.

Overall, Tears of the Sun is a gripping and intense war drama that explores themes of courage, sacrifice, and redemption. While it received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, the movie has since become a cult classic and is widely regarded as one of Bruce Willis' best performances.

title: A Guy Thing
tagline: Boy meets girl. Boy meets girl's cousin.
overview: Paul Morse is a good guy. When his friends throw him a wild bachelor party, he just wants to keep his conscience clean -- which is why he's shocked when he wakes up in bed with a beautiful girl named Becky and can't remember the night before. Desperate to keep his fiancée, Karen, from finding out what may or may not be the truth, he tells her a teensy lie. Soon his lies are spiraling out of control and his life is a series of comical misunderstandings.
plot:
Paul Morse and Karen Cooper are about to get married in Seattle. During his bachelor party, Paul has a chat with one of the dancers at the party, Becky Jackson, and they find that they have an affinity for each other. Paul wakes up the next morning and is terrified to see Becky in the bed next to him.
Assuming they slept together, Paul rushes Becky out of his apartment and hopes never to see her again. He tries to cover up the connection for the remaining six days before the wedding. Unfortunately, Becky unexpectedly shows up around town and turns out to be Karen's cousin. Even worse, Becky's malicious ex-boyfriend, police detective Ray Donovan, had Becky followed and photographed. Becky and Paul meet again to steal those pictures from Ray's apartment.
Further problems arise with family and friends consistently showing up at the wrong times. Genital crabs, dirty underwear in the toilet tank, a horny best friend, and a best man/brother who is in love with the bride all provide for a week of wedding preparation hijinks. Through the snowballing of all his implausible lies and half-truths, Paul receives corroboration and support from an unexpected corner; what seems to be a coordinated network of other men, including friends, complete strangers and, to Paul's astonishment, Karen's own father; all who give the same explanation: "It's a guy thing".

title: Open Water 2: Adrift
tagline: Fatigue. Hypothermia. Death.
overview: A weekend cruise on a luxurious party yacht goes horribly wrong for a group of old high-school friends when they get stuck in the water many miles from shore and a happy reunion turns into a fight for survival.
plot:
Open Water 2: Adrift, also known simply as Adrift, is a 2006 German English-language survival thriller directed by Hans Horn. Susan May Pratt, Richard Speight Jr., Niklaus Lange, Ali Hillis, Cameron Richardson and Eric Dane star as a group of friends stranded in the open sea. Marketed as the second entry in the Open Water series, it is not a direct sequel to the 2003 film, and it was inspired by the short story "Adrift" by the Japanese author Koji Suzuki, from which it took its original title. Lionsgate released it on DVD in the United States in February 2007.

Dan, a wealthy man who has just bought a new yacht, invites his old school friends for a weekend cruise. Among them are Amy and her husband James, who bring their infant daughter Sarah, along with Zach, Lauren and Dan's new girlfriend Michelle. Amy has been terrified of water ever since her father drowned while swimming with her when she was a child, and she refuses to remove her life jacket even on deck.

Far out at sea, most of the friends jump into the water for a swim, while Amy stays aboard with the baby. As a joke, Dan scoops Amy up and leaps overboard with her, ignoring her screams. Only then does the group realise that no one has lowered the boarding ladder. The hull is too high and smooth to climb, and the baby is left alone on deck. The friends try every idea they can think of to get back aboard, including tying their swimsuits together into a makeshift rope, while their strength slowly fades. A passing boat full of teenagers mistakes their frantic waving for a friendly greeting and sails away, and a mobile phone ringing in clothes hanging over the deck remains frustratingly out of reach. As the hours pass, exhaustion, panic and old resentments turn the friends against one another, with fatal consequences.

The film builds its tension around a simple, plausible premise, with almost all of the action taking place in the water beside the yacht. Amy's phobia gives the story its emotional core, as she must overcome her fear in order to save her daughter.

The film received mixed reviews, holding an approval rating of about 45 percent on Rotten Tomatoes; critics praised its claustrophobic premise and some of the performances, but found the characters unsympathetic and their decisions frustrating. It was later released on Blu-ray in 2010 as a double feature with the original Open Water.

title: Big Momma's House
tagline: This FBI agent is going undercover... and he's concealing more than a weapon.
overview: When a street-smart FBI agent is sent to Georgia to protect a beautiful single mother and her son from an escaped convict, he is forced to impersonate a crass Southern granny known as Big Momma in order to remain incognito.
plot:
Big Momma's House is a comedy film released in 2000, directed by Raja Gosnell and produced by 20th Century Fox. The movie stars Martin Lawrence as Malcolm Turner, a former FBI agent who goes undercover to infiltrate a group of thieves.

The story begins with Malcolm Turner (Martin Lawrence), a tough and skilled FBI agent who is tasked with taking down a group of professional thieves known as the "Big Momma's Gang." The gang is led by a mysterious woman named Big Momma, whose true identity remains unknown. Malcolm is given a disguise - that of an elderly woman named Mama Leona - to infiltrate the gang and gather evidence against them.

As Mama Leona, Malcolm must navigate his new life as an elderly woman, complete with a wig, glasses, and a cane. He struggles to adjust to his new persona, but eventually becomes more confident in his disguise. Meanwhile, he befriends the gang members, including Frankie (Paul Satterfield), who becomes his unlikely ally.

As Malcolm gains the trust of the gang, he discovers that Big Momma is not just any ordinary thief, but a mastermind with a complex plan to steal millions of dollars from a wealthy businessman. The gang's leader, Big Momma, has a personal vendetta against the businessman and will stop at nothing to get what she wants.

As Malcolm delves deeper into the gang's operations, he must balance his undercover work with his growing feelings for Frankie's sister, Sherry (Jessica Lundy). However, his cover is threatened when one of the gang members discovers his true identity as a man.

In the end, Malcolm and Big Momma engage in an epic battle of wits, with Malcolm using his FBI training to outsmart her. The movie culminates in a thrilling showdown between Malcolm and Big Momma, resulting in the downfall of the gang and the exposure of their nefarious plans.

Throughout the movie, Martin Lawrence delivers a hilarious performance as the bumbling but lovable Mama Leona, bringing humor and charm to the film's lighthearted moments. The chemistry between Malcolm and Frankie adds an extra layer of comedy to the story, making Big Momma's House a fun and entertaining ride from start to finish.

Overall, Big Momma's House is a classic comedy film that showcases Martin Lawrence's comedic talents and provides plenty of laughs along the way.

title: Metropolis
tagline: Welcome to Metropolis
overview: Kenichi and his detective uncle, Shunsaku Ban, leave Japan to visit Metropolis, in search of the criminal, Dr. Laughton. However, when they finally find Dr. Laughton, Kenichi and Shunsaku find themselves seperated and plunged into the middle of a larger conspiracy. While Shunsaku searches for his nephew and explanations, Kenichi tries to protect Tima (a mysterious young girl), from Duke Red and his adopted son Rock, both of whom have very different reasons for wanting to find her.
plot:
Metropolis (Japanese: Metoroporisu) is a 2001 Japanese animated cyberpunk drama film loosely based on Osamu Tezuka's 1949 manga of the same name. It was directed by Rintaro from a screenplay by Katsuhiro Otomo and produced by Madhouse, with conceptual support from Tezuka Productions. The Japanese voice cast includes Kei Kobayashi, Yuka Imoto, Kōki Okada, Tarō Ishida and Kōsei Tomita.

In the vast, plutocratic city of Metropolis, humans live alongside robots built to construct and maintain it, but the city's impoverished citizens, forced into its squalid lower levels, resent the machines and blame them for their unemployment. Duke Red, the city's richest and most powerful man, celebrates the completion of the Ziggurat, a colossal skyscraper housing military and scientific facilities. His adopted son Rock leads the Marduks, a paramilitary group that hunts down rogue robots. Meanwhile, the Japanese detective Shunsaku Ban and his young nephew Kenichi arrive in Metropolis to arrest Dr. Laughton, a scientist wanted for organ trafficking. Unknown to them, Red has secretly hired Laughton to build an extraordinarily advanced android, modeled on and named after his late daughter, Tima, who is to serve as the central control unit of a superweapon hidden atop the Ziggurat that will allow him to dominate the world. Jealous of the android, Rock shoots Laughton and sets his laboratory on fire. In the chaos Kenichi finds the newly awakened Tima, and the two fall into the city's sewers, separated from Shunsaku. As they make their way through the lower city, Kenichi protects Tima, who does not know that she is a robot, and the two grow close as her humanity develops. Their journey brings them into contact with a human resistance movement planning a revolution, while political intrigue, a ruthless military commander and the obsessed Rock all close in on them, and Tima's true nature and purpose threaten to bring catastrophe to the city.

Metropolis received highly positive reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes it has an 87% approval rating based on 67 reviews, with a consensus that its eye-popping visuals more than compensate for its relatively routine story, and Metacritic assigned it a score of 75 out of 100. Roger Ebert of the Chicago Sun-Times gave it four out of four stars, calling it one of the best animated films he had ever seen.

title: Spider
tagline: The only thing worse than losing your mind... is finding it again.
overview: A mentally disturbed man takes residence in a halfway house. His mind gradually slips back into the realm created by his illness, where he replays a key part of his childhood.
plot:
Spider is a 2002 psychological thriller produced and directed by David Cronenberg, based on Patrick McGrath's 1990 novel of the same name, which McGrath adapted for the screen himself. Ralph Fiennes stars as a mentally ill man haunted by his childhood, with Miranda Richardson, Gabriel Byrne, Lynn Redgrave and John Neville. The film premiered in competition at the 2002 Cannes Film Festival and received only a small release at the end of the year through Sony Pictures Classics, but it was highly praised by critics.

Dennis Cleg, known since childhood as "Spider", is a schizophrenic man who has just been discharged from a psychiatric institution after many years. He is placed in a grim halfway house in London's East End for people with mental illness, run by the stern landlady Mrs. Wilkinson. Scribbling in an illegible script in a notebook, Spider wanders the derelict streets, gasworks and canal of the neighbourhood where he grew up and pieces together his memories of a fateful period of his childhood in the 1950s.

In these memories, which he watches as a silent adult onlooker, young Spider lives with his loving mother and his father Bill, a plumber who drinks in the local pub. Bill begins an affair with Yvonne, a coarse local prostitute, and in the boy's recollection the two lovers murder his mother with a spade one night and bury her in an allotment. Yvonne then moves into the family home and takes the dead woman's place, presenting herself as Spider's new mother to the boy's horror.

In the present, Spider's grip on reality weakens. He begins to see Mrs. Wilkinson's face turn into Yvonne's, stretches webs of string across his room, and steals the landlady's keys to sneak into rooms of the house. His memories move towards a second death: the young Spider rigs a contraption of string to turn on the gas in the kitchen while Yvonne sleeps. But when the body is carried out, it is his mother lying there. The truth emerges that there was never any murder by his father and no Yvonne in the house: the boy, consumed by delusion, killed his own mother and recast her as a stranger.

Late one night the adult Spider creeps into Mrs. Wilkinson's room, still seeing her alternately as Yvonne, but he stops when she wakes and becomes herself again. She reports him, and he is taken back to the asylum.

Spider has 85% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 83, and Cronenberg won the Genie Award for Best Director. Fiennes and Richardson were widely praised.

plot:
In Oro Valley, Arizona, high school troublemaker Sean Boswell races classmate Clay in their respective cars, a 1971 Chevy Monte Carlo and a 2003 Dodge Viper SRT-10, where they end up ramming each other with Clay crashing his Viper into a cylinder pipe and Sean winning the race and wrecking his Monte Carlo. While Clay's family wealth helps him escape punishment, Sean is sent to live with his father, a U.S. Navy lieutenant stationed in Tokyo, to avoid jail time, as he is a repeat offender.
Sean befriends military brat Twinkie, who introduces him to drift racing. Driving to an underground car meet in Twinkie's 2005 Hulk-themed Volkswagen Touran, Sean gets into a confrontation with Takashi, the "Drift King" (DK), over Takashi's girlfriend Neela. Sean agrees to race Takashi's Nissan 350Z in a Nissan Silvia S15 lent to him by retired drift racer Han Lue, only to lose and severely damage the Silvia due to his unfamiliarity with drifting. To repay the debt, Sean agrees to work for Han.
Han begins teaching drifting to Sean, whom he mentions as the only person ever to stand up to Takashi, due to his uncle, Kamata, being a member of the yakuza. Sean masters the art, practicing in a 2003 Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution VIII, and gains further respect after defeating Takashi's lieutenant, Morimoto. Han and Sean become friends.
Sean eventually asks Neela out on a date; Neela explains that after her mother died, she moved in with Takashi's grandmother. An irate Takashi assaults Sean the next day, telling him to stay away from Neela. Neela leaves Takashi and moves in with Sean and Han.
After Kamata reprimands Takashi for allowing Han to steal from him, Takashi and Morimoto confront Han, Sean, and Neela. Takashi threatens Han with a gun, and Han, Sean and Neela flee after Twinkie creates a distraction. Takashi and Morimoto pursue the trio, with Morimoto crashing and dying, and Han buying Sean and Neela time to escape. The chase ends when Sean and Neela's Evo crashes, while Han's 1994 Mazda RX-7 Veilside is T-boned by a 1992 Mercedes-Benz W140 and then explodes, killing him. Takashi later draws a gun on Sean, but his father draws on Takashi; the standoff ends when Neela agrees to leave with Takashi. Sean and his father make amends, while Twinkie gives money to Sean to compensate Kamata for the stolen funds. Sean delivers the cash to Kamata and challenges Takashi to a drift, with the loser leaving Tokyo. Kamata agrees, with Takashi's condition they downhill-drift a mountain pass that only he has descended successfully. Sean and Han's crew restore a 1967 Ford Mustang Fastback that Sean's father recovered and tune it to drift specifications, making use of the engine and other components from the wrecked S15.
On the mountain, Takashi initially leads, but Sean's practice and training allow him to catch up. Desperate, Takashi rams Sean repeatedly.

title: The Order
tagline: Every soul has its price.
overview: For centuries, a secret Order of priests has existed within the Church. A renegade priest, Father Alex Bernier, is sent to Rome to investigate the mysterious death of one of the Order's most revered members. Following a series of strangely similar killings, Bernier launches an investigation that forces him to confront unimaginable evil.
plot:
The Order, also released as The Sin Eater, is a 2003 supernatural mystery thriller written and directed by Brian Helgeland. It reunites the director with Heath Ledger, Mark Addy and Shannyn Sossamon, whom he had directed in A Knight's Tale (2001), alongside Benno Fürmann and Peter Weller. The story follows a young priest investigating a suspicious death in Rome who uncovers a sin eater, a figure able to absolve sins outside the Church's authority.

Father Alex Bernier, a disillusioned member of the Carolingians, a fictional order devoted to exorcism and fighting demonic forces, learns that the order's head, Father Dominic, has died mysteriously in Rome. Cardinal Driscoll, an influential Vatican figure and candidate for the papacy, sends him to investigate. Before he leaves, he is visited by Mara Williams, an artist he once tried to exorcise, who had attacked him during the rite and been committed to an asylum; she senses he is in danger, and he lets her come along. Examining Dominic's body, Alex recognises marks left by a sin eater. With his fellow Carolingian Thomas Garrett, he secretly buries Dominic, who was excommunicated and denied consecrated ground. Driscoll gives Alex an ancient dagger and a fragment of parchment bearing an Aramaic incantation, which Alex takes to be a means of destroying the sin eater. Seeking answers, Alex and Thomas are led to the mysterious Black Pope of an underground sect, and a riddle from a dying man brings Alex to the sin eater himself, William Eden, at St. Peter's Basilica, while Thomas is hurt by demons. The weary, centuries-old Eden wants Alex to succeed him, but Alex refuses, intending to leave the priesthood for Mara. Eden then fatally wounds Mara, disguising it as a suicide attempt, and Alex eats her sins so she can reach heaven. Thomas discovers that Driscoll is the Black Pope and that the full text reveals the dagger rite transfers the sin eater's power. Too late to warn him, he arrives after Alex has stabbed Eden and inherited the role. Dominic, Eden and Driscoll had all used him. Alex exposes Driscoll, refuses to absolve him when the ruined cardinal attempts suicide, and resolves to grant salvation only to those he judges worthy.

Ledger plays Alex, with Sossamon as Mara, Fürmann as Eden, Addy as Thomas and Weller as Driscoll. 20th Century Fox released it on September 5, 2003. Critics panned it, giving it 10% on Rotten Tomatoes, with Rolling Stone's Peter Travers dismissing it as "The Exorcist warmed over".

title: Dante's Peak
tagline: The pressure is building...
overview: Volcanologist Harry Dalton comes to the sleepy town of Dante's Peak to investigate the recent rumblings of the dormant volcano the burg is named for. Before long, his worst fears are realized when a massive eruption hits, and immediately, Harry, the mayor and the townspeople find themselves fighting for their lives amid a catastrophic nightmare.
plot:
Dante's Peak is a 1997 American disaster film directed by Roger Donaldson and starring Pierce Brosnan, Linda Hamilton, and Jamie Renée Smith.

The movie begins with Dr. Harry Dalton (Pierce Brosnan), a volcanologist who has spent his life studying volcanic eruptions. He is married to Dr. Kate McCord (Linda Hamilton), a geologist, and they have a young daughter named Nicki (Jamie Renée Smith). The family lives in the small town of Dante's Peak, which is located near an active volcano.

As the story unfolds, Harry becomes increasingly obsessed with his work, neglecting his family life. Kate, on the other hand, tries to balance her career and family responsibilities. title: Elizabethtown
tagline: It's a heck of a place to find yourself
overview: Drew Baylor is fired after causing his shoe company to lose hundreds of millions of dollars. To make matters worse, he's also dumped by his girlfriend. On the verge of ending it all, Drew gets a new lease on life when he returns to his family's small Kentucky hometown after his father dies. Along the way, he meets a flight attendant with whom he falls in love.
plot:
Drew Baylor is a shoe designer for Mercury, a global sportswear company. When his latest shoe, meant to be his great life accomplishment, is found to have a flaw, it costs the company $972 million, and Drew is shamed by his boss, Phil, before he is asked to speak to the press—his future unknown and likely finished at Mercury.
Disappointed in his failure, and the subsequent breakup with his fair-weather office girlfriend, Ellen, Drew stacks his expensive clothes and other valuables on the street for scavengers to take, then prepares to end his life. He stops at the last moment to answer a persistent phone caller, who turns out to be his sister, Heather, telling him that his father, Mitch, has died while visiting family in Elizabethtown, Kentucky. When his mother, Hollie, refuses to go because of a long-time dispute between her and the Kentucky Baylors, who are bitter about Hollie and Mitch moving to the West Coast, Drew volunteers to retrieve his father's remains and plans to go through with the suicide upon his return.
On the flight to Kentucky, Drew meets flight attendant Claire, who is managing the almost completely empty 747. To make her shift easier, she strikes up a conversation with Drew and invites him to move up to first-class seating. Depressed about his work failure, he tries to ignore the bubbly, quirky Claire who has nothing to do on the flight except talk to him incessantly about Kentucky and alludes to her boyfriend, "Ben", who is a workaholic. At the end of the trip, Claire gives him a paper with directions, helpful tips, and her phone number to help him get to his destination before they part. Drew dismisses Claire, who seems to be trying to get the last of his attentions as he seeks the airport exit.
Arriving at Elizabethtown, Drew is met by the family. He makes arrangements for cremation at his mother's request, despite the family's objections. While staying at a hotel, where a raucous bachelor party and wedding reception is being held, Drew calls his mother and sister, then his ex, Ellen, as he struggles with boredom and depression. Finally, he calls Claire, who is also alone because Ben is away working, and they talk for hours. She impulsively suggests they meet at sunrise, before she has to depart on a flight to Hawaii. They have a quiet, platonic moment, and then they part ways as she leaves for her trip.
Drew struggles between the family members and his mother's demands regarding burial arrangements. His mother is manically attempting self-improvement to compensate for the loss of her husband. Claire suddenly appears at the hotel, claiming Drew's needs for help outweigh her needs for a tropical vacation. They tour various parts of Kentucky and she helps him at the funeral home, picking out the urn and keeping Drew emotionally on track.
During a post-dinner discussion with the older family, Drew sees the stovetop flame and panics about the cremation. Rushing to the funeral home, he is too late to stop his father's cremation.

The story begins with Fred Jones (Freddie Prinze Jr.), Daphne Blake (Sarah Michelle Gellar), Velma Dinkley (Linda Cardellini), Shaggy Rogers (Matthew Lillard), and Scooby-Doo (voiced by Neil Fanning) arriving at the Coolsville High School, where they plan to spend their summer vacation. The gang decides to solve the mystery of the haunting, which leads them to uncover a sinister plot involving a rival businessman, Emile Mondavarious (Tim Blake Nelson), who seeks to buy out the school's founder, Mr. Coolidge (John Mahoney). As they dig deeper, they discover that Mondavarious is using his wealth and influence to scare people away from the school, in order to drive down its value.

Throughout their investigation, the gang encounters various supernatural entities, including ghosts, monsters, and a mysterious curse. However, as they progress, it becomes clear that these events are being manipulated by Mondavarious's accomplices, who are using special effects and disguises to create the illusion of paranormal activity.

As the mystery unfolds, Shaggy and Scooby-Doo become increasingly entangled in the plot, often providing comedic relief with their antics. Meanwhile, Velma uses her intelligence and research skills to uncover the truth behind the haunting, while Daphne and Fred work together to gather evidence and expose Mondavarious's scheme.

In the end, the gang discovers that Mondavarious is using a combination of special effects, disguises, and manipulation to create the illusion of paranormal activity. They also learn that he has been trying to buy out the school in order to build a new shopping mall on its site.

With the truth revealed, the gang exposes Mondavarious's scheme, and he is brought to justice. The movie ends with the gang being hailed as heroes for solving the mystery, and they all share a laugh together as Scooby-Doo enjoys his favorite food, Scooby Snacks.

Overall, Scooby-Doo (2002) is a fun and lighthearted take on the classic cartoon series, with plenty of humor, action, and adventure. The movie stays true to the spirit of the original series while also introducing new characters and plot twists to keep things fresh.

The crew of a modern-day salvage ship, led by Captain Peter Cullen (played by Julián Sands), discovers the long-lost Avalon while searching for treasure in the North Sea. They start experiencing bizarre occurrences, such as hearing eerie whispers, finding cryptic messages scrawled on walls, and encountering ghostly apparitions. As the story unfolds, it becomes apparent that the ship was involved in a tragic accident 30 years ago, resulting in the loss of all hands on board. The crew soon discovers that they are not alone on the ship and that the ghosts of the dead sailors are trying to communicate with them.

As the crew delves deeper into the mystery, they realize that the ship was carrying a cargo of gold and other valuable treasures when it set sail on its ill-fated voyage. The ghosts, however, are not just seeking revenge but also trying to warn the living about the dangers of the sea.

The climax of the film takes place in the ship's engine room, where the crew discovers a hidden logbook belonging to the ship's captain. As they read through the entries, they learn that the captain had made a pact with a mysterious figure to ensure the safe passage of his crew, but at a terrible cost.

Overall, Ghost Ship is a tense and atmospheric horror film that explores themes of tragedy, loss, and the supernatural. While it may not be as well-known as some other horror films, it has developed a cult following over the years for its creepy atmosphere and eerie plot twists.

title: The Italian Job
tagline: Get in. Get out. Get even.
overview: Charlie Croker pulled off the crime of a lifetime. The one thing that he didn't plan on was being double-crossed. Along with a drop-dead gorgeous safecracker, Croker and his team take off to re-steal the loot and end up in a pulse-pounding, pedal-to-the-metal chase that careens up, down, above and below the streets of Los Angeles.
plot:
Professional safecracker John Bridger's team has plans to steal $35 million worth of gold bars from a safe in Venice from Italian gangsters who had stolen it weeks earlier. Professional fixer Charlie Croker, computer expert Lyle or "Napster", wheelman Handsome Rob, explosives expert Left Ear, and inside man Steve comprise the team. Although the heist is successful, Steve double-crosses them as they drive towards Austria with the bullion; with another crew, he takes it for himself and kills John. Rob drives the van over the bridge into the water to protect the others, using air tanks from the heist to stay alive. Steve leaves them for dead.
A year later in Philadelphia, Charlie finds Steve, under a new identity, laundering the gold through Ukrainian jeweler Yevhen to finance his lavish lifestyle in Los Angeles. Charlie gathers the team, and also recruits John's daughter Stella, a skilled private safecracker, offering her the chance to avenge her father's death. They stake out Steve's mansion, and Stella, disguised as a cable technician, maps out its interior and determines the location of Steve's safe containing the bullion. Unaware of Stella's identity, Steve asks her out on a date. The plan is to blow the safe while Steve is away on his supposed date, using three heavily modified Mini Coopers to transport the gold out of the mansion. Supplier Skinny Pete gets the explosives and mechanic Wrench modifies the cars.
On Steve's last visit to Yevhen, Yevhen accidentally reveals that he knows about the Venice heist, and Steve shoots him dead to cover his tracks. Mashkov, the leader of a Ukrainian crime family and Yevhen's cousin, traces the gold back to Skinny Pete via Yevhen's ex-employee Vance.
On the night of the planned heist, the crew discovers that Steve's neighbors are having a party, forcing them to abort as the explosives would draw attention. Stella meets Steve anyway, but inadvertently gives away her identity by using her dad's catchphrase. The team arrives to protect her, and Steve taunts them as he says he still has the upper hand.
Aware that Charlie intends to steal it back, Steve decides to move the gold to Mexico City. His plan, which involves transporting the gold via armored car from his L.A. home to a private plane at LAX, is overheard by Napster using a phone tap. Charlie and his gang make a new plan to steal the gold en route to the airport by hijacking the city's traffic control system to force the armored car to a planned spot where they will execute the heist.
On the day, they are surprised when three armored trucks leave Steve's mansion, but Napster determines which one carries the bullion and manipulates the traffic accordingly. As Steve is monitoring the transport by helicopter, they maneuver the truck to the target spot and detonate explosives to drop the part of the road with the truck into the subway tunnel below. Opening the truck, they find the gold in a different safe from the one Stella saw earlier.

Throughout the movie, Viola's disguise leads to various comedic situations, including her attempts to navigate male-dominated spaces and her struggles with her own identity. As she navigates her relationships and personal growth, Viola learns valuable lessons about love, friendship, and self-acceptance.

In the end, Viola's true identity is revealed, but not before she has formed strong bonds with Duke and the rest of the Illyria Prep community. title: Flyboys

overview: The adventures of the Lafayette Escadrille, young Americans who volunteered for the French military before the U.S. entered World War I, and became the country's first fighter pilots.
plot:
In 1916, a group of Americans arrive in France to serve in the French Air Service, L'Aéronautique militaire, in World War I. They are placed under the command of Captain Georges Thenault, with veteran flying ace Reed Cassidy as their mentor.
Pilot Blaine Rawlings runs out of fuel on a practice flight and crashes. He meets a young woman named Lucienne and the two develop a relationship. During their first mission – escorting bombers to attack a German ammunition depot in Jametz – they are ambushed by German warplanes, and two of the rookies are killed. A third makes an emergency landing but is killed on the ground by "the Black Falcon" – a German pilot flying a black aircraft. The chivalrous German pilot Franz Wolferd shakes his head in disapproval.
In a later battle, Rawlings' machine gun jams while he is chasing Wolferd. Wolferd flies alongside and salutes before banking away. Higgins is killed in the battle, and Jensen suffers an emotional breakdown and is unable to fly again. The French military learns that Beagle fabricated personal information and accused him of being a spy. He admits to a crime he committed in the United States, and is allowed to stay on. The American pilots intercept Germans warplanes attacking a column of civilians. Rawlings kills Wolferd when he attacks another American pilot. Beagle is brought down in no man's land, and is trapped by the wreckage. Rawlings lands and attempts to free him with help from French soldiers but is forced to amputate Beagle's hand. Learning that German forces have entered Lucienne's village, Rawlings attempts to rescue her in a stolen plane. Lucienne is wounded during their escape, and Rawlings is awarded the Croix de Guerre for bravery by his grateful commander.
Porter is killed attacking a German Zeppelin and Cassidy, mortally wounded by the Black Falcon, flies into the zeppelin, destroying it. Rawlings reunites with Lucienne, is promotoed to Squadron Leader, and his plane is presented with an eagle, which had been Cassidy's insignia. Escorting another bombing run on the Jametz ammunition depot, Lowry's plane catches fire and he shoots himself. Rawlings fights through several enemy planes, shooting them down until only the Black Falcon remains. After a long dogfight, the wounded Rawlings comes alongside and shoots the Black Falcon dead with his pistol.
Jensen returns to Nebraska to a hero's welcome at the end of the war. Skinner enlists in the US Army but is kept from flying due to his race; he later joins the Airmail Service. Beagle marries an Italian woman and starts a flying circus. Rawlings tries to find Lucienne in Paris but returns to Texas alone, becomes a rancher, and never flies again.

title: The Jacket
tagline: Terror has a new name.
overview: A military veteran goes on a journey into the future, where he can foresee his death and is left with questions that could save his life and those he loves.
plot:
The Jacket is a 2005 American science fiction psychological thriller film directed by John Maybury and starring Adrien Brody, Keira Knightley, Kris Kristofferson and Jennifer Jason Leigh. Partly based on Jack London's 1915 novel The Star Rover, published in Britain as The Jacket, it was written by Massy Tadjedin from a story by Tom Bleecker and Marc Rocco, with music by Brian Eno and cinematography by Peter Deming.

Gulf War veteran Jack Starks survives a seemingly fatal bullet wound to the head and returns to Vermont in 1992 suffering from bouts of amnesia. On a roadside he helps a young girl, Jackie, and her alcoholic mother start their broken-down truck, giving Jackie his dog tags. Soon afterward he accepts a ride from a stranger, and the car is stopped by a policeman; Starks is later found by the road beside the officer's body. Unable to remember clearly, he is found not guilty by reason of insanity and committed to a mental institution, where the harsh Dr. Thomas Becker and the kinder Dr. Beth Lorenson oversee his care. Becker subjects him to an unauthorized treatment: he is drugged, bound in a straitjacket and shut inside a morgue drawer.

In this state Starks finds himself transported fifteen years into the future, where he meets an adult Jackie working at a diner. She takes him in for the night, but when he finds his own dog tags in her apartment, she tells him that Jack Starks died on New Year's Day 1993. On later journeys he gains her trust, and together they try to change his fate. Lorenson, meanwhile, risks her career to treat a friend's troubled son. Convinced at last by Starks's knowledge of the future, Lorenson takes him on January 1, 1993, to the home of Jackie and her mother, where he leaves a letter warning the mother that she will die after falling asleep with a lit cigarette, leaving Jackie orphaned. Back at the hospital, Starks slips on ice and hits his head, and bleeding badly, he persuades sympathetic staff to put him in the jacket once more. In 2007 he finds that his letter has transformed Jackie's life: she is now a cheerful nurse, and as she drives him to her hospital, her mother, alive and well, telephones.

The Jacket premiered at the 2005 Sundance Film Festival and was released by Warner Independent Pictures on March 4, 2005, grossing $21.1 million on a $28.5 million budget. Reviews were mixed, with 44% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, which called it creepy style over substance.

title: Ringu 0
original_title: リング０　バースデイ
tagline: Discover the secret...
overview: Taking place thirty years before the events of Ringu, Ringu 0 provides the shocking background story of how the girl on the video became a deadly, vengeful spirit.
plot:
In the present, a girl confesses to her friend that she watched the cursed videotape. She also recounts having nightmares, including seeing Sadako's murder by Dr. Ikuma.
30 years prior, Miyaji, the fiancé of a fellow reporter who was killed during Shizuko's infamous ESP demonstration, interviews Shizuko's daughter Sadako's former elementary school teacher Sudo, about Sadako's nensha powers. Sudo recounts how Sadako was withdrawn as a child and predicted her classmates drowning in the ocean during a field trip. Meanwhile, 19-year-old Sadako joins an acting troupe as an understudy. Her natural charisma infuriates the lead actress, Aiko, whose relationship with the troupe director, Shigemori, sours due to the latter's newfound favor for Sadako. Aiko is later found dead, having been haunted by a figure in white, so Sadako takes her place. Sadako and troupe sound director Hiroshi Toyama are attracted to each other, much to the disappointment of costume designer Etsuko Tachihara, who harbours feelings for Toyama. While praised by Shigemori and Toyama, the other troupe members grow to distrust and fear Sadako, as they suspect that she is the one who caused Aiko's death and other supernatural occurrences, including an apparition of a girl in white with long hair similar to Sadako's.
Miyaji is told by Sudo that Shizuko descended into madness before her suicide, ever since moving to live with Dr. Heihachiro Ikuma, and that Sudo heard strange childlike noises in the attic. Etsuko, wanting to discover Sadako's origins, contacts Sadako's psychiatrist, but he refuses to answer and throws away Sadako's troupe's poster; the poster is taken by Miyaji's assistant, allowing him and Miyaji to locate Sadako in the troupe. When they start photographing her, she telekinetically breaks the camera; the two discover that all the photographs contain ghostly faces and a girl with long hair, confirming Miyaji's suspicion of "two" Sadakos. Shigemori, obsessed with Sadako, says he will kill her first if she tries to kill him, and proceeds to strangle her. Toyama interrupts, and Shigemori is killed through a blow that also wounds Toyama. Sadako heals him just by touching him; later, she helps a disabled man regain his ability to walk. After finishing their last play, the two confess their love and promise to leave the troupe and live together.
The play is a disaster as Sadako, influenced by recordings of her mother's demonstration played by Etsuko, sees visions of her mother during the demonstration and kills her psychiatrist. The troupe members, discovering Shigemori's body, corner her and beat her to death. Pursuing the "second" Sadako, they visit Ikuma at his home, who tells them that Sadako split into two beings resembling each of her parents; the malevolent one, who resembles her unknown father, is kept from growing by Ikuma in the attic. Before they can kill it, both Sadakos merge and escape with Toyama.

title: Gone in Sixty Seconds
tagline: Ice Cold, Hot Wired.
overview: Upon learning that he has to come out of retirement to steal 50 cars in one night to save his brother Kip's life, former car thief Randall "Memphis" Raines enlists help from a few "boost happy" pals to accomplish a seemingly impossible feat. plot:
Gone in Sixty Seconds is a 2000 American action heist film directed by Dominic Sena and produced by Jerry Bruckheimer Films. The movie stars Nicolas Cage, Angelina Jolie, and Robert Duvall.

The story begins with Randall "Memphis" Raines (Nicolas Cage), a former car thief who has retired from the business after a stint in prison. Memphis is haunted by his past and struggles to connect with his estranged daughter, Sara (Amber Valletta). He's also being pursued by a ruthless crime lord named Earl (Christopher Eccleston).

One day, Memphis receives an offer from a wealthy collector, Julian (Robert Duvall), who wants him to steal 50 high-performance cars within 60 days. The catch is that the cars are all highly valuable and extremely difficult to steal. Memphis agrees to take on the challenge, but only if he can do it with his old crew.

Memphis reunites with his former partner, Bobby (Angus Macfadyen), and together they assemble a team of skilled thieves, including Sara's boyfriend, Ben (Benjamin Bratt). The team includes a mechanic, a safe-cracker, and an expert in car customization. As the deadline approaches, tensions rise within the group, and Memphis must navigate his complicated relationships with his crew members.

As the heist unfolds, Memphis and his team face numerous obstacles, including rival thieves, corrupt police officers, and treacherous terrain. The stakes are raised when Memphis discovers that one of the cars is a rare 1967 Shelby Cobra, which holds sentimental value for him.

Throughout the film, Nicolas Cage delivers an energetic performance as the charismatic but troubled Memphis. His character's backstory is gradually revealed through flashbacks, showcasing his rise to fame as a car thief and his subsequent fall from grace.

The movie's climax features an intense car chase sequence, where Memphis and his team must outrun their pursuers while navigating the streets of Los Angeles. The film concludes with a dramatic showdown between Memphis and Earl, which ultimately leads to the redemption of Memphis' character.

Overall, Gone in Sixty Seconds is an action-packed thrill ride with a talented cast and impressive car stunts. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the movie has developed a cult following over the years, thanks to its memorable characters, witty dialogue, and high-octane action sequences.

title: Pulse
tagline: You are now infected.
overview: When their computer hacker friend accidentally channels a mysterious wireless signal, a group of co-eds rally to stop a terrifying evil from taking over the world.
plot:
When Josh Ockmann enters a dark university library hoping to find a man named Douglas Ziegler, he is attacked by a humanoid spirit that sucks the life force out of him. Some days later, Josh's girlfriend, Mattie Webber, visits his apartment, seeing evidence that it has not been well kept. Josh tells Mattie to wait in the kitchen while he walks off. While waiting, she finds Josh's pet cat locked in a closet and dying from severe malnutrition. But when she rushes to tell him, she finds that he has committed suicide by hanging himself with an Internet cable.
Mattie and her friends begin to receive online messages from Josh asking for help but assume that Josh's computer is still on and that a virus is creating the messages. Mattie learns that Josh's computer has been sold to Dex McCarthy, who finds several strange videos on the computer. Mattie receives a package that Josh mailed two days before his death. Inside are rolls of red tape and a message telling her that the tape keeps "them" out, although he does not know why. Later, Dex visits Mattie and shows her video messages that Josh was sending to Ziegler. Josh had hacked Ziegler's computer system and then distributed a virus. This virus had unlocked a portal that connected the realm of the living to the realm of the dead. Josh believed he had coded a counter to the virus and wanted to meet Ziegler at the library. Josh's counter-program is found on a memory stick taped inside the PC case with red tape.
Dex and Mattie visit Ziegler and find his room plastered in red tape. They believe that the red tape keeps the spirits out. Ziegler tells them of a project he worked on where he found "frequencies no one knew existed". Opening these frequencies somehow allowed the spirits to travel to the world of the living. Ziegler also tells them that these spirits "take away your will to live" and where to find the main server infected with the virus.
Dex and Mattie find the server and upload Josh's fix, causing the system to crash and the spirits to vanish. Moments later, the system reboots and the spirits return, leaving Mattie and Dex with no option but to flee the city by car. Over the car radio, Mattie and Dex hear a report from the Army announcing the location of several "safe zones" with no Internet connections, cell phones or televisions. As Dex and Mattie are driving to a safe zone, a voice-over from Mattie is heard saying, "We can never go back. The cities are theirs. Our lives are different now. What was meant to connect us instead connected us to forces that we could have never imagined. The world we knew is gone but the will to live never dies. Not for us and not for them". The film closes by showing various clips of abandoned cities, which include a window of an apartment with Josh looking through it.
