title: Keeping Mum
tagline: Some family secrets are best kept...buried.
overview: A pastor preoccupied with writing the perfect sermon fails to realize that his wife is having an affair and his children are up to no good.
plot:
Keeping Mum is a 2005 British black comedy directed by Niall Johnson, who co-wrote the screenplay. Rowan Atkinson stars as a distracted village vicar, with Kristin Scott Thomas as his frustrated wife, Maggie Smith as their new housekeeper and Patrick Swayze as an American golf instructor. Entertainment Film Distributors released it in the United Kingdom on December 2, 2005.

The film opens decades earlier, when a young pregnant woman named Rosie Jones boards a train with a large trunk that begins leaking blood. Inside are the bodies of her unfaithful husband and his lover. Found guilty of manslaughter on grounds of diminished responsibility, she is committed to an institution for the criminally insane.

Forty-three years later, in the sleepy village of Little Wallop, the Reverend Walter Goodfellow is so absorbed in writing the perfect sermon for an upcoming church convention that he fails to notice his family falling apart. His neglected wife, Gloria, has begun an affair with her lecherous golf instructor, Lance; their teenage daughter, Holly, goes through boyfriends at an alarming rate; and their young son, Petey, is tormented by bullies at school. Into this household comes Grace Hawkins, a sweet, elderly new housekeeper. Grace quietly sets about solving the family's problems in her own lethal way. She disposes of a neighbor's constantly barking dog, and its owner, sabotages the bullies' bicycles and dispatches Lance, hiding the bodies in the vicarage pond. She also gently helps Walter reconnect with his wife, suggesting he add humor to his sermons and pointing out the romance in the Song of Solomon.

As harmony seems to return, Walter leaves for his convention. Gloria and Holly then see a news report about the release of an elderly woman convicted of murder and realize that Grace is Rosie Jones, Gloria's long-lost mother. Gloria insists that you cannot simply kill people who cause you problems, a point on which, Grace admits, she and her doctors never agreed. The women resolve to keep the secret from Walter and Petey. After an interfering parishioner dies of shock during a misunderstanding, Grace slips away from the family. When two workmen inform Walter that the pond must be drained, Gloria smiles tightly and offers them tea, and a final shot reveals their bodies in the pond alongside the others.

Reviews were mixed; Rotten Tomatoes' consensus praised its strong cast but found the black comedy uneven, and Metacritic gave it 53 out of 100.

title: Children of Men
tagline: The future's a thing of the past.
overview: In 2027, in a chaotic world in which humans can no longer procreate, a former activist agrees to help transport a miraculously pregnant woman to a sanctuary at sea, where her child's birth may help scientists save the future of humankind.
plot:
In 2027, total human infertility has led to wars and global depression, pushing civilization to the brink of collapse as humanity faces extinction. The UK has transformed into a totalitarian police state in which asylum seekers are arrested and put in camps. Daily life is full of bombings, rationing, decay and propaganda. The populace mourns as they hear the news that the youngest person alive in the world is killed at age eighteen.
Theo Faron, a former activist turned cynical, depressed bureaucrat, is kidnapped by the Fishes, a militant refugee rights group led by Theo's estranged wife, Julian Taylor. The pair separated after their son's death in 2008. Julian offers Theo money to acquire transit papers from his cousin, the Minister of Arts, for a young refugee woman named Kee. Theo visits his cousin inside an elite mini-city within London where the powerful enjoy all the pleasures of the past. Theo obtains joint transit papers from his cousin, then tells Julian that he is willing to escort Kee himself in exchange for more money. Luke, a Fishes member, drives Theo, Kee, Julian, and Miriam (Kee's associate) towards Canterbury, but they are ambushed and Julian is killed. After the rest escape, Luke kills two police officers that stop them.
At a farm safe house, Kee reveals to Theo that she is pregnant, making her the only known pregnant woman in the world. Julian intended to take her to the Human Project, a secret scientific research group in the Azores dedicated to curing humanity's infertility. That night, Theo eavesdrops and learns that Luke and other Fishes orchestrated Julian's death, while also intending to kill Theo and use Kee's baby as their political tool. Theo orchestrates an escape for himself, Kee, and Miriam (revealed to be Kee's midwife) to the secluded hideaway of Jasper Palmer, a bohemian, old friend of Theo.
The group plans to reach the Human Project ship, the Tomorrow, that Julian had scheduled to arrive offshore at Bexhill, a notorious refugee detention centre. Jasper arranges for Syd, an immigration officer to whom Jasper sells cannabis, to smuggle them into Bexhill as refugees, from where they can take a rowboat and rendezvous with the ship. The next day, the Fishes arrive at Jasper's hidden entrance, forcing the group to flee. Jasper stays behind to stall them and is murdered by Luke. At an abandoned school, Syd meets Theo, Kee, and Miriam, and helps them board a bus to the camp where Kee's water breaks; Miriam feigns mental illness as a distraction and is dragged off the bus.
In Bexhill, their contact Marichka, a Romani woman, provides Theo and Kee a room, where Theo helps Kee give birth. The next day, Syd arrives to tell them that fighting has broken out between the military and refugees, and that the Fishes have infiltrated the camp. He reveals that Theo and Kee have a bounty on their heads and attempts to capture them. Marichka and Theo fight off Syd, and the group takes shelter with a kindly, elderly Russian couple.

title: One Missed Call
tagline: Death cannot be put on hold...
overview: People mysteriously start receiving voicemail messages from their future selves, in the form of the sound of them reacting to their own violent deaths, along with the exact date and time of their future death, listed on the message log. The plot thickens as the surviving characters pursue the answers to this mystery which could save their lives.
plot:
While out at a mixer with friends, Yoko Okazaki misses a call on her cell phone, playing a peculiar ringtone different from her usual one, and notices the caller ID says it came from her own number. She and her friend Yumi Nakamura listen to the message left on the phone, dated two days into the future, and hear Yoko's voice say that it's starting to rain, followed by a horrendous scream. Two days later, Yumi gets a call from Yoko and realizes that Yoko is saying the words they heard in the voice mail. Yoko screams as she is violently thrown off an overpass onto a speeding train. Her severed hand is then seen dialing a number. Although authorities assume suicide, her schoolmates recall similar deaths that were preceded by voicemails. Yoko's new boyfriend Kenji Kawai tells Yumi he got a voicemail from himself dated two days later, with a timestamp two minutes from now. As Yumi looks on, Kenji is inexplicably pulled down an elevator shaft. As he bleeds to death on the bottom, a red jawbreaker falls out of his mouth as his phone dials another number by itself.
A nervous Yumi invites her friend Natsumi Konishi to stay with her. Yumi turns both of their cell phones off, but Natsumi still receives a call from her own number and receives a photo instead of a voice mail, showing herself with a shadowy figure behind her. The media picks up on the story and offers Natsumi a chance to be exorcised on live TV. Despite Yumi's protests, Natsumi anxiously agrees.
Yumi meets Hiroshi Yamashita, a detective who has been investigating the curse that also claimed the life of his sister Ritsuko. Yamashita shares that the next victim is called one minute after the previous death, and victims are found with red jawbreakers in their mouths. Their investigation leads them to a hospital which has since changed its building and number. Yumi recognizes a sound she heard before Kenji's death as the spraying of an asthma inhaler. They trace the autopsy records to a girl named Mimiko Mizunuma who died from an asthma attack and whose mother Marie went missing. Ritsuko's journal shows that whenever Mimiko had an attack, her sister Nanako would suffer some injury at the same time. They suspect that Marie had Munchausen syndrome by proxy and harmed her own children for attention.
The night of Natsumi's exorcism goes horribly wrong. Yumi and Yamashita barge into the studio to see the exorcist be violently blown back by an invisible force and Natsumi die after her limbs are contorted at impossible angles, after which a jawbreaker drops out of her mouth, and a cursed voicemail arrives for Yumi. When Yamashita escorts her home and encourages her to stay with her family, she reveals to Yamashita that her mother abused her as a child.
At an orphanage, Yamashita meets Nanako, who will not speak but has a teddy bear that plays the same melody as the ringtone from the calls to the victims. Yumi goes to the abandoned hospital alone and encounters the spirit of Mimiko.

title: Lady in the Water
tagline: Time is running out for a happy ending.
overview: Apartment building superintendent Cleveland Heep rescues what he thinks is a young woman from the pool he maintains. When he discovers that she is actually a character from a bedtime story who is trying to make the journey back to her home, he works with his tenants to protect his new friend from the creatures that are determined to keep her in our world.
plot:
Lady in the Water is a 2006 American fantasy film directed by M. Night Shyamalan. The movie follows the story of Cleveland Heep, a quiet and unassuming apartment dweller who discovers a mysterious pool in his building's basement that seems to be inhabited by a mythical creature known as the "Lady in the Water." As Cleveland delves deeper into the mystery, he uncovers a complex web of secrets and lies that threaten to upend his mundane life.

At its core, Lady in the Water is a film about the human desire for connection and meaning. The movie explores themes of loneliness, isolation, and the search for transcendence in a seemingly ordinary world. Cleveland's encounter with the Lady in the Water serves as a catalyst for him to re-examine his own life and relationships, forcing him to confront the emptiness and disconnection that can accompany modern urban living.

The film also touches on the idea of mythology and its role in shaping our understanding of ourselves and the world around us. The Lady in the Water is a symbol of something greater than oneself, representing a longing for magic, wonder, and connection with the unknown. Through Cleveland's journey, Shyamalan invites the audience to consider the ways in which we often seek to escape or transcend our mundane lives through fantasy, mythology, or other forms of escapism.

title: Spiral
overview: A young pathologist seeks answers to the mysterious death of a friend and soon comes into contact with the same cursed videotape that caused the death of the friend's wife and son, which is haunted by the curse of Sadako, a relentless spirit.
plot:
Spiral (Japanese: らせん, Hepburn: Rasen) is a 1998 Japanese supernatural horror film directed by George Iida and based on Koji Suzuki's 1995 novel of the same name. It was conceived as the sequel to Hideo Nakata's Ring (1998), and the two films were released in Japan simultaneously as a double feature, in the hope that the popularity of Suzuki's novel and an earlier television adaptation would boost box-office returns. Koichi Sato stars as the pathologist Mitsuo Andō, with Miki Nakatani, Hinako Saeki as Sadako Yamamura, Shingo Tsurumi and Shigemitsu Ogi. It was released in North America as Rasen and in several other territories as The Spiral.

Following the events of Ring, the body of Ryūji Takayama, the former husband of journalist Reiko Asakawa, is examined by his old friend and rival, the pathologist Mitsuo Andō, who is grieving the drowning death of his own young son. During the autopsy Andō finds a cryptic numerical message in Ryūji's body. Soon afterward, Reiko and her son Yōichi are found dead in a car crash, and Andō learns about a cursed videotape that is said to kill anyone who watches it exactly one week later.

With the help of Mai Takano, Ryūji's student and girlfriend, Andō investigates Ryūji's death and the story of Sadako Yamamura, the young woman with psychic powers whose spirit appears to haunt the tape. Scientific analysis suggests that the deaths are caused by a mysterious virus resembling smallpox, and Andō tries to understand why some victims die while others survive. Despondent and believing that his rival's ghost is guiding him, Andō eventually watches the video himself. Strange events multiply around him, and he discovers that the curse is spreading in new ways and that Sadako has a far more ambitious plan than mere revenge, one that offers Andō a temptation connected to his own grief and threatens to change the world.

Spiral was overshadowed by Ring, which became a major hit and spawned an international franchise, and it was poorly received by audiences who expected a conventional ghost story rather than a medical mystery. The continuity of the series was later revised with Ring 2 (1999), which ignored Spiral's events. Retrospective assessments have been more generous: Den of Geek called it neither as poor as its reputation suggests nor a lost gem, while Collider described it as a gonzo sequel that should not be forgotten.

title: The Wicker Man
tagline: Some sacrifices must be made
overview: A sheriff investigating the disappearance of a young girl from a small island discovers there's a larger mystery to solve among the island's secretive, neo-pagan community.
plot:
The Wicker Man is a 2006 folk horror film written and directed by Neil LaBute, a remake and reimagining of the 1973 British film of the same name that also draws very loosely on David Pinner's 1967 novel Ritual. Nicolas Cage stars as police officer Edward Malus. Made for $40 million, it was filmed in British Columbia, Canada, mostly on Bowen Island, in the summer of 2005. Warner Bros. Pictures released the film in the United States and Canada on September 1, 2006.

Edward hears from his former fiancée, Willow Woodward, that her daughter, Rowan, has gone missing, and travels to the island in Puget Sound, off the coast of Washington, home to a community of neo-pagans. They are led by Sister Summersisle, an elderly woman who embodies the goddess they worship and who explains that her ancestors fled persecution in England, only to face it again in the Salem witch trials before settling on the island. The community is mostly female and lives off its honey, whose production has recently declined. The islanders deflect Edward's questions about Rowan. He sees two men carrying a bag that seems to drip blood, digs up a fresh grave that holds only a burned doll and finds Rowan's sweater in the churchyard. At the school, Sister Rose tries to hide the register, in which Rowan's name has been crossed out, and when Edward demands to know how Rowan died, she says "She'll burn to death" before correcting herself to the past tense. Willow then admits that Rowan is Edward's daughter.

On the day of the fertility rite, Edward disguises himself in a bear suit to join the procession and finds Rowan tied to a tree, ready to be burned. He frees her and they flee into the woods, but Rowan leads him straight back to Sister Summersisle. Edward realizes the search was a trap from the start: Willow, Summersisle's daughter, had chosen him as a human sacrifice to restore the honey harvest. The islanders shut him inside a giant wicker man, and Rowan sets it alight. Six months later, Willow and Sister Honey approach two police officers in a Seattle bar and go home with them.

Ellen Burstyn plays Sister Summersisle, with Kate Beahan as Willow, Molly Parker as Sister Rose and Leelee Sobieski as Sister Honey. The film earned a rare F CinemaScore and 15% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and received five Golden Raspberry nominations, though Paul Sarossy's cinematography won a Canadian Society of Cinematographers award. It grossed $38.8 million.

title: 7 Seconds
tagline: Timing is everything.
overview: When an experienced thief accidentally makes off with a Van Gogh, his partner is kidnapped by gangsters in pursuit of the painting, forcing the criminal to hatch a rescue plan.
plot:
7 Seconds is a 2005 crime action thriller directed by Simon Fellows and released direct to DVD. Wesley Snipes stars as Jack Tulliver, a professional thief and former special forces soldier, with Tamzin Outhwaite as the military police sergeant Kelly Anders, Georgina Rylance as Suza, Pete Lee-Wilson as the Russian gangster Alexei Kutchinov, Deobia Oparei as Spanky, and Serge Soric as Mikhail Mercea. The title refers to the seven-second timers seen in the film's opening heist.

Jack leads a crew in a meticulously planned robbery of an armored convoy in Bucharest, a job that should net each member around $3 million. But a rival gang shows up at the same moment, tipped off by a traitor within the operation, and the ambush leaves most of his team dead, among them his partner Frank "Bull" Mercea. Jack escapes with the most valuable piece of the loot, a mysterious sealed case, and makes a getaway through the city by hijacking Anders's car, leaving the sergeant under suspicion from her own colleagues.

The case turns out to hold a Van Gogh painting, which Jack hides in a locker at a bus station as a bargaining chip. One of his crew has been taken hostage by the gang's boss, Kutchinov, a sadistic Russian millionaire who controls the Romanian racketeers behind the ambush and wants the painting. Determined to rescue his colleague, Jack reluctantly joins forces with Anders, and the pair become entangled in a web of shifting loyalties, double-crosses and car chases through Bucharest's streets and nightclubs, as Jack tries to work out who betrayed him. In the end they are saved by Bull's brother Mikhail, a Romanian mobster who avenges his brother by shooting Kutchinov and the traitor, Suza. Afterward Jack and Anders discover that the painting, long thought to be a forgery, is in fact genuine and extremely valuable.

The film was shot over 32 days in the summer of 2004 in Bucharest and at Castel Film Studios in Romania, and Sony Pictures Home Entertainment released it on DVD in the United States on 28 June 2005 and in Britain that September. It was a commercial failure, and critics were largely dismissive. Reviewers found the plot confusing and the script sloppy, though some praised a few energetic car chases and fight scenes and felt Snipes's engaging performance kept it watchable.

plot:
Fantastic Four is a 2005 superhero film based on the Marvel Comics team created by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby. Directed by Tim Story and written by Mark Frost and Michael France, it stars Ioan Gruffudd as Reed Richards, Jessica Alba as Susan Storm, Chris Evans as Johnny Storm, Michael Chiklis as Ben Grimm and Julian McMahon as Victor von Doom, with Kerry Washington. It tells the origin story of the team, who must learn to live with the extraordinary abilities they gain after being exposed to cosmic rays in space. It was the second live-action Fantastic Four film to be produced, after an unreleased version produced by Roger Corman.

Scientist Reed Richards and his friend Ben Grimm persuade Victor von Doom, the head of Von Doom Industries, to give them access to his space station so that Reed can study the effects of a cosmic energy cloud on living samples. Victor brings along his chief geneticist, Susan Storm, who is Reed's former girlfriend, and her reckless brother Johnny. The cloud arrives ahead of schedule, and while Reed, Susan and Johnny rush to help Ben, who is outside on a spacewalk, Victor seals himself behind the station's shields. The storm strikes them all. Back on Earth, the four develop strange powers: Reed can stretch his body like rubber, Susan can turn invisible and project force fields, Johnny can engulf himself in fire, and Ben is transformed into a massive, rock-skinned creature of tremendous strength. After they use their abilities to avert a disaster on the Brooklyn Bridge, the media dubs them the Fantastic Four. Johnny revels in the fame, but Ben is devastated when his fiancée leaves him, and Reed vows to find a cure. Working from his laboratory in the Baxter Building, Reed tries to build a machine that can reverse the changes, while Victor, ruined by the mission's failure and blaming Reed, discovers that the storm has also changed him, turning his body into living metal able to generate electricity. title: Demolition Man
tagline: The future isn't big enough for the both of them.
overview: Simon Phoenix, a violent criminal cryogenically frozen in 1996, escapes during a parole hearing in 2032 in the utopia of San Angeles. Police are incapable of dealing with his violent ways and turn to his captor, who had also been cryogenically frozen after being wrongfully accused of killing 30 innocent people while apprehending Phoenix.
plot:
Demolition Man is a science fiction action film directed by Marco Brambilla, released in 1993 by Warner Bros. Pictures.

In the year 2032, the United States has become a utopia where crime and violence have been eradicated through advanced technology and social engineering. The city of San Angeles is a marvel of efficiency and order, with everything controlled and monitored by the government. John Spartan (Sylvester Stallone), a tough and experienced cop, is tasked with stopping a notorious terrorist named Simon Phoenix (Wesley Snipes).

However, just as Spartan is about to apprehend Phoenix, he is cryogenically frozen for 30 years after being mortally wounded in the line of duty. When Spartan is thawed out in 2064, he finds that the world has changed dramatically. The city is now a futuristic metropolis with flying cars and robots, but also a society where people are more complacent and less willing to take risks.

Spartan soon discovers that Phoenix has been thawed out as well and is now a free agent, wreaking havoc on San Angeles. With the help of Dr. Raymond Cocteau (Sandra Bullock), a brilliant scientist who created the cryogenic freezing technology, Spartan must navigate this new world to stop Phoenix and restore order.

As Spartan tries to adjust to his new surroundings, he clashes with the authorities, particularly the self-absorbed and arrogant Chief John Kilbourne ( Nigel Hawthorne). Meanwhile, Cocteau becomes romantically involved with Spartan, but their relationship is complicated by her feelings of guilt over creating a being who was frozen for 30 years.

Throughout the film, Spartan's old-school values and methods are at odds with the new society. He must learn to adapt to this futuristic world and work with Cocteau to stop Phoenix. Along the way, he discovers that Phoenix has a personal vendetta against him and is using his newfound freedom to exact revenge.

The climax of the film features an epic battle between Spartan and Phoenix, with the two former adversaries engaging in a high-tech showdown. In the end, Spartan emerges victorious, but not before realizing that his old ways may be too much for this new world.

Demolition Man received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, but it has since become a cult classic, praised for its witty dialogue and over-the-top action sequences. The film's themes of social commentary and satire are still relevant today, offering a commentary on the dangers of complacency and the importance of individual freedom.

Overall, Demolition Man is an entertaining and visually stunning sci-fi action film that explores the consequences of a utopian society gone wrong.

title: Unbreakable
tagline: Some things are only revealed by accident
overview: An ordinary man makes an extraordinary discovery when a train accident leaves his fellow passengers dead — and him unscathed. The answer to this mystery could lie with the mysterious Elijah Price, a man who suffers from a disease that renders his bones as fragile as glass.
plot:
Unbreakable is a 2000 American superhero thriller written, produced and directed by M. Night Shyamalan. Bruce Willis stars as a man who walks away unhurt from a catastrophic train crash and begins to suspect he has extraordinary powers, with Samuel L. Jackson as the fragile comic-book enthusiast who seeks him out, Robin Wright as his wife and Spencer Treat Clark as his son. Shyamalan structured the story to mirror the three-part arc of a traditional comic book.

In 1961 Philadelphia, Elijah Price is born with broken limbs caused by osteogenesis imperfecta, a disease that makes his bones extremely brittle. Decades later, David Dunn, a former star quarterback now working as a security guard and stuck in an unhappy marriage, is the only survivor of a derailment that kills every other passenger on his train, and he emerges without a scratch.

After a memorial service, David finds a note asking whether he has ever been ill, inviting him to Elijah's comic-art gallery. Elijah lays out his theory that if he lies at one extreme of human fragility, someone must exist at the other who is practically unbreakable. Sceptical, David nonetheless discovers he can lift far more weight than he expected, while his son Joseph becomes convinced his father is a superhero. Elijah suggests that water, which nearly drowned David as a child, is his one weakness, and David admits he faked an injury after a car crash to quit football because his wife Audrey disliked the violence.

With Elijah's encouragement, David comes to see that his instinct for spotting dangerous people is a form of extrasensory perception: by touching strangers he glimpses crimes they have committed. He follows a janitor who has invaded a family's home and holds the children captive, frees them, survives being thrown into a pool and kills the intruder. Renewed, he reconciles with Audrey and quietly shows Joseph a newspaper sketch of the unknown hero.

When David shakes Elijah's hand, he sees that Elijah engineered a series of deadly disasters, including the train crash, in his search for a hero. Embracing the nickname Mr. Glass, Elijah casts himself as the villain, and a closing title reveals that he is committed to a psychiatric institution.

Released on November 22, 2000, the film grossed about $248 million worldwide on a $75 million budget and drew generally positive reviews, holding a 70% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: Firewall
tagline: Nothing Is More Dangerous Than A Man With Everything To Lose.
overview: State-of-the-art security system creator, Jack Stanfield has cemented his reputation as a man who's thought of everything. But when a criminal finds a way into Jack's personal life, everything Jack holds dear is suddenly at stake.
plot:
Firewall is a 2006 American action thriller film directed by Richard Loncraine and starring Harrison Ford, Virginia Madsen, and Karl Urban.

The movie begins with Jack Stanfield (Harrison Ford), a former FBI agent who has retired to a quiet life in the suburbs. He works as an insurance investigator for a company called First National Insurance Company, where he is responsible for investigating claims related to arson and other forms of property damage.

One day, Jack's wife, Kate (Virginia Madsen), is kidnapped by a group of professional thieves who are led by Robert 'The Ghost' Devereaux (Ben Kingsley). The kidnappers demand that First National Insurance Company pay $10 million in exchange for Kate's safe return. They also threaten to kill her if their demands are not met.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Jack is being forced back into action by his former colleagues at the FBI, who believe that he has valuable skills and knowledge that can help them track down The Ghost and his team. However, Jack is reluctant to get involved, as he wants to protect his family and live a peaceful life.

Despite his initial reluctance, Jack agrees to work with the FBI to track down The Ghost and rescue Kate. He uses his expertise to analyze clues and follow leads, which ultimately lead him to a warehouse where The Ghost's team is hiding.

As Jack gets closer to rescuing Kate, he realizes that The Ghost has set a trap for him. The Ghost reveals that he has been playing a cat-and-mouse game with Jack all along, using his knowledge of Jack's past and his skills as an investigator to manipulate him into doing his bidding.

In the end, Jack is able to outsmart The Ghost and rescue Kate. However, not before realizing that The Ghost was actually working for a larger organization that had been manipulating events from behind the scenes. The movie ends with Jack reflecting on the experience and realizing that he has been given a second chance to make things right.

Throughout the movie, Harrison Ford delivers a strong performance as the protagonist, bringing depth and nuance to the character of Jack Stanfield. The supporting cast, including Virginia Madsen and Karl Urban, also deliver solid performances that add to the tension and suspense of the film.

Overall, Firewall is an action-packed thriller that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats from start to finish. With its strong performances, clever plot twists, and tense action sequences, it's a must-see for fans of the genre.

The film begins with Norbit (Eddie Murphy) as a child, living with his mother, Mrs. Johnson (Thandie Newton), and her eccentric boyfriend, Rasputia (Shari Headley). As Norbit grows up, he becomes infatuated with Rasputia, but she treats him poorly and makes him feel like an outcast.

As an adult, Norbit works as a janitor at a nightclub owned by his mother. He is still pining for Rasputia, who has become a successful businesswoman. However, when Rasputia marries the club's owner, Mr. Wong (Rudy Youngblood), Norbit becomes jealous and feels left out.

One day, Norbit meets a beautiful woman named Kate (Meagan Good), who is working at the nightclub. Despite their instant attraction, Norbit is too shy to approach her. Meanwhile, Rasputia continues to treat Norbit poorly, making him feel like an inferior being.

As the story progresses, Norbit's life becomes more complicated when he discovers that Mr. Wong is planning to sell the nightclub and move away. Desperate to save his mother's business, Norbit comes up with a plan to win Rasputia back and prove himself as a worthy partner.

In the end, Norbit's plan succeeds, and he wins Rasputia's heart. However, in a surprising twist, it is revealed that Rasputia has been using her charms to manipulate Norbit all along. Despite this, Norbit realizes that his love for Rasputia was genuine, but he also learns to appreciate himself and find happiness on his own terms.

The movie ends with Norbit and Kate sharing a romantic kiss, while Rasputia is seen walking away alone, having finally realized her true feelings for Norbit. The film concludes on a hopeful note, suggesting that Norbit has found love and acceptance in the end.

Overall, Norbit is a heartwarming story about self-discovery, love, and acceptance. Eddie Murphy's performance as the titular character brings humor and charm to the film, making it an enjoyable watch for audiences of all ages.

Step Up is a 2006 American dance drama film directed by Jon M. Chu and written by Michael Genet. The movie stars Channing Tatum, Jenna Dewan, and Rob Brown.

The story begins with Tyler Gage (Channing Tatum), a troubled teenager who has just moved to Baltimore from Texas after getting into a fight at his previous school. He is forced to attend a local community college, where he meets Nora Walker (Jenna Dewan), the daughter of a dance instructor, and her friends.

Tyler is initially hesitant to join the school's dance team, but after seeing Nora perform, he becomes fascinated with dance and decides to join the group. However, his lack of experience and rough demeanor make him an outcast among the other dancers.

As Tyler spends more time with the dance team, led by Eva (Izabella Mlinarz), he begins to learn the basics of hip-hop dance from Nora's father, Chet Walker (Will Kemp). He also starts to develop feelings for Nora, but their social differences and his troubled past make it difficult for them to connect.

Meanwhile, Tyler's rival, Chase Collins (Rob Brown), is a talented dancer who is also vying for the top spot on the team. The two dancers engage in a series of intense dance battles, both on and off the stage.

As the competition heats up, Tyler finds himself drawn into the world of competitive dance, where he must confront his own demons and learn to work with others towards a common goal. With Nora's support, he begins to master the art of dance and eventually earns the respect of his teammates.

The movie culminates in a high-stakes dance competition at the school's annual Spring Fling event, where Tyler and Chase face off against each other in an epic dance battle. In the end, Tyler emerges victorious, but not without learning valuable lessons about perseverance, teamwork, and the power of dance to bring people together.

Throughout the movie, the film's soundtrack features a mix of hip-hop and pop music that perfectly captures the energy and spirit of the dance team. The choreography is also noteworthy, with many impressive dance sequences that showcase the talents of the cast.

Overall, Step Up is a fun and inspiring movie that celebrates the beauty of dance and the transformative power of art to bring people together. With its talented cast, catchy soundtrack, and high-energy dance sequences, it's no wonder that this movie became a cult classic among fans of dance and music.

title: Goal!
tagline: Every Dream Has A Beginning
overview: Like millions of kids around the world, Santiago harbors the dream of being a professional footballer... However, living in the Barrios section of Los Angeles, he thinks it is only that--a dream. Until one day an extraordinary turn of events has him trying out for Premiership club Newcastle United.
plot:
Goal!, also known as Goal! The Dream Begins, is a 2005 British sports drama film directed by Danny Cannon from a screenplay by Mike Jefferies, Adrian Butchart, Dick Clement and Ian La Frenais. The first installment of the Goal! trilogy, it stars Kuno Becker as Santiago Muñez, an amateur player who gets an unlikely chance at professional football, with Alessandro Nivola, Stephen Dillane and Anna Friel. Made with the cooperation of FIFA, it features real teams and players, and Adidas reportedly contributed $50 million toward its budget and marketing.

Santiago, an undocumented Mexican immigrant in Los Angeles, plays for a local team while working as a gardener with his father, Hernan, and as a busboy. Glen Foy, a former player and scout, spots him and arranges a trial with Newcastle United. Hernan, who doubts his son's prospects, takes Santiago's savings to buy a truck, but his grandmother, Mercedes, secretly gives him the money to go. In Newcastle, Santiago struggles in the mud and under pressure from teammate Hughie McGowan, but manager Erik Dornhelm grants him a month's trial. Fearing rejection, he hides his asthma from the club nurse, Roz Harmison. Before the decisive reserve match, Hughie destroys his inhaler, and after a poor performance Santiago is let go.

On the way to the airport, his taxi picks up Gavin Harris, a talented but undisciplined recent Newcastle signing, who learns about the asthma and tells Erik. Erik keeps Santiago on condition that he receives treatment, and Santiago moves in with Gavin. Coming on as a substitute against Fulham in his first-team debut, he wins a penalty that secures victory, as Hernan watches proudly on television, though Erik scolds him for selfish play. A night out with Gavin lands the pair in The Sun, Santiago's friend Jamie suffers a career-ending injury, and his friendship with Gavin frays. When Hernan dies of a heart attack, Santiago nearly flies home but stays after talking with Roz, with whom he begins a relationship. Picked to start the final game of the season against Liverpool, he sets up Gavin's late equalizer and then scores a free kick to win 3–2, earning Newcastle a Champions League place.

Buena Vista International released Goal! in the United Kingdom on 1 October 2005. Reviews were mixed, with 42% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 53; critics praised the football sequences but found the story full of sports film clichés.

title: Air Force One

plot:
Air Force One is a 1997 American action thriller film directed by Wolfgang Petersen and produced by Jerry Bruckheimer. The movie stars Harrison Ford as President James Marshall, a former Vietnam War hero who becomes the commander-in-chief of the United States.

The story begins with President Marshall's (Harrison Ford) family - his wife, Nancy (Sally Skerritt), and their two children, Sam (Joe Pesci) and Megan (Evelyn Hartt) - on board Air Force One as it takes off from Andrews Air Force Base in Maryland. The plane is headed to a summit meeting with Russian President Kirin (Gary Oldman).

As the plane reaches cruising altitude, a group of heavily armed terrorists, led by the ruthless and cunning Vladimir (Gary Oldman), infiltrate the cockpit and take control of the aircraft. They are seeking to hold the President hostage in exchange for the release of their imprisoned comrades.

The terrorists, who claim to be members of an anti-American organization, begin to make demands, including the withdrawal of U.S. troops from Russia and the recognition of Russian interests around the world. The President, determined to protect his family and the country, refuses to comply with their demands.

As the situation escalates, Air Force One is forced to fly over hostile territory, making it difficult for the President's team to respond effectively. Meanwhile, the terrorists continue to make threats against the passengers and crew, including a threat to kill the children if their demands are not met.

title: The Invisible
tagline: Life, death and something in between.
overview: After an attack leaves him in limbo -- invisible to the living and also near death -- a teenager discovers the only person who might be able help him is his attacker.
plot:
The Invisible is a 2007 American supernatural teen thriller directed by David S. Goyer, a remake of the 2002 Swedish film of the same name and based on the Swedish young-adult novel by Mats Wahl. Justin Chatwin, Margarita Levieva, Chris Marquette, Marcia Gay Harden and Callum Keith Rennie star. It is often cited as the start of the modern wave of Hollywood remakes of Swedish films, and it was the last release under Disney's Hollywood Pictures label.

Nick Powell is a high school senior who secretly plans to skip graduation and go to a writing program in London, defying his emotionally distant, controlling mother Diane. His best friend Pete confides that he is being bullied by Annie Newton, a troubled girl who runs with a gang of violent thieves and whose boyfriend Marcus is on parole. After Annie robs a jewellery store and Marcus tips off the police, she is arrested and decides that Pete informed on her. She beats him until he gives up Nick's name, believing Nick is already on a plane. In fact Nick has given away his ticket. Annie and her gang ambush him on his way home from a party, beat him savagely and, thinking him dead, dump his body in a storm drain in the woods.

The next morning Nick goes to school and finds that no one can see or hear him. As police investigate his disappearance, he realises he is not dead but trapped between life and death while his body lies unconscious, and he desperately tries to reach Pete and Annie to save himself. Under police pressure, Marcus forces Pete to help move the body and plots to kill Annie, while the guilt-stricken Pete attempts suicide. Annie, meanwhile, begins to sense Nick's presence and hear fragments of his voice. Visiting his room, she comes to see how alike they were.

Annie confronts Marcus and Pete to learn where the body has been moved. Marcus tells her but shoots her as she leaves; she shoots him in return and calls the police with Nick's location. Nick is rescued and taken to hospital, where Annie dies of her wounds just as he wakes. Later, Nick and Annie's little brother Victor send a model plane carrying a message to her over the river.

The film was not screened for critics and received generally negative reviews. It grossed about $26.8 million worldwide, $20.6 million of it in North America.

The mutants, led by the deformed and sadistic Papa (Robert Longstreet), begin to stalk and terrorize the family. The mutants are a result of genetic mutations caused by radiation exposure, which has twisted their bodies into grotesque forms. As the family tries to survive, they realize that they are trapped in the valley with no way out.

The plot thickens as the family members start to disappear one by one, and the remaining survivors must fight for their lives against the mutants. The tension builds up as the family is forced to confront their own personal demons and work together to survive.

The Hills Have Eyes received mixed reviews from critics but was a commercial success, grossing over $60 million worldwide. The movie's graphic violence and gore were widely criticized, but it also sparked a debate about the limits of on-screen violence in horror films.

Overall, The Hills Have Eyes is a tense and unsettling horror film that explores themes of family dynamics, trauma, and survival. While it may not be to everyone's taste due to its graphic content, it is a well-crafted movie that will keep you on the edge of your seat until the very end.

title: Turistas
tagline: There are some places tourists should never go
overview: A group of young backpackers' vacation turns sour when a bus accident leaves them marooned in a remote Brazilian rural area that holds an ominous secret.
plot:
Turistas, released in the United Kingdom and Ireland as Paradise Lost, is a 2006 American horror film produced and directed by John Stockwell from a screenplay by Michael Arlen Ross. It stars Josh Duhamel, Melissa George, Olivia Wilde, Desmond Askew, Max Brown and Beau Garrett, with Miguel Lunardi as the surgeon Zamora.

American backpacker Alex is touring Brazil with his sister Bea and her friend Amy. After their bus crashes on a remote road, they team up with two British travelers, Finn and Liam, and Pru, an Australian who speaks Portuguese. The group finds a beach bar full of partying tourists, but after a day in the sun they are drugged and wake up on the empty beach with their money, luggage and passports gone. A young local named Kiko offers to take them to his uncle's house deep in the forest. On the way, he badly injures his head diving into a pool beneath a waterfall. At the isolated house, the travelers find medicine, supplies and a drawer full of other people's passports.

That night, a helicopter brings Zamora, a doctor who arrives with his medical team and armed men. The tourists are beaten and captured, while Kiko escapes. Zamora removes Amy's organs while she is still alive, telling the bound Finn that he is taking back what rich foreigners have taken from Brazil and sending the organs to a hospital in Rio de Janeiro to help the poor. With Kiko's help, the others break out of their cages. Finn is rescued but shot dead as they escape, and Liam stays behind to fight and is captured. The survivors flee through the jungle to an underwater cave, where Zamora kills Kiko and wounds Alex. Separated in the flooded passages, Bea kills an archer working for the gang. When the three survivors come out of the cave, Alex attacks Zamora with a rock, but henchman Jamoru arrives with a rifle. Ordered to kill the tourists, Jamoru instead shoots Zamora and walks away. Villagers take in the survivors. At the airport, Alex advises a pair of arguing tourists to take the plane rather than the bus.

Turistas was the first American film shot entirely in Brazil. It was also the first release from Fox Atomic, a label of 20th Century Fox, which opened it on December 1, 2006. It debuted in eighth place and grossed about $14.7 million worldwide. Critics were largely negative. Rotten Tomatoes' consensus said that beautiful scenery and cinematography could not make up for wooden acting and a stale, predictable plot.

He is married to his wife, Dr. Margaret Dean (Regina King), and they have a young son together. However, their happiness is short-lived as Robert's boss, Franklin Haines (Jon Voight), assigns him to investigate the death of a former colleague.

As the stakes rise, Robert teams up with a computer expert named Kit (Gary Baseman), who helps him understand the extent of The Net's capabilities.

As the story unfolds, Robert discovers that he has been identified as an enemy of the state by the NSA. He learns that his investigation into the death of his colleague was not just a coincidence, but rather a deliberate attempt to expose the agency's wrongdoing. With Kit's help, Robert sets out to take down The Net and bring Agent Gibson to justice.

The plot thickens as Robert and Kit go on the run, using advanced technology to evade the NSA agents. Along the way, they encounter a mysterious woman named Susan (Linda Fiorentino), who becomes entangled in their quest for truth.

As the action unfolds, Robert's personal life begins to unravel. His marriage is put to the test as he struggles to balance his work and family responsibilities with his newfound mission to take down The Net. In a thrilling climax, Robert and Kit face off against Agent Gibson and his team in a high-stakes battle of wits and technology.

In the end, Robert succeeds in destroying The Net and exposing the NSA's wrongdoing. However, not before Agent Gibson reveals that he has been working for a shadowy organization known as "The Syndicate," which is pulling the strings from behind the scenes. As Robert returns to his normal life, he knows that there are still many secrets lurking in the shadows, waiting to be uncovered.

Overall, Enemy of the State is a gripping action thriller that explores themes of government surveillance, corporate greed, and personal freedom. With its breakneck pace and memorable performances, it has become a classic of 90s action cinema.

As the trial progresses, it becomes clear that Courtenay's actions were motivated by fear and prejudice against people with HIV/AIDS. The court ultimately rules in Andrew's favor, awarding him $1.4 million in damages.

In the end, Andrew Beckett emerges victorious, but not without scars. The film concludes on a hopeful note, as Andrew begins to rebuild his life and find a new sense of purpose. The movie's powerful message about the importance of empathy and compassion resonates long after the credits roll.

Overall, Philadelphia is a masterful drama that explores themes of prejudice, identity, and the human condition. With outstanding performances from Tom Hanks and Denzel Washington, this film remains a powerful and thought-provoking classic of American cinema.

overview: Bridget Jones is becoming uncomfortable in her relationship with Mark Darcy. Apart from discovering that he's a conservative voter, she has to deal with a new boss, a strange contractor and the worst vacation of her life.
plot:
Bridget Jones: The Edge of Reason is a romantic comedy of 2004 directed by Beeban Kidron and written by Andrew Davies, Helen Fielding, Richard Curtis and Adam Brooks, based on Fielding's 1999 novel and serving as the sequel to Bridget Jones's Diary (2001). Renée Zellweger returns as Bridget, with Colin Firth as her boyfriend Mark Darcy, Hugh Grant as her former lover Daniel Cleaver, and Jim Broadbent and Gemma Jones as her parents.

Bridget is blissful in her new relationship with Mark, until she meets his young and beautiful assistant, Rebecca Gillies, and her confidence collapses. At work in morning television, she reluctantly agrees to co-host a travel series with Daniel. Hoping for a proposal, she attends a Law Council dinner with Mark that becomes a string of humiliations. After a row, Mark comes to her flat to apologize, tells her for the first time that he loves her and takes her skiing in Lech, Austria, where Rebecca also turns up. A pregnancy scare proves negative.

At a lunch with their parents, Mark's brush-off of questions about marriage wounds Bridget, and when he declines to answer her suspicions about a phone message from Rebecca, she ends the relationship. She heads to Thailand with her friend Shazza and Daniel to film the travel show. After accidentally eating hallucinogenic mushrooms, she grows flirtatious with Daniel again, but the arrival of a prostitute he had ordered convinces her he has not changed. Shazza's young fling, Jed, gives her a decorative snake bowl that ends up in Bridget's luggage, and when airport sniffer dogs find cocaine hidden inside, Bridget is thrown into a crowded cell. She befriends her cellmates, teaching them Madonna's "Like a Virgin". Mark arrives to tell her she will soon be free, but when she lets him believe she slept with Daniel, he coolly leaves.

Back in London, Mark brawls with Daniel in a fountain for abandoning Bridget, and Bridget returns home a minor celebrity. Her friends reveal that Mark personally tracked down Jed and secured the confession that cleared her. Rushing to his house, she finds Rebecca there, but Rebecca confesses that she is attracted to Bridget herself and kisses her; Bridget gently declines. Bridget asks Mark for another chance, and he proposes. At her parents' renewal of their vows, she catches the bouquet.

Shot in London and Austria between October 2003 and February 2004, the film grossed about $265 million worldwide, though critics found it predictable.

title: The Incredibles
tagline: No gut, no glory
overview: Bob Parr has given up his superhero days to log in time as an insurance adjuster and raise his three children with his formerly heroic wife in suburbia. But when he receives a mysterious assignment, it's time to get back into costume.
plot:
The Incredibles is a 2004 animated superhero film produced by Pixar Animation Studios and released by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie follows the story of a family with superpowers, who are forced to hide their abilities and live a normal life.

The film begins with Bob Parr (Mr. Incredible), a former superhero known as Mr. Incredible, who is now a suburban dad living in Municiberg, New Jersey. He works for a company called Supers Inc., which provides superheroes with jobs and benefits. However, Bob's life is not as ordinary as it seems. He longs to return to his superhero days and save the world from evil.

Bob's wife, Helen (Elastigirl), is also a former superhero known as Elastigirl, who has been forced to retire due to her age and the lack of respect for superheroes in society. Their children, Dash and Violet, are also gifted with superpowers - Dash can run at incredible speeds, while Violet can turn invisible and project force fields.

The family's life is disrupted when a mysterious figure named Buddy Pine ( Syndrome) appears, claiming to be a huge fan of Mr. Incredible. However, it soon becomes apparent that Buddy has an ulterior motive - he wants to become a superhero himself and destroy the superheroes who have been deemed "outdated" by society.

Buddy's plan is to use a device called the Omnidroid, which can absorb and neutralize superpowers. The Omnidroid is designed to hunt down and eliminate all superheroes, making it easier for Buddy to become the world's greatest superhero.

As the story unfolds, Bob, Helen, Dash, and Violet must work together to stop Buddy and his Omnidroid. Along the way, they discover that their powers are not just a gift, but also a responsibility. They learn to use their abilities in creative ways to outsmart the villain and save the day.

The climax of the movie features an epic battle between the Parr family and Buddy's Omnidroid. The family uses their unique powers to work together and defeat the robot, saving the city from destruction.

In the end, Bob and Helen are able to reconcile with each other and find a way to balance their superhero lives with their family life. They also learn that being a superhero is not just about having powers, but also about working together as a team and using one's abilities for the greater good.

The Incredibles received widespread critical acclaim for its engaging storyline, memorable characters, and stunning animation. The movie was a commercial success, grossing over $631 million worldwide and spawning two sequels, Incredibles 2 (2018) and a short film, Jack-Jack Attack (2005).

title: Let's Go to Prison
tagline: Welcome to the slammer
overview: When a career criminal's plan for revenge is thwarted by unlikely circumstances, he puts his intended victim's son in his place by putting him in prison...and then joining him.
plot:
Let's Go to Prison is a comedy film that explores the complexities of friendship and loyalty through the lens of two unlikely friends who find themselves in a precarious situation. The movie delves into the theme of camaraderie, as the two main characters, Vince and Nathan, form an unbreakable bond despite their vastly different backgrounds.

As they navigate the challenges of prison life, the film highlights the importance of loyalty and trust in relationships. Through their experiences, the characters learn to rely on each other and support one another, even in the face of adversity. This theme is expertly woven throughout the narrative, adding depth and humor to the story.

The movie also touches on the theme of redemption, as both Vince and Nathan are forced to confront their past mistakes and work towards a better future. Their journey is marked by moments of self-discovery, growth, and ultimately, forgiveness.

Furthermore, Let's Go to Prison pokes fun at the absurdities of the prison system, using satire to critique the harsh realities faced by inmates. The film's lighthearted tone belies its commentary on social issues, making it an entertaining yet thought-provoking watch.

Overall, Let's Go to Prison is a heartwarming and hilarious exploration of friendship, loyalty, and redemption, set against the backdrop of a chaotic prison environment.

title: Goal! II: Living the Dream
tagline: This time the dream is real.
overview: Tempted away from Newcastle United to join Real Madrid, rising star Santiago Munez finds this latest change of fortune the greatest challenge yet - personally as well as professionally. He is reunited with Gavin Harris, though they must compete to be on the team, and estranged from fiancee Roz, whose nursing career keeps her back home.
plot:
Goal II: Living the Dream is a 2007 sports drama directed by Jaume Collet-Serra from a screenplay by Mike Jefferies, Adrian Butchart and Terry Loane. The sequel to Goal! (2005) and the second part of a trilogy, it stars Kuno Becker as the Mexican footballer Santiago Muñez, with Alessandro Nivola, Anna Friel, Stephen Dillane, Leonor Varela, Elizabeth Peña and Rutger Hauer, and features cameo appearances by real Real Madrid players.

Santiago, now a star at Newcastle United, is signed by Real Madrid, where he is reunited with his flamboyant former teammate Gavin Harris. His fiancée, Roz, stays behind in Newcastle to finish her nursing training, and the long-distance relationship soon strains. Santiago makes a winning debut and quickly becomes the club's new star, but fame brings complications. He is approached by Enrique, a younger half-brother he never knew, who shows him a photograph of their mother, Rosa María, who abandoned Santiago as a small child, and he learns that his grandmother knew she was living in Madrid.

Distracted, Santiago is sent off in his first start, and after a drunken night with the television presenter Jordana García he misses the team flight to a Champions League match in Norway, earning the wrath of manager Rudi van der Merwe. He fires his loyal agent Glen Foy, injures his ankle and cancels Christmas plans with Roz, and when a second kiss with Jordana is leaked to the press, Roz breaks off their engagement. Meanwhile Enrique steals Santiago's Lamborghini and crashes it, and Santiago is arrested after taking the blame and assaulting a photographer at the hospital, where he finally sees his mother.

After scoring the goal that sends Madrid into the Champions League final, Santiago visits Rosa, who explains that she fled to Madrid after being attacked, and returned to Mexico to find the family gone to the United States. Reconciled with his mother and Enrique, he asks Rudi to start Gavin in the final against Arsenal to help his friend's career, and apologizes to Roz. Madrid fall behind 2–0, but after coming on, Santiago sets up a goal for Gavin and scores the equalizer, before David Beckham wins the match with a late free kick.

Released in the United Kingdom on February 9, 2007, the film received mixed to negative reviews for its predictable and melodramatic script and grossed only about $7.8 million worldwide, though it later found a cult audience. Goal III followed in 2009.

title: Save the Last Dance
tagline: The Only Person You Need To Be Is Yourself.
overview: After the death of her mother, Sara moves to the South Side of Chicago to live with her father and gets transferred to a majority-black school. Her life takes a turn for the better when befriends Chenille and her brother Derek, who helps her with her dancing skills.
plot:
Save the Last Dance is a 2001 American romantic drama film that explores the complexities of social class, identity, and the struggle for self-discovery. The movie delves into the world of two young women from different backgrounds who find themselves drawn to each other despite their vastly different lifestyles.

The film's narrative revolves around Sara Johnson, a white ballet dancer from a wealthy family in Chicago, who is forced to re-evaluate her life when her mother passes away. She finds solace in hip-hop dance and meets Derek Reynolds, a black teenager from the wrong side of the tracks, at a local club. As they spend more time together, Sara begins to confront the societal expectations placed upon her and the limitations imposed by her privileged upbringing.

Through their relationship, the film sheds light on the tensions between cultural identity and social status. The contrast between Sara's world of elegance and refinement and Derek's gritty reality serves as a backdrop for exploring themes of class struggle, racism, and the search for authenticity. As Sara becomes more immersed in Derek's world, she begins to question her own values and the privileges that have defined her life.

The movie also touches on the theme of self-discovery, as both characters navigate their identities and grapple with the expectations placed upon them by others. Through their relationship, they learn to let go of their preconceptions and find a sense of belonging in each other's worlds.

Ultimately, Save the Last Dance is a poignant exploration of the human experience, one that challenges its viewers to confront the complexities of social class, identity, and the power of love to transcend boundaries.

title: United 93
tagline: September 11, 2001. Four planes were hijacked. Three of them reached their target. This is the story of the fourth.
overview: A real-time account of the events on United Flight 93, one of the planes hijacked on 9/11 that crashed near Shanksville, Pennsylvania when passengers foiled the terrorist plot.
plot:
United 93 is a 2006 docudrama written, produced and directed by Paul Greengrass about United Airlines Flight 93, one of the four planes hijacked during the September 11 attacks and the only one that failed to reach its target, because of the actions of its passengers. Alongside events on board, the film follows government officials and air traffic controllers as they watch the attacks unfold, recreating the hijacking and its aftermath as closely as possible in real time.

On the morning of September 11, 2001, four al-Qaeda hijackers led by Ziad Jarrah pray in a Newark hotel before boarding Flight 93, whose passengers include Tom Burnett, Todd Beamer, Jeremy Glick, Lauren Grandcolas and Mark Bingham. While the flight sits delayed on the ground, controllers lose contact with American Airlines Flight 11, realise it has been hijacked, and then see it and United Airlines Flight 175 strike the twin towers of the World Trade Center.

Once airborne, Jarrah hesitates before the hijackers finally act. They stab a passenger and the two pilots, herd the passengers to the rear with the threat of a fake bomb, and Jarrah turns the plane towards Washington, D.C., aiming for the Capitol. On the ground, American Airlines Flight 77 hits the Pentagon and FAA operations manager Ben Sliney orders the closure of all American airspace.

Through calls to their families on the airphones, the passengers learn of the other attacks and understand that the hijackers intend to die. With the flight crew they gather improvised weapons and plan to storm the cockpit so that a passenger with a pilot's licence and a former air traffic controller can try to land the plane. After praying and making final calls home, they rush the hijackers at Beamer's cry of "Let's roll", overpower two of them and discover the bomb is fake. As they batter down the cockpit door, Jarrah throws the aircraft into a dive, and the plane crashes into a field in Pennsylvania, killing everyone on board. Closing titles note that the order to shoot down hijacked aircraft was given only after Flight 93 had crashed.

Released on April 28, 2006, United 93 opened second at the American box office and became one of the most acclaimed films of the year, with a 90% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes. It earned Academy Award nominations for Greengrass's direction and for its film editing.

title: The Phantom of the Opera
tagline: The classic musical comes to the big screen for the first time.
overview: Deformed since birth, a bitter man known only as the Phantom lives in the sewers underneath the Paris Opera House. He falls in love with the obscure chorus singer Christine, and privately tutors her while terrorizing the rest of the opera house and demanding Christine be given lead roles. Things get worse when Christine meets back up with her childhood acquaintance Raoul and the two fall in love
plot:
The Phantom of the Opera is a musical drama film directed by Joel Schumacher, released in 2004 by Warner Bros. Pictures. The movie is an adaptation of Gaston Leroux's 1910 novel of the same name.

The story takes place at the Paris Opera House in the late 19th century. The Phantom (Gerard Butler), a mysterious and disfigured musical genius, lives beneath the opera house. He is a recluse who uses his talent to create music that haunts the opera's performers. The Phantom becomes obsessed with Christine Daaé (Emilie de Ravin), a young and talented soprano.

Christine is discovered by the opera's manager, Monsieur Firmin (Patrick Wilson), and becomes an overnight sensation. However, she soon attracts the attention of the opera's leading tenor, Raoul, Vicomte de Chagny (Ciarán Hinds). The Phantom becomes jealous of Christine's relationship with Raoul and begins to terrorize the opera house.

As the story unfolds, it is revealed that the Phantom was once a musician who fell in love with Christine when she was a child. He became her mentor and taught her how to sing. However, Christine eventually left him for Raoul, which led to the Phantom's disfigurement and his descent into madness.

The Phantom kidnaps Christine and forces her to perform at the opera house, where he can hear her sing. Meanwhile, Raoul tries to rescue Christine from the Phantom's clutches. The Phantom becomes increasingly unhinged as Christine's relationship with Raoul deepens.

In a dramatic confrontation, the Phantom reveals his true identity to Christine and Raoul. However, instead of killing them, he allows Christine to leave with Raoul. As they depart, the Phantom disappears into the darkness, leaving behind his mask and his music.

The movie ends with Christine and Raoul reunited, but the Phantom's legacy lives on through his music. The film features a range of memorable songs, including "Music of the Night," "All I Ask of You," and "Masquerade."

Overall, the 2004 adaptation of The Phantom of the Opera is a visually stunning and emotionally charged retelling of Gaston Leroux's classic novel. While it deviates from the original story in some ways, it captures the essence of the Phantom's tragic love story and his enduring legacy as a musical genius.

title: Happy Feet
tagline: WARNING: May Cause Toe-Tapping.
overview: Into the world of the Emperor Penguins, who find their soul mates through song, a penguin is born who cannot sing. But he can tap dance something fierce!
plot:
Happy Feet is a 2006 animated musical comedy-drama film produced by Kennedy Miller Productions, Village Roadshow Pictures, and Warner Bros. Feature Animation. The movie follows the story of Mumble, an Emperor Penguin who lives in Antarctica.

The film begins with Mumble, a young Emperor Penguin, born to parents Norma Jean and Memphis. However, Mumble is different from his peers as he has two left feet instead of the traditional right-left flipper arrangement. This makes it difficult for him to dance like other penguins, which is an essential part of their mating rituals.

As Mumble grows up, he struggles to find his place among his colony. He tries to fit in by mimicking the movements of the other penguins, but his clumsiness and lack of coordination make it impossible. The elders of the colony view Mumble's uniqueness as a curse, and they shun him.

One day, Mumble meets Gloria, an Adelie Penguin who is different from the rest of her colony due to her love for singing. Gloria becomes Mumble's friend and confidant, and together they explore the world beyond their colony. They discover that humans are polluting the ocean, causing a decline in fish populations, which affects the penguins' food supply.

Mumble decides to embark on a journey to find the source of the problem and save his colony. He sets out with Gloria and a group of penguin friends, including Ramón, a wise-cracking Rockhopper Penguin who becomes Mumble's mentor. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous ice caves, fierce predators, and rival colonies.

As Mumble navigates this new world, he learns to accept himself and his uniqueness. He discovers that his two left feet are not a curse but a gift, allowing him to tap dance in a unique style that captivates the humans. The humans, led by a kind-hearted scientist named Adelie, work together with Mumble's colony to find a solution to the pollution problem.

The climax of the film features an epic dance battle between Mumble and his rival, Ramón, which showcases their respective tap dancing skills. In the end, Mumble's unique style wins over the humans, and they work together to clean up the ocean and restore the fish populations.

The movie concludes with Mumble returning home as a hero, celebrated by his colony for his bravery and creativity. He finds love with Gloria, and they start a family of their own. The film ends on a hopeful note, emphasizing the importance of self-acceptance, friendship, and working together to overcome challenges.

Overall, Happy Feet is a heartwarming story about embracing individuality and finding one's true purpose. The movie features stunning animation, catchy musical numbers, and lovable characters that make it a delight for audiences of all ages.

title: Beyond Borders
tagline: Where hope survives.
overview: Sarah Jordan, an American living in London in 1984, is married to the son of a wealthy British industrialist. She encounters Nick Callahan, a renegade doctor, whose impassioned plea for help to support his relief efforts in war-torn Africa moves her deeply. As a result, Sarah embarks upon a journey of discovery that leads to danger, heartbreak and romance in the far corners of the world.
plot:
Beyond Borders is a 2003 American romantic drama about international aid workers, directed by Martin Campbell and starring Angelina Jolie and Clive Owen, with Teri Polo, Linus Roache, Noah Emmerich and Kate Ashfield in supporting roles. James Horner composed the score. The film reflected Jolie's real-life work in humanitarian relief, and alongside its release she published Notes from My Travels, a collection of journals from her missions as a Goodwill Ambassador for the United Nations refugee agency.

In 1984, Sarah Jordan is a sheltered American socialite married to a wealthy Englishman and living in London. At a charity gala, an uninvited guest, the renegade doctor Nick Callahan, bursts in to deliver a furious plea on behalf of starving children in his care, bringing with him an emaciated refugee boy. Deeply shaken and drawn to Nick and his cause, Sarah impulsively leaves her job at an art gallery and uses her own money to bring a convoy of food and medical supplies to his remote relief camp in famine-stricken Ethiopia, where she meets Nick and his colleague Dr. Elliott Hauser.

The experience transforms her. Over the following decade Sarah becomes a dedicated aid worker with the United Nations refugee agency, while her marriage grows distant. Her paths with Nick cross repeatedly in some of the world's most dangerous places, including Cambodia under the threat of the Khmer Rouge, where the two finally act on their long-suppressed attraction, and later Chechnya. She discovers that the harsh realities of war and politics, the compromises demanded by those who fund relief, and her persistent romantic attraction to the passionate, self-destructive Nick are changing her life in ways she never anticipated. When Nick goes missing in Chechnya, Sarah risks everything to find him, a decision that ends in tragedy.

The film was shot in locations including Namibia and Canada. It was a critical and commercial failure. Rotten Tomatoes reports a 14% approval rating from 102 reviews, with a consensus calling it well-intentioned but sanctimonious and exploitative in its use of human suffering as a backdrop for romance, and Metacritic gave it 32 out of 100. Jolie received a Golden Raspberry nomination for Worst Actress for this film and Lara Croft Tomb Raider: The Cradle of Life.

title: Big Nothing
tagline: They wrote the book on how not to be criminals.
overview: A frustrated, unemployed teacher joins forces with a scammer and his girlfriend in a blackmailing scheme.
plot:
Big Nothing is a 2006 black comedy crime film directed by Jean-Baptiste Andrea, starring David Schwimmer and Simon Pegg alongside Alice Eve, with Natascha McElhone, Jon Polito and Mimi Rogers in supporting roles. The film premiered at the Cardiff Film Festival in November 2006 and was released in the United Kingdom the following month. Although the story is set in a small town in Oregon, it was shot largely on the Isle of Man and in Wales, including Barry in the Vale of Glamorgan and locations around Monmouthshire, with additional scenes filmed in British Columbia.

Schwimmer plays Charlie, a former schoolteacher who is struggling to support his family and who manages to get fired on his very first day working at a call centre. His cynical co-worker Gus, played by Pegg, approaches him with what he presents as an easy and victimless scheme: Gus has evidence that a local reverend has been visiting pornographic websites, and he proposes that they blackmail the clergyman for a large sum of money. Josie McBroom, a former teenage beauty queen played by Eve, overhears them and forces her way into the plan as a third partner.

The scheme collapses almost immediately. While Gus goes to the reverend's house, Charlie heads to a bar to set up an alibi, only to discover that the person who could contradict it is drinking there. Hurrying to the house, he finds the reverend apparently dead and no sign of Gus, and in a panic he hides the body in a septic tank, a decision that turns out to have been fatal for a man who was not actually dead. Man of the Year is a 2006 American political comedy-drama with thriller elements, written and directed by Barry Levinson and produced by James G. Robinson. Robin Williams stars as Tom Dobbs, the host of a satirical political talk show who runs for president, and the cast also includes Christopher Walken, Laura Linney, Lewis Black and Jeff Goldblum.

Dobbs's show taps into public frustration with divisive, special-interest politics. He laughs off an audience member's suggestion that he run for the White House, but after a wave of online support he announces a campaign on the air, gets on the ballot in 13 states and joins a national debate with Democratic incumbent President Kellogg and Republican Senator Mills. Meanwhile Eleanor Green, an employee of Delacroy, the company supplying the country's voting machines, discovers that its system does not count correctly, but company head James Hemmings deletes her warning e-mail. Dobbs initially takes the campaign so seriously that he worries his manager, Jack Menken, and producer Eddie Langston, but at the debate he reverts to comedy and climbs in the polls. On Election Day the early returns follow exactly the pattern Eleanor predicted, and Dobbs sweeps his 13 states, winning enough electoral votes to become president-elect.

When Eleanor presses the issue, she is attacked at home and injected with drugs, then discredited as an addict and fired. She tracks Dobbs down and works out the flaw: regardless of the actual votes, the software favors names with double letters in alphabetical order, so Dobbs beats Kellogg, who beats Mills. Dobbs, increasingly smitten with her, plans to reveal the truth, but Delacroy preempts him by claiming Eleanor tried to rig the vote for him, and its agents pursue her until one rams the phone booth she is calling from. In her ambulance she convinces Dobbs, and although polls show most Americans want him in office, he announces on Saturday Night Live's Weekend Update that the vote was flawed and covered up and that he will not run in the new election. In 1959, after his Hamlet musical Funny Boy flops, washed-up Broadway producer Max Bialystock hires nervous accountant Leo Bloom. Going over the books, Leo notes that because flops are expected to lose money, no one checks their finances, so a producer who oversold shares in a sure failure could pocket up to $2 million. Leo first refuses to join Max's scheme, but, dreaming of becoming a producer, he quits his firm to form Bialystock & Bloom. Seeking the worst play ever written, they find Springtime for Hitler, an adoring tribute by ex-Nazi Franz Liebkind, and win the rights by swearing his sacred Siegfried Oath. They hire the flamboyant, failing director Roger De Bris and his assistant Carmen Ghia, who agree on condition that the show be made "gay", and Max takes on Ulla, a Swedish woman who arrives to audition, as a secretary. Max raises the money by romancing elderly women, while Leo falls for Ulla.

Franz wins the role of Hitler at auditions but breaks his leg on opening night, and Roger takes his place. The audience is appalled until Roger's outrageously camp Hitler makes them read the show as satire, and it becomes a hit. Panicked that their fraud will be exposed, Max and Leo quarrel, and Franz, enraged that they mocked his idol, tries to shoot them, drawing the police. Max is arrested while Leo flees to Rio de Janeiro with Ulla, but Leo returns to defend his partner in court, and the judge sends both to Sing Sing with Franz. Their prison musical, Prisoners of Love, earns them a pardon from the governor, and Max and Leo become successful Broadway producers. In a post-credits scene, the cast and Brooks sing the audience out of the theater.

Universal Pictures released the film in North America, opening in limited release on December 16, 2005, before going wide on December 25. Competing against films such as King Kong and The Chronicles of Narnia, it grossed about $38 million worldwide against a $45 million budget. Reviews were mixed, with 51% on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it stale and stagy, and 52 on Metacritic.

title: Wrong Turn
tagline: It's the last one you'll ever take.
overview: Chris crashes into a carload of other young people, and the group of stranded motorists is soon lost in the woods of West Virginia, where they're hunted by three cannibalistic mountain men who are grossly disfigured by generations of inbreeding.
plot:
Wrong Turn is a 2003 American slasher film directed by Rob Schmidt and written by Alan B. McElroy, starring Desmond Harrington, Eliza Dushku, Emmanuelle Chriqui, Jeremy Sisto and Kevin Zegers. The first installment of the Wrong Turn series, it was conceived as a 1970s-style horror film and produced by Summit Entertainment with Constantin Film, with creature effects designed by Stan Winston. It follows a group of people stalked by deformed, inbred, cannibalistic mountain men in the forests of West Virginia.

After two college students are killed while rock climbing in a remote stretch of woods, medical student Chris Flynn, driving through the mountains to a business meeting, is held up by a traffic jam. Rather than wait, he gets directions to a back road from an unhelpful old gas station owner and turns onto Bear Mountain Road, where he crashes into a car stranded by barbed wire laid deliberately across the pavement. The car belongs to five friends on a camping trip: Jessie, Carly, Scott, Evan and Francine. Evan and Francine stay with the vehicles while the others look for help, but both are soon killed by unseen attackers. Chris, Jessie, Carly and Scott stumble onto an isolated cabin full of human remains and are forced to hide when its occupants, three cannibal brothers known as Three Finger, Saw Tooth and One Eye, return carrying Francine's body. After escaping, the survivors are hunted through the forest, coming across the cars of earlier victims and seeking refuge in an old watchtower, from which they radio for help. The cannibals set the tower ablaze, and in the chase through the trees and along a waterfall the group is steadily whittled down. With Jessie captured and taken back to the cabin, an injured Chris must find a way to rescue her and escape the mountain men's territory.

Despite grossing $28.7 million worldwide against a $12 million budget, Wrong Turn received mixed reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes, 41% of 82 critics' reviews are positive, with a consensus calling it an unremarkable slasher that fails to distinguish itself from others of its ilk. The film launched a franchise of sequels and a 2021 reboot.
